Furthermore, functional cardiac drug assessment is performed by characterizing contractile responses to norepinephrine and isradipine. This NERIS approach is expected to be widely applied in cardiomyocyte mechanophysiology and cardiac drug assessment.

articles.title: Poly(acrylamido) PEG-Alternative Lipids Rescue mRNA Efficacy during Repeated Dosing and Enhance Immune Cell Delivery
articles.abstract: Following the successes of the messenger RNA (mRNA) lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines against COVID-19, mRNA-LNPs are being explored for varied multidose applications including cancer immunotherapies and protein replacement therapies. LNPs rely on poly(ethylene glycol)-lipid (PEG-lipid) coatings for stability, but increasing anti-PEG antibody prevalence threatens repeat-dose efficacy and increases pseudoallergic risk, creating an urgent need for alternatives. Here, we introduce poly(acrylamido) lipids (PAM-lipids), a family of polymer lipids that effectively replace PEG-lipids in mRNA-LNP formulations. Systematic variation of monomer chemistry, molar mass, and end group reveals critical structure–activity relationships determining LNP size, polydispersity, and transfection efficiency. Varying PAM monomer chemistry allows minimization of antipolymer antibody cross-reactivity, with multiple PAM-lipids demonstrating no anti-PEG antibody binding. Several PAM-LNPs exhibit superior mRNA transfection efficacy to PEGylated clinical benchmarks in vitro and in vivo across multiple cell types, organs, routes of administration, and mRNA cargos. In particular, lead PAM-LNPs enhance mRNA delivery to dendritic cells (up to 120-fold in vitro and 3-fold in vivo) and macrophages (4-fold in vivo), with 2.5-fold superior lymph node expression, driven in part by increased cellular association and lymphoid targeting. Crucially, PAM-LNPs evade circulating anti-PEG antibodies to rescue lost mRNA efficacy after repeated dosing, resulting in 300% mRNA expression relative to that of PEG-LNPs. These findings demonstrate PAM-lipids as a chemically varied, immunologically compatible family of PEG alternatives for mRNA-LNP therapeutics.

articles.title: Riveting Rubidium in Alkali-Metal Layers: High-Performance P2-Type Layered Oxide Cathodes for Potassium-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Layered manganese-based oxides for potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) suffer from severe structural degradation, primarily due to irreversible phase transitions, Jahn–Teller distortion, and sluggish K+ diffusion kinetics. Here, we propose an alkali-metal site riveting strategy by selectively incorporating oversized Rb+ ions into the prismatic sites of P2-type K0.55Mn0.8Ni0.1T0.1O2. The introduced Rb+ acts as a rigid pillar, expanding the interlayer spacing and reinforcing adjacent transition-metal–oxygen (TM–O) bonds. This synergistic modulation not only widens the two-dimensional diffusion channels for rapid K+ transport but also effectively suppresses the detrimental P2–P′2 phase transition and mitigates Jahn–Teller distortion of Mn3+. Consequently, the optimized K0.55Rb0.025Mn0.8Ni0.1Ti0.1O2 cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 105.3 mAh g–1 at a current density of 20 mA g–1, outstanding rate capability (56.1 mAh g–1 at 500 mA g–1), and long-term cycling stability with 82.1% capacity retention after 500 cycles. Furthermore, a pouch cell paired with a soft carbon anode achieves 81.3% capacity retention over 300 cycles. This work demonstrates that anchoring oversized cations in alkali-metal layers provides a universal and effective strategy toward near-zero-strain layered oxide cathodes for advanced PIBs.

articles.title: Visible Light Modulates Macrophage Phenotype and Photoresponsive Carbon Monoxide Delivery
articles.abstract: Photoresponsive drug delivery systems are often described as bioorthogonal. However, certain wavelengths and intensities of visible light are known to modulate cellular phenotypes. This apparent discrepancy highlights a gap in knowledge with direct implications for the design of photoresponsive drug delivery systems. In this report, we investigated the response of primary macrophages to visible light (405–630 nm) due to their broad tissue distribution, phenotypic plasticity, and central role in orchestrating immune responses across diverse pathologies. We found distinct wavelength-dependent changes in cytochrome c oxidase activity, metabolic function, cytokine secretion, and biomarker expression at clinically relevant intensities of light. Further investigation of red light (630 nm) demonstrated complex dose-dependent metabolic and phenotypic responses. To illustrate the clinical implications of these findings, we employed 470 nm-triggerable carbon monoxide-releasing micelles to deconvolute the individual and combined effects of light exposure and therapeutic payloads. Our findings suggest that macrophages respond in a wavelength and intensity-dependent manner, and incorporating photoresponsive carbon monoxide-releasing systems elicits distinct immunomodulatory responses compared to irradiation alone. This work establishes a basic design framework for leveraging light parameters such as wavelength and intensity to achieve desirable immunomodulatory responses with photoresponsive drug delivery systems for specific disease applications.

articles.title: Visualizing Single-Cell Secretion with Electrochemiluminescence Imaging
articles.abstract: Secretory proteins encode cellular states not only through their abundance but also through their intracellular transport before being released. However, visualizing protein secretion behavior with molecular specificity and a low background remains challenging. Here, we report VEGF-responsive electrochemiluminescence (ECL) nanoemitters that enable spatiotemporal mapping of intracellular protein distribution at different stages of the secretion process by integrating a metal–organic framework (MOF) confining Ru(bpy)32+ with DNA tetrahedral gates (DTGs) programmed with aptamers. The MOF core provides bright, stable, and electrically addressable ECL emission, whereas the discrete DTGs regulate coreactant accessibility and prevent premature emission until VEGF recognition triggers gate displacement and restores ECL activity, converting intracellular molecular recognition events to quantitative optical signals. This architecture enables rapid, concentration-dependent, and selective activation, allowing high contrast discrimination of VEGF-rich tumor cells from epithelial cells. Under DFO stimulation, single-cell ECL imaging revealed heterogeneous VEGF upregulation and mapped its progressive redistribution from the perinuclear region to the cell periphery during secretion. This gated ECL platform enables quantitative spatiotemporal visualization of protein secretion behavior beyond the static molecular localization.

articles.title: Influence of coherent elastic strain on phase separation in BCC Nb–V alloys
Influence of intrinsic oxygen vacancies on interface atomic structure and functionality in fluorite and bixbyite heterostructures
A Tailored Multifunctional Lithium Organosilicate Salt Constructing Robust Interphases for High Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted extensive attention due to their high energy density. However, when lithium (Li) metal is paired with high‐voltage cathode materials, its practical application is limited by issues such as continuous oxidative decomposition of electrolytes and the incompatibility between electrolytes and aggressive electrodes. Herein, we synthesize a fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt (i.e., lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate, LiPBS) to address the aforementioned challenges. The results show that the LiPBS can form a protective and rigid‐flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode surface. Simultaneously, PBS− readily forms a coordination ion pair (CIP) with Li+, constructing an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li anode. Furthermore, Si─O groups in the LiPBS can effectively scavenge HF and H2O from the electrolyte. These advantageous properties enable LiCoO2 (LCO, 1.89 mAh cm−2)/Li (50 µm) coin and pouch cells to exhibit excellent cycling performance at high voltages and elevated rates‒for example, retaining 82% capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C and 4.5 V, compared to 80% retention after only 67 cycles for the LiPF6‐based counterpart. This performance is maintained even at an elevated temperature of 50°C. This work highlights the crucial role of lithium organosilicate salt in determining the electrochemical performance of LMBs.

articles.title: Axial Cl‐Coordinated Porous FeCoZn Trimetallic Single‐Atom Catalysts: Breaking the Linear Scaling Relation for Superior Oxygen Reduction Reaction and Ultrastable Zinc‐Air Batteries
articles.abstract: Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M–N4. To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single‐atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF‐8‐derived ion exchange and gas‐phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M–N4 configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half‐wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge‐discharge cycling in zinc‐air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge‐type adsorption of O2 and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.

articles.title: In Situ Defect Engineering of Atomically Dispersed Iridium on Mesoporous Mixed Oxide Frameworks for Robust PEM Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble‐metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid‐etching‐assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh‐loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal‐support interaction to establish a highly electron‐deficient, rigid Ir‐O‐Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g−1 at 1.53 V versus RHE (31‐fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mgIr cm−2, it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial‐relevant 1 A cm−2. Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation‐prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum‐mechanical origin: strong metal‐support interaction‐induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d‐band center to ‐3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity‐stability trade‐off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial‐grade acidic water electrolysis.

articles.title: Oxyhalide‐Derived Nb‐O‐Cl Interfacial Frameworks for Mitigating Oxygen‐Related Degradation and Facilitating Li+ Transport in High‐Voltage Ni‐Rich Cathodes
articles.abstract: High‐voltage Ni‐rich cathodes coupled with sulfide solid electrolytes suffer from coupled instability of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and Li+ transport discontinuity under deep delithiation. Conventional oxide coatings mainly act as passive barrier layers that separate reactive contacts but remain structurally isolated from layered cathodes without simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and Li+ transport. Here, we report an oxyhalide‐enabled interfacial chemistry strategy based on a reconstructive Nb‐O‐Cl framework on LiNi0.83Co0.07Mn0.10O2 cathodes (denoted as C‐NCM). Derived from a mixed‐anion LiNbOCl4 (LNOC) precursor, the Nb‐O‐Cl framework undergoes mechanochemically assisted interfacial reconstruction, forming an amorphous oxyhalide interphase coupled with a Nb‐containing near‐surface region. Unlike passive oxide barriers, this chemically integrated architecture simultaneously reshapes the local Ni‐O electronic environment and mediates interface‐crossing Li+ transport. Nb‐O/Nb‐O‐Cl coordination redistributes local charge and is associated with improved retention of highly oxidized Ni‐O configurations and mitigated oxygen‐related irreversible evolution, while the Cl‐containing oxyhalide framework provides an ionically conductive transition region that facilitates Li+ migration across the cathode/electrolyte interface. Accordingly, C‐NCM exhibits reduced sulfide‐derived interphase formation and slower resistance growth, together with 88.17% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 4.5 V under high cathode loading. This work shifts cathode/sulfide‐electrolyte interface design from passive oxide‐barrier protection toward reconstructive mixed‐anion interfacial chemistry.

articles.title: Tracing and Healing Multiscale Defects for Cost‐Effective Lithium Carbonate‐Derived Layered Oxide Cathodes
articles.abstract: Lithium carbonate (LC) is markedly cheaper than lithium hydroxide (LH) but remains underused for layered oxide cathodes because LC‐derived materials perform poorly. Here, using a mid‐Ni cathode, LiNi0.65Co0.05Mn0.30O2 (N65), we trace this performance gap to LC‐induced defects that span length scales, from atomic‐scale disorder to nanoscale and microscale porosity. These defects originate from three features of the carbonate pathway that act across the solid, liquid, and gas phases, namely decoupled dehydration and lithiation, late melting of the carbonate, and a locally oxygen‐deficient atmosphere from evolving CO2. Guided by this picture, we heal the defects with a single secondary heat treatment (SH) that adds an optimized amount of LH, simultaneously replenishing lithium, restoring an oxidizing atmosphere, and densifying the structure. The resulting N65‐LC SH achieves discharge capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability comparable to those of the LH counterpart, while cutting the lithium precursor cost by 9% to 16% relative to conventional all‐LH synthesis. More broadly, the gap between LH and LC is not an intrinsic property of the carbonate but a consequence of a precursor‐specific pathway that, once traced, can be engineered around to unlock low‐cost, high‐performance Ni‐based layered oxide cathodes.

articles.title: A Multifunctional Smart Window for Adaptive Solar, Thermal, and Electromagnetic Management in Buildings
articles.abstract: Smart windows could reduce building energy demand, but most regulate only one or two spectral bands and do not address the increasingly complex electromagnetic environments of modern buildings. Here we report a multifunctional window that combines electrochemical switching with low-frequency mechanical reorientation to control visible, near-infrared, long-wave infrared, and microwave responses. A transparent Ti3C2T x MXene electrode (T 550 nm > 60%, R s ≈ 40 Ω/sq) and a PEDOT:PSS layer enable electrochemical regulation of glare and solar heat gain through coupled visible–near-infrared optical switching. Reorientation of a Janus interface switches the outward long-wave emissivity (ε LWIR) between ∼0.83 and ∼0.38 for cooling- and heating-oriented operation. The device also shows reversible X-band shielding modulation from 15.5 to 20.2 dB. Comparative chamber tests, climate-resolved building simulations and carbon accounting suggest reduced annual HVAC demand and associated CO2 emissions in representative climates.

articles.title: A Precursor Doping Source Layer Engineering to Suppress Antisite Defects Enabling High Efficiency in Cu2ZnSnS4 Solar Cell
articles.abstract: Pure‐sulfide kesterite Cu2ZnSnS4 (CZTS) is an attractive photovoltaic absorber, but its efficiency is largely constrained by antisite defects (e.g., CuZn) and the associated band‐tail‐induced carrier losses. Here, we develop a precursor doping source layer (PDSL) engineering, in which an ultrathin CdS layer deposited on the porous CZTS precursor surface serves as an active Cd dopant during sulfurization. Different from conventional Cd cation doping, this localized PDSL targeted releases dopant during CZTS absorber formation, enabling Cd incorporation to be coupled with thermodynamics of phase evolution and kinetics of grain coalescence. Such reaction‐coupled Cd delivery stabilizes Zn‐site occupation and weakens Cu/Zn interchange, thereby mitigating CuZn‐dominated defect responses and disorder‐induced band tails. As a result, trap‐assisted recombination and energetic fluctuations are reduced, leading to improved carrier transport and collection. The obtained pure‐sulfide CZTS/ZTO photovoltaic device delivers an efficiency of 12.23% and a large‐area (1.00 cm2) efficiency of 10.31%, reaching the leading level of efficiency reported for non‐alloyed pure‐sulfide kesterite thin‐film solar cells. This work highlights PDSL design as an effective approach for overcoming defect‐limited performance in kesterite photovoltaics.

articles.title: Beyond Primary Nucleation: Molecular Basis of Peptide Crystal Secondary Nucleation at Soft Interface
articles.abstract: The formation of peptide 2D crystals with well‐organized molecular arrays by primary nucleation mechanism have provided an efficient way to incorporate biofunctions into the underlying single layer graphene and MoS2, leading to broad applications for biosensing, biomedicine and bioelectronics. Further realizing a high‐level architecture of peptide 3D crystals coupling with the underlying nanomaterials would expand its applications for the next‐generation bionanodevices, while facing a big challenge. A layer‐by‐layer stacking of 3D peptide assemblies through secondary nucleation (SN) mechanism at soft interface provides an available strategy while its molecular basis has been rarely explored. We utilized time‐resolved 3‐dimensional atomic force microscopy (3D‐AFM) to directly observe SN and growth mechanism of stacked peptide 3D crystals on highly oriented pyrolytic graphite (HOPG). Moreover, the formation details of peptide 3D crystals including nucleation sites, growth dynamics, molecular‐resolution nanostructures, phase transitions, and cross‐seeding growth were discovered. Such non‐traditional methodology in engineering peptide 3D crystals would bring new prospects for nanoscience and nanotechnology.

articles.title: Bifunctional Carbon‐Sensitized Hollow Heterojunctions for Dual‐Mode Sensing of Emerging Contaminant 6‐PPD
articles.abstract: N‐(1,3‐dimethylbutyl)‐N′‐phenyl‐p‐phenylenediamine (6‐PPD), a ubiquitous rubber tire antioxidant, poses a severe threat to ecological safety due to its pronounced ecotoxicity. This work achieves the unprecedented dual‐mode photoelectrochemical and electrochemical (PEC‐EC) sensing of 6‐PPD through a dual‐mode platform endowed with bifunctional catalytic signal amplification. Integrating a novel hollow Bi@BiOBr/CdLa2S4 heterojunction with multiwalled carbon nanotubes, this dual‐mode platform delivers highly stable, efficiently amplified signals. It demonstrates exceptional sensing performance with remarkably broad linear ranges from 1 to 10000 nM for PEC and 1 to 20000 nM for EC. By coupling Kelvin probe force microscopy and density functional theory with comprehensive characterizations, the intrinsic sensing mechanisms, specifically the charge transfer pathways and catalytic adsorption preferences, are systematically elucidated. Crucially, this dual‐signal cross‐validation ensures reliable quantification in complex real‐world matrices, and portable on‐site analysis is achieved via smartphone Bluetooth integration. Ultimately, by synergizing advanced heterojunction engineering with a dual‐mode sensing strategy, this work establishes a robust and highly efficient methodology for emerging contaminant monitoring with exceptional application prospects.

articles.title: Coordination‐Based Regulation of Integrated Photoanodes for Boosted Water Oxidation
articles.abstract: Photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting for hydrogen evolution has been deemed a promising approach for solving the world's sustainable energy‐related and environmental challenges. However, poor charge separation in semiconductor photoelectrodes is the major challenge to overall solar energy conversion efficiencies. Moreover, n‐type semiconductors as photoanodes exhibit sluggish water oxidation kinetics. Coordination‐based regulation between semiconductors and cocatalysts as a form of interface optimization in integrated photoanodes has been proved an effective strategy to optimize charge transfer and water oxidation processes. Herein, recent critical headway on improving the efficiency of semiconductor‐based photoanodes for water oxidation via coordination‐based regulation is reviewed. In particular, this review aims to clarify how coordination‐based regulation achieves performance enhancement through the joint modulation of surface states and spin‐electronic states. The mechanism of coordination‐based regulation in integrated photoanodes on charge transfer and water oxidation kinetics prioritization scheme is demonstrated in detail. These benefits of coordination‐based regulation for efficient and stable water splitting devices will show huge advantages in the future.

articles.title: Correction to “A MOF‐Based Core–Shell System Enables Controlled Release and Ordered Assembly of Nano‐Hydroxyapatite for Enamel Remineralization”
Decoupling Li+ Transport in Self‐Healing Polymer Dual‐Salt Electrolytes for Room Temperature Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) stand as leading candidates for advancing high-energy-density lithium metal batteries toward next-generation applications. However, the inherent crystallinity of conventional polymer matrices severely limits ionic conductivity (IC) and Li+ transference number (tLi +), while imposing large interfacial resistance and uncontrollable lithium dendrite growth—critical bottlenecks hindering practical room-temperature application. Herein, we report a dual-salt incorporation strategy within a self-curing polymer framework to overcome these challenges. The anion-anion interactions of the dual-salt system within the polymer network immobilize the anions, thereby liberating a greater number Li+ ions. Additionally, the salt-polymer interactions alter the polymer energy levels, cooperatively enhancing the IC to 2.23 mS cm−1 and the tLi + to 0.55. The electrolyte sustains stable Li||Li symmetric cycling for over 2000 h. When integrated with a LiFePO4 cathode, the full cell delivers 133 mAh g1 at 1C with 75% capacity retention over 700 cycles, while the NMC811||Li cell achieves 135 mAh g−1, retaining 72% of its initial capacity over 250 cycles. Additionally, the electrolyte exhibits inherent flame retardancy and uniform Li+ plating-stripping, effectively suppressing dendrite penetration. This design strategy provides a viable route to ambient-temperature, self-curing GPEs that enhance battery safety and suppress dead lithium.

articles.title: Dual‐Site Engineering of a Noble‐Metal‐Free Z‐Scheme Heterojunction for Radical‐Kinetics‐Steered Selective C–C Coupling
articles.abstract: Selective photocatalytic C─C homocoupling of amines remains challenging due to uncontrollable radical kinetics and over‐oxidation. Herein, we construct a noble‐metal‐free Z‐scheme Cr‐TiO2@N‐C/CdS heterojunction photocatalyst that decouples thermodynamic and kinetic control through a dual‐site strategy. The incorporation of N‐doped carbon buffer layer not only resolves the intrinsic work function mismatch between Cr‐TiO2 and CdS for efficient Z‐scheme charge transfer, but also facilitates rational control over the sequential arrangement of interfaces, thereby precisely regulating the coupling sites. Thermodynamically, Cr‐induced impurity levels near the valence band edge of TiO2 moderate hole oxidation potential, preventing over‐oxidation of benzylamine. Kinetically, at the CdS surface, strong electronic interactions between surface three‐coordinated Cd atoms and the Ph(•CH)NH2 radical impede further oxidation to imine, maintaining a high local radical concentration and exclusively driving C─C coupling. Consequently, under blue light, this heterojunction selectively converts benzylamine to the corresponding diamine (∼80% selectivity and an apparent quantum yield of 2.78%) with simultaneous high‐rate hydrogen evolution through a concerted proton‐coupled electron transfer pathway. This selectivity is broadly applicable to other benzylamine derivatives and benzyl alcohol systems. This work demonstrates that coordinated regulation of redox and surface reaction sites provides a robust strategy for achieving controllable radical dynamics and selective C─C bond synthesis.

articles.title: Energy‐Autonomous Janus Nanofibrous Textile for Sustainable Bi‐Directional Thermal Management and Self‐Powered Wearable Electronics
articles.abstract: Achieving energy autonomy and zero‐energy bidirectional personal thermal management (PTM) in wearable electronics remains a formidable challenge. Here, we fabricate an energy‐autonomous Janus PS@PT textile via a multifunctional synergistic filler strategy, integrating alkyl‐chain‐modified silica and photothermal nanoparticles into poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF‐HFP), denoted as PS and PT, respectively. This strategy yields synergistic effects: the fillers act as PTM enhancers for adaptive regulation, as dielectric modifiers increasing the β‐phase content, and as charge trap centers strengthening interfacial polarization, raising the dielectric constant to 1.27 times that of pristine PVDF‐HFP. Under 1000 W/m2 irradiation, the PS layer achieves radiative cooling of ∼2.7°C (net cooling power 97.1 W/m2) with 95.3% solar reflectance and 92.2% MIR emissivity, while the PT layer delivers solar heating of ∼12.9°C (net heating power 260.43 W/m2) with 49.9% solar absorptance. Significantly, the functional fillers substantially optimize the dielectric properties and charge‐trapping capability, effectively suppressing high‐temperature performance degradation. At 85°C, the output voltages of PT and PS show enhancements of 159.7% and 144.9% relative to room‐temperature values. This work establishes a new paradigm for synergistically enhancing PTM capability and stable triboelectric output in a single device, offering a promising pathway toward multifunctional integration in smart textiles.

articles.title: Engineering Acidic CO2 Electroreduction for Efficient and Durable Formic Acid Production
articles.abstract: Electrochemical synthesis of formic acid (HCOOH) via the carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR) in acidic electrolytes can circumvent the severe CO2 loss in alkaline and neutral conditions. However, simultaneously attaining high HCOOH production efficiency and durable long‐term operation in acidic CO2RR remains a critical bottleneck impeding the technology's practical deployment. Herein, we first discuss the core challenges faced by acidic CO2RR to HCOOH, most notably the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, serious catalyst deactivation, and the inherent trade‐off between product selectivity and carbon utilization efficiency. Then, key strategies to improve CO2 to HCOOH conversion efficiency are systematically summarized, with a focus on stabilization of key reaction intermediates and rational engineering of the catalytic microenvironment. Additionally, effective approaches to enhance catalyst durability, as well as the design of advanced electrolyzer configurations tailored for acidic CO2RR systems, are elaborated. We end the review by outlining the existing challenges and future directions for accelerating the industrialization of acidic CO2RR to HCOOH.

articles.title: Engineering Ni0/δ+‐Coσ+ Pairs to Facilitate Interfacial Water Restructuring and Promote Volmer‐Heyrovsky‐Dominated Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Metal phosphide alloy materials exhibit application potential in alkaline water electrolysis for green hydrogen production. However, interfacial H2O structure, along with protons kinetic behavior at the interface in hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) remain elusive. Herein, we report a site‐substitution‐electronic modulation strategy to construct P‐bridged Ni0/δ+‐Coσ+ pairs in Ni mesh (NM) supported NiCoP (NiCoP‐NM), wherein Co substitution at Ni sites modulates the electronic structure and generates an electron‐rich Ni center. The experiment and theoretical studies reveal that the Ni0/δ+‐Coσ+ pairs redistribute the electron spin orientation at Ni sites, strengthening H* binding, and increasing surface H* coverage, which accelerates Heyrovsky kinetics by facilitating H2 release. Additional, Ni0/δ+‐Coσ+ pairs reorganize the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network and increase K+ concentration in closest ion plane, leading to stronger H2O adsorption (−1.52 vs. −0.96 eV on NiP‐NM) and a lower H2O dissociation barrier (1.59 vs. 1.64 eV on NiP‐NM), thereby facilitating Volmer kinetics via boosting H2O activation. Consequently, NiCoP‐NM achieves outstanding HER performance with an overpotential of only 86.75 mV at 100 mA cm−2, along with stability over 1000 h. This work offers a new strategy for designing metal phosphide alloys that tailor interfacial water structure and proton dynamics for advanced electrosynthesis.

articles.title: Flexible Neuromorphic Softness Sensory System
articles.abstract: Accurate softness sensing remains a challenge for artificial tactile systems, as conventional force‐based sensing misses key deformation cues. Biological perception instead uses active, displacement‐controlled exploration. Here we report a biomimetic neuromorphic tactile system that integrates iontronic softness sensing, spike‐based signal encoding and organic synaptic processing to enable softness sensory system. Displacement‐controlled operation of a hemispherical pressure sensor produces more discriminative temporal deformation signals than simple pressure sensors. Machine learning reveals interpretable temporal features and confirms high classification accuracy. The signals are encoded into spikes and processed by an organic synaptic device, enabling in‐sensor classification without digital post‐processing. Synaptic outputs demonstrate that material softness can be inferred directly from the excitatory postsynaptic current without complex post‐processing. This work establishes a sensor‐to‐synapse neuromorphic framework for softness perception.

articles.title: From Steric Liability to Structural Asset: Non‐Benzylic Cation–π Anchoring Unlocks Hierarchical Hydrogen‐Bond Networks in Ultra‐Tough Recyclable Aromatic Polyurethane Elastomers
articles.abstract: Aromatic polyurethane elastomers offer intrinsic mechanical advantages, yet their bulky backbones are widely regarded as a steric liability that precludes the formation of ordered hydrogen‐bond networks essential for high toughness. This long‐standing conflict has consequently forced the field to rely on aliphatic precursors. To address this, we introduce thiabicyclononane‐pyridinium ionic crosslinkers to engage the aromatic hard segments through cation–π interactions. This strategy effectively transforms the inherent steric hindrance of benzene rings from an impediment into a potent driving force for assembling dense, hierarchical hydrogen‐bonded networks. The resulting elastomer (MA‐S) exhibits exceptional mechanical integration, featuring a high tensile strength of 60.3 MPa, an ultra‐high toughness of 283 MJ m−3, outstanding impact resistance and a fracture energy of 198 kJ m−2. These properties stem from the synergistic energy dissipation of hydrogen bonds, dynamic covalent bonds, and cation–π interactions. In addition, these multiple dynamic bonds endow the material with remarkable mechanical property retention (>95%) after multiple thermo‐compression cycles. Furthermore, the aromatic‐rich architecture enables robust π–π interfacial integration with carbon fibers, demonstrating a viable route toward closed‐loop recyclable structural composites. Consequently, this work establishes a versatile molecular design paradigm for creating sustainable, high‐performance polyurethanes that successfully reconcile mechanical robustness with dynamic recyclability.

articles.title: High‐Pressure and High‐Temperature Co‐Engineering of Dislocations and Chemical Short‐Range Order Mitigates the Strength–Ductility–Corrosion Trade‐Off in CoCrNi Medium‐Entropy Alloy
articles.abstract: Conventional processing makes it difficult to develop chemical short‐range order (CSRO) while retaining a high dislocation density in CoCrNi medium‐entropy alloy. Annealing promotes local ordering but accelerates dislocation recovery, whereas deformation introduces dislocations without producing a comparable ordered state. Here, high‐pressure and high‐temperature (HPHT) treatment at 5 GPa and 600°C for 2 h yields 1.3 ± 0.3 nm CSRO domains (projected area fraction, 26.9 ± 3.2%) and a dislocation density of (6.8 ± 0.3) × 1013 m−2 without appreciable grain‐size change. First‐principles calculations show that pressure favors the ordered configuration through a negative ordering volume and raises vacancy formation enthalpy, limiting recovery. This architecture raises yield strength from 326 to 537 MPa and ultimate tensile strength from 800 to 880 MPa while retaining ∼72% elongation. Dislocations dominate the initial strengthening, while nanotwinning, microband formation, and deformation‐induced phase transformation develop within the HPHT‐induced dislocation–CSRO architecture. The same architecture also accelerates Cr‐dominated primary passivation in 0.1 m H2SO4, reducing passive current density from 9.55 to 1.50 µA/cm2. Surface‐sensitive analyses reveal a higher oxide‐like Cr3+/hydroxide‐like Cr3+ ratio and faster development of interconnected Cr─O‐rich regions. These results establish a pressure‐regulated defect‐engineering route integrating strengthening, sustained plasticity, and improved primary passivation.

articles.title: High‐Voltage Electrospinning‐Assisted Defect Engineering in Oxide‐Derived Cu Nanowires Enables Selective CO2 Electroreduction Toward C2+ Products
articles.abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction toward multicarbon (C2+) products remains challenging because conventional Cu catalysts lack the ability to simultaneously optimize intermediate stabilization, proton transfer, and C─C coupling kinetics. Here we report a high‐voltage electrospinning‐assisted defect engineering strategy to regulate the electronic structure of Cu catalysts for selective C2+ electrosynthesis. Defect‐rich CuO nanowire precursors were fabricated by high‐voltage electrospinning and subsequently reconstructed into oxide‐derived Cu (OD‐Cu) nanowires enriched with abundant electronically perturbed Cu sites. The resulting OD‐Cu nanowires exhibit substantially enhanced C2+ selectivity compared with conventional Cu catalysts. Mechanistic studies reveal that high‐voltage electrospinning‐assisted defects reorganize the reorganization of the interfacial water configuration and proton‐transfer dynamics while strengthening Cu─*CO π‐backbonding interactions, thereby optimizing *CO stabilization and promoting hydrogen‐assisted C─C coupling. This work establishes a direct correlation between high‐voltage electrospinning‐assisted defect regulation, electronic structure modulation and multicarbon formation kinetics, providing a general strategy for designing efficient Cu catalysts for selective C2+ electrosynthesis.

articles.title: In Situ Formed Co(OH)F Enabling Electronic and Atomic‐Level Structure Optimization in Medium‐Entropy Fluoride Cathodes for Zinc Batteries
articles.abstract: Cobalt‐based cathodes have attracted considerable attention in aqueous zinc batteries, however, their application remains impeded by intrinsic trade‐off between high electrochemical activity and long‐term cycling stability. Herein, an entropy‐regulated fluoride cathode is proposed to overcome the limitations via co‐engineering electronic and atomic structures. Specifically, x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and first‐principle calculations collectively demonstrate that Co(OH)F is formed in situ within the fluoride matrix during electrochemical cycling and induces electron reconstruction. Concurrently, the generated Co(OH)F shortens Co─F bond length within the entropy‐regulated fluoride, reinforcing atomic‐level structural integrity and enabling excellent cycling performance. Moreover, a hollow architecture is integrated to homogenize flux and electric field distributions, ensuring sufficient accessibility of active sites while mitigating interfacial degradation. Consequently, the assembled zinc battery exhibits a high specific capacity of 252.3 mAh·g−1 and superior cycling stability (92.4% capacity retention after 25 000 cycles at 10 A·g−1 and 90.8% capacity retention after 50 000 cycles at 20 A·g−1). This work demonstrates a synergistic approach that simultaneously achieves high redox activity and structural robustness in cobalt‐based cathodes for zinc batteries.

articles.title: Industrial‐Grade Recyclable Carbon Fiber‐Reinforced Dynamic Thermoset Composites
articles.abstract: Dynamic thermoset resins (DR), defined as thermosets containing dynamic covalent bonds, present a promising solution for addressing the challenge of closed‐loop recycling in carbon fiber reinforced thermoset (CFRP) composites. However, achieving large‐scale preparation of DR‐based CFRP and ensuring their compatibility with industrial equipment and production remain significant challenges. To address this issue, this work presents a full‐chain process solution, encompassing the molecular structure design, prepreg and product manufacturing, and recycling stages. Specifically, we successfully synthesize an industrial‐grade DR (IDR) with adjustable viscosity through the construction of a physically interpenetrating network between polyethersulfone chains and a polyester‐based dynamic covalent network. Large‐scale production of CF/IDR prepreg is achieved by existing industrial coating and roller impregnation techniques. Subsequently, CF/IDR prepregs are processed utilizing established industrial cutting, lamination, and autoclave curing to produce a large‐scale aircraft panel (1 m × 2 m), that reveals a reliable buckling performance with a strain of −3133 µε. Notably, the panel exhibits solvent‐assisted recyclability, owing to the dynamic reversible reaction of the IDR network, which enables complete recovery of both the resin and CF bundles. Moreover, the dynamic performance of the IDR network imparts reshapability and repairability to the panel. Therefore, this work demonstrates the feasibility of employing dynamic resin‐based CFRP in industrial applications.

articles.title: Insights into Local Framework Conformations of pH‐Tunable Electro‐Optic‐Catalytic β‐Cyclodextrin‐Synthetic Polymer System: Selective Dual‐Mode Sensing and Electrocatalysis of Amino Acids
articles.abstract: In polymeric system, local framework conformations provide an effective route to generate supramolecular architectures from identical structural units; herein, pH‐tunable realization in electro‐optic‐catalytic semisynthetic‐polymers for dual‐mode fluorogenic‐electrochemical amino acid sensing/ electrocatalysis is reported. Initially, synthetic fluorescent electroactive conducting polymers (FECPs) were synthesized using N,N‐dimethylacrylamide and cis‐butenedioic acid through polymerization in an aqueous medium. The optimized FECP3 was modified with β‐cyclodextrin to rigidify the matrix and fix the orientation of ─C(═O)N/ ─C(═O)OH groups, inducing local framework conformations. Combined computational and pH‐dependent spectroscopic‐electrochemical studies confirmed two local framework conformations in all the β‐cyclodextrin/FECP3 (LFCFECPs). In optimum LFCFECP2, coexistence of LFCFECP2‐A and LFCFECP2‐B was validated by the excitation‐dependent emission profile and cathodic peaks of C═N+→C•─N in cyclic voltammogram of LFCFECP2‐A‐/ LFCFECP2‐B‐modified glassy‐carbon electrode (LFCFECP2‐A|GCE/ LFCFECP2‐B|GCE). LFCFECP2‐A and LFCFECP2‐B exhibited pH‐selective dual‐mode sensing, enabling fluorogenic‐electrochemical detection of Tyrosine and Tryptophan in aqueous solution/ cow milk/ soybean extract at pH 6.0 and 8.0, respectively, with rapid response, low detection limits, and high reproducibility. Compared to LFCFECP2‐A|GCE/ LFCFECP2‐B|GCE, LFCFECP2‐A/ LFCFECP2‐B film working‐electrode (WE) displayed a higher electroactive surface area. Therefore, LFCFECP2‐A and LFCFECP2‐B films (WEs) were employed for efficient electrocatalytic conversions of Tyrosine and Tryptophan to Dopaquinone and 3a‐hydroxyhexahydropyrrolo[2,3‐b]indole‐2‐carboxylic acid with 95.35 and 92.31% conversion efficiencies, respectively.

articles.title: Loop Corrected Virtual Tactile Interaction: From Haptic Sensing to Feedback Based on Integrated Glove Interface
articles.abstract: Advanced tactile interfaces, regarding sensing and feedback functions, have revolutionized tactile interaction in virtual reality. These two build a bridge facilitating communication between the physical and virtual world, but were developed independently. A glove interface integrated with sensing and feedback is proposed for loop‐corrected virtual tactile interaction. It consists of an iontronic tactile sensor and micro‐discharge electrotactile feedback, which are integrated on the opisthenar and palm side of the textile glove, respectively. Iontronic sensor is modified with various sized micro pyramid and its springback hysteresis is reduced to 5.82% for dynamic pressure monitoring. Meanwhile, the electrotactile feedback is optimized with ideal micro‐gap discharge contributing to a safe current (about 40 µA) on the skin, supporting frequent electrostimulation for hierarchical feedback. In this loop‐corrected system, the iontronic tactile sensor can provide various pressure data originating from joint bending, consisting the data source for controlling the virtual hand, while the monitored virtual operation state is informed in the physical world by electrotactile feedback, and then the hand gesture is corrected according to feedback of various degrees to adjust the virtual counterpart. Thus, closed‐loop tactile interaction is accomplished, and this loop‐corrected glove interface is promising for realizing complicated but precise manipulation tasks in VR‐based human‐machine cooperation.

articles.title: Manipulating Spectral Location in a Cr3+‐Activated Broadband Garnet Phosphor Toward Highly Efficient NIR Pc‐LEDs
articles.abstract: Near‐infrared phosphor‐converted light‐emitting diodes (NIR pc‐LEDs) are highly attractive due to compact, low‐cost, and portable characteristics. Despite the discovery of several efficient and thermostable NIR garnet phosphors, the output power and photoelectric conversion efficiency of the fabricated NIR pc‐LEDs remain severely limited, hindering their practical deployment. Herein, we address this challenge by a single‐site substitution design of Ge4+ for Si4+ in a garnet host Y2MgAl4SiO12 (YMASi). The newly developed Y2MgAl4GeO12 (YMAGe):Cr3+ phosphor demonstrates a substantially red‐shifted broadband NIR emission (90 nm shift, peaking at 809 nm) with an ultra‐broad full‐width at half maximum (FWHM) of 152 nm, along with good thermal stability (82%@423 K). Remarkably, this substitution simultaneously enhances the internal and external quantum efficiencies by factors of 1.8 and 2.1, respectively. Combining atomic‐resolution imaging with spectroscopic analysis, we unravel the origin of the spectral redshift and the underlying mechanism for the luminescent enhancement. Benefiting from these outstanding properties, driven by 100 mA, a prototype NIR light source fabricated with YMAGe:Cr3+ achieves a high output power of 51.6 mW and photoelectric conversion efficiency of 22.7%, thereby demonstrating strong potential for multifunctional applications including night vision, biological imaging, non‐destructive testing, and plant growth lighting.

articles.title: Microfluidic Architecting of Patchy MXene Core‐Shell Particles for Ultralow‐Loading Photothermal Shape‐Memory Actuation
articles.abstract: Shape memory polymers capable of remote actuation are promising for soft robotics, adaptive structures, and biomedical devices, yet efficient photothermal actuation remains limited by particle aggregation, localized thermal hotspots, and poor energy utilization. Here, we introduce a microfluidic architecture‐engineering strategy that transforms MXene nanosheets into spatially distributed patchy core–shell particles for efficient near‐infrared (NIR)‐triggered actuation at ultralow loadings. Flow‐focusing microfluidics assembles Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets into 7–10 nm patchy shells around polymeric cores, suppressing restacking while maximizing accessible photothermal interfaces. Incorporated into poly(L‐lactic acid), these particles enable the composite to reach its glass‐transition temperature within 10 s under NIR irradiation (850 nm, 1.8 W cm−2) at MXene loading of only 0.0024 wt%, resulting in ≈95% shape recovery within 25 s. In contrast, composites containing directly dispersed MXene exhibit localized heating and achieve only ≈63% recovery after 150 s. Combining Monte Carlo photon transport and finite‐element thermal simulations, we show that the patchy‐shell architecture enhances photon harvesting and volumetric heat generation by spatially distributing photothermal interfaces throughout the material. This work establishes architecture‐controlled photothermal transport as a design principle for next‐generation smart composites and demonstrates microfluidic engineering of functional particle architectures as a scalable route toward high‐performance remotely actuated materials.

articles.title: Moderate Li–N Coordination Between Dibromopyrazine and Polysulfides Enables High‐Rate Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
articles.abstract: Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries are promising candidates for high‐energy storage, yet their practical application is limited by poor rate capability. To date, the conversion of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) remains a major challenge due to the high energy barrier of the liquid–solid conversion from Li2S4 to Li2S. Herein, to overcome this barrier, dibromopyrazine (DBP) was identified through screening as an effective electrolyte additive owing to its unique Br─C═N functionality, which weakens Li–S bonding via moderate Li–N coordination through the electron‐withdrawing effect of Br, thereby enabling effective LiPSs anchoring without impeding conversion. In the electrolyte containing 0.04 M DBP, the interaction favors Li2S4 formation at 2.3 V and promotes three‐dimensional (3D) Li2S deposition. Consequently, the Li–S coin cells deliver a high capacity of 785 mAh g−1 at the high rate of 6 C and a low capacity decay rate of 0.09% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 1 C. A 2 Ah pouch cell also demonstrates stable cycling over 100 cycles at 0.5 C. This work highlights a coordination‐modulated moderate‐interaction strategy for accelerating LiPSs conversion in Li–S batteries.

articles.title: Molecular Bridging Enables Uniform and Solvent‐Resilient Buried Contacts for Efficient and Stable Perovskite/TOPCon Tandem Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) enable high‐performance inverted perovskite solar cells and perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells, but polar solvents can partially disrupt preformed SAMs and produce nonuniform buried contacts, a challenge amplified on silicon substrates. Here, 3‐(9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)propan‐1‐aminium iodide (CzPA) is introduced as a molecular bridge at the SAM/perovskite buried interface. The carbazole unit promotes π–π interactions with the SAM, improving monolayer retention during solvent exposure, while the terminal ammonium group interacts with iodide‐containing precursor species to regulate interfacial nucleation. Furthermore, the iodide ions can effectively passivate the iodide vacancies at the buried interface. The reconstructed interface accelerates early‐stage nucleation, promotes orientationally ordered crystal growth, and reduces residual tensile stress, thereby yielding a more p‐type heterojunction and effectively suppressing non‐radiative recombination. CzPA‐modified wide‐bandgap inverted single‐junction cells deliver a PCE of 23.79%. Applied to perovskite/tunnel oxide passivating contact (TOPCon) tandems, this strategy improves perovskite continuity in pyramid valleys, enabling 1 cm2 devices with a PCE of 33.4%. Unencapsulated tandems retain 88% of their initial PCE after 800 h of one‐sun maximum‐power‐point tracking and 90% of their post‐burn‐in PCE after 737 h at 85°C, underscoring the robustness of the reconstructed buried interface.

articles.title: Multifunctional Interface Modifier Enables High‐Performance Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Wide‐bandgap (WBG, ≥1.68 eV) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) represent promising top‐cell candidates for monolithic perovskite tandem photovoltaics. However, fast crystallization kinetics of perovskite precursors and incomplete surface coverage of hole‐transporting self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) commonly degrade perovskite film quality and introduce detrimental defects at the buried interface. Herein, we report a buried‐interface engineering strategy using a rationally designed dioxaboranaphthoanthracene‐based modifier, which exhibits preferential accumulation at the perovskite buried interface. The results support additional interfacial coverage associated with DOBNA‐3PA enrichment, while modulation of perovskite crystallization kinetics enlarges grain size and reduces residual strain, contributing to improved interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the inverted 1.68 eV PSC delivers a champion power conversion efficiency of 24.55% with an open‐circuit voltage of 1.281 V and a fill factor of 85.39%, alongside a negligible hysteresis index of 1.37%. The device retains 94% of its initial efficiency after 1800 h of storage in ambient air (40–45% relative humidity) under ISOS‐D‐1 testing protocols. Notably, this strategy exhibits outstanding generalizability across different perovskite bandgaps, enabling PCEs of 26.44% and 21.04% for 1.54 and 1.78 eV PSCs. This work establishes a dual‐function modifier strategy for improving both perovskite bulk crystallization and buried interface modification, offering a generalizable pathway toward highly efficient and stable WBG PSCs.

articles.title: Neuron Mitochondria Targeted “Zipper Peptide” Delivery for VHL‐Inhibiting Therapy in Parkinson's Disease
articles.abstract: Von Hippel‐Lindau (VHL) emerges as a promising target for neuroprotective treatment in Parkinson's disease (PD), but the challenging druggability hampers therapeutic development. Herein, we report a leucine zipper‐inspired peptide design for VHL‐targeting therapy, in which spontaneous formation of α‐helical structure yields high affinity and biostability, and a symmetrical hetero‐charge distribution on the α‐helix is easier to zip peptide into nanogel, followed by complexing with lipids and T7 peptide for dopaminergic neuron‐targeted mitochondria therapy. After systemic administration, the peptide‐lipid nanocomplex could reach dopaminergic neurons within 2 h, and release the VHL‐inhibiting peptide upon acidic pH to effectively disrupt VHL/Dishevelled‐2 (DVL‐2) interaction. Downstream β‐catenin and hexokinase 2 (HK2) proteins are elevated, promoting mitochondrial homeostasis, metabolic activity, and energy production for neuronal protection. The VHL‐targeting peptide therapy effectively ameliorates neurodegenerative pathologies and motor/coordination deficits in both MPTP‐induced injury and α‐synuclein overexpression PD models. Collectively, this study provides an innovative peptide drug design and a dopaminergic neuron‐targeting strategy for the neuroprotective treatment of PD.

articles.title: Ordered Cu─Pd Intermetallic Alloy With Complementary Facets Enables Efficient Urea Electrosynthesis via Accelerated C─N
articles.abstract: CO2 and nitrate are widespread contaminants. Co-electrolysis of them to produce urea enables eco-friendly pollution treatment and agricultural support, while bare Cu suffers low selectivity, quick deactivation and dominant hydrogen evolution reaction competition. Herein, we synthesize long-range ordered concave CuPd intermetallics (f-CuPd) by liquid reduction and gradient annealing. Characterizations confirm annealing converts disordered face-centered cubic d-CuPd to ordered body-centered cubic phase. Fully ordered f-CuPd exposes complementary (211) and (001) facets with evenly mixed Cu and Pd without segregation. Its ordered atomic arrangement induces Pd to Cu charge transfer and restrains Cu surface oxidation. Electrochemical measurements reveal exceptional electrocatalytic activity toward urea synthesis, attaining a urea production rate of 74.78 mmol h−1 gcat −1 and steady catalytic activity throughout 28 h of uninterrupted electrolysis. In situ spectra track the reaction and prove the ordered structure adjusts interfacial water to generate active hydrogen and avoid competitive adsorption of CO2 and nitrate intermediates. Density functional theory calculations uncover a unique synergistic effect between two crystal facets. The (211) facet drives efficient CO2 activation to form *CO intermediates, while the adjacent (001) facet facilitates nitrate reduction and C─N coupling with substantially reduced kinetic barriers. Reaction intermediates migrate across distinct crystal facets, driving highly efficient urea formation.

articles.title: Organic Ligand‐Functionalized CoN2‐C‐N2Ni Dual‐Atom for Tailored Proton and Non‐Proton Transfer in Hydrogen Evolution and Triiodide Reduction
articles.abstract: Regulating the sustained transport and local concentration of reactive intermediates is essential for accelerating kinetics; however, constructing effective pathways for transferring both protonic and non‐protonic intermediates remains challenging. Herein, we present organic ligand‐functionalized interfacial engineering by anchoring trimesic acid (TMA) to MXene‐supported Co/Ni dual‐atom sites (TMA‐CoNiDA‐MXene) to establish carboxyl‐mediated proton and non‐proton transport channels. By leveraging continuous π–π stacking and deprotonated ─COO− groups in aromatic frameworks, TMA‐CoNiDA‐MXene facilitated the capture and delivery of I*/H* intermediates toward Co/Ni dual active sites, while also mitigating localized excessive accumulation of I*/H*. By exploiting the expanded interlayer spacing, stabilized CoN2‐C‐N2Ni centers, and tailored transport pathways, TMA‐CoNiDA‐MXene achieved a photoconversion efficiency of 8.62% as a counter electrode in iodine‐based solar cells and attained 10 mA cm−2 with an overpotential of only 71 mV in the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). This work provides insightful perspectives on integrating carboxylated organic ligands to jointly transfer protonic and non‐protonic intermediates and offers new approaches for organic–inorganic interfacial design in other complex systems.

articles.title: Rational Construction of Multicomponent Electrocatalyst via Cluster‐Nanoparticle Synergy for Enhanced Hydrogen Production Coupled With Hydrazine Oxidation at Large Current Densities
articles.abstract: Hydrazine-assisted water electrolysis enables low-energy-consumption hydrogen production while simultaneously facilitating the harmless treatment of hydrazine-containing pollutants. Herein, a hydrothermal and air-annealing strategy was employed to simultaneously anchor Ru nanoclusters and Pt nanoparticles on NiO nanowires, thereby constructing a bifunctional Pt-Ru/NiO catalyst with synergistic dual-sites for the hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). This study reveals that the incorporation of Pt and Ru effectively tailors the electronic configuration, optimizing the free energy of hydrogen adsorption/desorption and N2H4 dehydrogenation kinetics, thus endowing the catalyst with outstanding HER and HzOR electrocatalytic activity. To attain the current density of 1000 mA cm− 2, Pt-Ru/NiO merely requires working potentials of 0.158 V for HER and 0.157 V for HzOR, respectively. Impressively, with Pt-Ru/NiO functioning as cathode and anode, the assembled full hydrazine electrolyzer yields 200 mA cm− 2 at an extremely low cell voltage of just 0.057 V, with stable operation sustained for more than 100 h. This work provides a design framework for cluster-particle dual-site synergistic systems and offers a new pathway for hydrazine-assisted high-efficiency electrolytic hydrogen production technology.

articles.title: Sacrificing Initial Active Area for Superior Structural and Interfacial Stability in MoSe2/C Anodes for All‐Solid‐State Lithium Batteries
articles.abstract: Conversion‐type materials for all‐solid‐state lithium batteries face low conductivity, sluggish kinetics, severe volume expansion, and unstable interfaces. Herein, a MoSe2/C composite is fabricated via a wet‐chemical synthesis approach combined with shell engineering. Density functional theory calculations show that the carbon skeleton enhances conductivity, improves Li+ adsorption, and lowers the diffusion barrier. In situ and finite element analyses confirm that the hollow carbon mitigates volume expansion and redistributes stress. Distribution of relaxation times analysis reveals that stress buffering suppresses interfacial degradation and enhances Li+ migration. Pseudocapacitive analysis shows a slightly higher contribution for pristine MoSe2 due to face‐to‐face stacking versus point‐contact packing in MoSe2/C, which sacrifices some initial active area. However, the carbon skeleton accelerates the kinetics of the remaining active regions and provides excellent stress buffering and interfacial stability. Consequently, the MoSe2/C anode exhibits rate capability and long‐term cycling performance in both half‐cells (11 000 cycles at 3 A g−1) and full‐cells (200 cycles at 0.1 C). This work proposes a counterintuitive strategy of “trading part of the initial active area in exchange for superior structural and interfacial stability,” offering a rational design paradigm for conversion‐type materials.

articles.title: Scalable Interfacial Engineering of Covalently Interlocked Hierarchical CNT/Phase Change Composite for Multifunctional Thermal Management and EMI Shielding
articles.abstract: Carbon nanotube (CNT)‐based hierarchical architectures offer a promising platform for engineering multifunctional materials with synergistic thermal, electrical, and optical properties. However, weak interfacial coupling between CNTs and growth substrates compromises structural robustness, hindering practical implementation. Here, a scalable dual‐silanization‐assisted chemical vapor deposition strategy is developed to construct a covalently bonded organosilica interlayer, thereby creating a robust interlocked CF@CNTs hierarchical architecture. Experiments and density functional theory calculations reveal that interlayer enhances charge transfer and interfacial binding strength, suppressing CNT detachment. Leveraging this robust architecture, we fabricated a multifunctional phase change composite (PCC) that effectively resolves the inherent trade‐off between latent heat storage and thermal/electrical transport. The resulting PCC maintains a high latent heat of 210.17 J·g−1 while delivering a thermal conductivity of 0.760 W·m−1·K−1 and an electrical conductivity of 802.56 S·m−1. Consequently, it lowers electronic device operating temperatures by 9°C, achieves an average total shielding effectiveness of 41.51 dB·mm−1, and reaches a photothermal conversion efficiency of 93.36%. Notably, this interfacial engineering strategy is readily extendable to 0D, 1D, 2D, and 3D substrates, enabling scalable integration of CNT‐based architectures. This work establishes interfacial coupling engineering as a versatile design principle for constructing robust CNT‐based architectures, opening new opportunities for multifunctional materials.

articles.title: Solvent–Solvent Interaction Regulation Enables a Practical Ultra‐Low‐Temperature Electrolyte for Sodium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Organic electrolytes encounter critical challenges at low temperatures (LT), such as solvent crystallization and sluggish Na+ transport kinetics. While most studies have primarily focused on low‐viscosity ethers or highly fluorinated solvents for LT performance, their practical applications remain limited by inadequate stability and environmental and safety concerns. In this work, a low‐cost, highly safe electrolyte for LT applications was designed based on sodium‐ion pouch cells. Through methyl substitution at α‑H, the polarity of ethyl butyrate was enhanced, promoting interactions with propylene carbonate to construct a highly stable electrolyte with low solvation energy barriers. It exhibits an ultra‐low freezing point (−130°C) and superior kinetics, demonstrating excellent electrochemical performance in Ah‐scale pouch cells, including: a discharge capacity retention of nearly 70% at −60°C; maintaining 90% of initial capacity after 200 cycles of continuous discharge at 1C and −30°C; and a fast‐charge/discharge capacity retention of over 90% at 10C and 25°C. Furthermore, systematic analysis of sodium plating behavior on anodes at LT revealed that the electrolyte has significant advantages in suppressing sodium plating. Finally, successful engineering‐scale validation was conducted in a 5 Ah pouch cell, providing a safe, reliable, and practical electrolyte design strategy for LT sodium‐ion batteries.

articles.title: Substoichiometric [4+3] Strategy for Constructing Subvalent COFs with Acrylonitrile Unit Toward Solar‐Driven H2O2 Production from Seawater
articles.abstract: Rapid charge carrier recombination and limited active site availability remain major challenges for photocatalytic production of H2O2 in water, particularly in seawater. Herein, we propose a substoichiometric [4+3] strategy to construct a subvalent covalent organic framework (TAQ‐COF) functionalized with acrylonitrile and benzoxadiazole moieties and the off‐stoichiometry of the polymerization reaction preserves two unreacted aldehyde groups per node. The resulting TAQ‐COF exhibits outstanding visible‐light‐driven H2O2 production in pure water without any sacrificial agent, retains approximately 93% of its activity in seawater, and demonstrates excellent recyclability and antibacterial performance. Both theoretical and experimental evidence demonstrate that the enhanced local electron density surrounding the benzoxadiazole moieties in TAQ‐COF creates a favorable microenvironment for the proton‐coupled reduction of O2. Owing to its strong electron‐withdrawing effect and conjugated structure, the acrylonitrile unit markedly extends the lifetime of photogenerated charge carriers from 1.50 to 17.94 ns. Moreover, the enhanced surface hydrophilicity of TAQ‐COF sample promotes interfacial water enrichment, thereby favoring the proton‐coupled oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The synergy of these features endows TAQ‐COF with outstanding catalytic activity in the two‐electron ORR pathway. This work demonstrates that synergistic functionalization with acrylonitrile units in a substoichiometric COF yields robust photocatalysts.

articles.title: Thermodynamic Suppression of Deprotonation in Succinonitrile‐Based Electrolyte for Durable Solid‐State Sodium‐Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries (SSMBs) offer a low‐cost, safe, and high‐energy‐density energy‐storage technology. While succinonitrile (SN) is widely adopted in solid and gel electrolytes for its high dielectric constant, exceptional oxidative stability, and robust cathode compatibility, its practical application is limited by parasitic reactions with Na metal, including deprotonation and polymerization. Herein, we demonstrated a thermodynamic suppression strategy of deprotonation that substantially inhibits parasitic reactions in SN‐based electrolytes for durable SSMBs. By utilizing an acrylonitrile (AN) based polymer as the host framework, we establish an optimized interaction with free SN that thermodynamically disfavors the parasitic decomposition, effectively stabilizing the α‐hydrogens of the methylene groups against deprotonation. The rationally designed electrolyte exhibits high ionic conductivity of 2.17 mS cm−1 and exceptional compatibility with Na metal, enabling stable cycling of Na | Na symmetric cells for 6200 h. Na | Vanadium phosphate sodium full cells retain 95.6% capacity after 5000 cycles at 1.0 C, 93.4% after 10000 cycles at 2.0 C, and pouch cells with an ultra‐high cathode loading of 20 mg cm−2 demonstrate stable performance. This work establishes thermodynamic suppression of deprotonation as a foundational design principle for high‐energy‐density and long‐lifespan SSMBs.

articles.title: Two‐Dimensional Few‐Layer Selenides: From Materials to Applications
articles.abstract: Two‐dimensional (2D) few‐layer selenides attract much attention due to their unique electronic structures and layer‐dependent properties, which differ markedly from those of bulk layered selenides. Especially some transition metal diselenides, which undergo a transition from an indirect bandgap to a direct bandgap with reduced layer number, can meet the specific requirements of high‐performance optoelectronic devices. However, the stable, controllable, and large‐scale synthesis of few‐layer selenides remains a key bottleneck limiting their development. Furthermore, employing strategies such as edge engineering, heterostructure construction, and phase engineering to regulate their properties is equally important for maximizing their application value. Herein, the structural characteristics and layer‐dependent properties of various 2D few‐layer selenides are systematically introduced. Both top‐down and bottom‐up synthesis methods are emphasized. The relationship between the properties of 2D few‐layer selenides and their applications in energy storage, electronics, optoelectronics, thermoelectricity, and catalysis is revealed. Recent developments and potential directions for future research are discussed. This comprehensive review is expected to advance theoretical research on 2D few‐layer selenides and provide insightful guidance for their future functionalization and large‐scale applications.

articles.title: Ultra‐Thin Tow‐Based Discontinuous Composites—Material Overview and Aspirations
articles.abstract: Ultra‐thin Tow‐Based Discontinuous Composites (µt‐TBDC) are emerging as a transformative alternative to conventional continuous‐fiber composites, offering the potential to overcome longstanding limitations in manufacturability, waste, and design flexibility. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of µt‐TBDCs, spanning manufacturing, forming, mechanical characterization, and multi‐scale modelling. Experimental results demonstrate that reducing tow thickness fundamentally alters the material response, enabling µt‐TBDCs to achieve stiffness, strength, and notched performance comparable to quasi‐isotropic laminates, while delivering enhanced compressive strength, fatigue resistance, and significantly improved energy absorption in tearing. These gains are attributed to a transition towards stable, interface and fibre dominated‐controlled failure mechanisms, combined with reduced mesostructural variability arising from the increased number of tows through the thickness and reduced tow wavinesss. Analytical and numerical modelling approaches are reviewed, highlighting the effectiveness of simplified methods for predicting average behavior and the necessity of stochastic frameworks to capture strength and variability. Crucially, µt‐TBDCs enable a broad and tunable design space, where fibre properties, tow thickness, and architecture act as independent design variables rather than fixed constraints. By linking material architecture, processing, and structural performance, this work positions µt‐TBDCs as a paradigm shift in composite design, with significant implications for the future of high‐performance lightweight structures.

articles.title: Unleashing Multi‐Electron Storage in Synergistic Dual‐Active‐Center Bridged Covalent Organic Polymer Cathode for High‐Capacity and Long‐Life Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: The development of aqueous zinc‐ion batteries is hindered by the scarcity of advanced cathode materials. Covalent organic polymers (COPs) have garnered substantial interest due to their tunable structures. However, simultaneously achieving high capacity and structural stability remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we propose an active dual‐unit bridging strategy to construct an extended conjugated framework, enabling high specific capacity and structural stability. This bridging design integrates six‐electron‐storage hexaazatrinaphthalene (HAT) and redox‐active 2,5‐dihydroxy‐1,4‐benzoquinone (DHBQ) units, departing from the disadvantage that conventional strategies only rely on inactive linkers. Theoretical calculations and spectroscopic analyses elucidate a cascaded Zn2+ storage pathway characterized by the preferential reaction of HAT sites, followed by subsequent participation of the benzoquinone moieties. Electrochemical evaluations of the HAT‐DHBQ cathode reveal a high initial capacity of 316.2 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1, along with impressive cycling stability, as evidenced by maintaining discharge capacities of 190.3 mAh g−1 and 147.0 mAh g−1 after 10 000 cycles at 1.0 A g−1 and 5.0 A g−1, corresponding to low‐capacity attenuation rates of 0.0029% and 0.0030% per cycle, respectively. By synergistically integrating multi‐electron‐storage units through an active‐bridging strategy, this work establishes a promising molecular design paradigm for high‐performance organic active materials in aqueous multivalent‐ion secondary batteries.

articles.title: 2D Abrupt Nano‐Junctions Blending sp–sp2 Bonds on Atomically Precise Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Two‐dimensional heterostructures combining sp–sp2$^2$ hybridization—blending graphene with graphyne‐based allotropes—offer substantial potential for enhancing the tunability of electronic and transport properties while providing significant structural flexibility, which are desirable characteristics for next‐generation nanoscale electronics. Despite such potential, their experimental realization remains elusive, as synthesized carbon heterostructures are limited to doped, graphene‐based systems exhibiting exclusively sp2$^2$ hybridization. Here, the on‐surface synthesis of covalently bonded sp–sp2$^2$ lateral heterostructures between graphene nanoribbons and graphdiyne networks on Au(111) is demonstrated. Atomic‐resolution scanning tunneling microscopy, combined with density functional theory, reveals the formation mechanism of the covalent interfacial bonds between nanoribbons and graphdiynes, also highlighting the key role of surface chemistry. Bromine atoms, deriving from the molecules dehalogenation and chemisorbed along the nanoribbon, inhibit junction formation, but bonding efficiency can be boosted up to 66% by controlled removal of these byproducts. Electronic structure and transport calculations show that the 2D heterostructure by itself is characterized by disentangled properties for the two subsystems, forming an atomically narrow junction, enabling voltage‐tunable spatial current separation in two dimensions. These results define a viable strategy for engineering graphene‐based sp–sp2$^2$ heterostructures, paving the way for the design and synthesis of all‐carbon nanoscale electronic architectures.

articles.title: A Multifunctional Ionograsper Enabling Ion‐Redistribution Proximity Sensing and Structural‐Reconfiguration‐Driven Bidirectional Actuation
articles.abstract: Autonomous soft actuators are essential for untethered intelligent robotic systems. However, achieving energy‐efficient operation and long‐term shape retention in solid‐state platforms remains a significant challenge, as most conventional systems rely on continuous power input or complex fluidic architectures. Here, we report an environmentally adaptive ionic actuator inspired by the Venus flytrap, capable of self‐sensing and bidirectional deformation without sustained external energy. By incorporating azobenzene moieties into an ionogel network, we trigger a unique nanopore‐mediated Janus actuation. A single, low‐power UV pulse (35.3 mW cm−2) induces rapid photoisomerization and localized dehydration, forming surface nanopores that facilitate asymmetric moisture uptake. This structural reconfiguration drives directional bending that is passively maintained for over 10 min, which is an exceptionally long retention time compared to conventional soft actuators. Furthermore, electrification‐induced voltage signals enable zero‐bias proximity sensing. By integrating these synergistic characteristics, we demonstrate a biomimetic ionograsper that combines ion‐redistribution‐induced sensing with energy‐efficient light‐triggered actuation for sophisticated object manipulation. Overall, this work provides a robust strategy for developing multifunctional and power‐efficient soft robots capable of intelligent environmental interaction.

articles.title: A Multifunctional Ionograsper Enabling Ion‐Redistribution Proximity Sensing and Structural‐Reconfiguration‐Driven Bidirectional Actuation (Adv. Mater. 59/2026)
articles.abstract: Bioinspired Ionic Soft Actuators In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74981), Hong Chul Moon, Yong Min Kim, and co‐workers propose a multifunctional ionic soft actuator that integrates ion‐redistribution‐based proximity sensing with structural‐reconfiguration‐driven bidirectional actuation. UV‐induced photoisomerization and dehydration generate a nanoporous surface that promotes asymmetric rehydration, enabling long‐lasting deformation after a single low‐power stimulus, while mobile‐ion redistribution provides self‐powered non‐contact sensing for energy‐efficient soft robotic manipulation.

articles.title: A Receptor‐Mediated Endolysosomal Recycling Chimera Enables Catalytic TNF‐α Degradation for Sustained Treatment of Mucosal Inflammation
articles.abstract: Mucosal inflammatory disorders such as dry eye disease (DED) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), driven by TNF‐α‐mediated immune‐epithelial crosstalk, remain therapeutically challenging. Conventional inhibitors often suffer from poor mucosal permeability and transient efficacy with 1:1 binding. Although extracellular protein degradation (eTPD) technologies can eliminate pathogenic proteins, most of them operate stoichiometrically, limiting dosage efficiency and durability. Here, we report a receptor‐mediated endolysosomal recycling chimera (RECYC) platform that enables catalytic, recyclable degradation of TNF‐α with multiple turnovers, achieving sustained suppression of mucosal inflammation. RECYC integrates a pH‐responsive peptide that binds TNF‐α at physiological pH and releases it in acidic endosomes, with a CI‐M6PR‐targeting aptamer that remains pH‐stable to drive continuous recycling. The anti‐TNF‐α RECYC achieved efficient uptake and recyclable clearance of extracellular TNF‐α across conjunctival and colonic epithelial cells and macrophages, achieving superstoichiometric TNF‐α clearance with up to 7.5 catalytic turnovers. The ∼30 kDa RECYC exhibited superior tissue penetration in murine cornea and colon compared to inhibitory antibodies. In murine DED and IBD models, RECYC restored ocular surface homeostasis and reduced colon inflammation with low‐dose, infrequent administration. Human corneal limbus organoids further confirmed prolonged anti‐inflammatory activity. Together, RECYC establishes a modular, recyclable eTPD platform for sustained treatment of TNF‐α‐driven mucosal inflammation.

articles.title: A Transparent, High Refractive Index and Abbe Number Polymer for Visible Metalens by High Fidelity Nanoimprinting
articles.abstract: Simultaneously achieving high visible transparency, high refractive index (n), and a large Abbe number (υ D) in organic polymers remains a fundamental challenge. Here, a facile and efficient dual sulfur-mediated Michael addition strategy is reported to synthesize transparent high refractive index polymers (HRIPs) with large υ D. By combining main backbone de-conjugation to preserve visible transparency with rational side-chain engineering for n-tuning, the optimal polymer (H4) achieves an ultrahigh n of 1.86 at 589 nm alongside a large υ D of 34.93 and robust stability. Moreover, polymer H4 exhibits remarkable performance in nanoimprint lithography, replicating features down to 75 nm with aspect ratios up to 8.5 and a low volumetric shrinkage of only 3.23%. Notably, a nanoimprinted metalens prototype fabricated from H4 delivers a relative focusing efficiency of 49.8% at 550 nm (NA = 0.5), approaching the theoretical design value (52.94%). Therefore, the high refractive index polymer H4 bridges molecular design and manufacturable meta-optics, showing tremendous potential in scalable, flexible, next-generation photonic platforms by translating side-chain polarizability engineering into practical wavefront control.

articles.title: A Voltage‐Stabilizing MXene Additive Electrolyte Mitigates Interference From External Force on the Charge‐Discharge Process for Multifunctional Hybrid Structural Supercapacitors
articles.abstract: In structural energy storage devices (SESDs) that simultaneously store electrochemical energy and bear mechanical loading, the external force will normally affect the electrochemical performance of SESDs. One example is that, under cyclic bending stress, voltage ripples emerge in charge‐discharge curves, which cause voltage instability. In this study, we demonstrate that these voltage ripples originate from spatially heterogeneous electric field distribution within the mechanically deformed region. By using polarized electric fields formed through hydrogen bonding networks in MXene additive electrolyte, we can effectively homogenize the distribution of the electric field, thereby attenuating voltage ripples and smoothing the voltage curves. Moreover, the uniform electric field distribution promotes uniform Zn deposition and extends the device lifespan.
