Decanoic acid additively suppresses IL-1β and enables pharmacologic dexamethasone dose-sparing in LPS/ATP-stimulated THP-1 macrophages
articles.abstract: by Melissa A. Hausburg, Kaysie L. Banton, Christopher D. Cassidy, Robert M. Madayag, Carlos H. Palacio, Jason S. Williams, Gregory W. Thomas, Raphael Bar-Or, David Bar-Or Systemic inflammatory response syndrome, driven by trauma or infection, involves excessive innate immune activation. Dexamethasone (DEX), a synthetic glucocorticoid, suppresses inflammation, although adverse side effects limit its clinical use. The inflammasome, a multiprotein complex that assembles in response to inflammatory stimuli like ATP after lipopolysaccharide (LPS) priming, facilitates caspase-1 cleavage and release of the proinflammatory cytokine, interleukin (IL)-1β. We investigated whether DEX and decanoic acid (DA), a saturated medium-chain fatty acid, inhibited caspase-1 activity and IL-1β release in an LPS/ATP-stimulated THP-1 macrophage model and whether co-treatment would allow for pharmacologic DEX dose-sparing in vitro. PMA-differentiated THP-1macrophages were primed with LPS overnight and stimulated with ATP for 3 h in the presence of DA, DEX, or both. Viability and cytotoxicity were assessed. Caspase-1 activity and IL-1β were quantified, and EC50 values were calculated by nonlinear regression. In control conditions, LPS/ATP stimulation induced 5.56 (q1: 3.51 – q3: 6.38) ng/mL of IL-1β release. DA and DEX inhibited IL-1β with full dose-response EC50 values of 131.7 μM and 24.29 nM, respectively. DA concentrations exceeding 800 μM decreased cell viability. An 8 x 9-point DA/DEX dose matrix (0–500 μM DA; 0 to 1e4 nM DEX) was used to interrogate drug interaction for IL-1β inhibition and caspase-1 activity. DEX EC50 values remained within a narrow 95% confidence interval of 17.5–26.6 nM, regardless of DA background concentration. DA reduced caspase-1 enzymatic activity with a calculated EC50 value of ~140 μM; whereas, DEX did not. These data show that DA and DEX act independently. Furthermore, compared to DEX alone, the presence of DA allowed for equivalent in vitro IL-1β suppression at lower DEX concentrations, supporting pharmacologic DEX dose-sparing. Determination of whether this pharmacologic effect translates to clinically meaningful corticosteroid dose reduction requires further study.

articles.title: Deep learning–driven fine-resolution finger movement recognition from surface EMG signals
articles.abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) has emerged as an impactful tool for controlling advanced prosthetic devices by detecting and recording muscle electrical activity during motion. This study presents a unique technique for recognizing nine distinct classes of finger movements by utilizing the Ninapro database. To address an underexplored domain of upper-limb prosthetic control, this research targets fine-resolution individual finger movements rather than the broad range of hand gestures. A custom-made one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D–CNN) was developed and validated using a within-subject evaluation strategy and signals. The proposed model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 90.1%. An in-depth sensitivity/specificity analysis for each finger movement class was administered to gain key insights into current recognition capabilities. The findings presented in this study demonstrate the viability of fine-resolution finger-movement recognition, offering foundational insights that may inform the future development and refinement of control systems in the prosthetic field.

Feasibility of a machine learning model for predicting weight gain after kidney transplantation machine learning and weight gain after kidney transplantation
articles.abstract: Background Excessive weight gain after kidney transplantation adversely affects patient and graft outcomes. Machine Learning has been increasingly used to improve risk prediction across a range of transplant-related outcomes, yet its application to post-transplant weight trajectories remains unexplored. This study is the first to evaluate the feasibility of using Machine Learning algorithms to identify predictors of weight gain after kidney transplantation. Methods This retrospective cohort study analyzed 374 adult kidney transplant recipients. We developed an Elastic Net regression model with 10-fold cross-validation to predict body weight variation at 12 months post-transplant. The analysis screened a comprehensive set of demographic and clinical variables, including recipient characteristics, donor type, dialysis duration, and pre-transplant hypertension, to identify predictors within the training (75%) and testing (25%) datasets. Results Mean weight gain was 4.0 ± 7.4 kg. The Elastic Net model retained four predictors in the final model: female sex, deceased donor source, age, and pre-transplant body mass index. However, the model demonstrated limited predictive performance (R2 = 0.10; Mean Absolute Error = 8.7%), indicating that baseline variables explain only a small fraction of the observed variability in weight change. Conclusions This pioneering study establishes an analytical benchmark and reveals the informational limits of standard clinical datasets for predicting post-transplant weight gain. While Machine Learning application is feasible, current demographic and clinical variables are insufficient for precise individual prediction. Future models must integrate more granular behavioral and pharmacological data to achieve clinically actionable risk stratification.

articles.title: Global stakeholder preferences for point-of-care HIV nucleic acid amplification tests: A conjoint study
articles.abstract: by Kara M. Palamountain, Chethana Achar, Rebecca P. Kirby, Yukari C. Manabe, Debi Boeras, Michal Maimaran Introduction This study aimed to assess global stakeholder preferences for key attributes of point-of-care (POC) HIV Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (NAAT), with the aim of informing product development to support progress toward UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets. Methods A web-based conjoint survey was conducted in August through November 2024 among HIV clinicians, laboratory professionals, and researchers. Participants were asked to evaluate hypothetical POC HIV NAAT profiles varying by six attributes: sensitivity / limit of detection (LOD), sample-collection method, turnaround time (TAT), result format, price, and power source. Relative importance and part-worth utilities were calculated to assess trade-offs in decision-making. Results One hundred three respondents from 33 countries, primarily in Africa (75%), completed the survey. The relative importance placed on the attributes in the conjoint task varied based on the setting. In community and home-based settings, participants prioritized fingerstick sample collection (25.90%) and faster TATs (28.8%), even at the expense of sensitivity (15.70%). By contrast, respondents from hospitals and health centers valued tests with high sensitivity (42.6%, 40.9%) and faster TATs (31.5%, 22.6%). Across all respondents, price (7.0%), result format (3.30%), and power source (7.25%) were less influential. Conclusions Stakeholders were willing to make trade-offs among desirable attributes, prioritizing rapid turnaround time, strong sensitivity, and fingerstick sampling over affordability, power requirements, and result format in the conjoint task. These preferences vary by level of care and by use case, underscoring the importance of aligning product features with contextual needs. Engaging stakeholders early in the design process is critical to ensure new POC HIV NAAT technologies are both acceptable and scalable in low-resource settings.

articles.title: IL15.3, a synthetic antimicrobial peptide, attenuates LPS-induced inflammatory responses in RAW 264.7 macrophages via transcriptional and proteomic modulation
articles.abstract: Inflammation underlies numerous pathological conditions, driving the need for safe and effective anti-inflammatory agents. Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) are promising therapeutics due to their specificity, efficacy, and safety. This study evaluated the cationic antimicrobial peptide IL15.3 for anti-inflammatory activity and cytocompatibility in vitro. IL15.3 demonstrated low cytotoxicity in MTT assays using RAW 264.7 macrophages, normal human dermal fibroblasts (NHDF), and HaCaT keratinocytes. In LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 cells, IL15.3 significantly reduced nitric oxide (NO) production and reactive oxygen species (ROS) in a dose-dependent manner without affecting cell viability. qRT-PCR analysis revealed significant suppression of iNOS, COX-2, TNF-α, and IL-6 mRNA expression, alongside downregulation of NF-κB, JNK, STAT1, and STAT3, and a reciprocal shift in Keap1/Nrf2 expression suggestive of possible antioxidant pathway activation. Label-free proteomic profiling identified 5,191 proteins, revealing a multi-modal mechanism of action. IL15.3 treatment exclusively induced 4 anti-inflammatory proteins (ISG15, PEX14, TNIP3, PR) and upregulated negative regulators NRG1, DAB2IP, IL-18BP and SOCS5. Critically, IL15.3 suppressed key pro-inflammatory mediators including IKKβ, JAK1, JAK3, JNK, and IL-1RAcP, demonstrating comprehensive modulation of NF-κB, JAK/STAT, and MAPK pathways. In silico molecular docking further predicted potential interactions of IL15.3 with iNOS and the Keap1 Kelch domain, offering preliminary structural insight consistent with its putative dual anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity. Together, these findings indicate that IL15.3 exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity through multiple mechanisms in LPS-stimulated macrophages at transcriptional and proteomic levels. The coordinated upregulation of negative regulators and suppression of central inflammatory mediators collectively suggest that IL15.3 may represent a promising therapeutic candidate for inflammatory disorders.

articles.title: Institutional patterns in diagnosis and antifibrotic-era treatment uptake for IPF and PPF across U.S. centers
articles.abstract: by Bradley A. Sheffield, Brian J. Cassel, Apostolos Perelas, Patricia Sime, Peter Jackson Purpose For ten years, nintedanib and pirfenidone have been the only approved therapies for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), with nintedanib subsequently also approved for progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF). Previous studies demonstrate low antifibrotic (AF) uptake, but differences by site-of-care and AF uptake after seminal trials (IPF: INPULSIS/ASCEND; PPF: INBUILD) are not well characterized. We evaluated temporal trends in IPF and PPF diagnosis and AF use at academic (AC) versus non-academic (NonAC) centers. Methods Using the U.S. TriNetX Collaborative Network, we compared IPF and PPF incidence, prevalence, and AF use by center type using linear regression across post-trial and post–FDA-approval windows (IPF: 2015–2017, 2015–2024; PPF: 2020–2022, 2020–2024). Slope differences (Δslope) were calculated as AC minus NonAC annual slopes; therefore, positive values indicate faster increases at ACs, whereas negative values indicate faster increases at NonACs. Results Across both periods, IPF prevalence increased more rapidly at NonACs, while AF use was higher at ACs (2024: 33.5% vs 20.1%, p p p p = 0.009). During the post-INBUILD period (2020–2022), AF initiation rose faster at ACs (Δ slope +1.42 percentage points/year, p = 0.002), while overall AF slope differences were not significant. Outcome patterns for IPF revealed higher mortality and lung transplant in ACs, but lower respiratory failure and oxygen use. PPF showed higher respiratory failure and mortality in ACs, and no significant differences in lung transplant or oxygen use. Conclusions AF use in IPF and PPF was higher and rose faster at ACs, suggesting faster AC adoption and potential barriers at NonACs. Mixed outcome findings suggest referral and severity bias may partially explain differences, however, are unlikely to fully account for them. More research is needed to account for referral and severity bias. Given the small NonAC PPF cohort (n = 216), PPF findings should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Integrated conservation of linear heritage landscapes from a biocultural diversity perspective: A case study of the Huizhou-Hangzhou Ancient Trail, China
articles.abstract: Linear cultural heritage landscapes embody the long-term coupling relationships between ecological processes and human cultural practices, yet conservation models guided by a single ecological or cultural goal fail to meet their holistic management needs. Based on the perspective of biocultural diversity, this study takes the Huizhou-Hangzhou Ancient Trail (HHAT) as a case study and constructs a comprehensive conservation framework oriented toward spatial planning. Biodiversity and cultural diversity patterns are assessed and their spatial relationships are quantified using the coupling coordination degree model. The biocultural diversity index is further integrated with the Marxan systematic conservation planning model to identify Biocultural Core Protected Areas (BCCPA) and support differentiated spatial conservation strategies. The results indicate that biodiversity and cultural diversity along the HHAT exhibit a pronounced antagonistic coupling relationship: regions with antagonistic coupling account for 98.90% of the total study area, while coordinated regions make up only 0.02%. Based on the natural and cultural context of the study area, this pattern may be jointly influenced by rigid competition for small‑scale spatial resources, the dual effects of traffic corridors, and the cumulative effects of traditional livelihood activities. In response, an integrated conservation spatial pattern of one core area and two corridors is proposed, together with four conservation strategies: Conservation-Minimal Intervention, Conservation-Appropriate Revitalization, Restoration-Minimal Intervention, and Restoration-Appropriate Revitalization-enabling an effective translation from coupling diagnosis to spatial planning responses. This study advances understanding of biocultural interactions in mountainous linear heritage landscapes and provides a transferable methodological pathway for integrated conservation planning.

articles.title: More than gaming: Examining executive functions in esports players
articles.abstract: The main purpose of this study was to determine the differences in executive function performance levels of esports players who play First-Person Shooter (FPS) and Multiplayer Online Battle Arena (MOBA) game types compared to non-video game players (NVGPs). Other purposes of the study are to examine the relationships of executive function components and their relationships with in-game rank and total game play time variables. The study groups consisted of ninety volunteer participants, all of whom were male young adults between the ages of 18 and 34, 30 of whom actively played FPS video games, 30 of whom actively played MOBA video games, and 30 of whom NVGPs. Corsi Block-Tapping Test (CBT), Wisconsin (Berg) Card Sorting Test (WCST), and Stroop Test Çapa Form (ST) were used as data collection tools. According to the findings of the study; FPS players had significantly higher scores than NVGPs (p < 0.001, F = 8.55) in CBT and less error percentage than the NVGPs (p < 0.01, F = 5.58) and MOBA players had significantly less interference time than NVGPs in the ST (p < 0.001, F = 7.66). In addition, there was a significant negative correlation between CBT and ST interference times for all players (p < 0.05; r = −0.28) and a significant negative correlation between in-game skill and ST interference times for FPS players (p < 0.05; r = −0.41). These findings suggest that digital video game experience shapes cognitive profiles based on genre-specific demands; while FPS gameplay primarily enhances visuospatial working memory capacity, MOBA gameplay fosters stronger inhibition control, with higher in-game skill level reflecting superior inhibitory control in FPS gameplay, and relationship of visuospatial working memory and inhibition components demonstrating an underlying interrelated structure.

articles.title: Altermagnetism in Folded Iron Chain Systems
articles.abstract: Altermagnetism---moment-compensated magnetism with momentum-dependent spin splitting---has so far been realized primarily in N\'eel-type antiferromagnets. Here, we demonstrate altermagnetism in folded iron chain systems with block-type magnetic order (e.g.,$\ensuremath{\uparrow}\ensuremath{\uparrow}\ensuremath{\downarrow}\ensuremath{\downarrow}$). In the strictly one-dimensional (1D) case, altermagnetism is forbidden by the $[{C}_{2}||\mathcal{T}]$ symmetry, but it can emerge when such chains are stacked into a quasi-1D array. To generate altermagnetic spin splitting via this chain-stacking mechanism, two essential ingredients are required: a block-type spin order that spontaneously breaks the combined parity-time reversal symmetry, and the finite interchain hopping. Using first-principles calculations, we identify the ${\mathrm{K}}_{3}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{4}$ family as a promising platform that realizes this mechanism, hosting a $d$-wave altermagnet even without lattice ${C}_{4}$ symmetry. Moreover, owing to its lower symmetry, the block-type folded chain exhibits an isotropic altermagnetic spin splitting, which may manifest as an altermagnetic wrapping effect. Our findings unify real-space block magnetism and reciprocal-space altermagnetism, establishing folded iron chains as a tunable platform for zero-moment spintronic applications.

From these data, transverse-spin-dependent dihadron asymmetries are extracted using pairs of oppositely charged hadrons. These asymmetries ar…

articles.title: Genuine Quantum Strong Mpemba Effect by Eliminating Coherence
articles.abstract: Relaxation does not always reward patience: under certain conditions, a system initially farther from equilibrium can relax faster than one initially closer, a counterintuitive phenomenon known as the Mpemba effect. A conceptually transparent mechanism underlying this effect is the strong Mpemba effect, which commonly requires a unique slowest decay mode. However, for the Davies map, this condition is relaxed: the degenerate slowest modes are purely coherent. This allows the strong Mpemba effect to be realized by strategically eliminating coherence from the initial state. In this Letter, we design and implement a fully controllable optical setup to simulate the Davies map, whose validity is confirmed by verifying the semigroup property of the dynamics. We further demonstrate a genuine quantum strong Mpemba effect in the minimal quantum system, a single qubit. Our results experimentally confirm the key role of quantum coherence in this anomalous thermal relaxation. Moreover, our experimental setup provides a versatile platform for exploring quantum thermodynamics and a wider range of open-system dynamics.

articles.title: Magnon Chern Insulator in Two-Dimensional Fully Compensated Ferrimagnetic Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Achieving intrinsic Chern insulators (CIs) with zero net magnetization remains a long-standing and formidable challenge. Here, motivated by the unique opportunities that topological magnons offer for low-dissipation transport, we propose a general theoretical framework for realizing magnon CIs in filling-enforced fully compensated ferrimagnets with vanishing net magnetization. Moreover, we demonstrate that strong asymmetric intralayer Heisenberg interactions induce a type-III (broken-gap) magnonic band alignment, characterized by nonoverlapping magnon frequency gaps of the two layers, thereby enabling the emergence of magnon CIs. Remarkably, the asymmetric Bose-Einstein occupations of oppositely chiral magnon branches offer a distinct advantage in generating a giant magnon thermal Hall conductivity, which is forbidden in conventional antiferromagnets. Based on the Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model and first-principles calculations, we identify the experimentally accessible ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}/{\text{CrGeTe}}_{3}$ and ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}/{\text{CrSiTe}}_{3}$ heterostructures as ideal material platforms for realizing the proposed magnon CIs with fully compensated ferrimagnetism. These heterostructures host the nonzero magnon Chern numbers and chiral edge states, and remarkably display the strongly enhanced magnon thermal Hall effect comparable to that of ferromagnets, establishing fully compensated ferrimagnets as a promising platform for topological magnon transport without net magnetization.

articles.title: Role of Anisotropic Electronic Friction in Laser-Driven Hydrogen Recombination on Copper
articles.abstract: Ultrafast light-driven chemical dynamics at surfaces are governed by energy transfer from excited electrons to vibrational degrees of freedom. When this nonadiabatic energy transfer is anisotropic, it can lead to dynamical steering effects that affect reaction probabilities or nonthermal final energy distributions in molecules. Here, enabled by a machine-learning-based simulation framework, we compare isotropic and anisotropic models of electronic friction during laser-driven hydrogen evolution on the (111) facet of copper. While anisotropic electronic friction determines the rate of energy transfer into the adsorbate and the fluence dependence of desorption probabilities, final translational, vibrational, and rotational energy distributions are mainly governed by the potential energy landscape at the barrier and insensitive to nonadiabatic effects.

articles.title: Twinned Dynamical Decoupling
articles.abstract: Systematic pulse-area errors limit the fidelity of quantum control across many qubit platforms. We introduce twinned dynamical decoupling, an analytic family of sequences $T2n$ in which a pulse sequence is paired with its $\ensuremath{\pi}$-phase-shifted twin. This $\ensuremath{\pi}$-phase step cancels common-mode systematic pulse-area errors to all orders on exact resonance. Then the phases of the pulses in each of the constituent twins are determined in such a manner that detuning errors are suppressed to the highest possible order as well. We have derived a simple analytic formula for these phases applicable to arbitrary sequence length. We demonstrate the sequences with superconducting transmon qubits on the IBM Quantum processor ibm_torino and the IQM Quantum processor Garnet. The measured population plateaus agree closely with theory and show enhanced robustness compared to the most frequently used dynamical decoupling protocols.

articles.title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death
articles.abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation–induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.

articles.title: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules
articles.abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm 2 . With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm 2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.

articles.title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
articles.abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

articles.title: Electronic bound states in the continuum in a two-dimensional metal
articles.abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd 5 AlI 2 , a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd 5 AlI 2 gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.

articles.title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°–twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
articles.abstract: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti–programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

articles.title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
articles.abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

Natural product biosynthesis by guanidine prenyltransferases in plants and bacteria
articles.abstract: Guanidine exists almost exclusively as a resonance-stabilized cation, making its direct enzymatic functionalization challenging. We identified the cyanobacterial enzyme NosH, which catalyzes direct prenyl transfer to free guanidine. Structural and mechanistic analyses revealed guanidine activation by a two-aspartate clamp coupled to prenyl-donor binding through a distinct catalytic architecture. Guided by these features, we identified a large family of guanidine prenyltransferases across bacteria and plants. Plant enzymes produced guanidine alkaloids such as galegine in vitro and heterologous expression of a plant ortholog in Nicotiana benthamiana produced galegine in planta, providing a direct enzymatic link to plant-specialized metabolism.

articles.title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
articles.abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

articles.title: The AI debate is missing half the system
articles.abstract: Last month, leading executives of artificial intelligence (AI) companies warned the United Nations Security Council about the risks of losing human control over this rapidly advancing technology. Their recommendations focused heavily on safeguards, evaluation, and governance of AI models and systems, largely overlooking the risks that arise from the interactions of AI with people and institutions. AI safety needs to be addressed at the level of the human–AI system, not the AI model alone.

articles.title: The Monarch Bear
The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development
articles.abstract: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, more than 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell type–specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.

articles.title: Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
articles.abstract: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS 3 ), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κ aa ) and the transverse (κ ab ) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κ ab is extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along the b axis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.

articles.title: Ultrarapid decision-making in an avian brain
articles.abstract: Perceptual decision-making is well studied in mammals, but its operation in other vertebrates remains unclear. We show that carrion crows ( Corvus corone ) make deliberate decisions in a classic visual motion discrimination task with unprecedented speed, reporting choices in approximately 235 milliseconds on average, which is roughly twice as fast as has been observed in monkeys or humans and without sacrificing accuracy. Recordings from the pallial endbrain reveal that direction-selective neurons encode the upcoming choice as early as about 70 milliseconds after stimulus onset and about 170 milliseconds before the response, with ramping activity scaling with sensory evidence and converging at response onset. These findings highlight the extraordinary efficiency of avian decision-making circuitry, possibly shaped by evolutionary pressures for rapid visuomotor control.

articles.title: Visualizing symmetry-broken Chern insulators and their quantum melting
articles.abstract: In the presence of a magnetic field, electronic states of moiré quantum materials develop a Hofstadter spectrum that provides a distinctive setting for studying the interplay between band topology and strong electron-electron interaction. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we studied Hofstadter’s states in bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride and directly visualized the formation of interaction-driven symmetry breaking Chern insulators. Our measurements revealed the formation of phases that double, triple, or quadruple the moiré unit cell at fractional filling of the Hofstadter bands as well as states with complex intra–unit cell wave functions. We visualized two distinct quantum phenomena in different Chern states, including quantum melting driven by the appearance and proliferation of topological defects and a quantum transition co-occurring with phase competition and separation.

articles.title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity
articles.abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

articles.title: AD-Smart: Alzheimer’s trial will test diabetes and ADHD drugs on patients
articles.abstract: A new clinical trial has been launched in the UK that researchers hope will cut years from the search for treatments for Alzheimer’s disease.The study will test multiple drugs simultaneously, starting with two repurposed medicines already used to treat type 2 diabetes and attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).It will examine whether the medicines can lessen symptoms such as memory and thinking problems and help people maintain their quality of life.Alzheimer’s is the most common type of dementia, affecting around 600 000 people in the UK. Data published today show that the NHS in England met its target to diagnose dementia in at least 66.7% of the patients over 65 who are estimated to have dementia for the first time since March 2020.1No current NHS treatments can slow or stop Alzheimer’s, although medicines can be used to manage its symptoms.2 The AD-Smart trial (Alzheimer’s disease Systematic Multi-arm Adaptive Randomised Trial) aims to...

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau hepatitis B trial: controversial study cancelled after police raid researchers’ offices
articles.abstract: A controversial hepatitis B vaccine trial planned in Guinea-Bissau will not proceed, its principal investigator Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer has confirmed, after the country’s government refused to authorise the study.Schaltz-Buchholzer told The BMJ that “the military government has announced that they do not authorize the trial,” and it “will therefore not happen.”This confirmation comes two days after Guinea-Bissau’s judicial police searched the facilities of the Bandim Health Project in the African nation’s capital, Bissau, seizing a batch of hepatitis B vaccines.1The Bandim Health Project is a Danish run research organisation that Schaltz-Buchholzer and co-principal trial investigator Christine Stabell Benn are affiliated with.In a statement, Guinea-Bissau’s judicial police said the raid was part of an investigative procedure to clarify the circumstances related to the hepatitis B vaccines, “which will be subject to applicable legal procedures in order to ascertain the facts and any potential liabilities.”The judicial police did not say whether the trial,...

articles.title: Plaques and fissures on the lips
articles.abstract: A man in his 60s presented with a three month history of painless lesions on and around the lips which persisted despite treatment with antibiotics and antiviral drugs. He had a 20 year history of ulcerative colitis that had remained in remission for years. He did not report intestinal symptoms and was not taking immunomodulatory medication.Physical examination showed vegetative plaques with pustules and yellow crusts on the lips and perioral region, and multiple fissures on the inner side of the lips (fig 1). Laboratory tests showed eosinophilia (8.6%; reference range 0.4% to 8.0%) and mildy raised C reactive protein levels (10.30 mg/L; reference range 0.0 mg/L to 6.0 mg/L). Colonoscopy was declined.bmj;395/oct22_1/e100607/F1F1f1Fig 1Histopathological examination of the lesions combined with direct immunofluorescence tests indicated a diagnosis of pyodermatitis-pyostomatitis vegetans (PD-PSV).PD-PSV is a mucocutaneous disorder characterised by confluent pustules and erosions of the mouth and skin folds. It typically occurs in patients...

articles.title: Shamonda: As first ever human case is recorded, what you need to know
articles.abstract: A person in France has become the first ever human reported to have been infected with Shamonda virus, health authorities have announced.1Until now, the virus had only ever been detected in non-human animals and was considered by officials to be non-transmissible to humans.What happened in France?Details are limited, but what has been announced is that the patient was already receiving treatment for a serious illness that made them susceptible to infection and complications before being infected with Shamonda and dying earlier this month.Investigations into whether the virus caused or contributed to the patient’s death, and how the patient acquired the infection, are ongoing, said the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC).2What is Shamonda?Shamonda virus is a member of a large group of viruses known as bunyaviruses.3Although it was first identified in Nigerian cattle in the 1960s, Shamonda virus was found in European farm animals for the first time...

articles.title: New strategies for enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones
articles.abstract: Enantiopure α-stereogenic ketones constitute prevalent scaffolds in numerous natural products and pharmaceuticals while also serving as versatile and valuable building blocks for diverse synthetic transformations. Conventional methods for constructing chiral α-stereogenic ketones typically rely on the reaction of ketone enolates or enamines with electrophiles. However, the need for strong bases to generate these intermediates often limits the substrate scope. Additionally, achieving stereo- and regioselective formation of enolates or enamines from unsymmetrical dialkyl ketones remains a significant challenge. This review provides an overview of recent advances in the enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones, highlighting emerging strategies beyond classical chemistry, such as radical reactions, nucleophilic reactions, acyl–nickel-enabled cross-coupling, and enzyme-catalyzed dehalogenation.

articles.title: Selection-for-prediction: rethinking early cognitive development
articles.abstract: For decades, core knowledge accounts have proposed that early cognition is organized by innate, domain-specific conceptual or concept-like representations of objects, physical events, number, and agents. I propose a different starting point: infants’ behaviors may arise from domain-general attentional priors—evolutionarily shaped selection biases—interacting with perceptual mechanisms that organize information and support perceptual prediction, rather than from abstract, postperceptual representations. Attentional priors favor ecologically consequential information, including continuity, contact, and synchrony. When such information is disrupted, perceptual prediction error—rather than conceptual contradiction—may produce violation-of-expectation effects. Grounded in constraints on visual input and neural processing, this framework accounts for early successes and systematic failures, suggesting that development begins with perceptual-attentional mechanisms that shape selection, organization, prediction, and learning.

articles.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
articles.abstract: Standard implementations of softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy have two numerical bugs. The first bug, Softmax Collapse, rounds the target logit's gradient to zero if that one logit is much larger than the others, resulting in gradients that no longer sum to zero. The second bug, Softmax Cancellation, occurs when student logits are close to teacher logits, and produces non-zero gradients even when the student and teacher logits are equal. We present simple implementations of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy that fix both bugs. Our fix eliminates the previously-observed "Slingshot" phenomenon, speeds up grokking with weight decay, prevents accuracy collapse without weight decay, stops student networks from drifting away from the teacher during distillation, and shows that after memorization, logit growth is bounded by an equilibrium between weight decay and Adam's $ε$ hyperparameter.

articles.title: Action Learning for Scientific Simulations
articles.abstract: Understanding and controlling how systems evolve is central to science and engineering, where many problems require reasoning about complete trajectories. Existing approaches typically learn local dynamics or generate trajectories, but objectives constructed from individual transitions can miss dependencies across time, while generative models do not necessarily provide a tractable objective for evaluating and optimizing arbitrary paths. We study $\textit{action learning}$, the problem of recovering a stochastic action from trajectory observations, yielding a common objective for reasoning about dynamical systems. We introduce $\textbf{LEAP}$ ($\textbf{L}$earned $\textbf{E}$nergy on $\textbf{A}$ction $\textbf{P}$aths), which anchors the unknown action to a tractable reference process and learns the remaining correction by comparing observed trajectories with reference trajectories. This construction yields a differentiable objective on path space that can capture both local dynamical structure and nonadditive dependencies across time. Once learned, the same action can be flexibly reused for path ranking and inference, mechanism steering, constrained optimization and sampling. Across stochastic physical systems, many-body orbital dynamics and molecular simulations, LEAP recovers underlying dynamics, captures dependencies across time and enables transfer across inference objectives and physical conditions. We show that $\textit{action learning}$ is a promising framework for turning trajectory observations into reusable objectives for scientific inference and control.

articles.title: An Empirical Study of Recent Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph to Text Generation on Standard Benchmarks
articles.abstract: Knowledge graph-to-text (KG-to-text) generation verbalizes a set of knowledge graph triples into fluent natural language. While fine-tuned encoder-decoder models have long been the standard approach, recent LLMs are becoming increasingly competitive. We benchmark recent LLMs against fine-tuned encoder-decoder models, using reference-based metrics and graph-grounded reference-free LLM-based evaluation validated against human annotations. We observed that recent LLMs substantially narrow, and in several settings close, the gap with fine-tuned models on reference-based metrics, while performing better on graph-grounded metrics. LLM-based evaluation scores show limited correlation with reference-based metrics, suggesting that the two approaches capture different aspects of generation quality. Graph-grounded evaluation reveals that prompted models produce fewer contradictions and triple omissions than fine-tuned models, and these errors increase more rapidly with graph size for fine-tuned models, highlighting differences between the two approaches that reference-based metrics may not fully capture.

articles.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
articles.abstract: Looped architectures scale quality while keeping parameter count fixed by repeatedly passing activations through the same block of layers. During inference, each recurrence generates independent KV-caches, causing memory to grow linearly. To address this challenge, prior work has proposed KV-sharing (i.e., sharing KV-caches across depth), finding that, in some cases, the KV-cache of the final recurrence can be shared with the earlier recurrences without quality loss, a property we denote as KV-shareability. However, the mechanisms underlying KV-shareability remain poorly understood, with even identically trained looped architectures not consistently exhibiting it. In this paper, we study how KV-shareability can be enabled in looped models. We propose a two-stage method: in the first stage, we use stochastic depth during pretraining, which induces contractive residual dynamics that drive representations toward a common limit across recurrences. In the second stage, we propose BeNice!, a post-training method that broadcasts the final recurrence's KV-cache into the first recurrence, training it to produce compatible residuals while preserving the original model's quality. As a result, BeNice! enables KV-shareability while matching standard finetuning's unshared validation perplexity. Using BeNice!, we show that KV-sharing is complementary to alternative KV-compression methods, composing with memory-efficient sequence mixers (e.g., multi-latent attention, Kimi delta attention) and low-precision KV-cache quantization (e.g., fp8, mxfp8, nvfp4). Finally, in simulated low-memory, long-context inference, KV-sharing improves cache hit rates by up to 31.4%, increases throughput by up to 23.6%, and reduces p90 time-to-first-token by up to 83.6%.

articles.title: Beyond Best-of-$k$: Prior-Consistent DAPS for Ambiguous Nonlinear Inverse Problems
articles.abstract: Diffusion models have become strong priors for solving inverse problems. However, nonlinear inverse problems such as phase retrieval remain challenging when multiple measurement-consistent solutions are distinguishable only by the prior; we call such measurements ambiguous. Existing diffusion-based samplers rely on local approximations during reconstruction. For an ambiguous measurement, these approximations can allow measurement guidance to favor a measurement-consistent mode that is close to a prior-supported mode but is itself not supported by the prior. Evaluation often masks this type of failure by reporting the best-of-$k$ runs, where the best is selected by comparison to the ground truth. We introduce Prior-Consistent DAPS (PC-DAPS), a variant of Decoupled Annealing Posterior Sampling (DAPS) designed to address this failure case by maintaining multiple candidate solutions within a single sampling run. As annealing noise decreases, PC-DAPS prunes and replaces weaker candidates according to their prior consistency, without any ground-truth access. PC-DAPS reduces the incidence of prior-inconsistent samples and improves sample quality on nonlinear inverse problems while preserving sample quality and diversity on linear inverse problems.

articles.title: Beyond Causal Masks: Auditing and Localizing Hidden Future-Token Leakage in Adaptive Sequence Models
articles.abstract: Hidden future-token leakage can create false architectural gains: an autoregressive model may appear substantially better under teacher-forced evaluation while its free-running generation deteriorates. We investigate this failure in an adaptive residual-routing decoder whose sequence-level routing summary exposes prefix positions to future tokens despite a correct causal attention mask. An anomalous 24-layer checkpoint reduces validation loss from the baseline's 3.5958 to 1.4259, yet it fails a prefix-invariance audit and has substantially higher reference-model perplexity during generation. Layer-wise diagnostics and implementation inspection trace the violation to a full-sequence summary broadcast through the dynamic routing-query path. Two independently trained 12-layer causal repairs eliminate detectable leakage and return validation loss and reference perplexity to the control scale, removing the large apparent advantage. As diagnostic tools, we use the established prefix-invariance contract, maximum prefix-output discrepancy (LeakScore), complementary behavioral metrics, and layer-wise profiles. Supporting experiments cover six synthetic implementation pairs spanning five module families, clean pretrained controls, controlled fault injection, and cache consistency across numerical precisions. These results illustrate how hidden future-token access can produce misleading claims of architectural progress and why lower teacher-forced loss should be interpreted together with whole-model causal checks and free-running evaluation.

articles.title: Bilingual Language Models Capture Cross-Linguistic Influence in Second-Language Reading
articles.abstract: While monolingual language model (LM) surprisal is widely established as a predictor of reading times, it cannot capture the non-native (L2) reading dynamics that are shaped by the reader's first language (L1). In this work, we investigate whether the cross-lingual transfer within bilingual models aligns with human L1-driven biases during L2 reading. We evaluate bilingual models on eye-tracking data of readers from 12 diverse L1 backgrounds reading English texts. To isolate L1-specific transfer, we compare bilingual models trained on an L1 that matches the readers' L1 background to both a monolingual English baseline and bilingual models trained on other L1s. We demonstrate that matching the readers' L1 improves the prediction of L2 reading times. This predictive advantage is concentrated in late-stage eye-tracking measures, modulated by L1-L2 script overlap, and peaks among intermediate-proficiency readers. These findings provide evidence that bilingual LMs capture aspects of cross-linguistic influence, and that such influence is present in L2 reading behavior.

articles.title: CRANE: Post-Hoc Counterfactual Retrieval for Multimodal Classifiers
articles.abstract: Counterfactual explanation methods have been introduced for unimodal settings, with dedicated frameworks for tabular, timeseries, text, and image data, yet no post-hoc method has been designed for classifiers that learn from multimodal inputs. Existing explainability methods for multimodal classifiers apply modality-specific attribution independently to each input, which fails to yield coherent explanations and does not transfer to arbitrary pre-trained multimodal architectures. To address these shortcomings, we present CRANE (Counterfactual Retrieval via Agnostic Nearest-neighbour Explanations), the first post-hoc, model-agnostic framework for nearest-neighbour multimodal counterfactual generation that retrieves real training examples from the target class as candidate explanations, ensuring plausibility by construction. Across four heterogeneous datasets and three fusion strategies, we show that Multimodal Consensus Retrieval (MC-R), which intersects per-modality neighbour sets to identify instances jointly close to the query in every modality, emerges as the strongest multimodal strategy, achieving the best or joint-best outcome on three of four datasets while grounding every explanation in the joint training distribution. Unimodal strategies remain competitive when a single modality dominates the decision boundary.

articles.title: Can an Agent Debug a Web Corpus? Agentic Auditing of Slovak FineWeb2
articles.abstract: Multilingual pipelines such as FineWeb2 apply one recipe across a thousand languages, leaving the failure modes of individual languages unanticipated. We use an LLM once, as a corpus debugger rather than a classifier: a tool-using agent explores the corpus through a read-only, budgeted API and compiles each finding into an executable test, which a native speaker then validates. On the 26.5M-document Slovak portion of FineWeb2, three runs costing \$2.21-\$2.84 each found seven findings over four phenomena. The largest is a machine-generated content farm of 1,408,437 documents (5.32%) that passed the pipeline's filters, 86.6% of it passing even stricter thresholds. Blinded labels support 6 of the 7 findings (defect rates .53-1.00 against .08 in a random control) and do not support one. The compiled suite scans the full corpus in 0.7 s of wall-clock time without a GPU, against \$12k-\$90k per LLM classification pass. The best static sampling baseline validates more selectors than any agent run, at under half the cost. The agent contributes exact prevalence, a precision estimate checked against sampled documents, an account of why the pipeline missed each slice, and a reusable test. We release the framework, Slovak test suite, validation data and agent trajectories.

articles.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
articles.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits step-by-step rationales that appear to explain model predictions, but there is no guarantee these steps causally drive the final answer. In standard autoregressive generation, dense attention allows each reasoning step to attend to the full context, enabling the model to derive answers through direct lookup while generating plausible-sounding but post-hoc justifications. We introduce CausalCoT, an inference framework that enforces causal transparency by decomposing problems into a directed acyclic graph of atomic sub-questions, evaluating each node in an isolated context containing only its direct causal parents. This Markovian structure removes attention pathways to non-parent content, making downstream predictions sensitive to local reasoning rather than global context leakage. Across a diverse suite of reasoning benchmarks, CausalCoT preserves competitive predictive performance while improving explanation faithfulness, increasing causal sensitivity of intermediate reasoning steps by an average of 12 and up to 21 percentage points over the strongest baseline. The structured dependency graph additionally enables test-time interventions in which local corrections propagate predictably through downstream reasoning.

articles.title: Contestable Agents for Data Governance: Recording Human Stewardship of AI-Generated Metadata Across Structured and Unstructured Systems
articles.abstract: Industrial organizations hold operational knowledge in structured records, such as telemetry, point lists, and transactions, and in unstructured sources, such as manuals, service notes, communications, and inspection reports. Governance programs often manage these sources separately. Classifying, linking, and documenting them depends on a small group of employees with deep domain knowledge. Agents built on large language models can propose metadata, cite documents, and flag quality issues, but unreviewed proposals can spread errors into downstream systems. A perfunctory approval leaves no record of what a reviewer checked. We present contestable governance: specialist agents produce scored, cited arguments for disputed metadata decisions; a steward can accept, reject, modify, or add arguments before commit; and a governance record retains the evidence, interventions, and outcome. A versioned domain glossary supplies model-specific terms and acronym definitions to the agents. We describe the workflow, a triage path that reserves full argumentation for uncertain proposals while preserving review before commit, the scoring and record models, and a gate that controls which verified decisions become precedent. Two HVAC use cases illustrate the pattern: point classification using Brick Schema class labels, supported by an open reference implementation, and an illustrative warranty failure-mode decision linking claim fields and telemetry to service notes and revisioned bulletins.

articles.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
articles.abstract: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage. We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting. Under the illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5), TF-IDF with logistic regression and a threshold of 0.60 selected on calibration reduces test cost from 0.763 to 0.472, a 38.1% relative reduction (paired ratio-bootstrap 95% CI [35.7%, 40.4%]), while lowering wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%. Frozen calibration-selected policies also beat both always-route and always-defer on held-out test data in 14 of 16 settings in a post-hoc cost-parameter analysis. The strongest prompted configuration reaches 0.477 accuracy on a stratified 1,000-ticket test subset, versus 0.879 for fine-tuned DistilBERT on the same tickets. Isotonic lowers expected calibration error without reliably improving discrimination: GPT-4o-mini few-shot has one confidence value before and after recalibration and correctness AUROC 0.500. We therefore report correctness AUROC and tie-aware risk-coverage area alongside ECE. At the analytically derived break-even probability 0.80, seven prompted configurations defer all tickets; Haiku few-shot routes only 19/1,000. An LLM-only agreement control and margin/entropy rejection baselines further separate calibration from discrimination. The findings are scoped to this dataset, prompt design, model endpoints, and illustrative costs; the work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or universal deployment certification.

articles.title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
articles.abstract: \emph{Continuous-space} attacks find prompts that trigger malicious behaviors, such as overthinking, in black-box LLMs by sampling or optimizing over a low-dimensional Gaussian latent space and decoding it to text through a \emph{random mapping} and nearest-token lookup. Because the random mapping is not learned from language, its prompts can be highly unnatural, and as such easily detectable through input guardrails, and the risk estimates they yield are not grounded in natural prompts. In this paper, we demonstrate that the same continuous latent-space framework can be coupled directly to a learned generative distribution over language, a continuous diffusion language model (dLLM), which removes the artificial random mapping while preserving the standard-Gaussian latent formulation and the downstream sampling or optimization procedure. We evaluate this approach under two settings: sampling-based estimation using \emph{RareTrap} and optimization-based search using \emph{ThinkTrap}. We find that character-level perplexity drops from $10^3$--$10^7$ to 3--5 in RareTrap and from 20--28 to 4.3--5.4 in ThinkTrap. We also find that model risk estimates can differ by an order of magnitude across the two mappings.

articles.title: Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona)
articles.abstract: We propose a new regression method named Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona) that directly uses samples to estimate the state and its derivatives at a query point, along with their admissible bounds, without long global training. By casting the values and derivatives at the query and neighbouring samples as latent variables in a constrained optimisation problem, the burden of long training loops becomes one of on-demand local solves. We establish Diona's theoretical properties including finite-sample coverage and, in the noiseless case, convergence to the true state and derivatives under dense sampling. In a nonlinear regression benchmark on six functions of three to eight dimensions, Diona was more accurate than a Gaussian process (GP) on noiseless data especially with denser data sets. Furthermore, as with GP, it produced uncertainty bounds that contained the true value at more than 95% of query points in four functions. Diona's time to a first prediction after a data set update was three to four orders of magnitude shorter than that of the GP, and two to three orders shorter than that of a neural network, which was more accurate but offers no uncertainty quantification. This low latency is paid for by on-demand predictions, so this latency advantage applies when relatively few predictions are needed between data updates.

articles.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
articles.abstract: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution. Running all candidate solutions to completion can be computationally demanding, so recent work prunes the candidate pool after generating only a short prefix, committing further computation only to the surviving candidates. Existing pruning strategies divide broadly into two categories: Quality-based methods assign a score to each partial solution and discard those predicted to ultimately lead to an incorrect final solution, while diversity-based methods select partial solutions that follow different reasoning trajectories and are therefore likely to cover different final solutions. The tension between these two objectives is an instance of exploration versus exploitation, yet little to no prior work on pruning exposes this trade-off directly, let alone optimizes it. In this paper, we introduce a pruning procedure that addresses this trade-off directly by optimizing pass@$k$ over the selected solution pool. In particular, it chooses the pool to maximize the probability that at least one of its partial solutions, when continued to completion, yields a correct answer. Because this objective simultaneously rewards high-quality partial solutions and penalizes redundancy among them, quality and diversity are naturally balanced by the criterion itself rather than through separate ad-hoc design choices. On eight open-weight reasoning models, our method outperforms existing quality-based and diversity-based pruning strategies. The gains are particularly pronounced when the pruning procedure keeps a moderate number of partial solutions for continued generation, highlighting the value of directly balancing quality and diversity during pruning.

articles.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination
articles.abstract: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations, selecting high-level actions while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of centralized coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff dependencies. A prop legend and pot ingredient-count indicators provide explicit visual cues, while grid-based destinations support spatial grounding. The evaluation compares four VLMs on all 20 maps, measuring task score, order completion, delivery precision, action acceptance rate, and model API expenditure. A memory ablation on the same 20 maps examines the effect of a shared, self-authored notebook while retaining six-response action history in both conditions. The strongest evaluated model, \texttt{gpt-6-astra}, achieves 26.2\% mean order completion. Notebook memory has mixed score effects across models, with positive mean differences for Claude and Qwen and negative differences for GPT and Gemini.

articles.title: Efficient and Optimal Learning of Discrete Distributions with Person-Level Privacy
articles.abstract: We study learning a discrete distribution under person-level differential privacy in the batched setting. Given $n$ users, each contributing $m$ i.i.d. samples from an unknown distribution $μ$ over $[k]$, we seek an estimate of $μ$ with total-variation error $α$. We give polynomial-time algorithms under both pure and approximate differential privacy. Under pure $(\varepsilon,0)$-DP, we achieve $n = \widetilde O(k/(α^2 m)+k/(α\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k/\varepsilon)$, the first polynomial-time pure-DP guarantee matching the information-theoretic optimum up to logarithmic factors. Under approximate $(\varepsilon,δ)$-DP, we achieve $n = \widetilde O(k/(α^2 m)+k/(α\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k+\log(1/δ)/\varepsilon)$. At $δ=2^{-Θ(k)}$, this is $\widetilde O(k)$ for fixed $α,\varepsilon,m$ and failure probability. Our algorithms use a new degree-6 sum-of-squares estimator for learning from untrusted batches. Its key ingredient is a trace-bounded diagonal majorizer for the difference between the empirical covariance of the repaired batch averages and the multinomial covariance predicted by their mean. We prove that clean data admit this certificate through semidefinite-programming duality and a new application of the stronger symmetric form of Grothendieck's inequality due to Friedland and Lim. The certificate preserves the mean-dependent variance of multinomial batch averages, yielding the near-optimal robust rate $O(η\sqrt{\log(1/η)/m})$ and providing the score required by the privacy reduction. We also prove a statistical query lower bound ruling out a uniformly smaller order of error under fixed polynomial SQ resource bounds.

articles.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
articles.abstract: Tool-using language model agents rely on environmental facts to decide whether an action is permitted. When a tool response omits a safety-relevant fact, an agent may carry out a prohibited action even though the user request is benign and every returned statement is true. We introduce \bench{}, an executable benchmark for evaluating unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery in LLM agents under missing evidence. It contains 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains. By systematically suppressing critical facts, the benchmark measures unsafe execution under critical evidence omission and determines the minimum observed failure cardinality, including failures with full evidence and cases with no observed failure after exhaustive testing. An independent audit tool tests whether agents seek missing facts and then withhold prohibited actions while completing permissible tasks. The benchmark reveals substantial variation across the ten models in omission robustness, evidence acquisition, and appropriate action. Resistance to missing evidence does not necessarily translate into useful recovery. Recovery access reduces unsafe execution for all ten models, but agents differ in whether they actively obtain the missing facts and use them to act appropriately in both worlds.

articles.title: FairFRESH: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Fair and Explainable Household Food Recommendation
articles.abstract: Recommender systems typically serve one user at a time. However, in households, members share a finite pantry and follow different dietary rules, making independent recommendations prone to resource conflicts and dietary violations. We formulate household food recommendation as constrained fair division and present FairFRESH, a neuro-symbolic framework that learns per-member utilities, allocates foods under explicit welfare objectives, enforces dietary rules through a deterministic filter, and explains recommendations using Shapley and Banzhaf attributions. Theoretically, we show that no finite penalty guarantees compliance near a dietary-rule threshold, establish approximation guarantees for greedy allocation under utilitarian and smoothed Nash objectives in the stock-free model before filtering, and characterize the scale invariance of Nash welfare. We also use the minimax theorem to analyze rotating shared meals. On NHANES-derived data, the learned utility model achieves Recall@20 of 0.293, outperforming five learned recommenders (at most 0.244) but not a previous-day repetition heuristic (0.321). On held-out four-person households, Nash allocation reduces Gini disparity by 42% relative to conflict resolution while improving Recall@20 from 0.180 to 0.197. It comes within 2% of an upper bound on the smoothed Nash optimum, and rescaling one member's utilities changes at most 1.5% of assignments. All recommendations satisfy the encoded dietary rules, while attribution scores correlate with utility loss upon component removal (r = 0.76). In simulation, shared meals reduce pantry use by about one-third, and weekly rotation increases the worst-off member's utility by 38% over the best fixed meal.

articles.title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning via Algorithmic Stability
articles.abstract: Understanding catastrophic forgetting, in which learning new tasks degrades performance on previously learned tasks, remains a fundamental challenge in continual learning (CL). Existing theoretical analyses often rely on specific model or task structures and offer limited insight into how iterative optimization affects forgetting. To address this gap, we develop an algorithmic stability framework for expected population forgetting under SGD without prescribing a particular model architecture. Specifically, we decompose forgetting into intra-task and cross-task generalization gaps and empirical forgetting. To bound the generalization gaps, we track how a sample perturbation affects updates within a task and propagates through subsequent tasks. We consider constant, intra-task decaying, and continuously decaying learning-rate schedules. Comparing the two decaying schedules allows us to characterize how restarting learning-rate decay at task boundaries affects the propagation of historical sample perturbations. For empirical forgetting, we derive bounds for all three schedules by retaining cumulative gradient alignment along the optimization trajectory, without requiring convexity. Combining these results yields upper bounds on expected forgetting that capture the effects of training set size, the number of updates per task, the total number of tasks, learning-rate schedules, and cumulative gradient alignment. Finally, we conduct experiments on Split CIFAR-100 and Split MiniImageNet to examine the empirical implications of our theoretical findings.

articles.title: From Prompt Rules to Golden Data Model: Production-Scale Generation of Personalized, Compliant Pharmaceutical Claims
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate domain-specific commercial & medical content (e.g., claims, statements, and promotional phrases) in regulated industries such as pharmaceuticals. However, ensuring its regulatory compliance, factual accuracy, and audience-specific personalization remains a major challenge. We report a production case study asking whether moving compliance and personalization signal from prompt-level rules into retrieval time structured context improves pharmaceutical claims generation, using Composer, a deployed internal tool built on a Golden Data Model (GDM) of 1,867 pharmaceutical claims spanning four products. The GDM integrates claim metadata, references, audience labels, material type, usage history, Match Text Variant (MTV) links, and a six dimension quality score (6C). Across six product-audience segments, the context pipeline improves intended indication (+29%), intended content type (+62%) and intended target audience (+67%), 6C quality score (+86%), and claim reuse (+34%). Production log analysis over the deployment period shows a 29.5% reduction in weekly API cost. We report this as descriptive deployment evidence. This work is a systems and data architecture contribution: it shows that in a regulated, high-stakes domain, restructuring claim data for retrieval-time filtering is a more scalable lever than expanding prompt-level rules, and documents the engineering path data cleaning, graph linking, and quality scoring.

articles.title: How Ground Truth Shapes Retrieval Scores: Evidence-Aware Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Breast Lesions
articles.abstract: Purpose: To describe an evidence-aware retrieval evaluation protocol for a clinical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system over breast lesion management literature, addressing the dependence of retrieval scores on annotation coverage. Methods: An 18-document corpus and an 18-query development benchmark, with one Yes/No or WH-question per document, were used. Retrieval combined dense embeddings, BM25, and cross-encoder reranking. Chunk sizes of 128 to 1024 tokens, overlaps of 0 to 20%, and four retriever configurations were evaluated. Relevance was defined by evidence spans mapped to all containing chunks, treating overlapping chunks with equivalent evidence as relevant. Retrieval was evaluated using R-Precision, Recall@K, MRR, and nDCG@K. Separately, generation was assessed on a 512-token index at K=1 to 5 using DeepEval claim-level metrics, with deepseek-v4-pro as the LLM judge, and BLEU/ROUGE metrics. Results: The selected hybrid retriever, using 384-token chunks and 20% overlap, retrieved accepted evidence in the top three results for 17 of 18 queries. Recall@3, R-Precision, MRR@3, and nDCG@3 each reached 0.94. Ground-truth curation increased evidence spans from 25 to 37 and accepted chunk targets from 36 to 51 without changing retrieval rankings. Conclusion: Cross-encoder reranking achieved the highest retrieval scores. Expanded relevance annotations increased recognized evidence without changing rankings, highlighting annotation sensitivity. The small development set and retrieval-informed curation require independent validation, including radiologist assessment of evidence sufficiency.

articles.title: Jev-DLC: Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback
articles.abstract: Individual preferences often become visible only after deployment, when a user accepts one decision or revokes it in favor of another. Jev-style typed interfaces make this feedback explicit by identifying the selected action and, under revocation, the decision it replaces. We study how these consequences persist across requests as Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback (Jev-DLC). Jev-DLC treats each correction as both evidence about a recurring action identity and a directed relation between the preferred and rejected choices. It preserves these signals in complementary bounded channels above a frozen scorer and combines their scores to shape the next decision. The method retains no raw interaction history, adds no scorer call, and performs no runtime language-model backward pass. We also introduce TCPA-Bench, a chronological suite that credits a correction only through its effect on later decisions. On TCPA-Repeat, Jev-DLC reaches 44.83% user-macro accuracy overall, 2.43 points above Recent-4 history replay.
