We find that during the X-ray flash, inverse Compton scattering dominates the coupling between the gas and the radiation near the nozzle shock, where it adds X-ray energy much faster than thermal emission and may affect the dynamics. Outside the X-ray thermalization radii, its instantaneous X-ray production rate during the flash is comparable to or larger than the escaping X-ray luminosity, so it may contribute substantially to the X-ray emission from TDEs.

articles.title: Nanopillar metasurfaces uniting high optical reflectivity with ultracoherent nanomechanics
articles.abstract: Mechanically compliant mirrors are key components in cavity optomechanics. However, the requirements to achieve the best optical and mechanical performance are usually in direct competition. A high reflectivity for tightly focused beams entails thick reflectors, whereas ultracoherent flexural nanomechanics necessitates thin membranes. We eliminate this trade-off by introducing high-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces on top of a thin membrane. We pattern a 50 micrometer-diameter array of nanopillars to form a photonic crystal. The flat band behavior of guided resonances in the photonic crystal enables a reflectivity of 99.82(1)% for a tightly focused beam of 7 micrometer waist. The combination of two guided resonances creates a 100 nanometer-wide high-reflectivity band around 1550 nanometer. Simultaneously, the nanopillar patterning realizes a density-modulated phononic crystal that isolates an ultracoherent localized mechanical mode with a $Q\cdot f$-product of $2\cdot 10^{14}$Hz. The demonstrated nanopillar metasurfaces enable lightweight mirrors for room-temperature quantum optomechanics and for use as levitated mirrors or lightsails.

articles.title: Noise redistribution by stabilizer codes: an organizing view of concatenated three-qubit codes
articles.abstract: We present an organizing framework for concatenated quantum error correction based on the observation that the syndrome projection of a stabilizer code reshapes the noise channel in a code-determined manner. For any stabilizer code, one level of QEC maps the physical noise to a block-diagonal logical channel whose diagonal Pauli weights are fixed by the code geometry. Coherences between different syndrome classes vanish, and no physical Pauli twirl is required to reach this block-diagonal form. Concatenation can then be viewed as the iteration of the same redistribution step: the dominant logical error after one level selects the code used at the next. We instantiate the framework with the two smallest stabilizer codes, the bit-flip and phase-flip codes, and apply it to amplitude damping. The redistribution rules give the concatenation protocol $C_2(\hatσ_y) C_1(\hatσ_x)$, whose ideal-recovery fidelity scales as $f_l=1-\mathcal O(γ^2)$. Solving the crossover condition $F_l>F_{l-1}$ in the ideal-gate limit yields a critical damping parameter $γ_c\approx0.30$; in terms of the initial channel fidelity, $f=1-1.72755γ^2$. Under the same ideal-recovery assumption, we compare the overall gate accuracy rate with that of the five-qubit code. The scope of the framework, in particular for coherent and correlated noise, is stated explicitly.

articles.title: Nonlinear quantum noise polarization in macroscopic nonlinear QED
articles.abstract: We construct a quantum theory of light in nonlinearly responding materials with dispersion and absorption and, in particular, show the emergence of non-Gaussian noise associated with nonlinear absorption processes. Our theory is based on a path-integral formulation of the microscopic Huttner-Barnett model including cubic matter self-interaction required for $χ^{(2)}$ nonlinear processes. We show that the noise polarization emerges naturally from a decoupling of the stochastic weights of the bath response which, in case of cubic self-interactions, leads to a decoupling via Airy functions. As the theory is, by construction, consistent with the nonlinear fluctuation-dissipation theorem, it constitutes a viable quantum theory of light in nonlinear media.

articles.title: Norm-Aware Product Formulas for Hamiltonian Simulations
articles.abstract: With the target of efficiently solving the quantum-mechanical Schrödinger equation on future quantum computers, first- and second-order product formulas for the time-evolution operator are proposed, designed to exploit hierarchies in the operator norms of the individual Hamiltonian components. Inspired by the THRIFT product formula, these decomposition schemes achieve a suppression of the leading error term by a factor of alpha<1 with respect to the standard Lie--Trotter--Suzuki splitting of the same order, where alpha quantifies the norm ratio between the dominant and subdominant parts of the Hamiltonian. Unlike THRIFT, the proposed formulas retain the general product-formula structure, making them applicable to Hamiltonians whose terms act on an arbitrary number of qubits. The advantages of this approach are demonstrated through numerical experiments on engineered two-dimensional spin-1/2 XY model systems and isolated molecules within the double-factorization framework.

articles.title: Observation of Polarization Topology in Magneto-Optical BICs
articles.abstract: Polarization topology in momentum space is a fundamental characteristic of photonic bound states in the continuum (BICs), where the winding of far-field polarization defines a quantized topological charge. Although magneto-optical (MO) BICs combine polarization topology with magnetically tunable chirality, experimental characterization remains challenging because time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking complicates eigenpolarization extraction. Here, we experimentally resolve the momentum-space polarization topology of an MO BIC by reconstructing its two-dimensional far-field eigenpolarization texture. We extract the resonant output polarization using singular value decomposition of the polarization-resolved angle-resolved reflection matrix without invoking reciprocity. The reconstructed polarization azimuth winds counterclockwise by 2$π$ around the $Γ$-point singularity, yielding a topological charge of q = +1. Moreover, the polarization handedness can be reversed solely by varying the magnetic-bias strength, while the field direction and the measured topological charge remain unchanged. A non-Hermitian coupled-mode model traces this reversal to hybridization between the BIC mode and a leaky mode. This work establishes experimental access to momentum-space polarization topology in nonreciprocal photonics, opening a route to explore topological singularities and their evolution under active TRS breaking.

articles.title: One-shot entanglement generation and distillation via Petz recovery and binary hypothesis testing
articles.abstract: How much entanglement can two distant laboratories share when their connection is noisy? We relate this question to deciding which of two quantum hypotheses is present. Our one-shot bounds apply to entanglement generation over a quantum channel and to one-way entanglement distillation from a shared state. We use Cheng's trace inequality to bound the infidelity of a Petz decoder in terms of a binary hypothesis testing cost. Applying the inequality before averaging over codes reduces the error analysis to computing a second moment of random subspaces. The proof covers every integer target dimension and treats rank-deficient states explicitly. A corollary expresses the achievable entanglement through hypothesis-testing coherent information, with a single logarithmic error slack and exact integer rounding. We also prove an error-preserving conversion from entanglement generation codes to entanglement transmission codes: the target dimension decreases by only a constant factor at fixed error, and the decoder is the original decoder followed by local processing. Consequently, for both entanglement generation and entanglement transmission, arbitrary pure reference-input states yield the same coherent-information rate, second-order Gaussian correction at the original error tolerance, and explicit achievable logarithmic remainder. For commuting testing hypotheses, the logarithmic remainder improves to a constant. These results give a direct route from binary distinguishability to explicit recovery guarantees and finite-resource quantum communication rates.

articles.title: Phase-Matched Chirps for Energy-Efficient Excitation of Magneto-Mechanical Resonators
articles.abstract: Magneto-mechanical resonators (MMRs) are a recently proposed class of passive, wireless devices used for sensing and tracking. The operating principle of MMRs relies on an excitation of the sensor by oscillating magnetic fields, followed by an inductive readout to measure the sensor's dynamics. One challenge lies in generating efficient excitation signals to ensure maximum energy harvesting by the sensor. In this simulation study, we focus on chirped magnetic-field excitations and compare their performance with conventional constant-frequency excitation for both sinusoidal and rectangular waveforms. The results indicate varying levels of efficiency, with a sinusoidal linear down-chirp excitation signal yielding the largest deflection angle, offering the best potential for reducing the energy consumption and improving the temporal resolution of the measurement.

articles.title: Predictive electronic feedback control for narrow-linewidth lasers
articles.abstract: Narrow-linewidth lasers are essential for various key atom-laser interaction processes and optical setups in quantum coherent control, quantum precision measurement, and quantum information science. The Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique is the standard method for the frequency-stabilization of narrow-linewidth lasers, but the inherent time delay in its feedback loop inevitably induces excessive phase noise, commonly known as servo bumps. Previous solutions primarily rely on additional optical components outside the electronic feedback control loop. Here, we propose and implement a generic method based on the Smith predictor to address the time-delay issue entirely within the electronic part of the PDH feedback control loop. We systematically demonstrate its capability to suppress phase noise and reduce servo bumps by adding only a single Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) controller to the loop. This class of methods is demonstrated to be conceptually concise with minimal hardware overhead, effective in practice, and holds potential for a wide variety of future applications.

articles.title: Problem-aware sampling for bias and variance reduction in randomised Hamiltonian simulation
articles.abstract: Randomised quantum simulation algorithms such as qDRIFT reduce circuit depth by replacing deterministic product formulas with stochastic compilations, but achieving high accuracy can require many steps. In vanilla qDRIFT, Hamiltonian terms are sampled with probabilities proportional to their coefficient magnitudes. We propose StateDRIFT, a variant of qDRIFT which optimises its sampling distribution to estimate time-evolved quantities using knowledge of the initial state and target observable, with a provable truncation bound that keeps qDRIFT's guarantees. The distribution at each depth is chosen by solving an optimisation problem targeting bias and/or variance. StateDRIFT can significantly reduce the bias and variance of estimators, and hence circuit depth, which we test on short-time dynamics of lattice models and molecules under Jordan-Wigner up to 18 qubits. For example, with BeH2 StateDRIFT can reduce the number of two-qubit gates required to achieve a given accuracy from 11,201 to 983. StateDRIFT involves measuring observables and commutators on the initial state, so we propose two practical ways to estimate these: classical surrogates such as tensor networks, and classical shadows, which recover most or all of the saving from exact oracles in the systems tested.

articles.title: Quantum Constrained Hamiltonian Descent
articles.abstract: We propose Quantum Constrained Hamiltonian Descent (QCHD), a continuous-time quantum framework for optimization under smooth equality constraints. The unconstrained counterpart, Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD), minimizes a cost function by simulating the Schrödinger dynamics of a particle in the potential given by the cost function. Applying Dirac's formalism to the classical dynamics with constraints, we construct an intrinsic quantum Hamiltonian with a Laplace--Beltrami operator on the constraint manifold in a kinetic term. Its evolution preserves the constraints exactly without penalty terms and is expected to solve quantum-dynamically the constrained optimization problem. We analyze its relation to Quantum Hamiltonian Descent supplemented by a strong penalty term. For a squared-distance penalty, the effective tangential dynamics acquires an extrinsic-curvature potential and, in nontrivial normal-rotation sectors, a coupling to the normal-bundle connection. These embedding-dependent terms remain in the strong-penalty limit, generally yielding quantum dynamics different from QCHD. Numerical comparisons for circular, elliptical, and two simultaneous constraints show faster optimization and improved concentration near global minima for the initial states and finite penalty strengths considered.

articles.title: Qubits Are Not Enough: Deflation and Measurement Limits in Variational Quantum Modal Analysis
articles.abstract: Amplitude encoding stores an N-degree-of-freedom structural mode using ceiling(log2 N) qubits. This article develops an evaluation framework for variational quantum eigensolvers in finite-element structural dynamics. A Cholesky transformation maps the generalized eigenproblem to a symmetric mass-orthonormal Hamiltonian, ensuring Euclidean quantum-state orthogonality equals structural mass orthogonality. For higher modes, the deflation penalty condition is sharpened to a necessary-and-sufficient threshold, with a Davis-Kahan bound quantifying effects of approximate projectors. Numerical studies separate mapping correctness, ansatz expressibility, preprocessing, Pauli growth, finite-shot uncertainty, and damage localization. For 128-DOF chains, consistent-mass whitening increases transformed-operator density from 0.023 to 0.308 and Pauli terms from 576 to 2950. Exact state-vector experiments show qubit count and circuit expressibility are distinct. At 10^5 shots per Pauli term, first-mode frequency RMS error is 2.45%. In an oracle-state study, 10% stiffness loss is localized in 84.5% of trials. Results sharpen the deflation condition, quantify resource bottlenecks, and claim no speedup.

articles.title: Rank-One Loss Maximizes the Spectral Response Strength of Passive Full-Order Exceptional Points
articles.abstract: We consider finite-dimensional non-Hermitian systems in which all modes coalesce at a single exceptional point. For a rank-one anti-Hermitian contribution, the spectral response strength is computed exactly. For passive systems, we then derive a sharp upper bound at fixed exceptional-point decay rate and show that it is reached only when the decay operator has rank one, corresponding to a single independent dissipative direction. This establishes rank-one loss as the optimal configuration for enhancing the response of a full-order exceptional point. The bound holds for arbitrary order and improves on earlier passive estimates beyond second order. Two third-order trimers illustrate the result: a rank-one-loss system saturates the bound, whereas a passive rank-two-loss realization remains below it. The result turns dissipation into a design resource: concentrating the loss into a single effective dissipative direction maximizes the highest-order spectral response of a passive full-order exceptional-point device.

articles.title: Realization of a Superleak in a Quantum Gas
articles.abstract: Ultracold quantum gases offer a controllable and microscopically accessible platform for understanding and engineering superfluidity. Yet, realizing a superleak that selectively transports the superfluid while suppressing normal flow has remained elusive. Here, we harness an optical superlattice to realize such a superleak through dynamical selectivity. The superfluid undergoes coherent Josephson transport, whereas the normal component exhibits slow, thermodynamically limited response, resulting in a flow-rate contrast of 500(49). Exploiting this contrast, we demonstrate repeated filtering of the normal component and dynamical purification of the superfluid, while sustaining coherent driven oscillations for up to 100 cycles. Our results establish a controllable atomic superleak and open possibilities for manipulating transport and thermodynamics in quantum fluids.

articles.title: Reset-Enhanced Dissipative Quantum Metrology
articles.abstract: Quantum metrology is ultimately shaped not only by measurements, but also by the dissipative dynamics that prepare and maintain the probe. Nevertheless, a general mechanism for enhancing both steady-state and transient precision in open quantum systems has been lacking. Here we show that adding a simple reset channel provides such a mechanism: reset acts as a minimal dissipative control that can enhance metrological precision without modifying the intrinsic Hamiltonian or applying continuous coherent driving. We derive a unified quantum-Fisher-information (QFI) reset-rate response identity, showing how reset enhances steady-state and transient estimation while revealing a sharp transient distinction. For static-parameter estimation in diagonal dynamics, reset leaves the leading short-time QFI unchanged; for the separate task of elapsed-time estimation, it generates an immediate drift contribution that can scale quadratically with the reset rate in the short-time limit. For frequency estimation, the enhancement is instead dominated by a genuinely quantum eigenvector contribution. These results establish reset as a simple dissipative resource for open-system quantum metrology.

articles.title: Second- and third-order nonlinearities in silicon nitride waveguides via heterogeneous integration of lithium niobate membranes
articles.abstract: Thick, dispersion-engineered silicon nitride is a leading platform for integrated third-order nonlinear optics, supporting supercontinuum and frequency comb generation. However, it lacks the second-order nonlinearity required by many applications. Here we bond pre-fabricated x-cut thin-film lithium niobate membranes onto finished silicon nitride waveguides as a back-end step, compatible with commercially fabricated waveguides. A single silicon nitride waveguide generates an octave-spanning supercontinuum and, through the lithium niobate membrane, concurrent second-harmonic, sum- and difference-frequency generation. These results open new possibilities for thick silicon nitride photonics, from visible light generation to on-chip $f$-$2f$ comb self-referencing, a key step towards miniaturised timing and navigation quantum technologies.

articles.title: Shaping Near Fields of Photonic Modes into Topological Textures
articles.abstract: Topological textures of light, such as optical vortices and skyrmions, are attractive for high-density information encoding and light-matter interactions. In the near field, topologies have primarily been realized using polaritonic platforms that inherently tie the platform to the material dispersion, limiting their footprint due to propagation losses and restricting their operating spectral region. Here, we introduce a route to shape near-field topologies through the geometric engineering of a dielectric metasurface supporting a quasi-bound state in the continuum resonance, without the need for polaritonic surface waves. In-plane deformation of our metasurface bars conserves their resonance-driven near-fields locally, so that the metasurface geometry and the polarization of the illuminating light dictate the generated topology. By shaping silicon unit cells into geometries with rotational symmetry, we create optical topologies with controllable topological charge. Using phase-resolved scattering-type near-field optical microscopy, we experimentally characterize high-purity resonance-locked topologies such as vortices in concentric rings and topological charge doublets in Archimedean spirals. In contrast to conventional topological textures, our purely photonic mode-based field textures are stationary standing waves in the radial direction, without relying on surface-wave propagation or polaritonic dispersion, establishing a spectrally and spatially scalable platform for near-field topological photonics.

articles.title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
articles.abstract: We propose a new method for proving $L^2$ and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. We first establish the $L^2$ logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched Rényi-2 divergence. A tensor-power argument, combined with the quantum asymptotic equipartition property, then transfers this decay bound to relative entropy, yielding the modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. This approach provides a general framework for proving size-independent logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for quantum Gibbs samplers. We apply it to two regimes: one-dimensional quantum spin chains at every finite temperature, and finite-range quantum spin systems at sufficiently high temperature in any fixed dimension.

articles.title: The Impact of Markovian Errors on Random Circuits
articles.abstract: Randomized benchmarking (RB) returns a single decay parameter or gate error rate, but when the noise is gate-dependent that parameter is notoriously difficult to interpret. We study RB and related random-circuit benchmarks under small gate-local Markovian noise by factorizing each noisy gate into its ideal action followed by the exponential of a small error generator and then perturbing the RB $\mathscr{L}$ matrix, which models the RB decay. For any low-error gate set that satisfies the requirements of RB (it is a sequence-asymptotic unitary 2-design), we show that Pauli-stochastic error rates contribute linearly to the RB decay parameter, while Hamiltonian error rates contribute through a gauge-invariant quadratic form. Pauli-correlation and active generators are absent from the linear term and enter only at higher order. For the single-qubit native gate set $\{X_{π/2},Y_{π/2}\}$ we derive this quadratic form explicitly in terms of three first-order gauge-invariant (FOGI) coordinates: the two intrinsic over-rotations and one relational axis-tilt error. The resulting formula explains the dependence of DRB on the sampling distribution and the compilation dependence of CRB. These results turn RB decay rates into interpretable functions of experimentally meaningful elementary error rates.

articles.title: The Mechanism of Chirality in Plasmonic Structures: Asymmetric Resonance Modes
articles.abstract: This study presents a theoretical framework for understanding the mechanism of chirality generation and circular dichroism (CD) in chiral nanostructures, with a particular focus on the role of asymmetric plasmon resonance mode distributions. Although previous studies have linked chiroptical properties to resonance differences, the specific nature and origin of these differences have not been fully elucidated. Here, we provide a more detailed explanation by quantitatively analyzing the asymmetric electric-field components arising from mode asymmetry. Specifically, we examine the near-field symmetry of individual nanorods and corner-stacked coupled structures (CSCS). The results demonstrate that chirality arises from asymmetric electric-field distributions, which give rise to distinct phase and amplitude responses of the electromagnetic fields in the composite structure under right-handed circularly polarized (RCP) and left-handed circularly polarized (LCP) illumination. The absorption and CD spectra, which exhibit distinct features around $910\,\mathrm{nm}$, support this mechanism and provide valuable insights into the design of chiroptical materials. The proposed mechanism is not restricted to a specific chiral structure or resonance and offers a broader explanation for the generation of circular dichroism.

articles.title: The limits of magic-state distillation
articles.abstract: Magic-state factories are a major cost of fault-tolerant quantum computing, yet how few noisy inputs they need is known only for restricted protocols. We show that, for tolerating input faults, any stabilizer protocol, however adaptive, postselected or multistage, is no better than a projection onto one stabilizer code, and that for rational targets a fault pattern is harmful exactly when its complement is. Searches over all codes show that quadratic distillation of one T state needs exactly nine inputs and that the eight-input CCZ factory is optimal. At order $d$, one T state needs $n\geq2d$.

articles.title: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
articles.abstract: We examine the conditions under which quantum parameter estimation is compatible with the concept of a ``true'' quantity value: a unique value of the estimated quantity that exists prior to and independently of measurement. While quantum parameter estimation typically assumes that the quantity to be estimated is a parameter, we argue that this assumption can be lifted, opening the way to a more general formulation of estimation that may apply even in situations where the quantity to be estimated is no longer a parameter, but instead a quantum variable susceptible to quantum fluctuations. We identify three assumptions that characterize the way estimation is often presented in the quantum metrology literature, namely, as a procedure for inferring an unknown ``true value", which is assumed to be unique and to exist prior to and independently of measurement. Using our more general framework, we prove a no-go theorem showing that the preceding assumptions are jointly incompatible with two further assumptions: the completeness of the quantum state (no `hidden variables'), and the presence of entanglement between the probe systems and the system under measurement. We note that the presence of such entanglement is a generic prediction of standard quantum theory. Consequently, if one is not willing to accept hidden variables, nor willing to modify standard quantum theory by introducing a new physical mechanism that destroys entanglement at some scale or regime, then a realist account of estimation is ultimately impossible.

articles.title: A hormonal message for a longer life
articles.abstract: The steroid hormone dafachronic acid may carry the effects of reduced mTOR activity between tissues to coordinate metabolism and longevity across the body.

articles.title: Motor unit mechanisms of speed control in mouse locomotion
articles.abstract: During locomotion, the coordinated activity of dozens of muscles shapes the kinematic features of each stride, including systematic changes in limb movement across walking speed. Motor units, each of which consists of a single motor neuron and the muscle fibers it innervates, contribute to the total activation of each muscle through their recruitment and firing rate when active. However, it remains unknown how the nervous system controls locomotor speed by changing the firing of individual motor units. To address this, we combined quantitative behavioral analysis of mouse locomotion with single motor unit recordings from the lateral and long heads of the triceps brachii, which drive monoarticular extension of the elbow and biarticular movements of the elbow and shoulder, respectively. In contrast to prior studies employing bulk electromyography (EMG) to examine muscle activity, our recordings revealed the diversity of spike patterning across motor units, as well as systematic differences in motor unit activity across muscles and locomotor speeds. First, motor unit activity differed significantly across the lateral and long heads, suggesting differential control of these two closely apposed elbow extensor muscles. Second, we found that individual units were recruited probabilistically (during only a subset of strides), showing that the highly repeatable bulk EMG signals observed across strides, in fact, reflect varying subsets of individual motor units. Finally, although recruitment probability and firing rate both increased at faster walking speeds, increases in recruitment were proportionally larger than rate changes, and recruitment of individual units accompanied changes in limb kinematics. Together, these results reveal how the firing of individual motor units varies systematically across muscles and walking speeds to produce flexible locomotor behavior.

articles.title: Olfactory combinatorial coding supports risk–reward decision-making in Caenorhabditis elegans
articles.abstract: Olfactory-driven behaviors are essential for animal survival, but mechanisms for decoding olfactory inputs remain poorly understood. We have used whole-network Ca2+ imaging to study olfactory coding in Caenorhabditis elegans. We show that the odorant 1-octanol is encoded combinatorially in the periphery as both an attractant and a repellent. These inputs are integrated centrally, and their relative strengths determine the sensitivity and valence of the behavioral response through modulation of locomotory reversals and speed. The balance of these pathways also dictates the activity of the locomotory command interneurons, which control locomotory reversals. This balance serves as a regulatory node for response modulation, allowing C. elegans to weigh opportunities and hazards in its environment when formulating behavioral responses. Thus, an odorant can be encoded simultaneously as inputs of opposite valence, focusing attention on the integration of these inputs in determining perception, response, and plasticity.

articles.title: Copper-Mediated Valence Tautomerism Enables α -C(sp3)–H Alkylation of 1,3-Dicarbonyl Compounds and Tryptophans via Photocatalysis
articles.abstract: Carbonyl α-C(sp3)–H functionalization is a key approach to access functionalized pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and bioactive peptides. Conventional two-electron enol tautomerization strategies for this transformation often suffer from harsh reaction conditions and limited substrate tolerance. While valence tautomerism (VT) enables radical-type C–H activation, such reactivity has been exclusively realized with nickel catalysis, and copper-mediated VT remains unexplored for α-C(sp3)–H activation of carbonyls. Here, we present a dual photoredox/copper catalytic strategy that exploits copper-mediated VT to generate α-carbonyl alkyl radicals. These radicals undergo radical–radical cross-coupling with nucleophilic radicals generated by photocatalytic decarboxylation, delivering α-carbonyl alkylation products. The protocol features mild conditions and broad functional group tolerance, supporting peptide late-stage modification and gram-scale synthesis. Mechanistic studies and density functional theory (DFT) calculations validate a Cu(III)-mediated VT pathway for radical generation. This work establishes copper as a viable VT catalytic platform, expands the scope of dual photoredox/metal catalysis, and offers a versatile tool for biomolecular derivatization.

articles.title: Liquid Gallium Nanoislands on Zeolite: A Dynamic Confinement Strategy to Break the Catalytic Trade-Off in Hydrodeoxygenation
articles.abstract: Breaking the pervasive activity–selectivity–stability trade-off in catalytic hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report a bifunctional nanoisland catalyst (GaNPs-Pt/Beta) that overcomes this limitation by utilizing liquid gallium nanodroplets anchored on Beta zeolite as mobile nanoislands. These islands effectively restrict platinum single-atom migration and agglomeration. Concurrently, Brønsted acid sites provided by the zeolite sea facilitate the dehydration-etherification process. This synergy enables highly efficient transfer hydrogenation at the gallium–platinum interface, achieving selective C–O bond cleavage while preserving C═C bonds under mild conditions. Benefiting from this island-sea architecture, the GaNPs-Pt/Beta catalyst delivers high catalytic activity, achieving >99% cinnamyl alcohol conversion and 93.8% β-methylstyrene selectivity within 6 h at 160 °C, with recyclability demonstrated over nine cycles involving intercycle regeneration. This strategy is scalable to diverse α,β-unsaturated aldehyde/alcohol chemicals, demonstrating that zeolite-based liquid metal nanoislands provide a versatile platform for the sustainable synthesis of high-value chemicals.

articles.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Regiodivergent and Enantioselective Hydrosilylation of Internal Alkenes
articles.abstract: Enantioselective hydrosilylation of alkenes represents a direct and economical route to chiral organosilanes. However, achieving good regio- and enantioselectivity from the same alkene for the divergent synthesis of chiral silanes remains a formidable challenge, particularly for internal alkenes. In this work, we present a ligand-controlled nickel-catalyzed regiodivergent and enantioselective hydrosilylation of 1,2-disubstituted alkenes. This approach provides a direct access to both α- and β-trifluoromethylsilanes with high regio- and enantioselectivity. The resulting enantioenriched silane products are amenable to various stereospecific transformations. Moreover, density functional theory (DFT) calculations elucidate the origin of the observed regio- and enantioselectivity.

articles.title: Photoinduced Enantioselective α-Alkylation of Active Methines with Nonactivated Alkenes Using a Chiral Ytterbium Lewis Acid
articles.abstract: Catalytic enantioselective alkylation is a fundamental strategy for constructing molecular frameworks bearing chiral carbon centers. Herein, we report a photoinduced highly enantioselective catalytic α-alkylation of active methine compounds with nonactivated alkenes to construct chiral quaternary stereocenters. Cooperative catalysis using an organophotocatalyst and a chiral ytterbium Lewis acid bearing an Indapybox ligand efficiently promotes the alkylation of open-chain 2-substituted β-ketoesters, affording the desired products in high yields with high enantioselectivities (up to 96% yield and 96% ee). The reaction exhibits a broad substrate scope with respect to both the alkene and β-ketoesters components. Furthermore, the resulting products can be readily transformed into optically active 5-pyrazolone and 5-isoxazolone derivatives while maintaining high optical purity.

articles.title: Poly(Ionic Liquid)-Engineered Interfacial Water Reorganization for Selective Acidic CO2-to-Formic Acid Electroreduction
articles.abstract: Acidic CO2 electroreduction offers a promising route to improve carbon utilization compared with alkaline or neutral systems. However, maintaining high product selectivity at industrially relevant current densities remains challenging because local CO2 depletion and excessive proton availability intensify the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we develop a bismuth sulfide (Bi2S3) catalyst modified with a long-chain imidazolium poly(ionic liquid) layer (PIL@BS) for electrocatalytic CO2-to-formic acid conversion at pH 2. In a flow cell containing 3 M KCl, PIL@BS catalyst delivers a high Faradaic efficiency for formic acid (FEFA = 98.4%) at a current density exceeding 300 mA cm–2 and maintains over 80% FEFA after 120 h of continuous operation. Even at low 15 vol % CO2 concentration typical of industrial flue gas, PIL@BS retains higher FA selectivity than unmodified BS, underscoring the effectiveness of PIL in suppressing HER under CO2-limited conditions. Structural characterizations and electrochemical analyses reveal that the PIL backbone creates a hydrophobic interface while preserving CO2 affinity and high ionic conductivity, effectively mitigating the flooding issues and enhancing the local availability of CO2. Operando spectroscopies further show that PIL-regulated interface facilitates access to weakly hydrogen-bonded water. Such interfacial water reorganization disrupts the extended hydrogen-bond network, attenuating the continuous proton-relay pathways that promote the competing HER while maintaining localized proton transfer for CO2 reduction. Combined with theoretical calculations, these findings indicate that the PIL-modified microenvironment enables a direct and energetically favorable hydrogenation pathway toward FA formation. This work highlights the PIL-engineered interfacial microenvironment as a key factor for overriding the intrinsic selectivity of a catalyst and enabling practical CO2 valorization.

articles.title: SIFT-MS Enables Product-Specific Insight into Electrochemical Pulsed CO2 Reduction in Membrane Electrode Assemblies
articles.abstract: Pulsed electrolysis is a promising operating strategy for electrochemical CO2 reduction, but understanding how products form, accumulate, and are released during dynamic operation remains challenging, particularly in membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs). Conventional product analysis methods provide limited time resolution, making them poorly suited for resolving product-specific changes during pulses that are on the timescale of seconds. Here, selected-ion-flow-tube mass spectrometry (SIFT-MS) was used as a quasi-real-time analytical technique to measure the product concentrations during pulsed CO2 electrolysis in a MEA using a copper oxide nanoparticle-derived cathode catalyst. Methodology development for the SIFT-MS technique established the sampling and pulsing criteria required for reliable semi-quantitative analysis of the concentration of reaction products. Applying these methodology developments to pulsed electrolysis experiments unveiled how molecular structure influences product retention within the electrode and subsequent transport into the MEA outlet stream under pulsed CO2R conditions. A comparison of the measured concentrations of ethanol, ethylene, and acetaldehyde provided evidence that the formation of ethanol occurs through multiple contributing reaction pathways. The analysis of the measured concentrations of acetaldehyde, propionaldehyde, and 1-propanol provided evidence for the sequential formation of products through which the formation of aldehydes precedes the formation of 1-propanol. Overall, this work establishes SIFT-MS as a product-specific, quasi-real-time analytical technique for probing pulsed CO2R in membrane electrode assemblies that can unveil crucial information to aid in the development of future MEA electrolyzers and operational strategies.

articles.title: Spatially Decoupled Reaction-Diffusion Microenvironments in Mordenite Enable Highly Selective Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
articles.abstract: The selective oxidation of methane to value-added oxygenates represents a formidable challenge in heterogeneous catalysis, fundamentally limited by the thermodynamic trade-off between activating the reactant and preventing the subsequent overoxidation of fragile products. This vulnerability is deeply tied to the spatial accessibility within the catalytic microenvironment; highly open channels, while facilitating mass transfer, indiscriminately expose the generated products to secondary oxidation. Herein, we develop a site-selective construction strategy to establish spatially decoupled reaction-diffusion microenvironments within mordenite (MOR). By utilizing pyridine as a pore-blocking agent to occupy 12-membered ring (12-MR) channels, we preferentially localize the active Cu species, identified as bent mono-μ-oxo dicopper cores, within the well-defined 8-membered ring (8-MR) side pockets. This architecture induces a profound dual spatial effect. At the reaction level, the 8-MR acts as a nanoscopic kinetic shield by providing a customized local topology that suppresses the reactivity of oxygenated intermediates while retaining sufficient methane activation capability. Crucially, at the mass-transfer level, Cu incorporation into the 12-MR main channels is largely suppressed, allowing these channels to serve as unobstructed diffusion pathways and reducing the probability that desorbed methanol recontacts oxidative Cu sites during outward transport. Furthermore, by eliminating the structural heterogeneity inherent to non-selective synthesis, this spatially defined microenvironment and homogeneous Cu coordination structure enable the elucidation of the intrinsic structure-performance relationship. Under continuous operating conditions, this spatially engineered catalyst exhibits high methanol selectivity and productivity, ranking among the leading Cu-MOR systems for methane-to-methanol conversion. These findings demonstrate that designing a decoupled reaction-diffusion microenvironment can regulate catalytic selectivity beyond electronic-structure modulation, while also offering a generalizable method for the site-selective placement of metal ions within zeolite.

articles.title: Cesium-Triiodide-Mediated Crystallization Regulation of Pure-Iodide Wide-Bandgap Perovskites Enables Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Solar Cells Exceeding 30% Efficiency
articles.abstract: Pure-iodide wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites (∼1.68 eV) featuring eliminated photoinduced halide segregation are compelling top-cell absorbers for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells. However, their complex crystallization readily induces heterogeneous composition and structural defects, hindering performance improvements in the resulting devices. Here, we develop a cesium triiodide (CsI3)-mediated strategy to regulate intermediate-phase evolution of pure-iodide WBG perovskites. The CsI3-derived precursor chemistry reconstructs Pb-I coordination networks, suppresses premature organic-dominated intermediate nucleation, and promotes homogeneous phase conversion. The modulated crystallization pathway yields highly crystalline films with improved iodine uniformity and reduced non-radiative recombination losses. Consequently, single-junction solar cells achieve a stabilized power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 22.40%, which retains 95% of its initial efficiency after 1500 h of maximum power point tracking. More importantly, the associated perovskite-silicon solar cells deliver a stabilized PCE of 30.74% along with improved thermal stability, highlighting the great potential of pure-iodide WBG perovskites for efficient and durable tandem photovoltaics.

articles.title: Electrically Enabled Isothermal CeO2 Thermochemical Water Splitting below 900 °C
articles.abstract: Ceria-based thermochemical cycles offer a promising route to solar hydrogen, but require reduction above 1400 °C and large temperature swings. Here, building on electrically assisted CeO2 reduction, we demonstrate repeated isothermal CeO2-based water-splitting cycles at 700–900 °C and 0.5–2.0 V. Porous CeO2−YSZ bilayer pellets with different composition ratios undergo electrically assisted reduction and steam re-oxidation at the same temperature, producing O2 and H2 in separate steps without thermal cycling. The process reaches H2/O2 ratios up to 1.9, reproducible H2 productivity over 10 cycles, and H2 yields up to 49 ± 2 μmol gCeO2−1 cycle−1 after only 20 min of electrically assisted reduction. Extended-reduction experiments show that the best composition remains only ∼0.10 V below the applied bias on an equivalent thermodynamic-voltage basis. Reactor-scale projections based on gas utilization in an existing ceria reactor give a solar-to-H2 efficiency of 5.6% without assuming improvements to the CeO2−YSZ architecture.

articles.title: Rational Ionomer Design Directs Hydrogenation Pathways and Reactant Accessibility in Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction
articles.abstract: Ionomer engineering offers a powerful yet underexplored strategy for electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR), since the polymer tailors the microenvironment at the catalyst surface. Here, we rationally design high-performance ionomers by applying fixed-charge sign and hydration as design criteria. Synthetic anion-exchange ionomers (AEIs) enhance NO3– accessibility, and the highest AEI hydration is accompanied by a shift in the dominant hydrogenation pathway toward a favorable *H-mediated regime. Time-dependent attenuated total reflection surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) coupled with numerical simulation yields a 40.7-fold higher NO3– diffusion coefficient for the AEI than for Nafion. Potential-dependent in situ ATR-SEIRAS combined with kinetic isotope effect measurements and *H scavenging supports a pathway shift arising from a hydrated microenvironment enriched in free and weakly hydrogen-bonded water. The AEI-modified commercial Cu nanoparticle electrode reaches an NH3 yield rate of 13.8 mg h–1cm–2 and 98.0% Faradaic efficiency, positioning the fixed-charge sign and hydration as accessible design descriptors potentially transferable to other electrocatalytic reactions.

articles.title: Divide and Conquer Strategy Using Piezoelectric Nanofiber Scaffolds for Stage-Specific Delivery of Bone-Targeted Exosome Mimetics with Ago/AntagomiR-126
articles.abstract: Bone regeneration is a temporally regulated process requiring stage-specific biochemical cues and biomechanical stimulation; however, current scaffold-based delivery systems largely rely on passive release and fail to adapt to the dynamic healing phases. While previous PVDF-based scaffolds have focused on enhancing piezoelectric output or osteoconductive properties, they primarily function as passive materials without the dynamic regulation of therapeutic activity. Here, we present a multifunctional piezoelectric scaffold that enables mechanically triggered, temporally controlled delivery of bone-targeted exosome mimetics (EMs) loaded with AgomiR or AntagomiR-126. The scaffold features a three-dimensional piezoelectric architecture that generates electromechanical activation under physiological loading, allowing for coupling between mechanical stimulation and therapeutic release. In addition, these components are functionally integrated to coordinate phase-specific miRNA activity during the repair. Alendronate-functionalized EMs enable bone-selective localization, while AgomiR-126 promotes early angiogenesis and progenitor recruitment and AntagomiR-126 enhances late-stage osteogenic differentiation. In vivo studies demonstrated that this system significantly improved bone repair. Rather than introducing a new component, this work establishes a mechanically gated, temporally programmed miRNA delivery strategy for phase-specific bone regeneration.

articles.title: Effect of Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity in Half-Metallic La0.67Sr0.33MnO3 Thin Films
articles.abstract: Magnetism induced by the proximity effects of chiral molecules is a physical phenomenon that can be demonstrated with molecular layers as thin as 1 nm deposited on thin films of conventional ferromagnets. Although the chiral-induced spin selectivity effect has been widely explored in the context of spintronic applications involving charge transport through chiral molecules, due to its capacity to generate high spin polarizations at room temperature, the accompanying process of induced magnetization without applied current likewise presents opportunities for exploitation. In this work, we demonstrate that, unlike conventional ferromagnets, where the induced magnetization aligns with the chiral axis of the polymer, the CISS effect in half-metallic ferromagnets (La0.67Sr0.33MnO3) favors a quasi-perpendicular magnetization configuration. This preference for quasi-perpendicular magnetization is caused by the formation of a thermally driven steady state, which, due to different transport probabilities into the molecule, results in a modification of the domain-wall energy landscape. These results provide insight into the chiral-induced spin selectivity effect without net currents and also clarify mechanism for controlling magnetization within half-metallic thin films for spintronic devices.

articles.title: Electric-Field Tunable Spin Texture in Dual-Gated HfS2/Graphene van der Waals Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Spin–charge interconversion provides the essential link between spin information and electrical signals in spintronic devices. In spin–orbit coupled systems, spin–charge interconversion can contain multiple components associated with different spin-polarization directions, reflecting the underlying spin texture. Tuning this spin texture, therefore, provides a way to control not only the magnitude of spin–charge interconversion but also the balance among its different components. Graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures provide an attractive platform for this purpose because interfacial spin–orbit coupling can host multiple spin–charge interconversion channels that couple to different spin-polarization directions. Here, we demonstrate electric-field control of spin texture in a dual-gated HfS2/graphene van der Waals heterostructure, where independent control of carrier density and vertical electric field allows us to disentangle electrostatic doping from electric field-induced spin–orbit effects. Nonlocal spin precession measurements show that, near zero vertical electric field, spin–charge interconversion is dominated by a spin Hall component with out-of-plane spins. Increasing the vertical electric field enhances additional in-plane spin components with Rashba–Edelstein-like character, including contributions both parallel and perpendicular to the charge current. These results provide experimental evidence that a vertical electric field can reconfigure the effective spin texture and control the corresponding spin–charge interconversion components, demonstrating electrical tunability of spin–orbit functionalities.

articles.title: Enhanced Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect in Nano-Magnetic Metamaterials with Near-Perfect Coherent Absorption
articles.abstract: The ability to control magnetic systems without external magnetic fields has attracted attention recently, with all-optical magnetic switching showing increasing promise. Gaining fine control over light-matter interactions in magnetic nanostructures is essential for advancing opto-magnetic technologies but remains challenging because strong optical coupling must be achieved within ultrathin magnetic structures at the target wavelength. Here, we show that coherent optical interference can increase this interaction in patterned magnetic metasurfaces. Arrays of permalloy nanomagnets are placed on a thin dielectric spacer above a reflective back-plane, forming a magnetic metasurface whose reflected wavefront is defined by the nanomagnet geometry, fill factor, and spacer thickness. Destructive interference between the metasurface and back-plane reflections yields near-perfect absorption, exceeding 95% for circular nanomagnet arrays in both simulation and experiment. The absorbed power is dissipated almost entirely within the nanomagnets, with only a few percent lost in the metallic back-plane. Enhanced absorption is also accompanied by a stronger magneto-optical Kerr effect, driven by both increased light–nanomagnet interaction and reduced reflected background. These results provide a general approach for achieving high optical absorption and strong magneto-optical response in nanoscale magnetic systems, supporting advances in optically addressable spintronics, magnetic sensing, and all-optical magnetic control.

articles.title: Gas Separation through Graphene Nanopores Enabled by Thermally Robust Porous Organic Polymer Reinforcement
articles.abstract: Porous single-layer graphene (PG) offers an ideal platform for molecular-sieving membranes due to its atomically thin inorganic lattice and its ability to incorporate molecularly selective pores. However, the use of PG for high-temperature gas separation remains limited by the lack of a mechanically reinforcing film (MRF) that enables crack-free transfer onto porous supports and stable operation under pressurization. Here, we introduce a fluorinated porous organic polymer (FPOP) that provides the mechanical and thermal robustness needed to operate PG membranes at high temperature. The FPOP layer is deposited directly on PG from a molecular precursor solution. Upon drying and thermal annealing, it develops into a continuous cross-linked film that conforms to PG, maintains strong adhesion, and helps to avoid crack formation during the transfer of PG to a macroporous support. The FPOP film exhibits a quasi-ordered structure, forms an interface with graphene, and remains stable under pressurized conditions up to 350 °C. FPOP-supported PG membranes exhibit selective gas transport at elevated temperature (350 °C) and maintain their performance during extended mixed-gas operation. The membranes retain selective transport after humid/oxidative exposure and ambient storage. Importantly, the porous FPOP can regulate transport through enlarged nonselective graphene defects, thereby improving the selectivity of PG membranes. Overall, we demonstrate FPOP as a thermally stable MRF platform that enables crack-free PG transfer, high-temperature operation, and regulation of nonselective transport pathways.

articles.title: High-Throughput In-Operando Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy of Chemical Vapor Deposited Graphene for pH Sensing
articles.abstract: Reliable pH sensing in liquid environments underpins applications in energy storage, biosensing, and process monitoring, yet conventional graphene-based electrical devices introduce ohmic contacts, encapsulation layers, and electrochemical artifacts that can obscure intrinsic behavior. These approaches also fail to capture the strong spatial variability of commercial CVD graphene. Here, we present a fully contactless methodology for quantifying pH-dependent conductivity of large-area CVD graphene using through-substrate reflection terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS). A customized liquid cell with a THz transparent window preserves unrestricted access to the graphene–electrolyte interface while enabling centimeter-scale conductivity mapping and in-operando single-point monitoring during sequential pH modulation. By integrating spatially registered Raman mapping with automated quality-metric filtering, we extract statistically robust trends across thousands of pixels rather than isolated device regions. We show that pristine monolayer graphene exhibits the highest baseline conductivity and strongest pH sensitivity, whereas O2-plasma-introduced defects systematically suppress both. This scalable, remote, and inert probing approach establishes THz-TDS as a powerful platform for high-throughput characterization and robust liquid-phase sensing in thin films and 2D systems.

articles.title: Nano-Bioadhesives for Gastrointestinal Hemostasis and Healing: Integrating Artificial Intelligence for Precision Design and Application
articles.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding and mucosal injury remain clinically challenging because most bioadhesives lose performance under acidic, enzymatic, and peristaltic conditions. Nanotechnology has advanced adhesive design by enhancing mechanical integrity, degradation control, and antimicrobial activity; however, translating these gains into consistently favorable clinical outcomes is still difficult. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a route to accelerate and derisk development. Here, we identify predictive, multiobjective materials design as the AI domain most critical for GI nanobioadhesives because adhesion, hemostasis, degradation, biosafety, and healing must be optimized simultaneously. Predictive modeling, molecular simulations, and high-throughput experimentation enable rational control of adhesion strength, degradation kinetics, and biocompatibility, while machine-learning models expedite the discovery of optimal polymeric nanoparticle formulations. Emerging strategies such as digital twins and closed-loop optimization further support patient-specific and adaptive adhesive systems. By integrating AI-guided design with nanotechnology platforms, next-generation GI bioadhesives could unify rapid hemostasis, antimicrobial protection, and regenerative functions, thereby improving reliability and clinical translation. This review outlines the synergy between AI and nanotechnology and highlights priorities for advancing GI adhesive therapies from bench to bedside.

articles.title: Noise-Suppressed High-Performance WSe2 Phototransistors Enabled by Optically Programmed Remote Contact Doping
articles.abstract: Improving the sensitivity of two-dimensional semiconductor phototransistors requires increasing photocurrent while minimizing noise. However, conventional doping approaches often place charged dopants in or near atomically thin channels, introducing charge scattering, trap states, and noise that limit the signal-to-noise ratio. Here, we address this signal-noise trade-off in WSe2 phototransistors by using photoinduced charge trapping in patterned hBN to implement contact-selective remote doping. Under illumination with a negative gate voltage, trapped holes in hBN electrostatically n-dope WSe2 while remaining spatially separated from the transport channel. Patterned hBN confines the doping to selected regions, allowing the WSe2 near the metal electrodes to be remotely doped while leaving the channel undoped. This remote contact doping simultaneously suppressed the device noise by approximately 100–fold, reduced the effective density of electrically active traps by approximately 100–fold, and lowered the activation energy by 30–80 meV, indicating improved contact quality and more efficient carrier injection. As a result, the contact-doped phototransistors simultaneously exhibit enhanced responsivity of 99.7 A/W and a specific detectivity of 2.26 × 1011 Jones. These results establish optically programmed remote contact doping as a phototransistor-compatible contact-engineering approach to overcome the signal–noise trade-off in 2D phototransistors.

articles.title: Zooming into the Cytoskeleton: Nanodefect-Initiated Microtubule Catastrophe Filmed by High-Speed Atomic Force Microscopy
articles.abstract: Microtubule catastrophe is widely attributed to an end-driven loss of the GTP cap, implying that structural failure is confined to filament termini. Here, we show that this view is incomplete. Using high-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM), we directly visualize nanoscale structural failure in paclitaxel-treated microtubules in real time. We identify spontaneous lattice nanodefects that emerge within the filament shaft and act as internal initiation sites for disassembly. These defects arise from localized protofilament decoupling and lattice strain accumulation, which disrupt the cooperative interactions within the microtubule wall. Once a critical threshold is reached, these sites nucleate disassembly that propagates as distinct collapse trajectories, including bidirectional spreading from intralattice defects and inward convergence from opposing ends, in addition to classical end-initiated depolymerization. Rather than uniformly stabilizing the lattice, paclitaxel maintains microtubules in a metastable state in which internal stress heterogeneity persists and enables defect-driven failure. Our results establish lattice decoupling as a primary structural trigger of microtubule catastrophe and redefine it as a defect-mediated, spatially encoded transition. These findings provide a nanoscale mechanistic framework for understanding heterogeneous responses to microtubule-targeting chemotherapeutics, suggesting that drug resistance may arise from modulation of lattice integrity and defect propagation rather than drug binding alone.

articles.title: Chloride-mediated protective bilayer film on magnesium
Intragranular discontinuous precipitation enables exceptional strength and ductility in an additively manufactured high-entropy alloy
Synergistic enhancement of high-temperature strength and uniform plasticity in a Ti-rich refractory high-entropy alloy via strain-rate-modulated dislocation-B2 interactions
Tellurium trioxide as an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with ultrahigh work functions from first principles
A Paradigm Shift Toward Quasi‐Thermodynamically Stable Bulk Heterojunction Morphology Enabled by Controlled Crystallization Kinetics of High Quadrupole Moment Nonfullerene Acceptors
articles.abstract: Recent advances in high quadrupole moment (Q̂$\hat{Q}$) non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) have improved exciton diffusion and charge separation in organic photovoltaics (OPVs). However, conventional bulk heterojunctions (BHJs) with a balanced donor‐to‐acceptor ratio often exhibit amorphous mixed domains, introducing energetic disorder and limiting the optoelectronic potential and stability of high‐Q̂$\hat{Q}$ NFAs. Here, a diffusion‐driven 3D crystallization strategy is demonstrated using an NFA‐rich BHJ model (Non‐fullerene Matrix‐BHJ, NM‐BHJ) that suppresses electron trap states and charge localization, thereby reducing energy losses driven by static disorder. Notably, the laterally oriented 3D superstructures significantly enhance thermodynamic stability and improve resistance to morphological changes under thermal stress. OPVs incorporating the optimized NM‐BHJ retain 88.2% of their initial efficiency after 720 h at 65 °C and over 99% after 2400 h at room‐temperature. The obtained T90 of 644 h is, to the best of our knowledge, one of the longest experimentally verified lifetimes reported among Y‐series‐based BHJ systems in the literature, including those employing chemically modified oligomeric derivatives. Combined with its generality across different NFA systems, this study suggests that the NM‐BHJ strategy opens a new era for highly efficient and thermally robust OPV devices by morphologically overcoming the inherent thermal limitations of high‐Q̂$\hat{Q}$ NFAs.

articles.title: Advanced Energy Materials at 15: Advancing the Energy Transition From Fundamental Insights to Practical Technologies
articles.abstract: This Special Issue commemorates the fifteenth anniversary of Advanced Energy Materials and reflects the evolution of energy materials research from fundamental discovery toward practical technologies. Assembled in conjunction with the 2025 Wiley Forum Spring Meeting, the collection brings together 28 Research Articles and 10 Reviews spanning photovoltaics and optoelectronics, electrochemical energy storage and conversion, flexible and distributed energy technologies, and data‐driven materials discovery. Collectively, these contributions demonstrate how advances in materials chemistry, defect and interface control, multiscale characterization, scalable manufacturing, and predictive computation are enabling more efficient, stable, and deployable energy systems. The breadth of the collection underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and of evaluating innovations under realistic technological constraints. The Special Issue is dedicated to the memory of Professor Taiho Park, whose scientific vision, leadership, and service left a lasting legacy in the field. Sincere appreciation is extended to all contributing authors, reviewers, and the editorial team whose efforts made this anniversary collection possible.

articles.title: Alcohol‐Adduct Mediated Precursor Stabilization Strategies for Conformal SnO2 Layers in Highly Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Modules
articles.abstract: Perovskite solar modules (PSMs) attract significant attention for their superior optoelectronic properties, but significant cell‐to‐module (CTM) losses remain a critical issue to be addressed. Among the various factors, the primary reason for CTM losses is the incomplete, non‐conformal coverage of the electron transport layer (ETL) over large‐area, P1‐scribed transparent conductive oxide (TCO) substrates. In this work, we report an alcohol‐adduct mediated precursor stabilization strategy to achieve high‐quality, uniform SnO2 layers via controlled hydrolysis reaction kinetics. We employ a tin isopropoxide isopropanol (TIPI) adduct, which effectively modulates the electrophilicity and stabilizes the Sn center atom, followed by a sequential deposition of SnO2 nanoparticles. This double‐layer (DL) architecture exhibits superior optical properties, improved electron transport, and conformal coverage over large areas. As a result, PSMs fabricated with the TIPI (DL) SnO2 ETL exhibit a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.6% (reverse/forward average), with a certified PCE of 19.7% (aperture area = 213 cm2). In addition, the PSMs with TIPI (DL) SnO2 ETL demonstrated a wide processing window, maintaining a PCE over 20% regardless of variations in concentration or deposition speed, highlighting potential for in‐line commercialization. Furthermore, the modules exhibited good long‐term stability under damp‐heat and in outdoor field tests.

articles.title: Amorphous π‐Conjugated Passivator Facilitates Widening Process Window for Reliable Perovskite Solar Modules
articles.abstract: Although halide perovskite solar cells have achieved remarkable efficiencies close to their theoretical limits, durability against external factors and reproducible processing remain major barriers to commercialization. Conventional ammonium halide‐based surface passivation strategies enable effective defect passivation and charge selectivity via 2D/3D heterostructure formation, but their metastability and strong sensitivity to processing conditions limit long‐term stability and process window. In this work, we report an amorphous π‐conjugated passivator, (4‐(3‐iodo‐9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)butyl)phosphonic acid (I–4PACz). The asymmetric iodine substituent enhances the molecular dipole moment while simultaneously altering intermolecular interactions, thereby suppressing ordered molecular packing and enabling the formation of a uniform interfacial layer. The characteristics of I‐4PACz result in efficient charge extraction as well as widening process window. Perovskite solar modules applied to I‐4PACz as passivator between the perovskite and hole transport‐layer show a power conversion efficiency of 21.2% with 24.5 cm2 aperture size, and excellent long‐term stability retaining 85% of the initial efficiency for 884 h under 65°C and 40% relative humidity, and 98.7% of the initial efficiency for 525 h under continous illumination, respectively. Moreover, the minial dependence on blade‐coating speed also reinforces the suitability of this interfacial control strategy for inline and large‐area manufacturing.

articles.title: Amorphous π‐Conjugated Passivator Facilitates Widening Process Window for Reliable Perovskite Solar Modules (Adv. Energy Mater. 39/2026)
articles.abstract: Perovskite Solar Modules In article number e06809, Jaemin Lee, Nam Joong Jeon, Eui Hyuk Jung, and co‐workers demonstrate that an amorphous p‐conjugated passivator enhances performance and improves durability in perovskite solar modules. Treatment of the perovskite surface with the passivator renders a broader processing window to fabricate scalable perovskite solar modules due to diminishing thickness sensitivity.

articles.title: Anisotropic Strain‐Induced Centrosymmetry Breaking in Cubic Formamidinium Lead Iodide (α‐FAPbI3) Thin Films
articles.abstract: Organic–inorganic halide perovskites have emerged as promising materials for next‐generation optoelectronic devices due to their exceptional photophysical properties. Among them, α‐formamidinium lead tri‐iodide (α‐FAPbI3) with a cubic symmetry (space group of Pm3¯m$Pm\bar{3}m$) has garnered attention as a potential absorber in solar cells for its narrow bandgap and superior stability. The fundamental mechanisms governing its high performance have yet to be fully elucidated. In this study, we demonstrate that centrosymmetry breaking in [001] preferentially oriented α‐FAPbI3 thin films (POF) arises from inevitable anisotropic strain during film formation. Using circular polarization‐dependent pump‐probe transient absorption spectroscopy, we observe Rashba‐type band splitting exclusively in POF, indicating symmetry breaking. Angle‐dependent X‐ray diffraction and photoluminescence (PL) reveal significant residual stress in POF compared to randomly oriented films (ROF), confirming strain‐induced lattice distortion. Furthermore, time‐resolved PL and microwave conductivity measurements reveal top‐back inhomogeneous carrier dynamics and anisotropic charge carrier mobility, supporting the presence of the anisotropic strain‐induced symmetry breaking. Our findings provide direct experimental evidence that inevitable strain in POF induces static Rashba effects, offering new insights into strain engineering for high‐performance perovskite optoelectronics and potential quantum applications.

articles.title: Decoupling Chemical and Mechanical Contributions to Capacity Fading in Ni‐Rich Cathodes for Sulfide‐Based All‐Solid‐State Batteries
articles.abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) promise safer energy storage and the potential to outperform current lithium-ion batteries. Ni-rich cathodes deliver high energy density, whereas sulfide solid electrolytes offer exceptional Li+ conductivity and inherent mechanical compliance, making their combination particularly attractive. Yet their capacity fades rapidly because (electro)chemical and mechanical degradation occur concurrently within the cathode. Here, we propose an approach to decouple these two factors in LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2|Li6PS5Cl0.5Br0.5|Li metal cells by monitoring the state-of-charge window. Uncoated cathodes experience capacity fading primarily due to (electro)chemical degradation: interfacial reactions form resistive interphases consisting of NiO-like rock salt, SO x , PO x , and related species that hinder Li+ extraction, resulting in pronounced charge fading. A conformal LiNbO3 coating on the cathode surface suppresses interfacial reactions, significantly mitigating charge fading but revealing dominant discharge fading arising from mechanical degradation, such as particle cracking and interfacial delamination. While the protective coating stabilizes the interface and improves initial performance, the increased capacity intensifies electrode volume changes, underscoring the need for integrated electro-chemo-mechanical design strategies. Evaluating charge and discharge fading outlines the interplay between (electro)chemical and mechanical degradation and offers a new diagnostic framework to guide the development of more durable, high-energy-density ASSBs.

articles.title: Decoupling Framework and Composition Engineering via Sequential Selenium Source Switching for Efficient Sb2(S,Se)3 Thin Film Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Antimony selenosulfide (Sb2(S,Se)3) has recently attracted intense interest as an earth‐abundant, non‐toxic, and bandgap‐tunable photovoltaic absorber. However, conventional one‐step deposition routes typically produce films with inadequate crystallinity and inhomogeneous elemental distribution through the film thickness, which severely hamper charge transport and limit device performance. Herein, we introduce an innovative selenium‐source switching driven two‐step sequential deposition (SDE) strategy that decouples framework formation from compositional engineering to overcome these limitations. First, a selenourea‐based precursor is used to deposit a thick Sb2(S,Se)3 film serving as a primary light‐harvesting scaffold. Then, a sodium selenosulfate‐based precursor solution is applied for secondary deposition. Owing to the high reactivity of this solution system, selenium species readily penetrate into the as‐deposited film, inducing extensive ion diffusion and recrystallization throughout the bulk Sb2(S,Se)3 material. This SDE strategy simultaneously optimizes the vertical Se/S grading, tailors the bandgap profile, and eliminates bulk deep‐level traps and surface recombination centers. Consequently, the SDE‐Sb2(S,Se)3 device achieves a remarkable efficiency of 10.90%, placing it among the highest efficiencies for this material system. This strategy not only resolves the intrinsic bottlenecks of one‐step techniques but also provides a generalizable route for synthesizing high‐quality multicomponent chalcogenide films and offers new insights into ion‐exchange kinetics during sequential deposition.

articles.title: Degradation Pathways of Silicon‐Based Anodes in Lithium‐Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: Silicon offers high theoretical capacity as an alternative to graphite, yet it undergoes much more severe degradation, resulting in substantially poorer cycle and calendar life. In this context, a mechanistic understanding of degradation pathways is essential for designing silicon‐based anodes with performance comparable to graphite. In this review, we present a comprehensive overview of the degradation mechanisms governing silicon‐based anodes. The mechanisms are organized around active materials degradation at the particle level, which is governed by both intrinsic factors of silicon and extrinsic factors. At the electrode scale, we discuss electrode integrity loss, which arises from the breakdown of mechanical and electrical continuity. In addition, we differentiate solid electrolyte interphase instability into mechanical and chemical degradation mechanisms to clarify how each contributes to performance decay. We further describe lithium trapping as an additional source of irreversible capacity loss. Finally, we address crosstalk degradation that arises when silicon is used together with graphite, driven by mechanical and thermodynamic interactions between the two materials. This review provides an integrated understanding of the degradation pathways of silicon‐based anodes, offering insights that can guide material design and improve the performance of lithium‐ion batteries.

articles.title: Designing Weakly Solvating Electrolytes for Low‐Temperature Lithium Batteries
articles.abstract: The reliable operation of lithium‐based batteries (LBBs) under subzero conditions remains a fundamental challenge due to sluggish ion transport, increased interfacial impedance, and unstable solid–electrolyte interphases (SEIs). Popular high‐ and localized high‐concentration electrolytes partially alleviate these issues but still suffer from excessive viscosity and strong Li+‐solvent binding that hinder low‐temperature kinetics. Weakly solvating electrolytes (WSEs) offer a new paradigm by weakening Li+ coordination, promoting anion‐dominated solvation, and accelerating desolvation and interfacial charge transfer. This review provides a comprehensive review of WSEs, focusing on working mechanisms, structural design strategies, and interfacial chemistries. We also address molecular‐level solvation insights with electrolyte engineering to discuss how WSEs promote uniform lithium deposition, inorganic‐rich SEIs, and stable cycling at subzero temperatures. Finally, the review highlights future research directions—from quantitative solvation–performance correlations and data‐driven electrolyte design to interfacial diagnostics and scalability. By integrating molecular‐level understanding with predictive modeling and engineering validation, WSEs offer a transformative route toward all‐climate rechargeable batteries capable of stable and efficient operation from arctic to desert environments.

articles.title: Dry‑Contact Trimming for All‑Perovskite Tandem Solar Cells via Solid‑Solution Homogenization
articles.abstract: All‐perovskite tandem solar cells leverage the solid‐solution nature of metal halide perovskites to tune the band gaps of wide‐ and narrow‐bandgap subcells for current matching and high photovoltage. Sn–Pb mixed perovskites with band gaps of approximately 1.2–1.3 eV are attractive bottom absorbers, but Sn‐rich surface regions, depth‐dependent compositional inhomogeneity, and associated band‐alignment issues limit both photocurrent and photovoltage. Here, we introduce a layered‐perovskite‐assisted dry‐contact trimming (LDT) strategy to reconfigure Sn–Pb narrow‐bandgap perovskites after film formation. A Dion–Jacobson‐phase ethylenediammonium lead iodide (EDAPbI4) film is brought into transient solid‐state contact with the Sn–Pb perovskite and then removed after contact annealing. EDAPbI4 functions as a temporary solid‐state contact partner that removes Sn‐rich surface species and reduces depth‐dependent lattice and compositional inhomogeneity without forming a retained 2D capping layer. This reconfiguration alleviates reverse band bending at the Sn–Pb perovskite/transport‐layer interface, suppresses nonradiative interfacial recombination, and reduces open‐circuit‐voltage losses. The improved lattice/compositional uniformity also enables thick Sn–Pb absorbers to maintain efficient charge collection and high short‐circuit current density. Consequently, single‐junction Sn–Pb devices exceed 24% efficiency, and monolithic all‐perovskite tandem devices surpass 30% with reproducible performance and operational stability. These results identify LDT as a complementary post‐crystallization strategy for engineering mixed perovskite solid‐solutions and their interfaces.

articles.title: Dual Impact of Long‐Lived Localized Carriers Induced by Restricted Hole Transfer in Organic Photovoltaics and Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Organic semiconductors are key photoactive materials for solar energy conversion, including organic photovoltaics (OPVs) and photocatalytic hydrogen evolution. Here, we uncover a paradox: materials optimized for efficient charge extraction in OPVs exhibit different behavior when used as photocatalysts in aqueous colloids. To probe this contrast, we study nanoparticles (NPs) prepared from PM6:Y6 and its structural analogue D18:Y5, comparing their photophysical responses across photovoltaic and photocatalytic regimes. We observe an inverse relationship between power conversion efficiency in thin films and hydrogen evolution activity in dispersions. Y5‐based NPs show stronger aggregation, longer exciton lifetimes, and slower hole transfer, indicative of localized charges that promote interfacial redox chemistry. Density functional theory calculations reveal that Y5 possesses more negative electrostatic potential, facilitating charge localization favorable for hydrogen evolution. D18 also exhibits higher photoluminescence quantum yield and reduced non‐radiative recombination relative to PM6. Molecular dynamics simulations show that D18 forms stronger donor–acceptor interactions, stabilizing localized charges for proton reduction, whereas Y6 displays more higher acceptor–acceptor coordination, enabling efficient charge extraction in blends. Collectively, these findings establish the pivotal role of long‐lived, localized carriers in governing the charge dynamics of organic semiconductors and offer design principles for reconciling their dual photovoltaic and photocatalytic functionalities.
