articles.title: A Microporous Zr-Tetraphosphonate MOF with Permanent Porosity, Robustness, and Thermochemical Heat Storage Capability
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Combining high-valent metal cations with phosphonate linkers represents a promising strategy to address the limited stability of MOFs, yet permanently porous phosphonate MOFs (P-MOFs) remain rare due to the strong coordination propensity of phosphonate groups. Herein, we report IEF-10, a new microporous zirconium tetraphosphonate framework constructed from ZrO5F octahedral secondary building units and a pyrene tetraphosphonate linker. The material combines three features that are seldom achieved simultaneously in P-MOFs: permanent accessible microporosity (equivalent BET surface area ∼430 m2·g–1), accessible phosphonic acid functionalities (-PO3H), and exceptional thermal (up to 450 °C), mechanical (>3 tons), and chemical stability (pH 1–12, organic solvents). The structure exhibits reversible water adsorption with moderate uptake and experimentally determined capacities of heat storage of ∼400–500 J·g–1, reflecting a favorable balance between host–guest interactions and regeneration requirements. As a proof of concept, IEF-10 was evaluated for thermochemical heat storage under dynamic moist-gas flow conditions. Calorimetric measurements revealed fast heat-release kinetics (3–4 h), and excellent cyclability in terms of heat release (at least 10 cycles, total test duration of 5 weeks). The hydrophobic surface character is an advantage for long-term storage uses as the adsorbent can remain in a dry state between the charging and discharging stages even at low relative humidity levels in the reactor. These results demonstrate how the combination of permanent porosity, accessible phosphonic acid groups, and exceptional framework robustness can enable functional adsorption-driven energy storage while providing new opportunities for the development of porous zirconium P-MOFs.

articles.title: A Pseudo-Icosahedral RhH2Au10 Superatom: Two Hydrogen Atoms Acting as Gold-Atom Equivalents and Modifiers
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: A hydrogen atom is known to act as a gold-atom-equivalent dopant in gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) by contributing to the valence electron count. To gain insights into the interaction of multiple H atoms with AuNCs, we herein synthesized a di-H-atom-doped NC, [RhH2Au10(dppp)5]3+ (RhH2Au10; dppp = 1,3-bis(diphenylphosphino)propane), by exposing [RhAu10(dppp)5]3+ (RhAu10) to H2 gas; RhAu10 was generated in situ via hydride (H–) abstraction from [RhHAu10(dppp)5]2+. Comprehensive characterization of RhH2Au10 by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations revealed that the two H atoms occupy the two “missing” Au sites in the arachno-type RhAu10 core via dissociative adsorption of H2, forming a pseudo-icosahedral RhH2Au10 core. This core structure contrasts sharply with the previously reported di-H-atom-doped silver- or copper-based superatoms, in which the H atoms form an MH2 (M = Os, Ru, Rh) unit completely encapsulated within an icosahedral Ag12 or Cu12 shell. The RhH2Au10 core possesses an 8-electron closed-shell electronic configuration of (1S)2(1P)6, which is isoelectronic to the icosahedral RhAu12 superatom, thereby demonstrating the Au-atom equivalence of H atoms. Nevertheless, the two H atoms in the RhH2Au10 superatomic core act as structural modifiers compared to the RhAu12 superatom: (1) the degeneracy of the 1P orbitals is lifted by lowering the geometric symmetry, and (2) the HOMO–LUMO energy gap is expanded due to the reduced electronic confinement volume. This study demonstrates that multiple H atoms in a gold-based superatomic core not only behave as Au-atom equivalents but also serve as key components for modulating their fundamental properties.

articles.title: Boosting Ionomer Oxygen Transport via Pore Confinement in Carbon Supports for Low-Pt Fuel Cells
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Low-Pt proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are promising for hydrogen energy implementation, yet oxygen transport through ionomer-covered catalyst surfaces becomes increasingly limiting due to the resistance associated with dense ionomer films. Herein, we demonstrate a pore-confinement strategy to manipulate the spatial locality of Pt nanoparticles within porous carbon supports, enabling simultaneous regulation of ionomer distribution and molecular organization. Pt nanoparticles were selectively positioned on the external surfaces (Ptext/PC) or within the internal nanopores (Ptint/PC) of otherwise comparable supports, while maintaining similar Pt loading, particle size, and pore characteristics. Under H2-air condition, Ptint/PC delivered a peak power density ∼1.3 times higher than that of Ptext/PC, but a similar current density in the high-voltage region. Electrochemical analyses reveal that the performance enhancement originates from improved oxygen transport rather than catalytic activity. Wide-angle X-ray scattering and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the Pt nanoparticles confined within mesopores disrupt the dense packing of ionomer backbones, thereby boosting oxygen permeability at the catalyst–ionomer interface. By establishing a direct relationship between Pt locality, ionomer distribution, backbone organization, and oxygen transport, this work identifies catalyst locality as an effective parameter for engineering interfacial mass transport and provides a new design principle for low-Pt PEMFCs.

articles.title: Core–Shell Structures Govern Through-Space Interactions in Triblock Copolymers toward Deep-Red Clusteroluminescence
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Green fluorescent protein (GFP) and its derivatives have transformed biological imaging, yet fluorophores that simultaneously combine biocompatibility, structural programmability, and intrinsic long-wavelength luminescence remain scarce. Here, we develop a controllable one-pot polymerization strategy to construct nonconjugated triblock copolymers that can self-assemble into core–shell clusters. By modulating the hydrophilic–hydrophobic balance of copolymer chains, the core-to-shell ratio, chain packing, and electronic through-space interactions within the clusters can be precisely regulated, enabling tunable clusteroluminescence (CL) that extends to the deep-red and near-infrared emission region. Ultrafast spectroscopy further uncovers the excited-state dynamics of these core–shell clusters and reveals how the coupled evolution of electronic states and structures governs CL generation. Moreover, the core–shell clusters enable in vivo angiography under two-photon excitation, highlighting their potential as biocompatible nanofluorophores. These findings establish core–shell engineering as a general design principle for efficient clusteroluminogens, deepen the mechanistic understanding of CL, and pave the way for next-generation nanofluorescence technologies.

articles.title: Crossover from Asymmetric to Symmetric Electrowetting Linked to Double-Layer Restructuring
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Voltage-controlled wetting at solid–liquid interfaces is central to the performance of a range of electrochemical and microfluidic technologies, yet the molecular basis of polarity-dependent electrowetting remains unresolved. Classical electrocapillarity predicts a symmetric dependence of contact angle on applied potential, but experiments and simulations frequently exhibit pronounced asymmetry. Here, combining electrowetting measurements with atomistic simulations, we show that asymmetric wetting at aqueous carbon interfaces arises from the structure of the electrical double layer. By investigating aqueous KF and LiCl electrolytes at graphitic interfaces across lower concentration and water-in-salt regimes, we identify a crossover from strongly asymmetric electrowetting at lower concentration to a symmetric response at high concentration for KF, while LiCl retains a pronounced asymmetry. This transition is accompanied by corresponding changes in the solid–liquid interfacial tension, demonstrating that polarity-dependent wetting can arise from voltage-dependent molecular restructuring of the interfacial liquid, which modifies the interfacial thermodynamics, without invoking faradaic processes. We introduce interfacial connectivity, defined by the network of intermolecular interactions within the first adsorption layer, as a molecular descriptor linking double-layer structure to macroscopic wetting behavior. These results demonstrate that electrolyte-controlled electrowetting can recover the symmetric electrocapillary limit under appropriate conditions and establish a unified framework connecting double-layer structure, interfacial free energy, and voltage-dependent wetting.

articles.title: Decoupling Dissolution from Water Oxidation at Single-Faceted High-Entropy Perovskite Electrodes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: High-entropy oxides (HEOs) are promising anode materials for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) due to their wide compositional space and electronic flexibility. However, their electrochemical dissolution and OER remain concurrent, preventing decoupled analysis of dissolution kinetics and stability. Here, we present a combined atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) strategy to decouple lattice dissolution from water oxidation under well-defined reaction conditions. Structurally analogous, atomically flat, single-faceted (001) ABO3 perovskite electrodes, La1–xSrx(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2)O3 with x = 0 and 0.3, serve as model systems to probe dissolution and OER kinetics in acid. Pipet-probed localized cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry reveal that the measured current contains contributions from both OER and lattice dissolution, the latter producing nanoscale dissolution pits beneath the SECCM droplet. By correlating pit-growth kinetics with total OER charge as a function of pulse duration (τ), overpotential (η), and pH, we quantitatively separate dissolution from OER. The proportional scaling between dissolution charge and total charge indicates that OER and dissolution proceed within a common kinetic regime, sharing a common intermediate. A rate-law-based analysis yields the standard dissolution rate constant (kd0 cm/s), transfer coefficient (α), and proton reaction order (b) for the dissolution of the 001 facet of both HEO-P. Our results unravel how aliovalent A-site substitution (30% Sr2+) alters dissolution kinetics, charge partitioning between dissolution and OER, and thickness-dependent stability, thereby enabling quantitative disentangling of the intrinsic activity and stability of HEO electrodes.

articles.title: Efficient Chemical Synthesis and Enzymatic Replication of 3′-Deoxyapionucleic Acid (ApioNA): An RNA-Selective XNA with Conformational Flexibility
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Xeno-nucleic acids (XNAs) have emerged as versatile platforms due to their sugar scaffolds that enable precise chemical tuning, leading to distinct classes ranging from fully compatible systems to orthogonal systems. However, sugar-modified XNAs capable of discriminating between RNA and DNA have remained elusive. In this work, we establish 3′-deoxyapionucleic acid (ApioNA) as a structurally flexible XNA with inherent RNA-selective hybridization properties. We achieved efficient production of ApioNA oligonucleotides through an efficient asymmetric synthesis of their building blocks and systematically characterized their properties. Thermal melting analyses demonstrate that ApioNA forms moderately stable duplexes with RNA while exhibiting weak pairing with DNA and negligible self-association. Quantum mechanical calculations reveal that the apiofuranose ring populates two low-energy puckering states, and the addition of an extra methylene group enhances backbone flexibility, thereby favoring A-form geometry for RNA pairing while requiring a higher-energy state to accommodate B-form DNA. Despite its weak affinity for DNA, ApioNA supports a complete enzymatic replication cycle using commercial Therminator and Bst 3.0 polymerases with approximately 98% fidelity and is processed by native E. coli machinery in vivo. This work fills the RNA-selective niche in the XNA functional landscape and establishes sugar puckering dynamics and backbone flexibility as key design principles for programming nucleic acid pairing specificity.

articles.title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Slaked Lime Utilizing a Diaphragm Flow Cell
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Slaked lime (Ca(OH)2) is one of the most widely utilized chemicals, with applications in diverse industries including construction, mining, water treatment, and chemical manufacturing. Currently, Ca(OH)2 is synthesized by coal-fired calcination of CaCO3 to make CaO, followed by exothermic hydration. Converting CaCO3 into Ca(OH)2 using electrochemically generated acid and base has attracted great interest because it could be powered by renewable electricity and would generate the CO2 byproduct in a pure form. Previous electrochemical Ca(OH)2 syntheses have incorporated the processing of calcium salts within the electrochemical cell to avoid acid–base recombination losses, but these cells have poor stability and high energy demand. Herein, we show that production of high-salinity acid and base solutions using a diaphragm flow cell (DFC) coupled with ex situ processing of CaCO3 substantially improves the efficiency of electrochemical Ca(OH)2 production. Using a closed loop with a simple KCl salt solution, we demonstrate the synthesis of >99% pure Ca(OH)2 for 0.088 to 0.10 kWh per mole at productive current densities of 158 to 334 mA cm–2.

articles.title: Energy Deposition Timescale Controls Chemistry in Pulsed Methane Plasmas
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Nonoxidative methane conversion offers a promising route for the coproduction of hydrogen and value-added hydrocarbons without CO2 emissions. Among emerging approaches, pulsed plasmas can provide potential advantages by enabling high energy deposition, rapid quenching, and generation of active nonthermal species. This work systematically investigates how pulsed energy deposition from nanosecond-to-millisecond time scales (10 to 50 mJ/pulse) influences methane plasma characteristics (electron density and gas temperature), reaction mechanisms, conversion, and energy efficiency. Nanosecond discharges produced the highest overall C2 selectivity (>70%), with up to 20% for C2H4; in this regime, methane dissociation proceeded through both electron-impact and thermal dissociation, whereas longer pulses were predominantly thermal. Pulsed plasma conversion was similar to thermal arcs (∼377 kJ/mol CH4) and specific energy requirements to produce C2H2 and H2 were 15 kWh/kg and 40 kWh/kg, respectively, in 100 μs long discharges. The product distribution was largely determined by thermal processes involving dehydrogenation reactions (Kassel’s reaction scheme). High gas temperatures preferentially favored C2H2 formation over C2H4, and C2H4 selectivity decreased with increasing pulse width. Overall, these results demonstrate that pulse width and energy can be used to tailor hydrocarbon selectivity and can help design pulsed plasma systems for efficient production of value-added hydrocarbons and hydrogen.

articles.title: Enhancing Propanol Production from CO2 Reduction with a Terbium-Doped Copper Nitride Electrocatalyst
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Propanol is one of the most complex products obtained from CO2 electroreduction (CO2R). Being an interesting precursor for synthetic fuels and a feedstock for the chemical industry, its electrochemical production has recently raised increasing interest. However, low selectivity for propanol has been achieved so far. Here, via exploring a variety of original lanthanide-doped copper nitride materials, we identified and characterized terbium-doped copper nitride as the most selective catalyst for propanol formation. It allowed CO2R to yield propanol with a Faradaic efficiency of 27% at a high current density of 300 mA cm–2 within a neutral (KHCO3 electrolyte) flow cell, surpassing the performance of previous CO2R catalysts. The high density of undercoordinated nitride-derived Cu sites, combined with the increased oxophilicity of the surface, likely promoted the selectivity toward alcohols. Thorough DFT calculations showed that Tb doping increased the affinity for oxygenate-associated C2* intermediates and lowered the free-energy barrier for reactions coupling the latter with CO* toward propanol.

articles.title: Fluorine-Mediated Molten-Salt Crystallization Regulates Phase Evolution and Structural Stability in Sodium Layered Oxides
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Ni- and Co-free P2-type Fe–Mn layered oxides with high Na concentrations are promising cathodes for sodium-ion batteries, but their practical use is limited by phase instability during Na-excess synthesis and structural degradation during cycling and storage. Although large single-crystal-like architectures could improve stability, controlled phase-selective crystallization in these cathode systems remains challenging. Here, we show that fluorine-assisted molten-salt synthesis enables controlled formation of large-particle Fe–Mn–Ti P2 cathodes with enhanced phase selectivity and structural coherence. Compared with Na-excess processing alone, NaF-assisted flux growth expands the P2 phase stability window and promotes large particles with uniform morphologies while preserving local layered ordering. Multiscale characterization further reveals more-reversible structural evolution and more homogeneous Mn redox behavior in the NaF-assisted material, together with a gradient-like fluorine distribution involving surface-enriched NaF-like species and lower level interior fluorine environments. These coupled structural, morphological, and chemical features collectively mitigate crack formation and deliver good cycling stability. In summary, NaF-assisted molten-salt synthesis shows promise in addressing key limitations of Ni- and Co-free P2-type Fe–Mn layered cathodes.

articles.title: The camtrapR R package: From data management to interactive ecological analysis of camera trap data
articles.abstract: Camera trapping has become an indispensable tool in wildlife ecology, generating vast datasets that require efficient and robust analytical workflows. The R package camtrapR was originally developed for preparing camera trap data for analysis in external packages and has since become a standard tool for this purpose. The analyses themselves, however, still had to be conducted elsewhere. Here, we present a major update that transforms camtrapR into an end‐to‐end analytical platform that unifies data import, exploration, covariate preparation, activity pattern estimation, occupancy modelling and spatial prediction. All new functionality is available as R functions and through surveyDashboard(), a new code‐free graphical user interface that guides users through the entire analytical pipeline. Data import supports widely used formats, including exports from the Wildlife Insights platform and datasets conforming to the Camtrap DP data standard. Exploratory tools generate species accumulation curves, maps of species detections and activity patterns for up to two species. Covariates can be extracted at camera trap sites from user‐supplied rasters or online sources, providing inputs for model fitting and, as raster layers, for spatial predictions. Users can fit single‐species and community occupancy models, some of the most widely adopted analytical frameworks in wildlife ecology, and map predicted occupancy across space. Community occupancy models are fitted in a Bayesian framework using JAGS or NIMBLE. These hierarchical models estimate species‐ and community‐level responses to environmental predictors and improve inference for rare species. The workflow includes convergence diagnostics and posterior predictive checks for model assessment and produces spatial predictions of species occupancy and species richness. The workflow can be implemented both in code and within the dashboard. By combining a code‐free interface with advanced modelling capabilities, camtrapR now makes robust camera trap data analysis accessible to a wider audience of ecologists, wildlife managers and students. This paper accompanies camtrapR version 3 and serves as the reference for its expanded functionality.

articles.title: Protein arginine methylation promotes global 3′UTR shortening in proliferating cells
articles.abstract: Griffith et al. show that arginine methylation drives production of short mRNA isoforms in rapidly dividing cells by enabling PCF11 to assemble productively into the cleavage and polyadenylation machinery. PRMT inhibition globally lengthens 3′UTRs across cancer cells, organoids, and T cells, revealing a targetable link between methylation and alternative polyadenylation.

articles.title: Independent Major‐Effect Loci and Limited Trait Associations Characterize Warning Colour Variation Across Sexes and Life Stages in the Wood Tiger Moth (Arctia plantaginis)
articles.abstract: Variation in warning colouration is common, despite strong positive frequency‐dependent selection favouring the most common morph and may arise from spatially or temporally variable selection or associations with other traits. We investigated the maintenance of warning colour variation in the wood tiger moth, Arctia plantaginis, which shows sexual dimorphism in colouration: two distinct male morphs controlled by a single locus, and continuous variation in female hindwing colour and larval warning signal size. Using whole‐genome sequencing of 657 individuals from a laboratory stock derived from a wild polymorphic population, we examined the genetic basis of multiple life‐history traits, chemical defence, pheromones and male activity. We specifically tested for associations with male colour and aimed to identify the genetic basis of female and larval colour variation. We detected separate major‐effect loci for female colour and larval signal size, which were different from the male colour locus. Hindwing melanism was the only trait associated with male colour, mapping to a nearby major‐effect locus and showing a link to reduced activity at higher temperatures. Female colour was phenotypically correlated with pheromone amount. However, apart from melanism, none of the traits measured showed an association with any of the loci controlling warning colours and we found no evidence that male colour is part of a ‘supergene’ or complex co‐adapted phenotype. Instead, our results indicate largely independent genetic architectures for warning colours, suggesting that variable selection rather than genetic associations may contribute to the maintenance of colour polymorphisms in this species.

Boosting NIR-II Luminescence via Ca2+-Formed Band Structure Modulation in Lanthanide-Doped Nanoparticles for Deep-Tissue Bioimaging
articles.abstract: Lanthanide-doped nanoparticles with near-infrared-II (NIR-II, 1000–1700 nm) emission hold great promise for deep-tissue bioimaging, yet their luminescence efficiency is often limited by conventional sensitization pathways. Herein, we go beyond this conventional paradigm by introducing a Ca2+-formed band structure modulation in the host lattice to dramatically boost the NIR-II emission of lanthanide-doped nanoparticles. Rational doping of Ca2+ ions restructures the energy levels, enabling the probe to efficiently capture excitation energy and channel it toward NIR-II-emitting lanthanide activators. This Ca2+-induced band structure modulation mechanism not only enhances the absorption cross section but also accelerates energy transfer to the NIR-II-emitting states. As a result, the designed nanoprobes exhibit excellent photostability and a high quantum yield. In vivo bioimaging demonstrates that the resulting nanoprobes enable deep-tissue visualization with an improved signal-to-background ratio. This work establishes a sensitization strategy that goes beyond conventional approaches, positioning lanthanide-based NIR-II probes as promising candidates for advanced biological imaging.

articles.title: Cathodoluminescence Wavefront Retrieval
articles.abstract: Free-electron-based nanoscopy enables the study of optical excitations in materials with deep-subwavelength spatial resolution, with cathodoluminescence (CL) being one of the most useful signals. When combined with an optical collection system, CL measurements can access multidimensional information on light; yet the phase of the emitted optical fields has remained largely elusive. Here, we demonstrate a reference-free phase retrieval approach for far-field CL wavefronts using the Gerchberg–Saxton algorithm implemented with real-space and angular-space CL intensity data. Applying this approach to representative nanostructures, including a planar surface, nanosphere, plasmonic crystal, and nanowire, we reconstructed distinct phase distributions that revealed their underlying radiation mechanisms. This reference-free framework offers a robust and flexible route for retrieving the phase of electron beam-excited optical fields without relying on a reference wave, making it readily extendable to a wide range of nanostructures.

articles.title: Electron-Beam-Assisted Formation of Simple-Cubic Silver
articles.abstract: Accessing crystal phases under nonequilibrium conditions is a central challenge for expanding the landscape of materials. Simple-cubic (sc) structures are considered energetically unfavorable in elemental solids and have previously been confirmed only in polonium. Here, we report the direct observation of a previously unrecognized sc-Ag formed under far-from-equilibrium conditions. Using electron beam irradiation inside a high-resolution transmission electron microscope as a trigger, we induced the radiolytic decomposition of silver iodide (AgI) and tracked the in situ formation of silver crystals in real time. Continuous imaging revealed that sc-Ag formation strongly depends on the polymorph of the precursor and occurs selectively from metastable γ-AgI. The sc-Ag exhibited unusually high chemical reactivity, undergoing gradual oxidation into silver oxide under high-vacuum conditions where conventional fcc-Ag remains stable. These findings demonstrate that irreversible crystal formation pathways can kinetically stabilize crystal structures inaccessible under near-equilibrium conditions and extend a previously inaccessible structural limit of metallic bonding.

articles.title: From Dense to Nanostructured Thin Film Anodes: Boosting Li-Ion Accessibility in TiO2 Thin Film Electrodes
articles.abstract: Dense TiO2 thin-film electrodes suffer from limited electrolyte penetration and restricted Li-ion transport, making the electrode architecture a critical parameter for efficient charge storage. Herein, glancing-angle deposition (GLAD) combined with reactive magnetron sputtering is used to engineer ion-accessible TiO2 nanocolumnar architectures without compositional modification or postprocessing. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations guided the selection of substrate tilt and azimuthal rotation conditions to control the column orientation, intercolumnar spacing, and open porosity. The predicted morphologies were subsequently validated by electron microscopy for the experimentally deposited thin films. Electrochemical measurements show that GLAD-engineered electrodes deliver up to approximately 4-fold higher areal capacitance than dense TiO2 films. ToF-SIMS depth profiling further reveals that Li species remain largely concentrated near the surface of dense films. In contrast, the GLAD-engineered nanocolumnar architecture allows for a more uniform Li distribution throughout the electrode depth. These results establish morphology-controlled ion accessibility as the primary origin of the enhanced electrochemical response.

articles.title: Intra- and Interlayer Excitonic Fine Structure of the Two-Dimensional Perovskite (PEA)2PbI4
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional halide perovskites host strongly bound excitons whose fine structure governs polarization selection rules and radiative recombination, yet spectral features in phenethylammonium lead iodide ((PEA)2PbI4) remain controversially assigned. Here, polarization-resolved low-temperature photoluminescence (PL) combined with first-principles G0W0+BSE calculations probes the intralayer and interlayer excitonic fine structure of this Ruddlesden–Popper perovskite. The low-energy multiplet is consistent with the intralayer excitonic fine structure governed by electron–hole exchange, crystal symmetry, and layer inequivalence in the two-layer unit cell, without requiring Rashba effects or exciton–polaron mechanisms as its primary origin. The weak doublet about 40 meV higher is best accounted for by interlayer excitons based on its energetics, splitting, and real-space character. Distortion-induced mixing of interlayer excitons with bright intralayer excitons provides a plausible explanation for the observed interlayer PL intensities and nearly orthogonal polarizations. These results support a layer-resolved excitonic picture encompassing both intralayer and interlayer states in (PEA)2PbI4.

articles.title: Photoinduced Surface Reconstruction Strategy for Enhancing AgBiS2 Quantum Dot Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Silver bismuth sulfide (AgBiS2) quantum dots (QDs) are promising candidates for eco-friendly solution-based solar cells. However, structural defects in QDs hinder high efficiency. Controllable synthesis of AgBiS2 QDs remains challenging, often yielding crystals with surface and lattice defects that promote nonradiative recombination. Improving AgBiS2 QD quality before film formation is crucial, as synthesis-related imperfections often persist in devices and inherently limit effective passivation later on. This study presents a photoinduced surface reconstruction method for AgBiS2 QDs that achieves nearly perfect ionic ordering with lower lattice strain, leading to denser films and better band alignment with charge layers than the initial AgBiS2 QDs. Corresponding solar cells achieve a power conversion efficiency of 9.71%, exceeding 8.16% for untreated solar cells. By enhancing AgBiS2 QD quality at the source rather than relying solely on downstream passivation, this approach offers a complementary pathway to high-performance QD solar cells.

articles.title: Pixelated Tellurium Nanowire Assemblies for Flexible and Polarization-Driven Multimodal Anticounterfeiting
articles.abstract: Anticounterfeiting technologies capable of enabling both visual authentication and machine-readable encryption are critically demanded. Here we present a wafer-scale and flexible tellurium nanowire (TeNW) platform with programmable localized orientation, enabling dual-mode anticounterfeiting based on polarization-encoded information. By employing a lock–shear and lift-off strategy, pixelated and highly aligned TeNW arrays with feature sizes down to 5 μm are realized on arbitrary rigid and flexible substrates, exhibiting dichroic ratios of up to 4.6 and stretchability exceeding 100%. Beyond passive optical security, the semiconducting nature of TeNWs allows these oriented arrays to function as active channels in asymmetric Schottky photodetectors, delivering broadband photoresponse (405–1064 nm), an anisotropic photocurrent ratio of 2.35, and an ultrafast response time of 430 μs under self-powered operation. Leveraging this capability, polarization-encoded information can be transduced into polarization-sensitive electrical signals, establishing a hardware-level security paradigm that physically encodes information in the material rather than in algorithms.

articles.title: Role of Stereochemistry on Electron Transport in Peptides
articles.abstract: Stereochemistry underlies structure–function relationships across biology and materials science. Here, we investigate electron transport in oligopeptide stereoisomers using single-molecule experiments and computational modeling. Our results show that stereochemical modifications in tyrosine-based peptides lead to significant variations in molecular conductance and transport distance along the peptide backbone, associated with changes in aromatic side-chain interactions and electronic coupling. In alanine-based peptides, stereochemical modifications alter molecular conductance through secondary-structure interactions associated with β-turn conformations. Molecular dynamics simulations and quantum mechanical calculations reveal the molecular origins of these stereochemistry-dependent structural and electronic properties. Overall, this work shows that stereochemical modification of nonterminal amino acids provides a means to control electron transport through distinct mechanisms involving aromatic side-chain interactions and secondary structure. These results establish stereochemistry as a molecular design parameter for controlling electron transport in peptide-based electronic materials.

articles.title: Unidirectional Magnetoresistance Driven by Nonequilibrium Antiferromagnetic Magnons
articles.abstract: Magnetoresistive effects are typically symmetric under magnetization reversal. However, nonlinear spin transport can give rise to unidirectional magnetoresistance in systems with strong spin–orbit interaction and broken inversion symmetry. Here, we report a large magnonic unidirectional spin Hall magnetoresistance (USMR) in a van der Waals antiferromagnet CrPS4 in contact with Pt, driven by the nonequilibrium magnon accumulation with a finite magnon chemical potential. In contrast to conventional magnonic USMR driven by magnetization fluctuations, this effect persists under strong magnetic fields and low temperatures. The magnitude of magnonic USMR in CrPS4/Pt exceeds that of YIG/Pt by more than 2 orders of magnitude and surpasses the electrical USMR in metallic Ta/Co bilayers by a factor of 2. Our results highlight magnon chemical potential gradients for nonlinear magnetoresistance in antiferromagnetic van der Waals heterostructures and open a route to magnon-based antiferromagnetic spintronic functionalities in two-terminal device geometries.

articles.title: Unveiling the Creep Recovery Behavior of Pseudo-Free-Standing Polymer Thin Films for Wearable Electronics
articles.abstract: Polymer thin films in wearable electronics undergo creep recovery during operation as on-body devices, resulting in unrecoverable strain that subsequently induces mechanical instability in the films. However, the creep recovery behavior of polymer thin films has not been investigated due to their intrinsic fragility and the difficulty in controlling ultralow loads for the films. We evaluate the creep recovery behavior of pseudo-free-standing polymer thin films as a function of creep stress, developing direct creep recovery testing with a feedback-based ultralow-load control system. Polystyrene (PS) thin films exhibit a sharp increase in unrecoverable strain with the onset of crazing. While poly(3-butylthiophene) (P3BT) thin films show a linear increase in the relative ratio of unrecoverable strain with increasing creep stress, poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) thin films exhibit a viscoelastic strain larger than unrecoverable strain. This work reveals the creep recovery behavior of polymer thin films and proposes a direct creep recovery testing method.

articles.abstract: An innovative artificial-intelligence application enhances weather forecasting in the difficult subseasonal range, providing accurate forecasts of precipitation, temperature and pressure 3–5 weeks in advance. The tool refines both physics- and AI-based weather models and improves the early prediction of extremes of heat, cold, rainfall and flooding.

articles.abstract: The discovery of Helicobacter pylori has revolutionized the prevention and treatment of gastritis, peptic ulcers, and, most important, gastric cancer. In the past 40 years, enormous progress has been achieved in the clinical and basic research on H. pylori infection. However, challenges in preventing and treating H. pylori infection exist owing to the lack of an H. pylori vaccine and the ever-increasing resistance to antibiotics worldwide. This review summarizes the history of and key milestones in H. pylori research, provides an update on the understanding of the pathogenesis and global burden of H. pylori infection and the screening strategy for the primary prevention of gastric cancer, and focuses on the emerging trends in the management of H. pylori infection.

Ianalumab for the Treatment of Patients with Sjögren’s Disease
articles.abstract: BackgroundSjögren's disease is a complex, systemic autoimmune disease with no approved targeted therapies. Ianalumab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody with a dual mechanism of action, depleting B cells through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and inhibiting B-cell activation and survival through blockade of B-cell activating factor receptor.MethodsWe conducted two 52-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease. Patients in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ianalumab (300 mg monthly) or placebo; patients in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 300 mg of ianalumab monthly or every 3 months or placebo. The primary end point was the change from baseline in the score on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) at week 48 (scores range from 0 to 123, with higher scores indicating greater disease activity). The first key secondary end point in the hierarchical plan for the NEPTUNUS-1 trial was an ESSDAI response (≥5-point reduction) at week 48; for the NEPTUNUS-2 trial, it was the change from baseline in the score on the Sjögren's Syndrome Symptom Diary (SSSD) or EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index (ESSPRI) at week 48.ResultsOverall, 275 patients underwent randomization in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial (ianalumab monthly, 137 patients; placebo, 138 patients) and 504 in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial (ianalumab monthly, 168 patients; ianalumab every 3 months, 167 patients; and placebo, 169 patients). In both trials, ianalumab monthly led to a significantly greater decrease in the ESSDAI score at week 48 than placebo, with a between-group difference of -1.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI], -2.6 to 0.0; P = 0.0496) in NEPTUNUS-1 and -1.0 points (95% CI, -2.0 to 0.0; P = 0.04) in NEPTUNUS-2. No significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI scores were observed at week 48. The incidence of serious adverse events was similar with ianalumab and placebo. Nonserious local injection-site and systemic injection-related reactions were more common in the ianalumab groups.ConclusionsIn these two trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease, ianalumab at a dose of 300 mg monthly resulted in a significantly greater decrease in disease activity at week 48 than placebo, although there were no significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI symptom scores. (Funded by Novartis Pharma; NEPTUNUS-1 and NEPTUNUS-2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05350072 and NCT05349214, respectively.).

articles.abstract: BackgroundRetatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for treating obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).MethodsIn two phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials nested within larger basket trials of once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide, we assigned adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and a body-mass index (the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of at least 27, without (TRIUMPH-1-OSA) or with (TRIUMPH-2-OSA) type 2 diabetes, to receive retatrutide (4, 9, or 12 mg) or placebo. The primary end point was the change in the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, the average number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep) at 80 weeks with 9 mg and 12 mg of retatrutide. For OSA-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy used for participants who had intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy used elsewhere. We also report intention-to-treat (ITT) results.ResultsA total of 243 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and 448 in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The baseline mean AHI was 58.6 and 55.9 events per hour, respectively, and the mean body weight was 119.6 and 115.9 kg. At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the AHI (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OSA were -22.9 (4 mg), -34.3 (9 mg), and -31.7 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -9.9 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -13.0 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -23.0 to -3.0], -24.4 [95% CI, -34.1 to -14.7], and -21.9 [95% CI, -32.2 to -11.5], respectively). The changes with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-2-OSA were -19.2 (4 mg), -24.7 (9 mg), and -25.4 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -10.3 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -8.9 [95% CI, -15.9 to -2.0], -14.4 [95% CI, -21.6 to -7.2], and -15.1 [95% CI, -22.5 to -7.7]). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -13.2 (95% CI, -22.6 to -3.9), -24.7 (95% CI, -34.1 to -15.3), and -22.5 (95% CI, -31.9 to -13.1) in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -8.8 (95% CI, -15.8 to -1.7), -13.9 (95% CI, -21.3 to -6.6), and -15.0 (95% CI, -22.5 to -7.4) in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The mean percent change in body weight with retatrutide (key secondary end point) was -12.5 to -22.2% in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -12.1 to -18.5% in TRIUMPH-2-OSA, versus -4.8% and -5.6% with placebo (treatment-regimen estimand). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.ConclusionsIn adults with OSA and obesity or overweight with or without type 2 diabetes, retatrutide resulted in significantly greater decreases in the AHI than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 and -2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05929066 and NCT05929079.).

An AGC kinase cascade regulates ROP signaling for the correct timing of pollen germination
articles.abstract: Model for PDK1‐AGC1.5/7 kinase cascade function in controlling pollen germination. Summary In flowering plants, the timing of pollen germination is crucial for successful fertilization and an important trait for seed and fruit crops. Environmental factors tightly regulate pollen germination, with germination‐suppressing conditions on the pollen‐producing anther and germination‐promoting conditions on the receiving stigma. Using genetic, biochemical, and cell biological methods, we show that this environmental sensitivity of pollen germination in Arabidopsis thaliana is regulated by a 3‐PHOSPHOINOSITIDE‐DEPENDENT KINASE 1 (PDK1)‐AGC1.5/AGC1.7 kinase cascade. We show that PDK1 hyperphosphorylates downstream AGC1.5/7 kinases to enhance their activity. Pollen‐specific phosphoproteomics identified multiple proteins involved in pollen growth whose phosphorylation is controlled by AGC1.5/7. Two germination‐promoting RHO OF PLANTS GUANINE NUCLEOTIDE EXCHANGE FACTORS (ROPGEFs) are phosphorylated by AGC1.5/7 at a novel site, reducing ROPGEF plasma membrane polarization. Loss of PDK1‐AGC kinase signaling resulted in precocious pollen germination on the anther, which was rescued by high AGC1.5 kinase activity. Conversely, AGC1.5/7 overexpression or a phosphomimic ROPGEF version inhibited precocious pollen germination. Distinct subcellular localization of PDK1 and AGC1 kinases upon pollen germination is likely to alleviate their inhibitory effect. Our data indicate that the correct timing of pollen germination requires the fine‐tuned activity of a PDK1‐AGC1 kinase cascade inhibiting ROPGEFs on the anther, preventing precocious pollen germination.

articles.title: B‐BOX DOMAIN PROTEIN 19 shapes tea quality by modulating the ratio of catechins and theanine and confers cold tolerance in tea plants
articles.abstract: A working model of the core regulator CsBBX19 which fine‐tunes tea quality and cold tolerance in tea plants. Summary Early spring cold spells threaten tea plant (Camellia sinensis) yield and disrupt the catechins‐to‐theanine ratio that determines the desirable balance of umami and astringency taste of tea. However, the molecular mechanism coordinating cold tolerance with this key quality trait remains unclear. Here, we identified a light‐responsive B‐BOX DOMAIN PROTEIN CsBBX19 as a core regulator simultaneously shaping tea quality and cold tolerance. Results demonstrated that silencing CsBBX19 relieves the transcriptional repression of theanine‐biosynthetic genes (CsTSI and CsAlaDC) to elevate theanine levels, yet weakens the activation of catechins‐biosynthetic genes (CsANS1, CsANR1, CsLAR1, and CsSCPL1/2/5) to reduce catechins content. The CsBBX19‐modulated theanine accumulation also enhanced the cold tolerance of tea plants by suppressing cell‐wall‐loosening EXPANSIN (CsEXPA10/20/21) and activating the CsCBF3‐mediated cold response pathway. Furthermore, the expression of CsBBX19 significantly reduced by light via a feedback loop involving CsHY5, which directly binds to the promoter of CsBBX19 to repress its transcription, while CsBBX19 conversely interacts with CsHY5 to reinforce its autoactivation, thereby fine‐tuning the catechins‐to‐theanine ratio and cold resilience in tea plants. Our findings underscore the central roles of CsBBX19 in light‐mediated cold response and tea quality formation, providing valuable targets for synchronously improving cold resilience and quality in tea plants.

articles.title: Duplication and functional divergence of TCP4 genes in turnip
articles.abstract: Target genes of BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b. Summary Gene duplication is widely recognized as a significant catalyst for plant adaptive evolution. The retained duplicated genes usually undergo functional divergence to govern plant growth and stress resistance. Turnip (Brassica rapa var. rapa) shows a broad capacity for environmental adaptation. Here, we investigate how duplicated TCP4 genes modulate turnip growth and development. We identify three TCP4 paralogs, BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b in turnip, characterize their expression patterns and analyze sequence variation in their conserved domains. We further model their three‐dimensional structures and compare their protein–protein interactions and downstream regulatory networks. We show that BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b exhibit distinct expression profiles. A single mutation within the conserved TCP domain leads to differences in protein–protein interactions among BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b. Combined with DAP‐Seq, ChIP‐qPCR and luciferase assays, our results demonstrate that BrrTCP4 and BrrTCP4a activate BrrCOs and BrrFTs to regulate turnip flowering, while BrrTCP4b preferentially participates in the trehalose synthesis pathway by targeting TPP and TPS genes. Our research findings indicate the functional divergence of BrrTCP4, BrrTCP4a and BrrTCP4b to balance growth and stress responses in turnip, thereby advancing our understanding of how gene duplication drives functional specialization and contributes to plant evolutionary adaptation. 概括 重复基因是植物适应性进化的重要催化剂。保留下来的重复基因会发生功能分化，进而调控植物的生长发育和抗逆性。蔓菁(Brassica rapa var. rapa)隶属于十字花科芸薹属，该属经历了一次特有的全基因组三倍化事件，是研究重复基因的理想材料。因此，本文我们研究了蔓菁TCP4重复基因如何调控蔓菁的生长发育。 共线性分析发现蔓菁BrrTCP4、BrrTCP4a和BrrTCP4b是基因组复制产生的三个重复基因。我们分析了它们的表达模式和其保守结构域中的序列变异。并进一步模拟了它们的三维结构，比较了它们的互作蛋白及下游调控网络的差异。 研究结果显示BrrTCP4、BrrTCP4a和BrrTCP4b具有不同的表达模式。保守TCP结构域内的单个氨基酸突变导致了BrrTCP4和BrrTCP4a与BrrTCP4b互作蛋白的差异。结合DAP‐Seq、ChIP‐qPCR和荧光素酶实验发现，BrrTCP4和BrrTCP4a直接激活BrrCOs和BrrFTs以调控蔓菁开花，而BrrTCP4b则通过靶向TPP和TPS基因优先参与海藻糖合成途径。 我们的研究结果揭示了BrrTCP4、BrrTCP4a和BrrTCP4b重复基因发生了功能分化，这种分化平衡了蔓菁的生长发育与胁迫响应。相关研究结果加深了我们对基因重复如何驱动功能分化并促进植物适应性进化的理解。

articles.title: Elevated CO2 drives nonlinear trait responses and reshapes growth‐virulence trade‐offs in a plant pathogen
articles.abstract: Temporal variation in carbon dioxide concentration within the crop canopy and in the atmosphere. Summary Atmospheric CO2 is rising at unprecedented rates. While its physiological effects on plants are well‐documented, the direct evolutionary impact on plant pathogens remains unknown. We investigated how CO2 interacts with other abiotic factors to shape the evolutionary potential of pathogens. We combined controlled CO2 gradient experiments with quantitative genetics to assess the interactive effects of CO2, temperature and geography on Phytophthora infestans. We measured intrinsic growth rate and aggressiveness, the two key pathogen traits, across seven geographically distinct populations and partitioned their phenotypic variance into heritability and plasticity components. Both intrinsic growth rate and aggressiveness showed a shared quadratic response to CO2, peaking c. 2000 ppm before declining. Elevated CO2 reduced phenotypic variance in aggressiveness under extreme concentrations. CO2 also reconfigured the life‐history correlation between growth and aggressiveness, shifting it from positive under ambient CO2 to negative near the optimum. Heritability exceeded plasticity for aggressiveness in most populations, indicating that virulence responds primarily through selection. Trait responses were modulated by local climate and geography, with the strongest CO2‐driven increases occurring under thermal and geographic extremes. Our results demonstrate that rising CO2 acts as a direct agent of selection, nonlinearly reshaping pathogen phenotypic architecture and life‐history strategies in a geographically heterogeneous manner.

articles.title: From isotopologues to isotopomers: advances in mass spectrometry‐based positional 13C analysis in plants
articles.abstract: Workflow of gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (GC‐MS)‐based 13C‐labelling analysis of plant metabolites. Summary Carbon fluxes throughout metabolic networks can be investigated experimentally through 13C‐isotope labelling experiments (13C‐ILE) and 13C‐metabolic flux analysis (13C‐MFA). 13C‐ILE involves the application of isotopically labelled substrates to a biological system to detect label distribution throughout the metabolic network, while 13C‐MFA is a computational approach that quantitatively estimates fluxes by fitting isotope‐labelling data to metabolic network models. 13C‐MFA can encompass more metabolic reactions and provide subcellular flux estimates that remain difficult to validate directly using current 13C‐ILE approaches. Overcoming major bottlenecks of 13C‐ILE is thus needed to improve and validate 13C‐MFA. Mass spectrometry (MS)‐based 13C‐ILE has been carried out mostly at isotopologue rather than isotopomer level. Isotopologues differ in their isotopic composition, while isotopomers have the same isotopic composition but at different positions within the molecule. Thus, 13C‐isotopomer approaches discriminate which atoms of a metabolite have received 13C, enabling better comprehension of the regulation of metabolic pathways. Here, we highlight the major challenges to improve MS‐based positional 13C analysis and discuss the advantages of this approach over MS‐based methods with low or no carbon‐positional resolution. We further demonstrate how positional 13C analysis has been used to estimate enzyme activity in vivo and to study plant metabolism.

articles.title: Leaf nutrient resorption across contrasting soil parent materials: it is not just about efficiency
articles.abstract: Box plots showing nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) concentrations in senesced leaves across contrasting parent materials for four site groups. Summary In theory, nutrient resorption from leaves should be higher in sites with lower soil nutrients, increasing the retention and reuse of nutrients that are limited in supply. However, evidence for this relationship has remained inconsistent for decades, particularly where the percent of nutrient resorbed is concerned. Furthermore, plant resorption responses to soil phosphorus (P) concentration remain poorly understood. Leaf nitrogen (N) and P concentrations and resorption percentages (efficiencies) were measured for 68 Australian plant species sampled across four nutrient-rich vs nutrient-poor site-pairs representing contrasting soil parent materials. N and P concentrations in senesced leaves were significantly lower on nutrient-poor than on nutrient-richer sites, enabling greater internal conservation of these nutrients on nutrient-poor sites. Resorption efficiencies averaged 45% for N and 69% for P and did not differ between contrasting soils. Though not sensitive to site, P resorption efficiency (PRE) was positively related to the proportion of labile P in leaves (R 2 = 0.54). We demonstrated for the first time that senesced leaf P concentrations and the corresponding PRE are distinctly shaped by plant adaptation to soil nutrient scarcity, and internal labile P pools, respectively. The high PRE of Australian species informs an upper bound for this process in global vegetation models.

articles.title: MYB156 promotes root sucker formation by repressing IDD14 and CKX1 to elevate cytokinin levels in Populus
articles.abstract: Schematic model illustrating MYB156‐mediated regulatory network controlling root‐sucker formation. Summary Root suckers enable clonal propagation of rooting‐recalcitrant poplars, conferring rejuvenated traits such as enhanced survival and accelerated growth. Despite widespread clonal propagation and ecological restoration, the essential genes controlling sucker development remain unidentified. MYB156 is a positive regulator of root sucker formation in white poplar (Populus davidiana × P. bolleana). MYB156 is predominantly expressed in proliferation‐competent root cells, including vascular cambium and phellogen. Gain‐ and loss‐of‐function analyses demonstrated that MYB156 overexpression enhanced root suckering and secondary growth, whereas myb156 mutants were severely compromised in both. Meanwhile, cytokinin levels increased two‐ to fivefold in roots with MYB156 overexpression but were significantly reduced in myb156 mutant roots. MYB156 directly represses IDD14 and CKX1, reducing cytokinin catabolism and alleviating IDD14‐mediated suppression of cytokinin accumulation; IDD14 RNAi lines similarly showed elevated cytokinin and enhanced suckering. Cytokinin response elements in the MYB156 promoter and MYB156 autoactivation establish a cytokinin‐MYB156 positive feedback loop amplifying cytokinin signaling in meristematic zones. Live imaging with the cytokinin response reporter TCSn:RFP demonstrated that suckering in MYB156‐overexpressing plants shifted from the phellogen to the vascular cambium. These findings establish a MYB156‐CKX1/IDD14‐cytokinin module that creates a permissive context for suckering, providing a transcriptional blueprint for clonal propagation.

articles.title: Bulk-Mediated Reflection of Chirality-Protected Surface Spin Waves
articles.abstract: Surface spin waves of the Damon-Eshbach type exhibit intrinsically nonreciprocal transport properties with a chiral dynamical field structure that localizes counterpropagating waves at opposite film surfaces. Such chirality has been predicted to suppress direct backscattering in thin films within frequency ranges free of bulk modes. However, how chirality influences reflection in thicker three-dimensional magnetic media, where a dense spectrum of bulk excitations overlaps with surface waves, remains unclear. Here we demonstrate that, in micrometer-thick yttrium iron garnet films, reflection of the chiral Damon-Eshbach wave from the boundary of the magnetic medium is accompanied by excitation of spatially localized thickness-quantized bulk modes, whereas reciprocal backward-volume waves reflect nearly elastically. Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy, infrared thermography, and micromagnetic simulations reveal standing bulk excitations at the reflecting boundary and quantify the associated magnon energy accumulation and dissipation. These results identify bulk-mode excitations as the physical pathway enabling reversal of chirally localized surface waves in thick films, thereby defining the limits of chirality-based backscattering immunity and providing a general framework for wave transport in nonreciprocal magnetic media.

articles.title: Contamination-Free Resolution of Cantor Spectra and Magic-Angle Localization in Moiré Quasicrystals and Aperiodic Media
articles.abstract: Quasicrystalline Hamiltonians host Cantor-like spectra, gaps, and critical states, yet conventional finite-patch diagonalization is often compromised by spectral pollution: spurious eigenvalues absent from the infinite system. We introduce a certified spectral-computation framework for aperiodic media, computing infinite-volume spectra of general Hermitian Hamiltonians with rigorous a posteriori error bounds and without imposing artificial boundaries or artificial periodicity. The method resolves fine spectral features and fractal dimensions universally across aperiodic systems. For twisted Penrose bilayers, angle-resolved certified spectra identify a magic angle at $\ensuremath{\theta}\ensuremath{\approx}27.228\ifmmode^\circ\else\textdegree\fi{}$, where ring-worm interference produces twist-controlled confinement. Across one- and two-dimensional quasicrystals, the results show how fractal spectral geometry organizes localization: lower box-counting dimension correlates with larger inverse participation ratio in substitution chains, while dodecagonal tilings exhibit compactly supported and algebraically confined critical modes. The framework also scales to three dimensions, delivering contamination-free, high-resolution spectra for a quasicrystal arising in acoustic metamaterials. Further examples involving quantum walks, continuum superlattices, longer-range hopping, and inhomogeneous magnetic fields demonstrate the broad reach of certified spectral computation as a route to predictive spectral design in aperiodic media.

articles.title: Diagrammatic Route to Multireference $GW$ for Strongly Correlated Molecules
articles.abstract: The $GW$ approximation is a cornerstone of many-body perturbation theory for computing single-particle excitations, yet it can fail qualitatively in strongly correlated systems where the single-reference picture becomes inadequate. To overcome this limitation, we develop a diagrammatic route to multireference $GW$ (MR-$GW$) from an interacting active-space reference, treating strong correlation nonperturbatively and the residual interaction through dynamical screening at the multireference random phase approximation level. Because the conventional diagrammatic self-energy expansion no longer applies, we define a practical one-shot MR-$GW$ approximation within a generalized diagrammatic framework, recovering standard $GW$ as a special case. Applications to prototypical correlated atoms and molecules show that the interacting active-space reference captures multiconfigurational satellite structures poorly described by single-reference $GW$, while dynamical screening generally improves the satellite energies as well as the leading ionization and electron-attachment energies. This work opens a diagrammatic route to Green's-function methods that combine nonperturbative strong correlation with dynamical screening.

articles.title: Experimental Tomography of Quantum Many-Body Hamiltonians in Solids via Thermalization
articles.abstract: Characterizing the unknown Hamiltonian of a quantum many-body system is essential for exploring fundamental physical phenomena and advancing frontier quantum technologies. However, the complexity of many-body interactions and limited control capabilities in realistic experimental systems render this…

articles.title: First Simultaneous Analysis of Transverse Momentum Dependent and Collinear Parton Distributions in the Proton
articles.abstract: We present the first simultaneous global QCD analysis of unpolarized transverse momentum dependent (TMD) and collinear parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the proton. Our Letter incorporates data from deep-inelastic scattering, Drell-Yan, inclusive weak boson, $W+$ charm, and jet production involving PDFs, as well as TMD Drell-Yan and $Z$-boson production data from fixed target and collider experiments sensitive to both TMD and collinear distributions. The analysis is performed at next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy for QCD resummation in TMD observables and next-to-leading order for observables described in collinear factorization. The combined analysis improves knowledge of both TMD and collinear PDFs, particularly in the sea-quark sector, providing a consistent simultaneous description of the aforementioned observables.

articles.title: Linear Ensemble-Constrained Quantum Monte Carlo: From Dilute Fermi Gas to Flat-Band Ferromagnetism
articles.abstract: We present a finite-temperature canonical-ensemble determinant quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that enforces an exact fermion number and enables numerically stable simulations of correlated lattice fermions. We propose a stabilized QR update that reduces the computational complexity from standard cubic scaling $O(\ensuremath{\beta}{N}^{3})$ to linear scaling $O(\ensuremath{\beta}N\text{ }\text{ }{N}_{e}^{2})$ with respect to the system size $N$, where ${N}_{e}$ is the particle number. This yields a dramatic speedup in dilute regimes (${N}_{e}\ensuremath{\ll}N$), opening unbiased access to large-scale simulations of strongly correlated low-density phases. We validate the method on the dilute Fermi gas with onsite Hubbard interactions, observing the suppression of the fermion sign problem in the dilute limit. Furthermore, we apply this approach to a one-dimensional flat-band system, where the canonical ensemble allows for precise control over filling. We reveal a ferromagnetic instability at low temperatures in the half-filling regime. Our linear-scaling approach provides a powerful tool for investigating emergent phenomena in dilute quantum matter.

articles.title: Next-to-Next-to-Next-to-Leading-Order QCD Corrections to Photon-Pair Production
articles.abstract: The production of two isolated photons at the Large Hadron Collider has applications in Higgs-boson phenomenology and in new-physics searches. In fact, measurements would provide more insight if a percent-level theoretical prediction were available. We account for next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order strong-interaction effects in the cross section for the first time. This is not only necessary to demonstrate the convergence of perturbation theory, but also results in a reduction of the theoretical uncertainty by a factor of 3 down to 3%. With this, we pave the way to improved analyses.

articles.title: Nonlinear Phonon-Assisted Up-Conversion Photoluminescence Under Vibrational Pumping at Liquid-Helium Temperatures
articles.abstract: Optical refrigeration in semiconductors is driven by anti-Stokes photoluminescence (PL) arising from phonon-assisted up-conversion. In the conventional picture, lattice vibrations remain in thermal equilibrium and the relevant phonon population is pump independent, so the up-conversion rate scales a…

articles.title: One-Positron Quantum Cyclotron
articles.abstract: A device that stores a single positron and controls its quantum states could measure its magnetic moment with unprecedented precision, testing a symmetry principle central to quantum field theory.

articles.title: Phase-Space Microscopes for Quantum Gases: Imaging Conjugate Variables and Momentum-Weighted Densities
articles.abstract: A new method lets quantum gas microscopes measure not only where atoms are but also how they move.

articles.title: Quantum Sensing Using Geometrical Phase in Qubit-Oscillator Systems
articles.abstract: We present a quantum sensing protocol for coupled qubit-oscillator systems that surpasses the standard quantum limit (SQL) by exploiting a geometrical phase. The signal is encoded in the geometrical phase that is proportional to the area enclosed in oscillator phase space. This area is amplified thr…

articles.title: Quasilinear Theory of Fast Flavor Instabilities
articles.abstract: Dense neutrino plasmas can develop instabilities that drive collisionless flavor exchange, equivalent to the emission of flavomons, the quanta of flavor waves. We treat these waves as independent linear degrees of freedom and develop a quasilinear theory, including backreaction on the neutrino distribution and nonresonant neutrino-flavomon interactions, while neglecting wave-wave processes. In a statistically homogeneous, axisymmetric model, the saturated neutrino and flavomon distributions agree closely with periodic-box solutions of the original quantum kinetic equation. Our results provide the first theoretical interpretation for the numerical observations. They also show that flavomon phases have little influence on the final state, supporting the quasilinear theory as a framework for capturing flavor evolution without resolving nonlinear small-scale dynamics.

articles.title: Selective Strain Tuning of Nonequilibrium Multiferroic Dynamics in ${\mathrm{BiFeO}}_{3}$
articles.abstract: Quantum materials are characterized by intertwined orders, and a fundamental goal in condensed matter physics is to achieve their selective control in such a way that one order parameter can be tuned while leaving others largely unaffected. Although significant progress has been made in thermal equilibrium, realizing such control out of equilibrium remains highly challenging. Here we employed in situ tensile strain to selectively manipulate the photoinduced lattice dynamics associated with ferroelectric and magnetic orders in multiferroic ${\mathrm{BiFeO}}_{3}$. By applying MeV ultrafast electron diffraction to freestanding ${\mathrm{BiFeO}}_{3}$ membranes under tunable strain, we showed that tensile strain markedly suppresses the ultrafast photoinduced reduction of the ferroelectric displacement. By contrast, the photoinduced dynamics of the antiferrodistortive rotation of the oxygen octahedra, which modulates the magnetic order, remains insensitive to strain. Not only do these findings reveal distinct microscopic pathways underlying nonequilibrium multiferroic dynamics, they also establish tunable strain as an effective route for engineering ultrafast phase control in correlated materials.

Commun. 16, 10114 (2025)] demonstrated that a driven overdamped colloidal particle in a harmonic trap immersed in a viscoelastic fluid can recuperate energy dissipated into the surrounding bath and convert it into useful work. In this Letter …

articles.title: Generalized Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon Hierarchy for Near-Integrable Dynamics
articles.abstract: The BBGKY hierarchy is generalized to systems with strong integrable contact interactions and generic long-range two-body ones, enabling the computation of experimentally measurable expectation values and correlations for classical and quantum systems.

articles.title: Tensor-Network Framework for Lindbladian Spectra and Steady States
articles.abstract: Researchers develop a tensor-network framework using complex-time evolution to accurately compute low-lying excitation spectra of open quantum systems.

articles.title: A comprehensive review on the physical mechanisms, influencing factors and recent advances of tension-compression asymmetry: from traditional metals to high-temperature structural materials
A climate action intervention increases four psychological motivators, as well as climate advocacy, activism and civic participation
articles.abstract: Urgent climate action is needed to keep warming below 2°C and protect hundreds of millions from climate collapse. As part of a broader Registered Report series, this study examined whether a longitudinal intervention designed to strengthen psychological correlates of pro-environmental behaviour could motivate n = 31 university students in The Netherlands to take climate action. The intervention was delivered over six weeks through interactive lessons and activities informed by psychological theories and interventions. The goal was to increase pro-climate behaviours by targeting 12 psychological factors. Participants completed surveys assessing these correlates, as well as ecological momentary assessments of individual and collective pro-climate behaviours before and after the intervention, and after three months (14 days each). A control group was included (n = 27). Results showed that 4 of the 12 psychological correlates increased significantly: emotional engagement, collective efficacy, the bottom-up theory of change (the belief that change can start from grassroots action and spread systemically) and climate appraisal. Three (except appraisal) remained elevated at the three-month follow-up. Civic engagement, advocacy and activism increased after the intervention in the experimental group relative to control group. The increase in activist behaviour was predicted by the development of a bottom-up theory of change.

articles.title: A remarkable sample of bird teeth from the palaeo-Arctic Prince Creek Formation of northern Alaska elucidates Late Cretaceous avialan richness
articles.abstract: Understanding the taxonomic affinity of putative avialan teeth is essential to assessing the geographic range and richness of Late Cretaceous toothed birds. Isolated teeth attributed to Avialae are known from numerous North American Late Cretaceous microfossil assemblages. However, because only a select few of these tooth types are known from teeth preserved in jaws, their taxonomic affinities remain uncertain. Several key morphologies used to diagnose avialan teeth are also present in non-avialan theropods and crocodyliforms, leading some to question whether many such isolated teeth belong to birds. Here, we provide detailed descriptions and high-resolution images of avialan teeth from the Late Cretaceous Prince Creek Formation (PCF) of northern Alaska. A total of 105 isolated teeth were identified as avialan and can be divided into seven distinct morphotypes. Crucially, decades of extensive microfossil sampling have failed to produce any evidence of crocodyliforms in the PCF, allowing us to rule out this possible identity. Further, the teeth described here can be distinguished from those of all non-avialan theropods known in the PCF. Our morphotypes thus provide an important framework for identifying bird teeth in other Late Cretaceous microfossil assemblages as well as understanding avialan diversity before the K–Pg extinction.

articles.title: A unified framework for calibration, decoding and resource-aware processing in hybrid quantum–classical machine learning
articles.abstract: Hybrid quantum–classical machine learning on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices suffers from three coupled overheads: hardware miscalibration, classical syndrome-decoding latency and shot noise on gradient estimators. We present quantum calibration and observable processing (QCOP), a unified closed-loop control layer integrating a spectral calibration engine (SCE), a hierarchical syndrome decoder (HSD) and an observable compression layer (OCL) within a single GPU-accelerated pipeline. Three theoretical bounds characterize the joint effect on logical error rate (LER), convergence rate and observable variance. On device-calibrated noise-model simulators (n=20 seeds), QCOP achieves up to 2× wall-clock training speed-up and approximately 40% variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) energy error reduction relative to the unaugmented baseline. A hardware pilot on ibm_nairobi at surface-code distance d=5 (2000 syndrome volumes, 8192 shots each, single calibration window) yields a 1.6× latency reduction and 1.9× LER reduction for the HSD over minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM)—directionally consistent with simulation but quantitatively smaller, indicating noise sources beyond the model. This pilot exercises the HSD alone: the SCE and the OCL have not been run on physical hardware, and the three modules have never been executed jointly on a device. The end-to-end QCOP benefits—speed-up, energy error reduction and variance reduction—are therefore not hardware-validated, and end-to-end hardware validation of all three modules remains future work. Code and model weights are available at https://github.com/hekimoghlu/QCOP.

articles.title: Advancements in bottom-up synthesis routes for monolayer graphene: a review
articles.abstract: The synthesis of monolayer graphene has progressed from exfoliation to bottom-up strategies, enabling increasing atomic-level control. This review compares key routes, chemical vapour deposition (CVD), SiC epitaxy, arc discharge, molecular assembly and single-atom catalysts (SACs) and evaluates their mechanisms, scalability and quality bottlenecks. CVD remains the most mature and scalable approach, delivering centimetre-scale-single-crystal films through optimized substrates, roll-to-roll annealing and dry transfer, yet transfer-induced defects and wafer-scale non-uniformity persist. SiC epitaxy enables transfer-free, wafer-scale graphene with well-aligned domains, but requires high temperatures and costly wafers. Arc discharge offers catalyst-free production of crystalline graphene flakes, although monolayer yield and purity remain limited. Molecular assembly provides unmatched structural programmability and atomic precision in nanoribbons and nanographene islands, typically restricted to micrometre scales and stringent conditions. SAC-mediated growth represents a precision limit, where isolated metal atoms catalyse single-carbon insertion or removal at graphene edges, though current demonstrations remain largely single-event observations. Complementing these routes, artificial intelligence/machine learning is increasingly used for parameter optimization, predictive modelling of domain size/uniformity/defects and automated quality control (convolutional neural network/ generative modelling and YOLO-based defect detection). Overall, industrially viable, defect-free monolayer graphene will require combining scalable growth, transfer-free integration, atomic-precision and AI-enabled closed-loop optimization.

articles.title: Applying psychometrics to large language model simulated populations: recreating the HEXACO personality inventory experiment with generative agents
articles.abstract: Generative agents powered by large language models (LLMs) demonstrate human-like characteristics through sophisticated natural language interactions. Their ability to assume roles and personalities based on predefined character biographies has positioned them as cost-effective substitutes for human participants in social science research. This paper explores the validity of such persona-based agents1 in representing human populations; we recreate the HEXACO personality inventory experiment by surveying 310 GPT-4 powered agents, conducting factor analysis on their responses, and comparing these results to the original findings presented by Ashton et al. (Ashton et al. 2004 J. Pers. Soc. Psychol. 87, 707–721 (doi:10.1037/0022-3514.87.5.707). Our results found (i) a coherent and reliable personality structure was recoverable from the agents’ responses demonstrating partial alignment to the HEXACO framework, (ii) the derived personality dimensions were consistent and reliable within GPT-4, when coupled with a sufficiently curated population, and (iii) cross-model analysis revealed variability in personality profiling, suggesting model-specific biases and limitations. We discuss the practical considerations and challenges encountered during the experiment. This study contributes to the ongoing discourse on the potential benefits and limitations of using generative agents in social science research and provides useful guidance on designing consistent and representative agent personas to maximize coverage and representation of human personality traits, while highlighting potential limitations of applying human psychometric frameworks to generative agents.

articles.title: Can consumers accurately identify loot boxes and loot box receipts?
articles.abstract: Loot boxes are randomized rewards in video games. Meta-analyses suggest relationships between loot box spending and problem gambling symptomatology, and early longitudinal evidence suggests loot box purchasers migrate into conventional gambling at higher rates than non-purchasers. Regulatory responses vary across jurisdictions, and even in jurisdictions that have banned loot boxes, evidence suggests their presence in games remains common. Consequently, consumers are often responsible for regulating their own, and their children’s, loot box purchasing. To effectively achieve this, consumers must first be able to identify loot boxes. Here, we investigated consumer accuracy in identifying critical features of loot boxes. Participants were tasked to identify basic facts about, pictures of, and receipts generated by loot boxes. Parents and non-gamers, compared with non-parents and gamers, respectively, were poorer at identifying loot boxes. Our results suggest that parents and non-gamers may be less equipped to make informed loot box purchasing decisions compared with non-parents/non-guardians and gamers, respectively. This may pose risks for parents and unaware incipient gamers. These are the first findings providing objective evidence about the relative ability of consumers to identify, and thus self-regulate purchases of, loot boxes and suggest that parents and non-gamers may require support to ensure informed purchasing decisions.

articles.title: Can monkeys and apes use sequence order to resolve perceptual ambiguity? A lack of evidence in two rhesus macaques and one language trained bonobo
articles.abstract: In human language, word order impacts how words are categorized and understood (as nouns, verbs etc.). We have demonstrated that this effect extends to non-linguistic stimuli, suggesting that the impact of sequence order on stimulus categorization is a domain-general, rather than language-specific cognitive process. Here, we ask if this process is evolutionarily conserved in other non-human primates. We developed a non-linguistic experiment and tested rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) and bonobos (Pan paniscus). Participants first learned to categorize shapes (as rounded, squared or pointed). We next assessed how they categorized ambiguous morph shapes by combining exemplars from each category. We provided sequential information by training the animals to select shapes in a specified order: rounded, then squared and then pointed. Finally, we assessed whether presentation in specific positions in this learned sequence would impact subsequent categorization of ambiguous morph shapes. In humans, an ambiguous morph was more likely to be categorized as the shape it replaced in a sequence. Non-human primates, however, showed no such effect, categorizing stimuli independent of their position in a sequence.
