articles.title: Microstructural evolution during isothermal tempering of a highly supersaturated metastable austenitic state of a PM high-speed steel
articles.abstract: This study investigates the microstructural evolution of the powder metallurgical high-speed steel PM HS 3-3-4 during isothermal holding within the transformation gap between pearlite and bainite formation. The focus is on the mechanism of carbide spheroidization and the proposed formation of a chemically graded carbide rim. The heat treatments were carried out in a quenching dilatometer, enabling precise control of the thermal cycles and isothermal holding conditions. Spatially resolved analytic microscopy techniques, including scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), Auger electron spectroscopy (AES) and atom probe tomography (APT), image analysis and complementary thermodynamic simulations (MatCalc) were used to characterize the carbide evolution. Isothermal holding increased carbide circularity, carbide volume fraction, and hardness, while MatCalc calculations predict a strong thermodynamic driving force for additional carbide precipitation. The analytic techniques revealed a compositional gradient of approximately 15 nm at the carbide-matrix interface in the isothermally treated condition, compared with a sharp transition of only 2-3 nm in the directly quenched state. This nanometer-scale gradient provides strong evidence for epitaxial, interface-controlled carbide growth and the formation of a chemically graded carbide rim. The associated solute depletion of the surrounding austenite provides a plausible explanation for its reduced stability, reflected by an increase in the martensite start temperature. The combined results demonstrate that isothermal holding promotes interfacial chemical reorganization, offering new insights into carbide spheroidization and providing a basis for tailoring carbide morphology and the resulting mechanical properties through heat treatment.

articles.title: Peridynamic Thermo-Mechanical Modeling of Cracking in Tungsten under Fusion-Relevant Heat Fluxes
articles.abstract: Plasma-facing materials (PFMs) are the primary armor materials in fusion reactors, protecting reactor wall components from extreme heat fluxes, energetic particles, and intense neutron irradiation. These harsh conditions induce thermo-mechanical stresses, irradiation damage, and overall degradation in PFMs. Among these, thermo-mechanical damage induced by extreme heat flux is one of the key factors limiting the lifetime of PFMs. We present a modeling and simulation approach for predicting thermo-mechanical cracking and damage in tungsten, a leading PFM candidate, under fusion-reactor-relevant heat fluxes. Specifically, we study damage induced by cyclic electron beam (e-beam) exposure under different combinations of base temperature and heat flux. We carry out component-scale thermo-mechanical simulations using CabanaPD, a peridynamics fracture mechanics code, informed by experimental data for recrystallized pure tungsten from the JUDITH e-beam facility. The simulations compare well with the experimental classification and enable identification of cracking thresholds across a range of heat fluxes and base temperatures. These predictions can provide detailed insights into the spatial distribution and temporal accumulation of cracks and damage, while offering a pathway for screening candidate PFMs and quantifying their lifespan under fusion-relevant conditions.

articles.title: Perpendicular Magnetization from Crystallite Boundaries in Polycrystalline Antiferromagnetic $γ$-FeMn
articles.abstract: Single-crystalline noncollinear antiferromagnets, such as Mn$_3$Sn, are actively explored as memory media, but they generally require high-temperature growth that is incompatible with industrial-scale device fabrication. Here, we show that polycrystalline films of antiferromagnetic $γ$-FeMn, grown at room temperature, develop a perpendicular magnetization and an anomalous Hall effect, opening an industrially compatible route to antiferromagnetic memory. While conventional noncollinear antiferromagnets demand near-perfect crystal order, $γ$-FeMn films derive their memory-enabling properties from crystal defects, particularly boundaries separating nanoscale crystallites. When the crystallite size $D$ falls below $\approx$ 30 nm, a field-switchable magnetization emerges and increases with the boundary density $\propto 1/D$. This magnetization is accompanied by a room-temperature anomalous Hall conductivity exceeding 10 S/cm, comparable to that of single-crystalline Mn$_3$Sn. Our systematic experimental results, including scanning magnetometry, indicate uncompensated spin moments in the boundaries coupled to the compensated antiferromagnetism within the crystallites. We further find that the perpendicular easy axis of the magnetization is stabilized by residual strain within the $γ$-FeMn film. Our findings in manufacturing-friendly polycrystalline $γ$-FeMn redefine crystal defects as enablers, rather than impediments, for scalable antiferromagnetic memory.

articles.title: Robust Anomalous Hall Effect in Epitaxial Cubic D0$_3$-Fe$_3$Ge Nanoplates Grown by Chemical Vapor Deposition
articles.abstract: The iron-based ferromagnetic materials have emerged as a promising system for spintronics due to their high Curie temperatures and significant anomalous Hall effect (AHE) driven by Berry curvature. While there have been investigations into the epitaxial growth of non-layered iron-based ferromagnetic materials, the realization of high-quality single crystal thin films continues to be a formidable obstacle. Meanwhile, the issues such as grain boundary scattering further hinder their characterization and application. Here, we report the first chemical vapor deposition (CVD) synthesis of single-crystalline cubic D0$_3$-Fe$_3$Ge nanoplates. This compound represents a substantial departure from the conventional hexagonal phases typically observed in the Fe-Ge system. Structural characterizations confirm the cubic lattice and stoichiometric purity of the crystals. Structural analysis identifies a strong epitaxial effect, resulting in a giant compressive strain of ~4.16% at the interface that relaxes gradually toward the surface. The second-harmonic generation (SHG) signals might further reveal that such interfacial strain disrupted the inherent centro-symmetry of the cubic phase. SQUID magnetometry shows robust room-temperature ferromagnetism and clear magnetic anisotropy. Magneto-transport measurements reveal a robust AHE that remains stable at temperatures far exceeding room temperature. The scaling observed between the anomalous Hall resistance and longitudinal resistance strongly suggests that this effect is dominated by the intrinsic Berry curvature mechanism. Furthermore, density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the huge epitaxial strain induces band reconstructions and creates dense spin-orbit coupling gaps near the Fermi level, effectively doubling the anomalous Hall conductivity to match our experimental observations.

articles.title: Robust topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff--Love shells by the Speed Method
articles.abstract: This paper presents a framework for robust topology optimization of Kirchhoff-Love (KL) multi-patch shells using isogeometric analysis and non-matching meshes and provides a CAD-compatible method. The material distribution is optimized via a NURBS-based level set method, enabling accurate boundary representation and seamless export to standard CAD/CAM workflows. The shape derivative is computed using the speed method, yielding a volume-based formulation that avoids boundary approximations and aligns with the isogeometric principle of coarse, high-order discretizations. This eliminates the need for local refinement, adaptive quadrature, or trimming as the descent direction for the compliance and volume objectives are obtained through a biharmonic equation. The framework is extended to robust optimization under uncertainty, accounting for stochastic loading and material properties via Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian Random Fields. Numerical examples demonstrate the method's efficiency and robustness across single- and multi-patch shells, reproducing literature results with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined IGA approaches. The developed methods and tools can be directly extended to problems involving stress-based optimization and risk-averse metrics. The numerical implementations are open-source and available on GitHub.

articles.title: Stabilizing and detecting electron fractionalization in the Hofstadter-Hubbard model
articles.abstract: Motivated by the recent progress in correlated Chern insulator physics in moiré systems, we investigate the half-filled triangular-lattice Hofstadter--Hubbard model and its electron fractionalization. Among various competing non-magnetic states, increasing the orbital flux stabilizes and broadens the $\mathrm{U}(1)_2$ chiral spin liquid phase in the Mott regime. In this exotic regime, the electron is fractionalized into gapped spinons and gapped chargons, whose effective bands are linked to the orbital flux. The convolution of the narrow spinon bands with the gapped chargon excitations produces rich and discernible structures in the electron spectral function and the density of states. These results not only identify the orbital flux as a control parameter for the detailed patterns of electron fractionalization and the nature of the Mott transition, but also provide the key spectral characteristics for the angle-resolved photoemission and scanning tunneling studies of the relevant systems, linking the free-particle band topology to intrinsic topological order in the correlated regime.

articles.title: Super-tetragonal ferroelectric barium titanate through anionic overstoichiometry
articles.abstract: Ferroelectric oxides, characterized by an electrical polarization that is switchable with an electric field, are an appealing class of materials for energy-efficient computing, electronics, and photonics. In thin films, the properties of ferroelectrics are commonly tuned using substrate-imposed epitaxial strain, an approach limited to biaxial strain states and a finite number of available substrates. Here, we demonstrate that is is possible to move beyond conventional epitaxial growth by using pulsed laser deposition under highly non-equilibrium conditions. Specifically, we show that this unconventional processing route allows us to stabilize a super-tetragonal phase of ferroelectric $\text{BaTiO}_3$. The key to this stabilization lies in the insertion of surplus oxygen atoms into the unit cell, resulting in peroxide bond formation that give rise to an aspect ratio of as high as 1.08. Notably, this super-tetragonal phase exhibits an enhanced ferroelectric polarization, reduced coercivity, lower leakage currents, and increased cycling endurance compared to conventional bulk-like $\text{BaTiO}_3$ films. These results, thus, showcase the potential of non-equilibrium growth for defect engineering to obtain emergent phases in complex oxides and tune their physical properties in thin films expanding the scope of traditional epitaxy.

articles.title: Suppression of Grain Boundary Nitrogen Degradation by Boron in Superalloys
articles.abstract: Superalloys enable the hottest sections of jet engines to operate at high temperatures, but environmentally assisted degradation limits their lifetime. In polycrystalline alloys, nitrogen penetrates beneath the protective surface oxides, to produce embrittling grain boundary nitrides. Boron is added in trace amounts to improve grain boundary strength, yet its role, if any, in oxidation-related degradation remains unclear. Here we show that boron segregates to an internal nitride--matrix interface in a Ni/Co-base $γ$/$γ^{\prime}$ strengthened superalloy. Both B-free and B-containing alloys develop stratified chromia/alumina scales at 800~$^{\circ}$C in \SI{100}{\hour}, but the B-free variant produces larger, deeper and more elongated Ti/Nb-rich subsurface grain boundary nitrides. Correlative 4D S/TEM and atom probe tomography identify the particle as a chemically complex B1 nitride and reveal interfacial boron segregation. This shows that trace alloying as an alloy strategy can control damaging internal reaction product precipitation and growth by core-shell segregation.

articles.title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
articles.abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) is essential for developing materials for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications. Here, we present a methodology for high-throughput calculation of LTC across large datasets of compounds sharing a common crystal symmetry. Our approach combines fine-tuning of the MatterSim 1M universal machine-learned interatomic potential with LTC calculations based on the solution of the Boltzmann transport equation. We introduce a symmetry-based few-shot fine-tuning strategy (SBFS-FT) based on low-rank adaptation. In this approach, MatterSim 1M is fine-tuned on a small, carefully selected set of compounds that share a common crystal symmetry. The resulting potential is then applicable for accurate LTC calculations for compounds with this crystal symmetry, even if they were not included in the fine-tuning set. We tested our methodology on datasets of half-Heusler compounds (space group 216), materials with space group 225, and spinels (space group 227). We demonstrated that LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M fine-tuned using SBFS-FT exhibited a mean absolute relative difference from the reference results (obtained using moment tensor potentials and polyMLPs) 2-3 times smaller than that achieved with the non-fine-tuned MatterSim 1M potential. Moreover, the accuracy of LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M after SBFS-FT was comparable to that achieved using the MatterSim 1M potentials individually fine-tuned for each compound. Importantly, SBFS-FT enabled generation of the potential suitable for accurate LTC calculations across large compound datasets substantially faster than fine-tuning of MatterSim 1M for each compound individually, reducing the computational time by approximately a factor of 5-7 for a dataset of 100 compounds.

articles.title: The Spectroscopic Atlas of Excitonic Complexes in hBN-Encapsulated S-TMD Monolayers: From Excitons to Oxcitons and Beyond
articles.abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) encapsulation has transformed the optical spectroscopy of semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers (MLs) by suppressing extrinsic disorder and enabling the resolution of an increasingly complex hierarchy of excitonic states. This Review provides a spectroscopy-oriented framework for understanding and identifying excitonic complexes in hBN-encapsulated Mo- and W-based MLs and their alloys. The discussion covers bright and dark excitons, Rydberg states, charged excitons, biexcitons, phonon-assisted replicas, and higher-order Fermi-sea many-body states, including hexcitons and oxcitons, with an emphasis on the experimental signatures that distinguish them. Particular attention is given to the combined use of photoluminescence and absorption-related spectroscopy, electrostatic gating, polarization analysis, excitation-power and temperature dependences, magnetic fields, and time-resolved measurements to establish microscopic assignments. The role of alloying as an additional degree of freedom for engineering the excitonic hierarchy, spin-valley configuration, and magneto-optical response is also highlighted. By organizing the rapidly expanding phenomenology around experimentally accessible fingerprints rather than individual material systems, this Review aims to provide a practical and broadly applicable guide for identifying, comparing, and engineering excitonic states in high-quality two-dimensional semiconductors.

articles.title: Two-dimensional structures formed by pair potentials: An analytical and numerical study
articles.abstract: Understanding the thickness dependence of the excess energy of thin films and identifying the deviation from the scaling law that holds for thicker films are crucial for predicting the formation of two-dimensional (2D) materials derived from nonlayered structures, commonly referred to as non-van der Waals (non-vdW) 2D materials. Here, we analytically study the excess energy of thin films as a function of the number of layers $N$, assuming pair potentials. We show that the $1/N$ scaling law of the excess energy breaks down in the monolayer limit when the interatomic interactions are long-ranged. The analytical results are confirmed by numerical simulations using the Lennard-Jones and Morse potentials. The present work suggests that non-vdW 2D structures can be formed by pair potentials alone.

articles.title: Vacancy-driven topological transition of a Chern insulator
articles.abstract: We develop a microscopic description of the strong-disorder transition in a Chern insulator using the in-gap ring states bound to individual vacancies. Using Green's function formalism, we construct an energy-dependent Hamiltonian describing their hybridization. In a commensurate periodic vacancy lattice, a Dirac inversion of the zero-energy vacancy kernel accounts for the change in the occupied-state Chern number of the full system. We treat weak positional disorder using the self-consistent Born approximation and numerical disorder averaging, and study independently distributed vacancies using transfer-matrix and multifractal scaling. The local Chern marker and current textures track the transition in real space. Together, these results highlight the role that nonperturbative ring states have as microscopic degrees of freedom through which strong disorder destroys the Chern phase.

articles.title: Zero-group-velocity modes in textured steel plates: experiments and elastic modeling
articles.abstract: Zero-group-velocity (ZGV) resonances are investigated as a non-contact ultrasonic probe of elastic anisotropy in textured steel plates. Directional laser-ultrasonic measurements were performed on 70% cold-rolled Ti-stabilized interstitial-free steel plates in the full-hard and recrystallized condition. Experimental results were compared with predictions based on effective elastic stiffness tensors derived from X-ray diffraction measurements. Classical Voigt-Reuss-Hill estimates and microstructure-resolved finite-element homogenization reproduce the measured angular dependence of the ZGV frequencies well for both states, with the finite-element KUBC/SUBC bounds considerably narrower than the classical Voigt-Reuss bounds. For the full-hard state, agreement with the texture-based model is obtained only after a recovery treatment. This indicates that dislocations present in the full-hard material contribute to its elastic response, an interpretation that is further supported by theoretical estimations. An identifiability analysis shows that the directional ZGV measurements provide access to at least three independently observable combinations of the stiffness tensor components, and concluding suggestions for application in recrystallization monitoring are provided.

articles.title: A compact ultracold strontium experiment
articles.abstract: We describe a compact and simplified experimental setup for the production of ultracold strontium atoms. Thanks to its low-power oven and coil-free Zeeman slower design, the vacuum system has an overall length of only 40cm including oven, Zeeman slower and all-glass science cell. The oven has a power consumption of 14W at 460°C and produces a collimated flux of 3 10^10at/(s cm^2) at this temperature. The laser system employs master-slave laser architecture throughout and requires neither second-harmonic generation nor tapered amplifiers, reducing cost and complexity. The system has been in continuous use for more than a year.

articles.title: A random sampling method to test the weak Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
articles.abstract: We introduce a random sampling method for testing the weak Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (wETH) that is particularly useful for large, sparse Hamiltonians. We test the method on a well-studied Rydberg atom system that exhibits both two- and three-body dipole-dipole interactions. Our results show that our method allows for the study of system sizes significantly beyond the limits of exact diagonalization. We find that the fluctuations in eigenstate expectation values decay as the Hilbert space dimension $D^{-1/2}$, consistent with wETH and in agreement with previous numerical results.

articles.title: Accurate Wichmann-Kroll vacuum polarization calculations with Gaussian basis set
articles.abstract: We apply a large Gaussian basis set of size up to $N = 500$ to calculate the all-order Wichmann-Kroll vacuum polarization correction in highly-charged ion. For a hydrogen-like system, this allows us to obtain an accurate correction value with a level of precision comparable to that of traditional methods. We demonstrate that values of effects that can be calculated as the difference between two quantities, such as the nuclear model correction, converge faster than the absolute value of the correction. We discuss the basis extrapolation methods and show their use in estimating the error due to incomplete convergence. Finally, we show an application of the Gaussian basis set to calculation of the vacuum polarization screening correction in lithium-like ions.

articles.title: An entanglement band structure for general multiqubit states
articles.abstract: Majorana drew a symmetric multiqubit state as points on the Bloch sphere, antipodal to the zeros of its overlap with spin coherent states. Projecting only one qubit of a general state leaves the others in a state that varies with direction. Its entanglement invariants are eigenvalues of a non-Hermitian matrix and form bands over the sphere. Exceptional points appear, without gain or loss, where the entanglement family of the rest changes. Circling one exchanges two bands, so the bands form one Riemann surface. At five qubits it fixes the entanglement class up to finitely many choices.

articles.title: Broadband Mid-Wave Infrared Imaging Enabled by All-Silicon Hyperboloid Metalens
articles.abstract: The mid-wave infrared (MWIR, 3-5 microns) is indispensable for thermal sensing, gas detection, long-range imaging, and free-space optical communications. Meta-optics offer a compact, lightweight, and potentially low-cost alternative to conventional refractive optics, making them attractive for size, weight, and power (SWaP)-constrained systems. However, their strong chromatic dispersion has largely restricted imaging to narrow spectral bands. Here, we demonstrate broadband imaging across the full 3-5 micron MWIR band using a single-layer silicon metasurface coupled with computational reconstruction. Remarkably, the reconstruction model is adapted using only four image captures, overcoming large training data requirements and enabling broadband image recovery despite the strongly wavelength-dependent optical response. In contrast to approaches that engineer complex, dispersion-optimized metalens profiles for broadband operation, our method leverages the wavelength-dependent information encoded by a simple 2cm diameter hyperboloid metalens. We show that this metasurface captures sufficient broadband intensity information for computational reconstruction across the entire MWIR band. These results establish a simple route toward broadband computational meta-optics without requiring broadband achromatic metalens designs, offering a promising platform for compact MWIR imaging systems.

articles.title: Conservation in Every Quantum Measurement Outcome?
articles.abstract: In quantum mechanics, conservation laws are usually understood only statistically and only in the context of unitary evolution: during such evolution, if an observable commutes with the Hamiltonian, its expectation value and Born-rule probability distribution remain unchanged. Individual measurement outcomes, however, disrupt even this weak form of statistical conservation. Recently, though, it has been argued that a stronger, non-statistical form of conservation, valid at the level of individual measurement outcomes, can be recovered. The proposal relies on the claim that any superposition of eigenstates of a conserved quantity must ultimately be prepared relative to another physical system, which serves as the relevant reference frame and remains correlated with the system being prepared. On this enlarged description, the change observed in the measured system is claimed to be exactly compensated by an opposite change in the preparer, thereby restoring conservation at the level of individual measurement outcomes. We analyze this proposal and argue that it faces significant conceptual difficulties. We show that the proposed mechanism is not adequately justified and, moreover, does not establish conservation in individual measurement outcomes as claimed.

articles.title: Convergence Analysis of the Quantum Blahut-Arimoto Algorithm and the Contraction Coefficient of Qubit Amplitude-Damping Channels
articles.abstract: In this work, we investigate the convergence rate of the quantum Blahut-Arimoto (BA) algorithm proposed for computing the coherent information of less noisy quantum channels. Previous work established exponential convergence under certain restrictive assumptions on the channel. Using a Taylor expansion around a positive definite optimizer, we show that, for an injective degradable channel whose degrading channel has a relative-entropy contraction coefficient strictly less than one, the algorithm converges at an exponential rate after sufficiently many iterations. We further verify this condition for qubit amplitude-damping (AD) channels in the relevant parameter regime. In addition, by analyzing the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori (BKM) metric on the Bloch ball, we derive an explicit characterization of the relative-entropy contraction coefficient of qubit AD channels. The proposed approach is further extended to calculate the relative contraction coefficient and the relative expansion coefficient of two qubit AD channels.

articles.title: DiffVortex: A quantum-inspired fast solver for incompressible flows
articles.abstract: Matrix-product-state (MPS) and quantized tensor-train (QTT) representations offer a promising framework for computational fluid dynamics, with logarithmic run time and memory scaling in mesh size when bond dimensions remain bounded. Existing MPS-based solvers are Eulerian: they compress velocity fields and enforce immersed-body boundary conditions through static masks or body-fitted coordinates. Moving or flexible bodies complicate this approach: deformation requires updating MPS masks every time step, while filamentary vorticity in high-Reynolds-number flows may resist low-rank compression. We propose a complementary approach: compress the Biot--Savart kernel rather than the flow state, evolve vorticity using Lagrangian vortex particles, and represent immersed bodies by bound vortex sheets on Lagrangian surface points. Our main theoretical result is a lifting theorem: QTT rank $r$ of the kernel implies matrix-product-operator (MPO) rank at most $2^d r$ for the corresponding convolution operator in $d$ dimensions, independent of grid resolution. This bound is sharp for our interleaved ordering. With quantics tensor cross interpolation, the moment-to-local stage of a single-level fast multipole method becomes a precomputed tensor-network contraction with quasi-linear complexity, retaining Lagrangian flexibility for immersed bodies. Our PyTorch implementation (\texttt{DiffVortex}) is end-to-end differentiable, runs on GPUs, and handles $6.7\times10^{7}$ particles on a single device. We validate against reference vortex-method results for an impulsively started cylinder and exact and reference solutions for inviscid elliptical vortices. We also demonstrate two-dimensional flows past rigidly moving, multiple, and deforming bodies, including gradients propagated through the full time integration.

articles.title: A mechanistic theory of planning in prefrontal cortex
articles.abstract: Planning is critical for adaptive behaviour in a changing world, because it lets us anticipate the future and adjust our actions accordingly. While prefrontal cortex is crucial for this process, it remains unknown how planning is implemented in neural circuits. Prefrontal representations were recently discovered in simpler sequence memory tasks, where different populations of neurons represent different future time points. We demonstrate that combining such representations with the ubiquitous principle of neural attractor dynamics allows circuits to solve much richer problems, including planning. This is achieved by embedding the environment structure directly in synaptic connections to implement an attractor network that infers desirable futures. The resulting ‘spacetime attractor’ excels at planning in challenging tasks known to depend on the prefrontal cortex. Recurrent neural networks trained by gradient descent on such tasks learn a solution that precisely recapitulates the spacetime attractor – in representation, in dynamics, and in connectivity. Analyses of networks trained across different environment structures reveal a generalisation mechanism that rapidly reconfigures the world model used for planning, without the need for synaptic plasticity. The spacetime attractor is a testable mechanistic theory of planning. If true, it would provide a path towards detailed mechanistic understanding of how prefrontal cortex structures adaptive behaviour.

articles.title: Complementary stable and dynamic prelimbic ensembles encode learned threat value underlying generalization and discrimination
articles.abstract: Adaptive behavior requires assigning emotional value to sensory cues and generalizing to similar stimuli. The prelimbic cortex (PL) is critical for threat expression and discrimination, yet its neuronal ensembles undergo substantial turnover over time. How stable population codes emerge despite this reorganization remains unknown. Using longitudinal calcium imaging in freely moving mice, we tracked PL activity for 30 days during auditory discriminative fear learning and retrieval. Despite substantial ensemble turnover, stable graded representations persisted in PL populations. A generalized linear model showed that the tone threat value explained graded activity better than freezing, indicating that PL primarily encodes stimulus significance. Population similarity across stimulus presentations was highest for shock-associated and highly generalized tones, suggesting a stable population code underlying threat generalization. Stable neurons preserved graded gradients across sessions, whereas learning modulated the rate of dynamic frequency-selective neurons. Together, these populations enabled stable threat-value coding despite ongoing ensemble reorganization.

articles.title: Correction: Inhibitors of the small membrane (M) protein viroporin prevent Zika virus infection
Correction: Stall force measurement of the kinesin-3 motor KIF1A using a programmable DNA origami nanospring
Novel but stable endosymbionts have contrasting effects on aphid dispersal and plant feeding damage in the cereal pest Diuraphis noxia
articles.abstract: Endosymbiotic bacteria can affect many ecological attributes of their insect hosts, including (in herbivorous insects) how they interact with plants where they feed. This raises the issue of whether deliberate endosymbiont introductions could be used to decrease crop damage caused by insect pests. Here, we investigate how transinfecting Rickettsiella viridis and Regiella insecticola endosymbionts into a novel pest aphid host, the Russian wheat aphid (Diuraphis noxia), influences population growth, alate production, dispersal ability, and crop damage. Both the Rickettsiella (originating from pea aphids) and Regiella (from green peach aphids) were stably maintained in their new host where they had contrasting effects. Rickettsiella increased the severity of aphid feeding damage on wheat and barley, resulting in greater leaf loss, chlorotic streaking, and higher aphid populations, whereas Regiella reduced aphid population growth and the severity of feeding damage by aphids. Their effects on dispersal morphology also differed: Regiella had no detectable impact on alate incidence, while Rickettsiella consistently suppressed wing formation in small cages, and in larger mesocosms with multiple wheat plants this endosymbiont suppressed dispersal. Endosymbiont-mediated changes in feeding damage did not involve the main plant immune response pathways: transinfected and wild type aphids induced similar levels of jasmonic acid, jasmonic acid-isoleucine, and salicylic acid in plant tissues, even though these plant defenses were strongly activated during aphid feeding. Novel endosymbionts can therefore modulate the severity of plant feeding damage by aphids as well as influencing aphid dispersal. Potential applications in controlling pest D. noxia populations are discussed.

articles.title: Strong mnemonic prediction errors increase cognitive control, attention, and arousal
articles.abstract: Ongoing experience is continuously processed in the context of past events. Divergence between current experience and memory-based predictions (i.e., a mnemonic prediction error; MPE) is theorized to be a signal that encoding, as opposed to retrieval, should be prioritized. We asked how MPEs place demands on control and attention-related processes, and whether these demands differ as a function of prediction strength. We investigated these questions across two experiments, wherein we recorded scalp electroencephalography and/or pupillometry as 101 young human adults performed an associative memory task. Strong MPEs, more so than weak MPEs, increased physiological indices of cognitive control (frontal theta), attention (posterior alpha and pupil size), and arousal (pupil size). Greater cognitive control (frontal theta) during strong MPEs promoted better learning of prediction-violating (i.e., unexpected) stimuli. Collectively, these findings reveal multiple pathways through which the mind and brain respond adaptively to violations of strong mnemonic predictions.

articles.title: p66Shc mediates SUMO2-induced endothelial dysfunction
articles.abstract: Sumoylation is a post-translational modification that can regulate different physiological functions. Increased sumoylation, specifically conjugation of SUMO2/3 (small ubiquitin-like modifier 2/3), is detrimental to vascular health. However, the molecular mechanism mediating this effect is poorly understood. We used cell-based assays and mass spectrometry to show that p66Shc is a direct target of SUMO2 and that SUMO2 regulates p66Shc function via lysine-81 modification. To determine the effects of SUMO2-p66ShcK81 on vascular function, we generated Shc1K81R mice and crossbred them toLdlr-/- mice to induce hyperlipidemia. Next, to determine p66ShcK81-SUMO2ylation-induced changes in endothelial cell signaling, we performed mass spectrometry followed by Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. Our data reveal that p66Shc mediates the effects of SUMO2 on endothelial cells. Mass spectrometry identified that SUMO2 modified lysine-81 in the unique collagen homology-2 domain of p66Shc. SUMO2ylation of p66Shc increased phosphorylation at serine-36, causing it to translocate to the mitochondria, a step critical for the oxidative function of p66Shc. Notably, sumoylation-deficient p66Shc (p66ShcK81R) was resistant to SUMO2-induced p66ShcS36 phosphorylation and mitochondrial translocation. Shc1K81R mice were resistant to endothelial dysfunction induced by SUMO2ylation and hyperlipidemia. Ingenuity Pathway Analysis revealed multiple signaling pathways regulated by p66ShcK81-SUMO2ylation in endothelial cells, highlighting JAK-STAT as a major pathway affected by SUMO2-p66ShcK81. Collectively, our work reveals SUMO2-p66Shc signaling as a fundamental regulator of vascular endothelial function. We discovered that p66ShcK81 is an upstream modification regulating p66Shc signaling and mediates hyperlipidemia-induced endothelial dysfunction and oxidative stress.

articles.title: Achieving Ordered-Cationic-Vacancy-Mediated Photohole Transfer Dynamics via Phase and Facet Engineering toward Highly Efficient Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting
articles.abstract: Defect engineering is promising to solve the photocarrier dynamics mismatch between rapid bulk recombination and sluggish surface oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in PEC water splitting but is limited by forming random or bulk defects. Herein, we adopt a phase and facet modulation strategy to construct a 2D defective spinel β-In2S3 photoanode with highly exposed, well-ordered indium vacancies (VIn). These VIn introduce a shallow acceptor level near the valence band (VB), which induces selective photohole capture to VIn shallow traps. The efficient and fast (∼0.13 ps) photohole transfer from the VB to the VIn state and the sharply elongated lifetime for photoholes accumulated at VIn, by facilitating band-edge exciton dissociation, induce separation efficiency nearly 100% even at low bias. Meanwhile, surface VIn lowers the OER barrier by boosting the conversion of *OH to *O and promotes surface reaction kinetics, enabling the photohole transfer efficiency to reach 95%. Thus, VIn simultaneously acts as photohole-capture centers and surface-active sites to optimize photohole separation and interfacial transfer dynamics. Through introducing and exposing ordered VIn to reaction interfaces, the β-In2S3-2D photoanode achieves a record-high photocurrent density of 9.7 mA cm–2 at 1.23 VRHE and an IPCE reaching 80% without hole scavengers. Such a regulation mechanism can guide reverse design of defective semiconductor photoanodes for efficient PEC conversion.

articles.title: Adsorbate Site Hopping—More Facts and Fiction: Driving Forces and Relevance for Heterogeneous Catalysis
articles.abstract: Adsorbate site hopping, defined here as surface-confined migration of adsorbed species or adsorbate equivalents between distinct sites, is a widespread phenomenon in heterogeneous catalysis and includes spillover between different surface phases. Because it enables communication between spatially separated functionalities, site hopping has often been viewed as a route to bifunctional catalytic synergy and, in some cases, to performance beyond constraints imposed by Brønsted–Evans–Polanyi relationships. However, its catalytic value is conditional rather than universal. Downhill migration to a stronger binding site may increase local barriers for subsequent transformation or introduce site-regeneration penalties, while kinetically accessible hopping may remain irrelevant if it does not reduce the energetic span of the catalytic cycle. In addition, apparent rate enhancements assigned to site hopping can arise from other modes of intersite communication, including desorption–readsorption, subsurface or bulk diffusion, ion–electron intersite coupling, catalyst restructuring, or changes in active-site identity. This Perspective develops a thermodynamic and kinetic framework for distinguishing these processes and assessing when site hopping becomes catalytically consequential. We discuss driving forces, hopping barriers, coverage and dynamic surface effects, kinetic signatures, and diagnostic pitfalls, with the aim of clarifying when site hopping can be used as a catalyst design principle.

articles.title: Diastereodivergent Synthesis of 8,12-Guaianolides Using Engineered P450 BM3
articles.abstract: 8,12-Guaianolides are a class of sesquiterpene lactones that exhibit diverse biological activities, which are often strongly influenced by structural variations, including the stereochemistry of the C8 oxygen substituent. Here, we report a concise, diastereodivergent approach to both 8α,12- and 8β,12-guaianolide scaffolds from santonin-derived triene 5 by combining engineered cytochrome P450 BM3-catalyzed allylic C–H hydroxylation with a photochemical rearrangement. The P450 BM3 mutant LG-23 selectively hydroxylates the C8α position of 5, whereas a single additional mutation, L437I, inverts the facial selectivity to favor C8β hydroxylation. Structure-guided mutagenesis and docking studies suggest that the β-methyl group of Ile437 remodels the active site and enforces a flipped substrate binding mode that directs the opposite C8 C–H bond toward the heme iron. The utility of this enzymatic stereochemical switch was demonstrated by the synthesis of the 8α,12-guaianolides xerantholide (1) and mikanokryptin (2) and the 8β,12-guaianolide 11,13-dehydroachalensolide (4). This study demonstrates that a single active-site mutation in P450 BM3 can switch the facial selectivity of C–H hydroxylation at one carbon center, providing a strategy for stereodivergent enzymatic oxidation in complex-molecule synthesis.

articles.title: Extremely High Turnover Number and Turnover Frequency of an Iron Chlorin Complex for Photocatalytic Water Oxidation
articles.abstract: Highly active water oxidation catalysts based on earth-abundant elements are strongly demanded for practical application of artificial photosynthesis. An iron complex with a chlorin ligand derived from chlorophyll-a demonstrated the highest turnover frequency (= 21.3 ± 0.3 s–1) and turnover number (= 6920 ± 110) among homogeneous catalysts reported for photocatalytic water oxidation utilizing [RuII(bpy)3]2+ (bpy: 2,2′-bipyridine) and S2O82– as a photosensitizer and a sacrificial electron acceptor, respectively. The molecular nature of the Fe chlorin complex during the photocatalytic water oxidation was confirmed by dynamic light scattering analysis and electrospray ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry. Also, kinetic studies suggested that the rate-determining step is O–O bond formation via coupling of two high-valent iron–oxo species formed by three-electron oxidation of the mononuclear Fe chlorin unit with water. The high planarity of the chlorin ligand enables the high-valent iron–oxo species to approach another iron–oxo unit closely, thereby facilitating O–O bond formation.

articles.title: Gold(I)-Catalyzed Asymmetric Transformations of 1-(1-Alkynyl)cyclobutyl Ketones: Access to Enantioenriched Cyclopenta[ b ]furans Bearing Vicinal Bridged Quaternary Stereocenters
articles.abstract: Present herein is a gold(I)-catalyzed asymmetric cascade reaction of 1-(1-alkynyl)cyclobutyl ketones. Upon activation by a chiral phosphoric-acid-tethered gold(I) complex, they undertake intramolecular 5-endo-dig cyclization, and the resulting oxocarbenium species engage in an asymmetric 1,2-alkyl migration to generate gold-containing cyclopenta[b]furan carbocations, which can be intercepted by a broad range of nucleophiles, including indoles, pyrroles, alcohols, and amines, providing efficient access to synthetically challenging tetrahydro-4H-cyclopenta[b]furans bearing vicinal bridged quaternary stereocenters with fair to high enantioselectivity. The intermediates can also participate in (3 + 2) annulations with suitable 1,3-dipoles to afford polycyclic architectures with high molecular complexity. Mechanistic studies and density function theory calculations elucidate the key factors governing the catalytic pathways and stereochemical outcomes.

articles.title: Influence of Extraframework Metal Species on the Kinetics and Spatial Distribution of Coke during Methanol-to-Hydrocarbons Conversion over ZSM-5 Catalysts
articles.abstract: The incorporation of selected extraframework cations is a common approach to tuning the performance of zeolite catalysts in industrially relevant methanol-to-hydrocarbons (MTH) conversion processes, although the mechanistic origin of their effects remains incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the relationships between MTH and coking kinetics, the nature and distribution of coke deposits, and the positions of extraframework calcium and zinc species in the ZSM-5 catalyst, which promote alkene and aromatic formation, respectively. At comparable Brønsted acid site densities, enhanced aromatics formation over zinc-containing ZSM-5 is accompanied by a 2× higher intrinsic MTH activity and a 150× faster active site loss than over the calcium-containing catalyst. Photoelectron photoion coincidence spectroscopy shows that faster coke-forming kinetics over the zinc-containing catalyst is linked to enhanced formaldehyde formation via methanol dehydrogenation, triggering a cascade of intermediates, such as dienes and aromatics, a pathway inhibited in the calcium-containing catalyst. This also leads to a higher fraction of high-molecular-weight coke in the zinc-containing catalyst and a predominance of surface graphitic coke in the calcium-containing catalyst, as revealed by complementary thermogravimetric, microscopic, and spectroscopic analyses. Powder neutron diffraction indicates that coke preferentially occupies the channel intersections and extends along the straight channels in both catalysts. However, the average coke orientation differs as calcium-containing ZSM-5 comprises more distorted intrapore aromatic deposits, whereas zinc-containing ZSM-5 accommodates more planar aromatic coke. The confinement of coke in micropores is consistent with the preferential location of cations determined by high-resolution X-ray diffraction analysis, which shows that calcium occupies two sites in the sinusoidal channels, with one of these pointing toward the channel intersections, whereas the smaller zinc-associated density is found at sites in five- and six-membered rings between main channels, at the expense of occupancy of sinusoidal channel-based positions. Consequently, faster coke-forming kinetics linked to the dehydrogenation activity of extraframework zinc species, together with lower spatial strain at channel intersections, favor the formation of more condensed, planar-like coke in zinc-containing catalysts. Conversely, the larger size and higher channel occupancy of calcium sites destabilize aromatics and hinder coke formation in this key intersecting zone. These results show that extraframework species influence not only the reaction kinetics but also the local organization and orientation of confined coke, in part through steric constraints associated with their crystallographic location.

articles.title: Rhodium-Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroformylation of Vinyl Ethers as a Key Step in the Synthesis of Chiral Fine Chemicals
articles.abstract: The rhodium-catalyzed asymmetric hydroformylation (AHF) of vinyl ethers provides a powerful synthetic step to yield chiral aldehydes as products or intermediates for industrially relevant fine chemicals. Out of the 40 chiral ligands tested, the phosphine-phosphorodiamidite (S,S,RP,S)-BettiPhos L7 and the phosphine-phosphoramidite ligand L6 performed best in this transformation, combining high activity, regio- and enantioselectivity. Branched 2-aryloxypropionaldehydes (16 examples) were obtained with b/l-ratios ranging from 3.1:1 to exclusive branched products, and with enantioselectivities between 79 and 94% ee. Interestingly, for these substrates, the selective decomposition of the linear aldehydes to the respective arenols and acrolein via β-hydride elimination was observed. Branched 2-alkyloxypropionaldehydes (3 examples) were obtained with fair b/l-ratios (1.7:1–2.6:1) and good to high enantioselectivities (85–95% ee). The utility of this transformation was demonstrated by synthesizing the commercial herbicide (R)-Mecoprop on a gram scale in 69% yield and 91% ee via hydroformylation of 4-chloro-2-methyl-1-(vinyloxy)benzene, followed by oxidation. The catalytic system could also be used under slightly modified reaction conditions for reductive asymmetric hydroformylation to produce in one-pot chiral 2-aryloxypropanols. The synthetic potential was further explored by applying the tandem asymmetric hydrohydrazonemethylation (AHHM) followed by reduction, yielding γ-chiral N′-substituted acetohydrazides as shown for 6 examples. Hydrogenolysis of the crude product mixtures results in the corresponding chiral primary amines, as demonstrated in the synthesis of 2-phenoxypropanamine from (vinyloxy)benzene with an overall yield of 74% and 94% ee on a gram scale. Moreover, another tandem reaction—specifically, the asymmetric hydrosulfiniminomethylation (AHSM)—enables access to halogen-containing chiral primary amines, as demonstrated by the synthesis of 2-(4-chlorophenoxy)propanamine in an overall yield of 53% and >99% ee.

articles.title: Cavity-Selective Host–Guest Assembly for Modular Buried-Interface Engineering in Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Buried-interface engineering is critical for inverted perovskite solar cells, yet integrating anchoring, charge transport, electrostatic regulation, and defect passivation within single molecular systems often creates intrinsic trade-offs. Here, we use cavity-selective host–guest recognition to construct a modular, recognition-directed interface. The cavity of dipolar 4-tert-butylsulfonylcalix[4]arene (tBSCA) selectively accommodates the terminal phenyl group of substrate-anchored Ph-4PACz. Comparisons with a structurally related calixarene analogue and competing inclusion orientations identify a thermodynamically preferred Ph-4PACz-tBSCA configuration, distinguishing cavity-selective association from nonspecific interactions. This preferred configuration underpins a preferentially organized dipolar interface that retains Ph-4PACz-mediated anchoring and charge transport while enabling tBSCA to regulate interfacial electrostatics, reduce interfacial defect sites, and suppress defect-assisted halide migration and interfacial accumulation. The resulting devices achieve a PCE of 27.36% (certified at 26.74%), and a 110 cm2 module delivers a certified efficiency of 22.61%. These results demonstrate configuration-selective molecular recognition as a strategy for the modular organization of complementary functions at buried perovskite interfaces.

articles.title: Charge-Density-Dependent Ionomer Effects in Pure-Water CO2 Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Pure-water membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) represent a promising strategy to eliminate (bi)carbonate salt precipitation for electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2R). However, the absence of alkali metal cations fundamentally restricts CO2 activation and intermediate stabilization, thereby reducing catalytic performance. Here, we overcome this limitation by identifying the ionomer charge density as a key molecular-level parameter associated with pure-water CO2R. By comparing anion-exchange ionomers with varying charge characteristics, we reveal that high-charge-density ionomer (HCDI) introduces a favorable catalyst–membrane interfacial environment, enabling superior macroscopic CO2R performance. HCDI-enabled MEAs achieve >99% CO Faradaic efficiency at 100 mA cm–2 and sustain ∼92% at 1000 mA cm–2. In situ diagnosis and electrochemical characterization reveal that the HCDI-functionalized interface produces a substantial *CO signal, while concurrently suppressing hydrogen evolution. By decoupling cation effects from liquid electrolytes, these findings support interfacial ionomer charge density as a useful comparative parameter for pure-water CO2 MEA electrolyzers.

articles.title: Macroporous Interlayers Stabilize Long-Lived Hole Polarons in Organic Semiconductor Photoanodes
articles.abstract: Integrating alternative oxidation reactions (AORs) into photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems is promising for unassisted hydrogen production and value-added chemical synthesis, yet organic semiconductor (OS) photoanodes suffer from poor charge extraction and short carrier lifetimes. Here, we address this bottleneck by stabilizing long-lived hole polarons through macroporous tin oxide (mcSnO2) interlayers. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that accelerated electron extraction through mcSnO2 stabilizes hole polaron states, substantially prolonging carrier lifetimes. Consequently, the optimized organic photoanodes outperform bare counterparts by more than 5.5-fold, retaining 74% of their initial photocurrent over 15 h for iodide oxidation and 61% over 35 h for ascorbic acid oxidation. Furthermore, integrating this robust organic photoanode with an OS-based photocathode enables the first bias-free organic PEC tandem cell coupling hydrogen evolution with AORs, delivering a remarkable solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 1.4%. These findings establish interfacial carrier lifetime engineering as an effective strategy for realizing high-performance and durable organic PEC systems.

articles.title: Achieving Robust Ferroelectric Properties of Hf0.6Zr0.4O2 Thin Films through the Pseudofield-Inducing Effect of Al0.85Sc0.15N Bottom Electrode
articles.abstract: Although ferroelectric (FE) Zr-doped HfO2 (HZO) is a promising material for ferroelectric random-access memory (FeRAM), achieving high remnant polarization (Pr) with a low coercive field (EC) at film thicknesses ≲10 nm remains challenging. This work demonstrates a multifunctional bottom electrode (BE) strategy by inserting a pristine, down-poled ferroelectric Al1–xScxN (ASN) layer into the BE, thereby inducing high mechanical stress and an internal field during HZO crystallization. The pristine down-polarization of ASN increased the c-axis preference of the overlying HZO film, as indicated by the contrast in the electrical characteristics and surface potential responses depending on the ASN poling direction. The ASN-containing BE imposes additional in-plane tensile stress on HZO due to ASN’s low thermal expansion coefficient, facilitating orthorhombic phase formation. Consequently, 9 nm-thick HZO on the ASN-containing BE exhibits a large 2Pr of 81 μC/cm2 by conventional polarization-electric field (P-E) measurement and 68 μC/cm2 by positive-up-negative-down (PUND) compared with that of the TiN BE (43 μC/cm2, and 41 μC/cm2) with a pristine negative-bias imprint. These effects enable a high 2Pr/EC ratio without a significant increase in EC after wake-up, resulting in faster switching characteristics. Furthermore, it also enables the 5 nm-thick HZO film to overcome the pristine pinched hysteresis associated with tetragonal-phase stabilization, thereby achieving robust ferroelectric performance while suppressing wake-up behavior.

articles.title: Crown Ether-Functionalized Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Monovalent Cation Separation
articles.abstract: Membrane-based separation offers a highly promising paradigm for the precise extraction of monovalent cations, which is critical for bioinspired engineering and advanced ion-separation applications. However, efficient discrimination among these cations remains profoundly challenging owing to their nearly identical valence states and comparable subnanometer hydrated diameters. Herein, we report the rational design and fabrication of crown ether (CE)-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that achieve efficient mono/monovalent cation separation while maintaining rapid ion transport. The integration of CE moieties into the framework architectures plays a dual role: narrowing the channels to the angstrom scale while simultaneously serving as specific recognition sites for target cations through host–guest interactions. Consequently, the optimal CE-functionalized TFP-TDA-2 COF membrane exhibits an exceptional K+/Na+ selectivity of 64 with a K+ permeation rate of 41.2 mmol m–2 h–1, surpassing previously reported COF membranes. Theoretical simulations reveal that, while the COF channels provide rapid transport pathway, synergistic CE recognition substantially lowers the thermodynamic dehydration and translocation barrier for K+ relative to Na+. Furthermore, the modular nature of this strategy enables the specific recognition of other targeted cations through precise side-chain engineering by covalently anchoring different crown ether derivatives. This study demonstrates an effective structural engineering strategy for efficient monovalent cation separation, offering an approach for the development of next-generation, single-ion-selective membranes for broad real-world applications.

articles.title: Low Energy Excitations in a [4]Triangulene Honeycomb Antiferromagnet
articles.abstract: Carbon-based synthetic lattices offer a versatile platform for the realization and control of correlated quantum effects at the nanoscale. Advances in on-surface synthesis have enabled the fabrication of increasingly complex molecular frameworks, providing opportunities for the exploration and engineering of custom tailored electronic and magnetic phases. Here, we report the design, on-surface synthesis, and characterization of a two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic framework (COF) assembled from D3h symmetric S = 3/2 [4]triangulene building blocks arranged in a honeycomb structure. Combined scanning probe microscopy and spectroscopy, corroborated by first-principles density functional theory (DFT) and GW calculations, establish an antiferromagnetic (AFM) insulating ground state. Low energy spectroscopy resolves spin excitations in both one-dimensional (1D) chains and extended 2D networks, providing direct insight into the emergent spin dynamics and establishing a modular platform to explore quantum magnetism in a π-conjugated organic system.

articles.title: Monolithic 3D Stacked Carbon Nanotube/Indium–Tin–Oxide Complementary Transistors for High-Frequency Logic and Sense Amplifier Integration with Memory
articles.abstract: Complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) maximize 3D integration density but face two fundamental bottlenecks: the stringent thermal budget of silicon-based sequential stacking and the inherent electrical mismatches in homogeneous material systems. To overcome these challenges, we demonstrate a monolithic 3D-stacked heterogeneous CFET architecture integrating back-end-of-line (BEOL)-compatible p-type carbon nanotube (CNT) and n-type indium–tin–oxide (ITO) channels. Both materials exhibit high carrier mobility and low-temperature process, which simultaneously resolve the bipolar transport disparity and mitigate thermal degradation. Consequently, the resulting CFET inverters exhibit favorable statistical uniformity and symmetric transfer characteristics, enabling the fabrication of versatile logic gates. Besides, a 5-stage ring oscillator (RO) achieves a high frequency of 334 MHz, with a 0.3 ns stage delay, demonstrating potential applications of CFET in high-speed digital circuits. Furthermore, bridging logic and memory, a CFET-based sense amplifier (SA) is integrated with an ITO-based planar capacitorless (2T0C) dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) cell. This hybrid system achieves data write/read operations and signal amplification, providing an architectural platform for next-generation ultradense 3D logic and memory systems.

articles.title: Multi-Terminal Reconfigurable Silver Nanowire Network for Associative-Learning-Like Response and Path Optimization
articles.abstract: Emulating associative-learning-like responses and hardware-state-guided path optimization using reconfigurable physical networks offers a promising route toward adaptive neuromorphic hardware. Herein, a multiterminal reconfigurable Ag nanowire network is presented. This network exhibits a honeybee-inspired associative learning response and provides experimentally measured conductance states for ant colony pathfinding simulations. By employing a multielectrode array to deliver synchronized odor-like and nectar-like electrical stimuli, the network dynamically reconfigures its conductance pathways in a training-dependent manner. Following training, the postsynaptic current increases by 2 orders of magnitude after the first learning cycle and reaches a sustained suprathreshold level after three cycles, demonstrating that the device can simulate long-term memory consolidation. Software simulations further show that the experimentally measured Ag NW learning states can modulate a handwritten digit recognition model through a hardware-derived memory gate, enabling conditioned-stimulus-only recognition to improve progressively during associative learning. Furthermore, specific stimulation protocols reconfigure the conductance pathways of the Ag NW network, and the resulting hardware conductance states are used as weighting factors in ant-colony-inspired software simulations. With these hardware-derived weights, the simulated optimal path length is reduced from 1643.54 units to 1415.18 units, corresponding to an improvement of approximately 14% in path-search efficiency. This study highlights the potential of integrating reconfigurable physical networks with bioinspired algorithms, offering a hardware-software codesign platform for future adaptive neuromorphic systems.

articles.title: Nanomesh Bioelectronics Inspired by Basement Membrane for In Situ Monitoring of Oxidative Stress at the Alveolar-Capillary Barrier
articles.abstract: Inhalable pollutants can cross the alveolar-capillary barrier into the bloodstream, and pollutant-elicited oxidative stress at this barrier is a well-recognized pathogenic driver of systemic diseases. However, direct quantification of oxidative stress at the dynamic alveolar-capillary barrier has remained unattainable due to the lack of sensing tools, substantially limiting our understanding of pollutant toxicology and associated pathogenesis. Herein, we develop nanomesh bioelectronics that simultaneously function as a basement membrane analogue and an electrochemical sensor. The bioelectronic interface recapitulates the native basement membrane’s nanofibrous architecture, ultrathin geometry, high permeability, and mechanical properties, while exhibiting stable electrochemical responses to H2O2 under cyclic stretching. When incorporated into lung-on-a-chip, the bioelectronics enable simultaneous reconstruction of the alveolar-capillary barrier and in situ quantification of oxidative stress during respiratory stretching. Using benzo[a]pyrene as a model carcinogenic pollutant, we uncover a biphasic regulatory role of vascular endothelium: an intact endothelium reinforces epithelial resistance to pollutant stimuli, whereas endothelial dysfunction converts protective crosstalk into pathological oxidative amplification. Rat models further confirm that systemic vascular health shapes pulmonary responses to environmental insults. The proposed bioelectronics provide a versatile tool for engineering biological barriers and dissecting intercompartmental crosstalk.

articles.title: Optical Fourier Surfaces for Free-Space Computer-Generated Holography
articles.abstract: Computer-generated holography can shape electromagnetic fields by encoding wavefront information in nanostructured surfaces. However, despite significant progress, hologram designs for visible and near-infrared wavelengths remain largely limited by fabrication constraints. Most implementations rely on lithographic methods that produce discretized surfaces that do not match the wave nature of light. Further advances would benefit from accurate, continuous (grayscale) control of interfacial profiles, which would allow straightforward design principles from Fourier optics to be applied. In this work, we introduce optical Fourier surfaces as a versatile, intuitive platform for free-space computer-generated holograms. Exploiting these arbitrarily wavy surfaces, we demonstrate three different design strategies for computer-generated holography. First, we use an analytical linear design approach based on sinusoidal lenses and gratings as fundamental holographic building blocks. Second, we enhance diffraction efficiencies through an iterative Fourier-transform algorithm. Finally, we extend our framework with differentiable inverse design, creating wavelength-multiplexed holograms that reconstruct distinct diffraction responses in a predefined image plane. Our results combine advanced thermal scanning-probe lithography with flexible design strategies to create useful structures for photonic applications, particularly in settings where rapid prototyping is crucial.

articles.title: Peptide Coacervates with Cathepsin B-Triggered Intracellular Cargo Release
articles.abstract: Understanding the molecular grammar of liquid–liquid phase separation has enabled rational design of peptide coacervates as intracellular therapeutic carriers with tunable viscoelasticity, controlled cargo partitioning, and enhanced cellular uptake. However, sequence-level determinants governing coacervate disassembly remain poorly characterized. Encoding protease-recognition motifs within phase-separating peptides offers controlled, localized catalytic disassembly without requiring global perturbation via macroscopic triggers such as pH, ionic strength, temperature, or redox potential. Yet, enzymatic cleavage of coacervates is spatially biased and constrained by limited enzyme partitioning, restricted substrate accessibility, and altered kinetics relative to the dilute phase. Here, we test whether the lysosomal protease cathepsin B (CatB)─often upregulated in cancer cells─acts on coacervates assembled from phase-separating peptides encoding CatB-recognition motifs to enable intracellular cargo release in cancer cells. Common CatB-recognition motifs (GFLG and EVCit), developed for linker-based delivery systems under dilute conditions, preserved phase separation but exhibited poor CatB-triggered cleavage and cargo release. In contrast, a de novo motif, FRFV, designed from CatB subsite preferences, retained catalytic activity as confirmed by mass spectrometry and enabled protease-triggered cargo release in vitro and in cancer cells. Thus, protease-recognition motifs require reevaluation within dense-phase architectures to enable efficient intracellular cargo release through coacervate disassembly.

articles.title: Sliding Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions with Ultrahigh Tunneling Electroresistance
articles.abstract: Sliding ferroelectricity in van der Waals materials offers an appealing route to compact, nonvolatile, atomically thin ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) with low switching energy, but achieving a large resistance contrast in such devices remains challenging because the weak out-of-plane polarization provides limited electrostatic modulation of the tunneling barrier. Here, using bilayer rhombohedral MoS2 as a sliding ferroelectric barrier, we demonstrate room-temperature sliding FTJs with tunneling electroresistance (TER) values exceeding 3.2 × 105. We show that this giant contrast arises from a height–width hybrid tunneling mechanism, in which polarization reversal simultaneously modulates the tunnel barrier height and switches a nanoscale interfacial depletion width, yielding exponential amplification of the tunneling contrast. Spatially resolved tunneling, piezoresponse, and Raman measurements reveal that local strain, rather than ferroelectric domain walls, dominates spatial variations in the TER by modulating the sliding ferroelectric dipole strength, the OFF-state depletion width, and the resulting TER amplification. Finally, planar 3R-MoS2 FTJs further validate this mechanism by exhibiting a TER above 105, a switching energy density of several fJ μm–2, and projected endurance beyond 106. These results provide fundamental insight into the nanoscale electrostatics in sliding ferroelectric-based tunnel junctions while pointing toward low-energy, high-contrast nonvolatile memory applications.

articles.title: Stress-Resilient Skin Wound Protection via Bioinspired Dual-Tier Architecture
articles.abstract: Mechanical tension destabilizes wound repair and drives fibrotic progression, yet current protection materials rarely reconcile the contrasting requirements of load-bearing and interfacial adaptability. To address this persistent mechanical conflict, a dual-tier hydrogel architecture was developed by integrating a stiff protective tier with a compliant adaptive tier to redistribute deformation and maintain secure adhesion under load. The stiff tier intercepted external stress, the compliant tier accommodated deformation, and dual interfaces regulated force transmission to avoid stress concentration on wound sites. The construct preserved bioadhesion energy exceeded that of various commercial products, and ex vivo distraction tests showed controlled wound opening with deformation control ratios of 70–90% compared with 30–40% for the commercial Mepiform patch. In a tension-driven murine model, the dual-tier patch demonstrated a reduction in scar area of approximately 97%, restored collagen angular dispersion and fiber diameter toward unwounded patterns, and lowered proliferative, inflammatory, immune, and mechanotransduction signals with significant improvement over Mepiform. These findings underscore the value of architecture-driven material design for achieving stable wound protection under fluctuating mechanical conditions.

articles.title: Anion‐Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal Batteries at Low Temperatures
articles.abstract: Anion-dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been intensively pursued for low-temperature sodium-metal batteries (SMBs), yet they face constraints from temperature-sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial control. Here we propose anion-cation-targeted regulation via Sn(OTf)2 that simultaneously constructs a solvent-reinforced solvation structure and electrochemically induces an alloy-based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) (Na15Sn4), which goes beyond the prevailing anion-centric strategy to address the critical challenges of SMBs at subzero temperatures. Competitive Sn2+-Na+ coordination excludes PF6 − from the primary solvation sheath, while OTf− and the ether groups of diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) coupling foster a solvent-dominated configuration, substantially reducing the Na+ desolvation energy barrier at low temperatures. This design enables Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells to deliver a recorded 1050 cycles at −20°C and 20 C, and nearly 700 cycles at −50°C. Ah-scale pouch cells sustain durable 450 cycles at −20°C, with a 6 Ah cell reaching 215 Wh kg−1 at 25°C (total cell mass). Our findings resolve the longstanding trade-off between low-temperature kinetics and stability in SMBs, offering a new design rationale beyond conventional interfacial engineering.

articles.title: Decoding Perovskite Interfaces: Machine Learning Uncovers Geometry‐Matched Dual‐Site Hydrogen Bonding
articles.abstract: Molecular passivation is central to efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics, yet interfacial molecules are still largely selected through chemical intuition and iterative experimentation. Here, an interpretable machine-learning framework is developed that extracts chemically meaningful structure–performance relationships from literature data and uses them to guide molecular screening. Using approximately 100 data points, the model quantitatively relates six molecular and material features to photovoltaic performance, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis ranks their relative contributions and identifies hydrogen-bonding capacity and adsorption strength as the two most influential factors. Guided by these data-derived relationships, nine previously unexplored molecules were screened, with 2-amino-thiazole-4-carboxamide (ATC) and 1-(2-aminoethyl)-1H-pyrrole-2,5-dione (MPD) emerging as leading candidates. Theoretical and experimental investigations show that MPD exhibits stronger Pb2 + coordination, whereas ATC forms stronger geometry-matched multisite N─H···I interactions, increasing the calculated iodide-migration barrier from 0.39 to 0.67 eV and suppressing interfacial iodide redistribution. ATC-modified cells achieve a PCE of 27.13% and a certified stabilized efficiency of 26.59%, while retaining 90% of their initial efficiency after 1460 h of unencapsulated operation. The strategy further delivers efficiencies of 24.01% and 21.14% in 20.98 cm2 rigid and 21.0 cm2 flexible modules, respectively, providing a data-to-mechanism route for rational and scalable perovskite interface engineering.

articles.title: Expanding the Chemical Space of Analytes in the 2G Crystalline Sponge Method: Size‐Compensation Strategy for the Structural Analysis of Low‐Polarity Small Molecules
articles.abstract: The second‐generation crystalline sponge (2G‐CS) is a novel type of crystalline sponge that incorporates hollow cages as molecular recognition modules within its crystalline framework. This advanced CS technology provides a versatile structural analysis technique applicable to a broad range of guest molecules, regardless of polarity, with molecular weights ranging from 300 to 1500. However, the method often fails when analyzing rather low‐polarity small molecules (MW 200–300) due to an “unfavorable chemical space,” where the host cavities are too large to facilitate sufficient host–guest interactions. Here we overcome this limitation by establishing a size‐compensation strategy based on cage‐mediated pair‐selective bimolecular recognition. By co‐encapsulating a target analyte with a shape‐complementary “modulator” (e.g., phenanthrene), we precisely tailor the cavity environment without the need for chemical modification of the host. This adaptive approach enabled the x‐ray structural determination of 24 of 30 low‐polarity C15 analytes, predominantly sesquiterpenoids, including absolute configuration determination for selected chiral analytes. This work translates a decades‐old molecular recognition phenomenon into a practical approach to crystallographic structure determination of low‐polarity sesquiterpenoids.

articles.title: Helical Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters for High‐Performance Anti‐Quenching Narrowband Blue OLEDs
articles.abstract: Multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) has established a new approach for narrowband blue organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs), yet effectively suppressing intermolecular interactions especially at high doping concentrations while preserving the intrinsic narrowband emission remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel designing paradigm is proposed for achieving anti‐quenching narrowband emission in MR‐TADF molecules by embedding the indeno[2,1‐b]carbazole unit into the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon skeleton. The proof‐of‐concept emitter DT‐BON1 reveals a favorable twist angle of 31.8°, manifesting formation of helical architecture within MR core. As a result, the emission peaks and full width at half maximum show virtually no variation with changing doping concentration from 1 wt% to 20 wt%. Moreover, the photoluminance quantum yields exceed 90% even at 20 wt% doping concentration endowed by the outstanding anti‐quenching characteristics. The DT‐BON1 based OLEDs can achieve maximum external quantum efficiency (EQEmax) of exceeding 30%. Especially, the alleviated exciton quenching effects can be firmly demonstrated by marginally decreased EQEmax values, attaining 29.2% in 10 wt%‐based OLEDs and 27.3% even in heavily doped devices (20 wt%), which is at a record high for MR‐TADF with blue emission at such high doping concentration.

articles.title: Supramolecular Enforcement of Planar Tetracoordinate Halides
articles.abstract: Planar tetracoordinate halides have been widely explored by quantum computational approaches but remain rare as deliberately targeted experimental motifs. Here we show that these geometries can be accessed by supramolecular enforcement, and challenge its connection to the VSEPR model. Bowl-shaped calix[4]pyrrolato indium units preorganize four lithium ions into a confined Li4 pocket that traps Cl−, Br−, and I− in strongly flattened to ideal planar tetracoordinate environments. Computational analysis of the parent tetrahedral [Li4X]3 + units reveals small planarization energies that can be overcome by a charge-attenuating host of appropriate shape. The experimental series shows that halide planarity is highly sensitive to subtle supramolecular effects, such as calix[4]pyrrolato doming and crystal packing, experimentally confirming the generally low angular deformation energies. The results establish supramolecular enforcement as a rational design principle for planar tetracoordinate heavier halides and show that such motifs are accessible outcomes of engineered electrostatic cavities.

articles.title: Unidirectional Hydrogen Migration Through Interfacial Engineering for Promoted Brønsted Acid Catalysis
articles.abstract: Though playing a critical role, the controllable and directional migration of reactive species in chemical reactions is still hard to achieve. Here, we propose an interfacial engineering strategy for constructing a hydrogen spillover nanodiode that channels hydrogen unidirectionally. Such a nanodiode design is materialized in a composite WO x /TiO2/Pt catalyst with spatially separated structure, where WO x and Pt particles are dispersed on the outer and inner surfaces of porous TiO2 nanotubes, respectively. This nanodevice permits forward H migration (Pt→TiO2→WO x ) while suppresses the reverse path (WO x →TiO2), as directly evidenced by in situ x-ray absorption fine structure characterization under hydrogenation and H2 generation reactions. This rectification behavior originates from the diode characteristics of the TiO2–WO x heterojunction, which hinders both proton and electron transfer from WO x to TiO2. Consequently, WO x /TiO2/Pt accumulates highly concentrated Brønsted acid sites in H2 atmosphere and thus exhibits superior catalytic performance compared to the closely contacted WO x –Pt/TiO2 catalyst. Up to 5.3 times higher liquid alkane yield has been achieved over WO x /TiO2/Pt relative to WO x –Pt/TiO2 in the polyethylene hydrocracking reaction. This nanodiode design strategy is general and can be extended to other catalysts/species, offering mechanistic insight and boosting catalytic performance in diverse reactions.
