Curvature-Controlled Polar–Dislocation Coupling in Freestanding Ferroelectric Oxide Heterostructures
articles.abstract: Curvature couples polarization, crystalline defects, and interfacial electrostatics in freestanding ferroelectric oxides. Here, we examine bent epitaxial Pb(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3/SrTiO3/Pb(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3 (PZT/STO/PZT) membranes using atomic-resolution electron microscopy, strain and polarization mapping, relative projected-potential reconstruction, and molecular dynamics simulations. The tensile-side PZT remains comparatively lattice-continuous and accommodates bending mainly through polarization rotation and domain reorganization. The compressive-side PZT exhibits dislocations, slip-related lattice offsets, surface steps, and localized strain concentration. Curvature-series observations and images across U-shaped and N-shaped regions indicate that the defect-rich region follows the local compressive stress state. Bending also breaks the approximate electrostatic symmetry of the two PZT/STO interfaces: the tensile side shows weakened negative interfacial contrast, whereas the compressive side shows a dislocation-associated increase in relative projected potential. These results identify curvature as a variable for selecting polar versus plastic relaxation pathways and modulating interfacial electrostatic landscapes in flexible ferroelectric heterostructures.

articles.title: Deep-Learning-Driven Dual Sensors Based on Single-Trapped Upconverting Particles
articles.abstract: Upconverting lanthanide-doped particles are widely used as nanoscale temperature sensors, particularly in biological and photonic environments. However, extending their functionality to simultaneously measure temperature and light intensity remains a challenge, as the luminescent response is highly sensitive to both the environment composition and its temperature. In this work, we combine deep-learning methods with large-scale spectral data sets to investigate the reliability of Er/Yb-doped particles to function as dual sensors. Spectral data are collected from single particles levitating in vacuum and ensembles of particles in application-relevant wet and dry media. Although traditional ratiometric methods reliably retrieve temperature irrespective of the environment and specific experimental apparatus, they fail to disentangle the complex dependencies needed for dual sensing. Our trained models overcome these limitations, accurately predicting both temperature and laser power despite environmental variability. This approach opens a new route toward robust, data-driven sensing with upconverting particles in complex or fluctuating conditions.

articles.title: Flexible Microlaser Emitter for Mechanical Sensing and Pulse Mapping
articles.abstract: Flexible photonic devices and soft microlasers have attracted increasing attention for wearable sensing, biomedical monitoring, and deformable optoelectronic systems. Their mechanical compliance enables intimate contact with soft biological tissues, allowing optical signals to be modulated by external mechanical stimuli. Such characteristics make flexible laser-based platforms particularly suitable for mechanical sensing and physiological signal detection. In this work, we present a flexible microlaser array-based photonic platform designed for mechanical sensing and pulse monitoring. By integrating microscale laser emitters into a soft, transparent matrix with a microstructured architecture, the device maintains stable laser emission while responding to external pressure and dynamic strain. The optical response of the microlaser array exhibits sensitivity to mechanical perturbations, enabling the detection of periodic signals associated with the human pulse. This work highlights the potential of flexible laser photonics as a versatile tool for noninvasive mechanical and physiological sensing in wearable healthcare applications.

articles.title: Magnetic Phase Diagram of Cr2Te3: The Hidden Role of Layer Stacking
articles.abstract: Using two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) ferromagnets in spintronic devices can enhance their performance through well-controlled vdW interfaces and reduced power consumption. Cr2Te3 appears as a promising candidate because of its strong perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, but the Curie temperature is limited to 180 K. In this work, we use annealing in air to uncover the magnetic phase diagram of Cr2Te3. We correlate magnetic properties with layer stacking and the interlayer distance; both depend strongly on the annealing temperature. In particular, disorder in layer stacking plays a key role in the magnetic properties of Cr2Te3 and more generally of vdW ferromagnets. By annealing at 375 °C, we can eventually raise the Tc of Cr2Te3 up to 303 K in the epitaxial Cr2Te3/WSe2 vdW heterostructure with in-plane magnetic anisotropy. This work provides a simple method to control the magnetic properties of 2D ferromagnets and incorporate them into spintronics devices.

articles.title: Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing
articles.abstract: Tools for manipulating RNA that rely on nonhuman proteins, such as ISC-based and Cas-based scaffolds, can lead to unintended and little-understood effects on human cells and present challenges in therapeutic translation. Replacing them with human proteins engineered for expanded, programmable functions could bypass the limitations of these foreign proteins. Here we demonstrate that human Argonaute 2 (AGO2) can be repurposed as a modular RNA targeting domain. AGO2 fused to a C-to-U deaminase enables AGO-led targeted editing of RNA (ALTER). Using guide RNAs that remodel target RNA structure for selective editing and reduced nuclease activity, we show that ALTER achieves, on average, 1.9-fold higher C-to-U editing on mRNA targets in HEK293T cells compared with Cas13 editors CURE and RESCUE. Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq revealed similar or lower levels of off-target editing compared to the same Cas13-based editors. Machine learning models predict that far fewer immunogenic peptides will result from ALTER and we show that ALTER is amenable to a validated workflow for artificial intelligence-directed deimmunization.

articles.title: A single amino‐acid switch reprograms ROP6 signaling to drive functional evolution in plants
articles.abstract: A single amino‐acid substitution reprograms ROP6 from PIN stabilization to endocytic degradation. Summary Rho‐related GTPases of plants (ROPs) are evolutionarily conserved molecular switches that typically maintain PIN‐formed proteins at the plasma membrane (PM), yet their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal that a single amino‐acid substitution at residue 194 acts as a core determinant, driving the evolutionary split between Brassicaceae and Malvaceae ROP6 orthologs: glycine enforces PM stabilization, whereas alanine licenses endocytic function. In cotton, the Malvaceae‐predominant alanine mutated GhROP6 displays an auxin‐independent manner. The distinct activity is attributed to the recruitment of three GhRIC effectors that directly bind the actin cytoskeleton and promote F‐actin assembly and bundling. The resulting actin reorganization facilitates GhPIN3a internalization and proteolysis, consequently enhancing cotton fiber elongation. Our findings demonstrate that a single amino‐acid change can reprogram ROP signaling and uncover a molecular switch underlying the functional evolution of ROP6 in regulating plant development.

articles.title: Comparative genomics of dark septate endophytes: shedding light on the enigmatic lifestyle and biology of DSEs
articles.abstract: Ancestral lifestyle reconstruction across the phylogeny of the 107 analysed fungal genomes. Summary Dark septate endophytes (DSE) are widespread root‐colonising fungi with poorly understood lifestyle and ecological functions. We investigated their genomic traits, sexual reproduction signatures, carbohydrate‐active enzyme (CAZyme) and secondary metabolites profiles, and tested whether genomic features distinguish DSEs and other endophytes from fungi with other lifestyles. We also reconstructed ancestral states to clarify the evolutionary origins of DSEs. We analysed 107 Ascomycota genomes representing diverse lifestyles, including nine newly sequenced DSE genomes. The dataset allowed us to test whether secreted enzyme profiles differ between fungi colonising roots vs shoots and those associated with grass vs nongrass hosts. DSEs evolved through multiple independent trajectories and diverse lifestyles and show remarkable metabolic diversity. They possess extensive degradative capacities and some of the largest biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) richness among fungi. Despite sharing BGC richness with other endophytes, DSEs form a distinct subgroup with fewer cellulose‐ and more hemicellulose‐targeting enzymes. Genomes also revealed genomic signatures associated with fungi colonising grass vs nongrass hosts and root‐ vs shoot‐associated niches. Our comparative genomics approach highlights how genome‐level data can deepen our understanding of endophytic lifestyle and the biology of the enigmatic DSE fungi.

articles.title: Tropical leaf phenology as a thermoregulation trait: how changes in crown structure modulate thermal dynamics for two dominant Hawaiian trees
articles.abstract: Study site and focal species. Summary Canopy and leaf temperatures often diverge from air temperature, influencing photosynthesis, water loss, and heat stress. While leaf traits are known to affect heat exchange, how changes in crown structure interact with environmental drivers to regulate canopy thermal dynamics is poorly understood, particularly in tropical forests. In a Hawaiian wet tropical montane forest, we used repeated UAV‐based (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) thermal and LiDAR (light detection and ranging) measurements of sunlit leaves within and across 397 tree crowns of Acacia koa and Metrosideros polymorpha to investigate (1) seasonal and species‐specific variation in crown traits; (2) how crown traits and environmental drivers interact to determine canopy–air temperature differences (Tdiff), within‐crown thermal variability (TcanSD), and maximum leaf temperatures (TcanMAX); and (3) whether crowns with greater seasonal structural change exhibit enhanced thermoregulation. All crown traits showed species‐specific seasonal dynamics, with trait–trait and trait–environment interactions shaping thermal metrics differently across species. In M. polymorpha, crowns with greater seasonal structural change exhibited lower relative Tdiff, whereas A. koa did not show this buffering effect. These results indicate that canopy thermoregulation emerges from interacting crown traits dynamically reshaped across phenological and seasonal cycles. Seasonal crown dynamics provide partial thermal buffering in some species, highlighting species‐specific pathways of thermal acclimation or vulnerability under climate change.

articles.title: Bose Polarons as Relativistic Unruh-DeWitt Detectors: Entanglement Harvesting from Bose-Einstein Condensates
articles.abstract: An impurity in a Bose-Einstein condensate with time-tunable coupling realizes an Unruh-DeWitt detector of the condensate’s effective relativistic phonon field.

articles.title: Cluster-Decorated Lieb Lattice: A Convenient and Reliable Platform for Tuning Flat-Band Energy
articles.abstract: Flat bands harbor exotic electron physics. A new way of realizing them could make the physics more accessible.

We compute the exact deformation energy across a broad range of indentations and for various model parameters, and we show that it can be reproduced …

articles.abstract: The origin of the solar corona’s million Kelvin temperatures remains a central unsolved problem. While the nanoflare hypothesis is widely accepted and describes magnetic reconnection events at coronal current sheets that are slowly formed by complex driver flows at the solar surface, the possibility…

It relies on projecting the Hamiltonian to the tangent space of the ground-sta…

articles.title: Topological and Trivial Valence-Bond Orders in Higher-Spin Kitaev Models
articles.abstract: We investigate the quantum phases of higher-spin Kitaev models using tensor network methods. Our results reveal distinct valence-bond-ordered phases for spin-1, spin-32, and spin-2 models. In all cases, we find translational symmetry breaking with unit cells being tripled by forming valence-bond ord…

articles.title: On the future of science and its wise pursuit
articles.abstract: Science’s endless frontier is a changing frontier. It requires a dynamic approach to governance, collaboration, and investment.

articles.title: Originating from nature: a review of the design, fabrication, and applications of cantilever bio-inspired sensors
Modern research group leaders in the biomedical sciences
articles.abstract: Modern-day group leaders are expected to excel not only in scientific research and teaching but also in leadership and in providing a safe and intellectually stimulating environment for the next generation of budding scientists. In this article, we explore the evolution of a modern-day group leader within and beyond the scientific community.

articles.title: Bispecific antibodies in NSCLC: immune reengineering to neutralize adaptive tumor resistance
articles.abstract: Over the past few decades, the emergence of immunotherapy and single-target drugs has brought new promise to the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Yet the high heterogeneity of NSCLC leads to both primary and acquired resistance that neither sequential monotherapy nor empirical combinations can effectively overcome. In contrast to the conventional coadministration of two separate monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) feature a series of molecular engineering designs that confer inherent synergistic antitumor effects. We propose that a network pharmacology perspective can be adopted to understand the application of BsAbs in NSCLC and to guide their subsequent development.

articles.title: The tumor macroenvironment as cancer metabolism’s next frontier
articles.abstract: The deregulated utilization of nutrients by tumors, first observed over a century ago, is recognized as a hallmark of cancer and continues to be exploited clinically to image neoplastic disease. Despite this historic focus on cancer cells and, more recently, their neighbors, metabolic reprogramming is not limited to the tumor microenvironment. Tumors also have the capacity to rewire the metabolism of cells throughout the body, including those at distant sites, often referred to as the tumor macroenvironment. Alterations in the metabolism of noncancerous tissues outside the local tumor ecosystem are gaining attention, but their origins and consequences remain incompletely defined. A deeper understanding of these changes may reveal previously unrecognized signatures of disease and unexplored opportunities for therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: The ongoing urgency of diversity science
articles.abstract: Efforts to extinguish DEI provoke questions about the ongoing significance of diversity science. We argue that this evolving context makes such research increasingly pressing, and we pose four questions that this environment both calls for and newly allows research to answer. Such science remains indispensable to society’s capacity to manage social differences.

articles.title: CRAFT-ε: A Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for the Static Relative Permittivity of Pure Organic Liquids
articles.abstract: The static relative permittivity is an important property in thermodynamic modeling, electrochemistry, and solvent design, but predicting it directly from molecular structure remains challenging because both electronic polarization and molecular dipole orientation contribute to the measured response. Here, we introduce CRAFT-ε (Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for ε), a conformer-resolved molecular descriptor model for predicting the static relative permittivity of neutral pure liquids. Conformer free energies, molecular dipoles, and atom-resolved polarizabilities are obtained from a GFN2-xTB/ALPB 10 workflow. The molecular dipole is decomposed into chemically defined polar-fragment vectors, allowing fitted corrections to retain both the magnitude and relative orientation of local dipolar contributions. Electronic and orientational polarization are combined with a group-contribution molar volume in the Onsager-Kirkwood-Fröhlich relation. A staged parameterization with 41 parameters is applied to nonpolar, polar, and hydrogen-bonding compounds. For 1393 liquids with permittivities between 1.5 and 183, CRAFT-ε reaches a five-fold cross-validated average absolute deviation of 2.40 ({R^2} = 0.93). Conformational averaging 15 is essential for liquids with several polar groups. Compared with an established fragment-based model with 139 parameters, it reaches a similar cross-validated RMSE (3.65 versus 3.41) with about a quarter of the parameters and applies to every liquid of the dataset. The resulting framework provides a computationally inexpensive route from molecular structure to liquid dielectric response and forms a basis for later application to solvent mixtures and electrolyte systems.

articles.title: Effect of interfacial water structure on the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions
articles.abstract: Weakly hydrated anions tend to partition to macromolecular surfaces, leading to salting-in at low salt concentrations. Recent studies have linked this partitioning to disruption of the interfacial water network. Here, we investigate the role of interfacial-water-network disruption as an indirect driving force for the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions and its interplay with direct solute-anion and anion-cation interactions using computer simulations. We study the adsorption of SCN$^{-}$ and I$^{-}$ ions on a model extended solute that interacts with water and ions only via van der Waals interactions. To probe the indirect contribution, we increase the effective solute size while simultaneously decreasing the attractive solute-water and solute-ion interactions, resulting in progressively greater disorder in the interfacial water network in pure aqueous solutions. Our results show that iodide adsorption increases despite weaker direct solute-iodide interactions and correlates with greater disruption of the interfacial water network, although iodide remains depleted overall. In contrast, preferential adsorption of SCN$^{-}$ decreases, but the rate of decrease becomes smaller at higher levels of interfacial-water-network disorder. This suggests that the indirect contribution associated with interfacial-water-network disruption partly compensates for the decrease in SCN$^{-}$ adsorption caused by weaker direct solute-SCN$^{-}$ interactions. Our results highlight that the indirect contribution associated with interfacial-water-network disruption promotes the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions on macromolecular surfaces, while the extent of adsorption also depends on direct solute-ion interactions and anion-cation pairing. This interplay may be particularly important in mixed-salt solutions, where the presence of strongly hydrated anions can also disrupt the interfacial water network.

articles.title: An integrated human forebrain organoid reveals microglia-mediated CD8+ T cell recruitment and neuroimmune dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease pathology
articles.abstract: Genetic evidence implicates immune dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet the neuroimmune mechanisms operating in human tissue remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a modular human forebrain organoid platform that systematically integrates human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia and CD8+ T cells to reconstitute multicellular AD pathology. This system enables functional interrogation of both innate and adaptive immune components in a human-relevant context. Using this platform, we demonstrate that microglia mediate amyloid-β clearance and neuronal maturation but also drive inflammatory activation and recruit CD8+ T cells through CCL4/5 signaling via CCR1/5 and CXCR3, establishing a neuroinflammatory feedback loop. Pharmacological targeting of CCR5 or CXCR3 blocks T cell recruitment and modulates autophagy in a microglia-dependent manner. This modular organoid platform provides a versatile tool for dissecting neuron–immune interactions and enables cell-type-specific therapeutic screening in human neuroinflammatory disease models.

articles.title: Multiplexed CRISPRi reveals a transcriptional switch between KLF activators and repressors in the maturing neocortex
articles.abstract: A critical phase of mammalian brain development takes place after birth. Neurons of the mouse neocortex undergo dramatic changes in their morphology, physiology, and synaptic connections during the first postnatal month, while properties of immature neurons, such as the capacity for robust axon outgrowth, are lost. The genetic and epigenetic programs controlling prenatal development are well studied, but our understanding of the transcriptional mechanisms that regulate postnatal neuronal maturation is comparatively lacking. By integrating chromatin accessibility and gene expression data from two subtypes of neocortical pyramidal neurons in the neonatal and maturing brain, we predicted a role for the Krüppel-like factor (KLF) family of transcription factors in the developmental regulation of neonatally expressed genes. Using a multiplexed CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) knockdown strategy, we found that a shift in expression from KLF activators (Klf6, Klf7) to repressors (Klf9, Klf13) during early postnatal development functions as a transcriptional ‘switch’ to first activate, then repress a set of shared targets with cytoskeletal functions including Tubb2b and Dpysl3. We demonstrate that this switch is buffered by redundancy between KLF paralogs, which our multiplexed CRISPRi strategy is equipped to overcome and study. Our results indicate that competition between activators and repressors within the KLF family regulates a conserved component of the postnatal maturation program that may underlie the loss of intrinsic axon growth in maturing neurons. This could facilitate the transition from axon growth to synaptic refinement required to stabilize mature circuits.

articles.title: A Curvature-Induced Pentagonal Oxide Motif Governs Ethylene Epoxidation Selectivity on Silver Nanoparticles
articles.abstract: Silver-catalyzed ethylene epoxidation is a cornerstone of the chemical industry, yet the operando surface structure of Ag nanoparticles and the identity of selectivity-governing active sites remain elusive. Here, we integrate machine learning potentials, stochastic surface walking global optimization, molecular dynamics simulation, and statistical analysis to resolve the surface landscape of Ag nanoparticles approaching experimentally relevant sizes under reaction conditions. Oxygen-induced reconstruction transforms pristine Ag facets into a globally amorphous oxide layer composed of three types of locally ordered ring motifs interspersed with structural defects. A pentagonal motif (ring5), topologically required to accommodate nanoparticle curvature and absent in conventional slab models, dominates the surface across all investigated particle sizes. Its recessed central Ag atom acts as an electronic charge buffer that weakens the critical C–Ag bond in the oxametallacycle intermediate, conferring high intrinsic ethylene oxide selectivity. Microkinetic analyses confirm that the oxygen species of ring5 regulate ethylene oxide yield, peaking at a nanoparticle oxidation degree of O/Ag ≈ 0.3–0.4. This work establishes a statistical paradigm for decoding active phases on realistic catalyst surfaces through dynamic structural ensembles.

articles.title: Chemoenzymatic Cascade Recycling and Upcycling of Polyurethane Elastomers
articles.abstract: The complex structure of polyurethanes (PURs) presents a major barrier to their efficient recycling. Here, we report a chemoenzymatic cascade that enables the simultaneous recycling and upcycling of PUR through rapid alkaline pretreatment followed by urethanase-catalyzed depolymerization. Using in-house-synthesized model polyether- and polyester-based PUR elastomers, we establish that soft-segment chemistry dictates the composition, morphology, and accessibility of the pretreated residues, thereby governing the efficiency of the subsequent enzymatic hydrolysis. This insight enabled translation of the cascade to a commercial PUR elastomer, achieving >93% chemical conversion and recovery of up to 1 mM 4,4′-methylenedianiline (MDA) (97.2% purity), corresponding to a 40-fold increase over the nonenzymatic control, together with polyols obtained in 95% isolated yield that were directly reused for PUR synthesis. Mechanistic studies further show that alkaline pretreatment enhances substrate accessibility for the enzyme, and structural analysis of urethanase SP2 reveals a carbamate-specific hydrogen-bonding interaction that promotes urethane hydrolysis while minimizing esterase activity. The cascade was additionally applied to highly crosslinked commercial PUR foams and adhesives, demonstrating its versatility toward industrially relevant waste streams. Overall, this work establishes a mechanistically informed chemoenzymatic platform for PUR depolymerization and provides a strategy for converting chemically recalcitrant PUR waste into reusable molecular building blocks.

articles.title: Direct Amidination of Alkenes Via C–H Activation of Pyridinyl Formimidamide Synthon
articles.abstract: Alkenes are among the most abundant and versatile feedstocks in synthetic chemistry, yet methods for their direct and regioselective conversion into nitrogen-containing frameworks remain scarce. In particular, the direct catalytic amidination of alkenes has remained underdeveloped. Herein, we report a rhodium-catalyzed anti-Markovnikov amidination of alkenes using a stable pyridinyl formimidamide synthon. This reaction enables the direct installation of amidine moieties onto a wide range of alkenes, including styrenes, aliphatic alkenes, and challenging internal alkenes that undergo efficient chain-walking with high regioselectivity and broad functional group tolerance, accommodating unprotected amines, phenols, and halides. The resulting pyridyl amidines can be readily transformed into amides, carboxylic acids and esters, establishing a practical platform for alkene diversification. Notably, late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules, including cyclosporine A, FK506, and quinine etc., provides access to previously inaccessible analogues. Mechanistic investigations, highlighted by the crystallographic capture of a key rhodium–aminopyridinyl formimidamide intermediate, provide compelling evidence for the proposed catalytic cycle. Collectively, this work not only fills a critical gap in alkene functionalization but also offers a concise and general route to high-value nitrogen-containing architectures.

articles.title: Dual-Enzyme Relay Catalysis Enables Asymmetric Construction of Nonadjacent Stereocenters in Polycyclic Alcohols
articles.abstract: The asymmetric construction of nonadjacent stereocenters in a single catalytic system remains a significant challenge due to the difficulty in controlling stereochemical relay between sequential transformations. Herein, we report a dual-enzyme relay catalytic system that integrates an artificial streptavidin-based copper metalloenzyme (Sav-Cu) with an engineered ketoreductase (KRED) for the one-pot synthesis of polycyclic alcohols bearing 1,3-non-adjacent stereocenters. In this relay process, the engineered SavDMase variant (S112A/K121D) catalyzes a non-natural decarboxylative Mannich reaction to establish the R-configured stereocenter in the enantioenriched ketone intermediate, which is then recognized by the engineered KREDAV mutant (S96A/Y190V) and reduced with high diastereo- and enantioselectivity to install the S-configured alcohol stereocenter, thereby furnishing the (R,S)-configured product as the dominant stereoisomer. The optimized system furnishes the products in up to 83% yield, 99% ee, and 96% de across a broad substrate scope, and is readily applicable to 2 mmol-scale synthesis. Structural analysis, docking, and molecular dynamics simulations support complementary roles of the two catalytic modules: SavDMase promotes productive organization of the Mannich step, while KREDAV stabilizes the reactive binding pose and constrains the hydride-transfer trajectory to enforce stereoselective reduction. This work demonstrates how artificial and natural enzymes can be integrated in relay catalysis to solve challenging stereochemical relay problems beyond the reach of individual biocatalysts.

articles.title: Entropy-Enhanced Catalysis Accelerates Low-Temperature CO2 Methanation via Intermediate Delocalization at Under-Coordinated Ru2+− V O Sites
articles.abstract: In heterogeneous catalysis, the electronic structures of catalysts' active sites are modified to optimize intermediate binding and bond activation for achieving high reaction activity. However, studies on regulating the atomic structures of catalytic materials to enhance the configurational diversity of adsorbed intermediates remain scarce. Herein, we demonstrate that engineering under-coordinated active site motifs enables an entropy-enhanced catalytic mechanism that harnesses the configurational freedom of surface intermediates to improve reaction rates at reduced temperatures. Using CO2 methanation as a model reaction, we identified that under-coordinated Ru2+−oxygen vacancy (Ru2+−VO) sites promote delocalized catalyst−intermediate interactions and reduce the reaction energy barrier. Stable Ru2+−VO sites were created on Au nanoparticle-grafted (RuOx)a(CeOy)b solid-solution nanorods through plasmonic effects under reducing conditions. Eyring plot analysis revealed an activation entropy gain of TΔΔS‡ ≈ 12 kJ mol−1 for CO2 methanation at 300 °C, in situ spectroscopy revealed a *HCOO-mediated pathway, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations indicated a 0.22 eV free-energy barrier for *HCOO formation on Ru2+−VO motifs. A CH4 production rate of 550 mmol gcat−1 h−1 with >98% selectivity and >280 h stability at 300 °C was achieved at a high gas hourly space velocity of 40,000−100,000 mL gcat−1 h−1. The findings provide a conceptual framework beyond adsorption energy optimization in catalyst design, showing that configurational entropy is a tunable descriptor for enhancing catalytic kinetics.

articles.title: Lewis–Brønsted Dual-Acid Sites Induced H-Down Interfacial Water Configuration and Accelerated Proton Transfer toward Enhanced Acidic Oxygen Evolution
articles.abstract: Efficient activation of interfacial water molecules and fast proton transfer are critical but challenging for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Herein, a Lewis–Brønsted dual-acid catalyst design strategy is proposed to achieve accelerated acidic OER by synergistically optimizing the configuration of interfacial water molecules and proton transfer kinetics on Mn-doped IrO2. In this catalyst, the Mn dopant serves as a Lewis acid site that readily captures hydroxyl groups, which perturbs the local hydrogen-bonding network and induces interfacial water molecules to form an H-down configuration toward surface active sites, thereby promoting the enrichment and dissociation of reactive interfacial water. On this basis, the formation of the Mn–Obri–Ir local structure enhances the Brønsted acidity of the bridge oxygen (Obri) site, accelerates the deprotonation of the Obri–H bond, promotes the formation of key OER intermediates and accelerates the reaction kinetics. Mn dopant also induces electron enrichment around Ir, suppresses excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ir species, and enhances catalyst stability performance. These synergistic effects enable Mn-IrO2 to achieve a 160 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm–2 and to operate stably for 1500 h at 10 mA cm–2 and 1200 h at 1.0 A cm–2 in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), demonstrating the promising potential of the Lewis–Brønsted dual-acid strategy in acidic OER catalyst design.

articles.title: Multiobjective Optimization of Synthetically Accessible Homogeneous Catalysts Reveals Tradeoffs for Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
articles.abstract: The selective conversion of methane to methanol remains a major challenge in catalysis, and no earth-abundant homogeneous catalyst has been demonstrated to carry out this transformation with high turnover. To explore previously synthesized complexes that might be amenable for this transformation, we start from macrocyclic ligands from experimental structures in the Cambridge Structural Database. After expanding this set of ligands with Hammett-tuning functionalization, we construct a design space of 21.9 million Mn and Fe catalysts. We employ active learning using neural network surrogate models with quantified uncertainty to efficiently identify catalysts with optimal methane-to-methanol turnover. We do this by jointly optimizing density functional theory (DFT)-computed hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and methyl radical rebound energetics. Square planar tetraaza-based macrocycles in combination with low-spin Fe(II) or Mn(II) emerge as a privileged class of transition metal complexes within the Pareto-optimal set, with Mn(II) catalysts exhibiting balanced energetic tradeoffs of the two steps. In contrast, porphyrin catalysts exhibit favorable HAT but unfavorable rebound, and seesaw catalysts, which are not widely employed, are indeed the least favorable in our set. Full reaction coordinate analysis of representative Pareto-optimal catalysts reveals that HAT and rebound thermodynamics no longer govern turnover, which is instead determined by the stability of the metal–oxo intermediate and the rebound kinetic barrier. Nonetheless, the resulting energetic spans for these catalysts remain competitive with known earth-abundant, methane-to-methanol catalysts, underscoring the effectiveness of active learning for discovering previously unexplored, synthetically accessible catalysts and unraveling catalyst design principles for methane-to-methanol reactivity.

articles.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Enantioselective Cyclizative Alkylation of 1,6-Enynes with Diazo Compounds and Alkyl Halides
articles.abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed cyclization of 1,n-enynes represents a versatile platform for the construction of structurally diverse chiral heterocycles. Despite substantial advances in this field, the enantioselective cyclizative alkylation of 1,n-enynes remains a formidable synthetic challenge, primarily due to the inherent difficulty in simultaneous control of regio-, chemo-, and stereoselectivity. Herein, we disclose a highly enantioselective cyclizative alkylation of 1,6-enynes employing two complementary alkylating reagents: diazo compounds and readily available alkyl iodides. This protocol proceeds under mild conditions and features broad substrate scope, delivering enantioenriched γ-lactams and pyrrolidine derivatives bearing quaternary stereogenic centers in good yields (up to 81%) and enantioselectivities (53 examples, up to 98% ee). Mechanistic studies corroborate that these two types of alkylating reagents follow entirely distinct catalytic pathways.

articles.title: Plasma-Enabled Direct Methane-to-Methanol Conversion on Zeolite-Confined Copper-Oxo Clusters: Insight into Vibrational Excitation and Radical-Mediated Process
articles.abstract: Selective one-step conversion of methane (CH4) to methanol (CH3OH) remains a grand challenge in catalysis, constrained by the trade-off between C─H bond activation and product overoxidation. Here, we integrate density functional theory (DFT) calculations with plasma-catalytic experiments to investigate direct CH4-to-CH3OH conversion using H2O as the sole oxidant on CuxOy clusters within MOR zeolite, compared to the CuO(111) surface. We show that C─H bond activation proceeds preferentially via homolytic H-abstraction on zeolite-confined CuxOy clusters, with Cu3O3/MOR exhibiting a low activation barrier of only 0.21 eV, more than three times lower than that on CuO(111). Vibrational mode-specificity analysis shows that the C─H stretching modes couple most effectively on higher-barrier surfaces. Importantly, we demonstrate that plasma-generated radical intermediates (CH3·, H·, OH·) reshape the reaction thermodynamics, with the Gibbs free energy shifting from endothermic (+1.13 eV) to exothermic (–3.21 eV and –8.25 eV), enabling pathways inaccessible under thermal conditions. Experimentally, Cu/MOR catalysts prepared by ion exchange, which favor well-dispersed zeolite-confined Cu-oxo sites, achieve the highest CH3OH production rate (0.26 mmol/h) at low plasma power (6.5 W), outperforming catalysts prepared by wetness impregnation. This work bridges Cu-oxo site topology, vibrational mode specificity, and radical-mediated thermodynamics, offering valuable insights for plasma-catalytic selective CH4-to-CH3OH conversion.

articles.title: Repurposing a Donor 2-OH Group for Catalyst-Controlled Stereodivergent Glycosylation
articles.abstract: The free C2-OH group of glycosyl donors is generally viewed as a liability in glycosylation because it can act as a competing nucleophile and compromise stereocontrol. Here, we show that this functionality can instead be harnessed as a programmable stereochemical element in a catalyst-controlled stereodivergent glycosylation. A single β-configured 2-hydroxy glycosyl 8-alkynyl-1-naphthoate donor was found to deliver either β- or α-glycosides simply by changing the gold(I) catalyst system. Triflate-based catalysts promoted highly β-selective glycosylation, whereas bistriflimide-based conditions enabled complementary α-selective glycosylation from the same donor. The method is applicable to a range of carbohydrate and noncarbohydrate acceptors and enables the programmable assembly of glucooligosaccharides bearing β-(1→6), α-(1→6), and alternating α/β-(1→6) linkages from a common donor platform. Mechanistic studies, including intermediate characterization, variable-temperature NMR experiments, computational analysis, and control glycosylations with the corresponding 2-O-Bn donor, reveal distinct roles of the donor 2-OH group in the two stereochemical manifolds.

articles.title: Solar-Driven Highly Active and Selective Conversion of Acetonitrile to Formic Acid over Oxygen Vacancy Engineered Tungsten Oxide
articles.abstract: Photocatalytic activation of inert chemical bonds represents a promising route for selective conversion of organic molecules such as acetonitrile (CH3CN) into value-added products. However, as the most common reactive oxygen species, •OH radicals are nonselective and usually lead to overoxidation reactions, making it difficult to realize the target product with both high activity and selectivity in the photocatalytic system. Here, we demonstrate that, through oxygen vacancy (Vo) engineering, selective CH3CN conversion into HCOOH is enabled over a WO3 photocatalyst under mild conditions. Under simulated solar irradiation, the as-prepared Vo-rich WO3 nanosheets display notable photocatalytic CH3CN conversion performance, with a HCOOH yield rate of 8.8 mmol g–1 h–1 and a selectivity as high as 86.5%. In combination of various in situ spectroscopic techniques, it is revealed that the Vo constructs a coupling match between of •OH radicals and •CH2CN intermediates on the WO3 photocatalyst surface, which facilitates the selective conversion of CH3CN into HCOOH while preventing its overoxidation. This work extends the conversion pathway of CH3CN in a photocatalytic route and provides deeper insight into the selective conversion of inert molecules.

articles.title: The Two Opposite Faces of Ceria as Redox Mediator in Methane Dry Reforming
articles.abstract: We investigate the interplay between carbon accumulation and redox-driven deactivation pathways in cerium-containing nickel (NiCe) and palladium (PdCe) bimetallic precursor materials upon eventual decomposition into a Ni- or Pd-ceria interfacial system during dry reforming of methane (DRM). By probing defined intermediate states, information from surface electronic structure, morphology, and bulk structure to track structural and chemical changes across several reaction, deactivation, and CO2 titration cycles is combined to identify how carbon accumulation, oxygen transfer, and dynamic metal–ceria interfacial interactions evolve under DRM reaction conditions. Despite their similar cerium-containing precursor architecture and surface composition, the two systems allow studying two detrimental deactivation processes. Bimetallic NiCe decomposes more readily into a Ni-ceria interface, where carbon formation is progressively suppressed. Loss of activity is a result of oxidation of Ni particles mediated by enhanced oxygen transfer from ceria. In contrast, bimetallic PdCe is much more decomposition-resistant, and the localized Pd-ceria interface exhibits high activity throughout multiple DRM cycles, even in the presence of substantial carbon deposition and filamentous carbon growth. The results demonstrate an intrinsic coupling between carbon accumulation and oxygen transfer to the metallic component, with carbon acting as a competing sink for reactive oxygen species. We emphasize the significance of dynamic interfacial structures and show that ceria-mediated oxygen transfer produces contrasting, metal-dependent catalytic outcomes. Whereas in NiCe, efficient oxygen delivery suppresses carbon accumulation, but progressively oxidizes Ni and diminishes methane activation, in PdCe, carbon generation outpaces oxygen-mediated removal, yielding a carbon-rich yet catalytically persistent surface.

articles.title: Colloidal ALD Epitaxial Shelling Enhances Stability and Photoluminescence of Blue Perovskite Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: A modified colloidal atomic layer deposition at room temperature grows a vacancy-ordered Cs2SnCl6 shell epitaxially on CsPbCl3 nanocrystals, avoiding the core degradation and parasitic shell nucleation that accompany high-temperature routes. The resulting core–shell nanocrystals achieve an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 62% and retain 65% of their emission after six months of ambient storage and 30% after 48 h of exposure to added water.

articles.title: Electrolyte-Derived Chemical Activation Enables Reversible Cathode Chemistry in Magnesium Batteries
articles.abstract: Rechargeable magnesium (Mg) metal batteries are promising high-energy-density alternatives to lithium-ion systems, yet sluggish cathode kinetics hinder their development. Departing from the conventional host-centric view, we demonstrate that reversibility in Mg batteries can be governed by electrolyte-derived reaction chemistry. Here, we harness trace water to impart controlled electrolyte reactivity, enabling electrolyte-derived Mg/Cl-containing species to participate in cathode activation. In tunnel-type MnO2, the regulated electrolyte induces lattice expansion and improves electrochemical reversibility. In organic cathodes, improved rechargeability is consistent with a stabilizing role of Cl– in anion-coupled redox. Because polar-solvent chemistry can irreversibly passivate Mg metal, a Sn/MgCl2 artificial interface suppresses parasitic anode reactions while preserving cathode activation. This strategy enables reversible electrochemistry across oxide, organic, and conversion cathodes, including α/γ-MnO2, methylphenothiazine, tetrathiafulvalene, and hybrid I2/O2 systems. These findings establish electrolyte-derived chemical activation as a guiding principle for regulating cathode reaction pathways in magnesium batteries.

articles.title: Manipulating Li2MnO3-Like Domain Dispersion in Lithium-Rich Layered Oxides Inherited from Precursor
articles.abstract: Leveraging oxygen redox in lithium-rich layered oxides paves the way for increasing the energy density of lithium-ion batteries, whose practical implementation is plagued by poor stability. Although a uniform Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is suggested to improve cycle stability, the synthesis–structure relationship governing domain formation remains underexplored. Here, we show that Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is derived by the precursor structure according to the degree of transition-metal separation. Through a comparative investigation of the synthesis mechanism, we reveal the templating effect that more clustered transition-metal oxide precursors lead to more localized Li2MnO3-like ordering in the final cathodes, a tendency also observed with a different lithium source. Furthermore, it is corroborated that cathodes with more dispersed Li2MnO3-like ordering derived from less-ordered precursors exhibit improved electrochemical stability with a mitigated voltage decay. Our findings highlight the significance of precursor design and engineering for structural regulation of high-performance lithium-rich layered oxide cathodes.

articles.title: Rational Integration of Multiple Additives for High-Temperature Lithium-Ion Batteries
articles.abstract: The rational combination of multiple electrolyte additives is a promising strategy for constructing stable interphases in lithium-ion batteries. However, unintended additive interactions can alter the preferential reduction/oxidation pathways at electrode surfaces, compromising cell performance. In this study, we identify a detrimental interaction between succinonitrile (SN) and lithium bis(oxalato)borate (LiBOB) on a graphite-silicon (Gr-Si) anode. Specifically, an electron-deficient boron-embedded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from LiBOB promotes the reduction of the electron-rich nitrile moieties of SN, disrupting fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)-driven SEI construction. Based on this mechanism, SN was replaced with triisopropanolamine borate (TPAB), which mitigates transition metal dissolution through its amine moiety while forming a robust borate-based cathode electrolyte interphase. Moreover, TPAB combined with LiBOB avoided detrimental side reductions at the anode–electrolyte interface. The FEC-LiBOB-TPAB combination creates thermally stable interphases on the Gr-Si anode and LiNi0.91Co0.08Al0.01O2 cathode (4.8 mAh cm–2), enabling 68.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 45 °C and 1C.

articles.title: Shear-Driven Structural Ordering Enables High Energy Density in Ferroelectric Polymer Capacitors
articles.abstract: Polymer film capacitors are fundamental to modern power electronics, yet low permittivity restricts their energy density. Although poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) possesses high intrinsic permittivity, stabilizing its polar structure remains thermodynamically challenging. Here, we report a scalable physical processing strategy to optimize PVDF-based films via a specialized shear-imposed coating methodology. By employing a micro-structured blade, we generate intense local shear flow fields that exert hydrodynamic tension to drive a coil-stretch transition. This process drives an α-to-β phase transition and templates the growth of oriented, polar-phase-rich crystal structures. Furthermore, we develop a stage-wise regulation strategy using binary solvents to orchestrate evaporation dynamics, effectively trapping these metastable shear-induced conformations before relaxation. Effective across the PVDF copolymer family, this method enables P(VDF-HFP) films to achieve a high energy density of 20.05 J/cm3, a 44% improvement over conventional casting. This work provides a general, non-chemical pathway for manufacturing high-performance functional polymers through multi-physical field synergistic regulation.

articles.title: Carbene-Mediated Stabilization of Reactive Copper–Chalcogenide Clusters: Defining the Operational Limits of Strong-Field Ligands in Multinuclear Nanoassemblies
articles.abstract: Atomic precision in metal–sulfur assemblies offers a transformative pathway to programmable nanomaterials, with applications spanning energy-efficient optoelectronics to highly selective CO2 reduction catalysis. However, the inherent lability of the metal–sulfur bond remains a formidable barrier to the rational design of robust frameworks. While strong-field ligands such as cyclic (alkyl)(amino)carbenes (CAACs) are gold-standard scaffolds for stabilizing reactive monometallic centers, their impact on the structural fidelity of multinuclear clusters remains elusive. Herein, we report a combined experimental and theoretical investigation of a CAAC-supported Cu8(μ3-S)4 cluster─a high-impact prototype for metal-chalcogenide systems with relatively weak metal–sulfur bonds. Through electrochemical and protonation studies, we demonstrate that while the potent σ-donor ability of the CAAC ligand successfully enforces solution integrity and thermal resilience, the structural boundaries of the multinuclear scaffold under chemical stress are ultimately governed by the core topology and metal–sulfur bond lability rather than local metal–ligand bonding. In-depth density functional theory (DFT) analysis demonstrates that while the CAAC ligands actively strengthen the peripheral Cu–S bonds via a pronounced inverse trans influence, the trigonal pyramidal (μ3-S) motifs remain vulnerable to proton-induced bond labilization and oxidative S–S coupling. Our findings establish that the design rules for multinuclear assemblies diverge fundamentally from monometallic species: whereas CAACs successfully passivate peripheral coordination sites to thermal decomposition, they do not preclude internal, core-mediated degradation pathways. These clear boundaries reveal that achieving structural durability in functional base metal–sulfur assemblies requires pairing strong local donors with supramolecular and/or multidentate ligand strategies designed explicitly to buttress the metal–sulfur core.

articles.title: Correction to “Cellular Transmigration Increases Nanoparticle Penetration Into Solid Tumors”
Enhancing Capacitance by Increasing Electric Double Layer Disorder in Ionic Liquid Mixtures
articles.abstract: Supercapacitors, possessing rapid charge–discharge time scales and cycle lifetimes, provide opportunities to mitigate fluctuations from intermittent energy sources. However, while supercapacitors exhibit lower energy densities to lithium-ion batteries, advancing supercapacitor energy density is necessary to improve their utility in applications requiring rapid operating time scales. Supercapacitor energy densities critically hinge on interfacial capacitances and electrolyte voltage windows. Ionic liquids have been heavily investigated as supercapacitor electrolytes due to promising properties like high electrochemical stability, nonflammability, and nonvolatility. Yet, energy densities of ionic liquid-derived supercapacitors are often limited by low interfacial capacitances due to pronounced ion–ion correlations. Here, we show capacitance can be significantly enhanced in ionic liquids over wide voltages by mixing ionic liquids to improve electric double layer entropy. Importantly, capacitance increases exhibited by mixtures persist over the entire electrochemical stability window, showing like-charged co-ions often play similar roles to oppositely charged counterions when determining double layer capacitance. By leveraging electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and surface forces measurements, we conclude that capacitive enhancements originate from changes in short-range nanostructures in ionic liquids, where atomic force microscopy measurements reveal that mixing ionic liquids results in more compact bound ion layers with increased disorder and compressibility. Notably, we find that long-range decay lengths are statistically similar between neat ionic liquids and an equimolar mixture at potentials where we report up to 150% capacitance enhancement, indicating decoupling between the bulk electrostatic decay length and interfacial capacitance. Overall, our results reveal that modulating compositional entropy of ionic liquid double layers provides avenues to increase supercapacitor energy densities and advance next-generation energy storage.

articles.title: Ferroelectric Switching of Skyrmion Topology in 2D Multiferroics
articles.abstract: Deterministic switching of skyrmion topology is a central frontier in topological spintronics, yet current paradigms rely almost exclusively on dissipative-current-driven spin torques. Here, we propose a fundamentally distinct mechanism for the nonvolatile switching of the skyrmion topology in two-dimensional multiferroics. We reveal that the intrinsic magnetoelectric coupling intimately links the out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization to interlayer magnetic exchange. Consequently, an electric-field-driven polarization reversal deterministically converts the interlayer coupling between the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic states. This macroscopic exchange reversal directly flips the microscopic skyrmion core polarity and reverses its topological charge, thereby stabilizing the two electrically addressable topological phases. Guided by our established design principles, we rigorously validate this mechanism in a Co2CF2/MoN2 multiferroic heterostructure by using combined first-principles calculations and atomistic spin simulations. Our findings bypass the limitations of continuous current injection, establishing a robust physical framework for energy-efficient multiferroic topological spintronics.

articles.title: Frustrated Lewis Pair Engineered Metal–Organic Frameworks for Enhancing Peroxidase Mimicking
articles.abstract: Natural enzymes achieve catalytic efficiency through the synergistic coupling of substrate activation and the efficient utilization of reactive intermediates. However, current nanozyme design paradigms focus predominantly on modulating substrate activation while overlooking the efficient utilization of highly reactive intermediates─a limitation that severely constrains substantial gains in catalytic activity. Inspired by the frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) composition of Fe2+ and tetrahydrobiopterin in tryptophan hydroxylase, we propose an FLP engineering approach to integrate 2,5-pyrazine-dicarboxylic acid (Pz) into the Materials of Institut Lavoisier-101 metal–organic framework (MIL-101(Fe)-H MOF) to construct MIL-101(Fe)-Pz MOF. This construct features pyrazine-nitrogen as a Lewis base and unsaturated Fe sites as Lewis acids. Compared with the Lewis acid-only MIL-101(Fe)-H MOF control, the as-fabricated FLP substantially accelerated the peroxidase-like activity of MIL-101(Fe)-Pz MOF, increasing the maximum reaction velocity by 4.83-fold when H2O2 was used as the substrate and by 17.88-fold when 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) was used as the substrate. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses revealed that the distinct electronic interactions within FLP facilitate electron transfer, promote H2O2 activation, improve hydroxyl radical utilization, and lower the reaction energy barrier, thereby boosting the reaction kinetics. This work highlights the indispensable role of substrate activation and active intermediate utilization in enhancing nanozyme performance and also provides guidance for the design of next-generation bioinspired nanozymes.

articles.title: Unfolding of Field-Free Spin–Orbit Torque Magnetization Switching in a van der Waals Heterostructure
articles.abstract: Heterostructures of 2D materials offer high tunability of magnetic properties, including current-induced magnetization switching by unconventional spin–orbit torques. The microscopic mechanisms governing spin-torque switching in van der Waals systems, however, remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate current-induced magnetization reversal in an Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) and WTe2 heterostructure using scanning harmonic magneto-optical Kerr effect microscopy. Spatially resolved magnetization maps show that field-free switching unfolds from asymmetric domain nucleation at the edges of the FGT flake, followed by domain wall propagation. This switching behavior is deterministic and bipolar, consistent with spin–orbit torques arising from the injection of both in-plane and out-of-plane spins from WTe2 into FGT. The critical currents for up-to-down and down-to-up switching differ because of asymmetric domain nucleation and directional domain wall pinning effects. Micromagnetic simulations reproduce the switching behavior observed experimentally, showing how the initial domain nucleation sites are determined by the sample geometry and combined influence of in-plane and out-of-plane spins and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Finally, by systematically varying the field-like and damping-like torque components and sweeping the spin polarization between in-plane and out-of-plane, we identify the torque configurations that yield the most efficient switching in van der Waals magnets with different shapes.

articles.title: Simultaneous strength-plasticity enhancement in Ti2AlNb alloy via laser powder bed fusion-induced heterostructuring over a wide temperature range
Boosting N,N‐Dimethylformamide Electrosynthesis via a Surface Active Additive
articles.abstract: Electrosynthesis of N,N‐dimethylformamide (DMF) via C─N coupling offers a sustainable alternative to energy‐intensive thermal routes but is hindered by low reactant concentration at the anode and sluggish proton‐coupled electron transfer. Here we report a new electrochemical route for DMF synthesis by the co‐oxidation of dimethylamine and ethylene glycol. Notably, over a CuO electrode, the addition of 0.5 mM sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS) to the electrolyte significantly enhances reaction kinetics and Faradaic efficiency for DMF (FEDMF), achieving a DMF production rate to 0.78 mmol h−1 cm−2, over three times higher than that without SDBS. Using a 25 cm2 CuO electrode in 0.5 M NaHCO3 with 0.5 mM SDBS, a current of approximately 2.0 A and a DMF production rate of 7.5 mmol h−1 are achieved. Mechanistic investigations reveal that SDBS acts as a multifunctional ionic anchor, reorienting its sulfonate group toward the anode and projecting its hydrophobic tail into the electrolyte under reaction conditions. This configuration suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction while simultaneously enriching reactants, promoting deprotonation and proton transfer, and facilitating electron transfer, thereby enhancing both reaction kinetics and FEDMF.

articles.title: Cascade Electrosynthesis of Aryl Imides and Sulfonimides From N2 via Integrated Nitrogen Fixation and C─N/S─N Bond Formation
articles.abstract: Direct synthesis of organonitrogen compounds from dinitrogen (N2) remains a formidable challenge because N2‐to‐C─N bond formation requires nitrogen fixation to be coupled with selective functionalization of N2‐derived intermediates before their termination as ammonia. Herein, we report a cascade electrochemical strategy that converts N2 into aryl imides and aryl sulfonimides in a gas‐diffusion electrochemical flow cell. Under proton‐donor‐free conditions, electrochemically generated Li3N is intercepted by acyl or sulfonyl chlorides, enabling one‐pot synthesis of aryl imides and sulfonimides from N2 in yields up to 57%. This represents a notably high yield for direct N2‐derived organonitrogen synthesis. This work couples N2 fixation and C─N/S─N bond formation, expanding electrochemical nitrogen fixation beyond ammonia synthesis toward direct construction of value‐added C─N/S─N bonds.

articles.title: Centrosymmetric Molecular Strategy With Quadruple Boron–Nitrogen Heteroarenes Enabling Efficient Ultra‐Narrowband Emission
articles.abstract: Realizing ultra‐narrowband multiple‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) with long‐wavelength emission remains a formidable challenge due to the increased vibronic coupling and excited‐state relaxation with the extension of π‐conjugated framework. In this contribution, a proof‐of‐concept of centrosymmetric molecular strategy fused with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes is proposed to develop ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters. Thus, two MR‐TADF emitters, called DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR, are prepared and characterized. Compounds DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR exhibit the emission peaks at 562 nm and 518 nm in toluene solution, respectively. Small full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) of only 16 nm (0.063 eV) for DCz‐MR and 12 nm (0.055 eV) for DAn‐MR are obtained in toluene, especially 14.2 nm (0.058 eV) for DCz‐MR and 8.2 nm (0.040 eV) for DAn‐MR in hexane. In solution‐processed phosphorescence‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes, DAn‐MR delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency of 24.8% with an electroluminescence FWHM of 27 nm. This research work provides a new method for designing ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters.

Decoding Innate T Cell Functionality in Tumor Immunity and Therapeutic Response
articles.abstract: Innate T cells, including invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells, mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells, and γδ T cells, bridge innate and adaptive immunity through rapid responses to nonpeptide antigens, metabolites, and stress-associated signals. In cancer, these populations can promote tumor surveillance through cytotoxicity, type 1 cytokine production, tissue-resident immune monitoring, and activation of broader antitumor networks. However, their functions are highly context dependent. Within suppressive tumor microenvironments, tumor-infiltrating unconventional T cell compartments may contain developmentally programmed innate-like subsets together with recruited or locally differentiated cells displaying dysfunctional, regulatory, or IL-17-associated features that support myeloid cell recruitment, chronic inflammation, immune evasion, and therapy resistance. This review discusses the major recognition pathways, functional states, microbiota- and metabolite-dependent regulation, and therapeutic targeting of iNKT, MAIT, and γδ T cells in cancer. We further highlight emerging strategies to harness these cells through endogenous activation, combination immunotherapy, and engineered cell platforms while limiting tumor-promoting inflammatory programs and treatment-associated toxicity.

articles.title: A microbiome-bile acid axis mediates protection from chronic liver disease in females
articles.abstract: isoUDCA, a female-enriched bile acid produced by a gut bacterial consortium favored by estrogen, promotes hepatic cholesterol handling and bile acid metabolism through SREBP2-STARD4-CYP7B1 signaling, thereby alleviating chronic liver injury.

The pyrin inflammasome senses OCTN2-mediated uptake of extracellular ʟ-carnitine from muscle injury or ingestion
articles.abstract: ʟ-Carnitine is a nonproteinogenic amino acid highly abundant in myocytes, and both excess ingestion of myocytes and myocyte necrosis are associated with systemic inflammation. Here, we find that the pyrin inflammasome senses extracellular ʟ-carnitine through the high-affinity carnitine transporter OCTN2 (SLC22A5) and this leads to IL-1β-mediated inflammation. Our findings position OCTN2 as a potential target to reduce inflammation from exogenous or endogenous sources of extracellular ʟ-carnitine.

articles.title: Selective USP32 inhibition reveals endosomal ubiquitin signaling and enables cell-permeable activity-based probes
articles.abstract: First-in-class selective chemical targeting of USP32 uncovers its role in endosomal ubiquitin signaling. Scherpe, Vermue et al. develop a covalent USP32 inhibitor and complementary activity-based probes that reveal known and new membrane trafficking substrates and enable direct interrogation of USP32 activity in cells.

articles.title: RUNX1-ETO oncoprotein levels determine the balance between endothelial reprogramming and pre-leukemic growth in a human ES cell model of AML
articles.abstract: In t(8;21) acute myeloid leukemia (AML), the RUNX1 DNA binding domain is fused to RUNX1T1 (ETO) producing the RUNX1-ETO fusion protein. We previously showed that t(8;21) leukemic stem cells aberrantly activate endothelial signaling pathways to initiate blast cell proliferation. Here, we employed a human embryonic stem cell (ESC) line carrying an inducible RUNX1-ETO transgene to determine whether endothelial signaling pathway activation depends on disease progression or is directly induced by RUNX1-ETO. Single-cell analyses demonstrate that RUNX1-ETO reprograms ESC-derived myeloid progenitors towards endothelial cells. We show (1) that endothelial reprogramming is RUNX1-ETO concentration-dependent and irreversible, (2) at similar RUNX1-ETO and RUNX1 expression levels, a sub-population of blood progenitors can escape reprogramming, and (3) keeps proliferating when co-cultured with endothelial cells. Our experiments highlight the role of cellular interactions in the maintenance of pre-leukemic cells and provide important insights into the earliest stages of genomic reprogramming by oncogenic transcription factors.

articles.title: The conserved NUS-1/DHDDS-1 complex links N-glycosylation to lipid and lysosomal homeostasis in C. elegans
articles.abstract: N-glycosylation is essential for proteome integrity, yet the systemic roles of the cis-prenyltransferase (cis-PT) complex remain poorly defined. Using Caenorhabditis elegans, we demonstrate that this complex is a dual regulator of global lipid and lysosomal homeostasis. Mechanistically, NUS-1 physically associates with the core oligosaccharyltransferase (OST) complex to coordinate N-glycan transfer. Loss of NUS-1/DHDDS-1 triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress, lysosomal collapse, and systemic lipopenia. This lipid defect arises from impaired N-glycosylation of the SREBP cleavage-activating protein (SCAP). cis-PT deficiency causes unglycosylated SCAP to undergo massive degradation and absolute physical entrapment within the ER, preventing SREBP nuclear translocation and downstream lipid synthesis. Furthermore, pathogenic mutations cause dysfunction through distinct molecular mechanisms: pocket integrity disruption or catalytic impairment. These findings uncover an essential crosstalk between protein glycosylation and global lipid metabolism, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding the systemic pathophysiology of congenital disorders of glycosylation (CDG).

articles.title: Isobavachalcone targets deubiquitinase OTUB1 to induce PD-L1 degradation and enhances antitumor immunity
articles.abstract: Zhang et al. demonstrate that isobavachalcone targets the deubiquitinase OTUB1 to promote PD-L1 ubiquitination and degradation in cancer cells. This regulation enhances T cell-mediated antitumor immunity and reshapes the tumor immune microenvironment to suppress tumor growth.

articles.title: Targeting oncogenic SOX2 condensates suppresses squamous cell carcinoma progression
articles.abstract: Luan et al. reveal that SOX2 condensates promote squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) progression by regulating chromatin organization and oncogene expression. The FDA-approved drug ixazomib selectively disrupts SOX2 condensates in an HSP70-dependent manner, offering an SCC-specific, biomarker-guided therapeutic strategy with high translational potential.

articles.title: Ligand-protected copper nanoclusters enable room-temperature semihydrogenation of terminal alkynes
articles.abstract: An atomically precise, ligand-capped Cu49 nanocluster is demonstrated to efficiently catalyze the semihydrogenation of alkynes at room temperature. Its unique surface coordination architecture governs substrate adsorption via steric effects; this structural feature, combined with the cluster’s remarkable stability, concurrently facilitates effective alkyne activation and ensures high hydrogenation selectivity. Notably, this work overcomes the conventional dependence on noble metals such as gold and palladium in hydrogenation catalysis, revealing the significant potential of ligand-protected copper nanoclusters for this transformation.

articles.title: Selective upcycling of polyesters to dicarboxylic acids via tandem depolymerization-dehydrogenative oxidation
articles.abstract: While polyester waste represents a valuable carbon resource for chemical production, its upcycling typically involves multiple steps for polymer depolymerization, intermediate separation, and subsequent conversion. This work establishes a tandem catalytic method that integrates depolymerization and selective upcycling in a single process, which selectively converts diverse commercial polyesters and mixed waste streams into valuable dicarboxylic acids.

articles.title: Artificial photosynthetic cells: bridging chemical energization with biological functionalization
articles.abstract: This review summarizes the bioinspired design principles, core modules, assembly strategies, unique functions, advances, and bottlenecks of artificial photosynthetic cells, and outlines future opportunities for synthetic photobiological systems.

articles.title: Strategies towards designing visible and near-infrared light driven molecular motors
articles.abstract: This review summarizes molecular design strategies for shifting molecular motors from UV to visible and near-infrared operation, with emphasis on recent advances and emerging applications.

ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial
articles.abstract: Point-of-care high-sensitivity cTn (cardiac troponin; hs-cTn) testing has the potential to expedite decision-making and reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay for patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction by ensuring that results are consistently available when sought by clinicians. We assessed the real-life effectiveness and safety of implementing point-of-care hs-cTn testing in the ED. We conducted a pragmatic, stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial. The control arm was usual care with an accelerated diagnostic pathway using a single-sample rule-out step with a central laboratory hs-cTn assay. The intervention arm used the same pathway with a point-of-care hs-cTnI assay. The primary effectiveness outcome was ED length of stay assessed using a generalized linear mixed model. The safety outcome was myocardial infarction or cardiac death within 30 days. Six sites participated, with 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals; mean 61±19 years of age; 49.5% female) from February 2023 through January 2025; 31 392 presentations were during the intervention arm. After adjustment for covariates associated with length of stay, the intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%–16%; P <0.001), corresponding to a reduction of 47 minutes (95% CI, 33–61 minutes) from a mean length of stay in the control arm of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was similar in the control and intervention arms (0.39% and 0.39%, respectively; P =0.54). Implementation of whole-blood hs-cTnI testing at the point of care into an accelerated diagnostic pathway was safe and reduced length of stay in the ED compared with laboratory testing. URL: https://www.anzctr.org.au ; Unique identifier: ACTRN12619001189112.

Opportunistic Screening for Chagas Disease Using an Artificial Intelligence–Enabled ECG: Prospective Evaluation of Feasibility and Diagnostic Accuracy
articles.abstract: Chagas disease (ChD), a neglected cardiovascular condition, affects 7.5 to 10.5 million people worldwide. Opportunistic screening during routine electrocardiography may allow earlier detection of unrecognized infections, enabling timely antiparasitic therapy or optimized cardiac care. This study prospectively evaluated the feasibility and diagnostic accuracy of an artificial intelligence (AI)–enabled ECG model enriched with 3 epidemiological questions (AI-ECG-EPI model) as an opportunistic screening for ChD in endemic regions of Brazil. We conducted a prospective study embedded in the Telehealth Network of Minas Gerais, Brazil, across 107 municipalities in hyperendemic and endemic regions. From October 2023 to September 2024, adults undergoing routine tele-ECGs were eligible. The primary exposure was the output of the AI-ECG-EPI model: all positive individuals and a 3:1 sample of negative individuals were invited for serology (index test–dependent sampling), the reference standard. Weighted analyses (inverse probability) accounted for this sampling design. Diagnostic metrics included sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios, area under the receiver operating characteristics curve, and area under the precision recall curve. The AI-ECG-EPI model was compared with both an epidemiological questions model and an AI ECG–only model. Among 75 779 eligible ECGs, the AI-ECG-EPI model was available for 59 154 individuals; 6812 (11.5%) screened positive. A total of 7804 selected were invited for serology, and 3509 completed testing (2517 positive; 992 negative). ChD was confirmed in 36.8% of positive and 9.3% of negative individuals. The weighted prevalence of ChD was 12.2%. Sensitivity was 34.3%, specificity 91.6%, harmonic mean of precision and recall score 0.52, and diagnostic odds ratio 5.69. The AI-ECG-EPI model showed higher discrimination than both the epidemiological questions model and AI ECG–only model (area under the receiver operating characteristics curve, 77.6% versus 70.0% and 64.5%, respectively; P <0.001). Precision recall curves showed higher precision across most recall levels. Exploratory analysis suggested improved risk reclassification (net reclassification improvement, 0.503). Performance was higher in women and in individuals with Chagas cardiomyopathy. In this community-based study, an AI-ECG-EPI model integrated into a public telecardiology network enabled feasible opportunistic screening for ChD in primary care. It showed acceptable diagnostic accuracy, with higher discrimination than epidemiological questions and AI ECG–only models, and identified many previously undiagnosed patients in endemic regions, supporting its potential role in scalable screening strategies. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov ; Unique identifier: NCT02646943.

articles.title: Radiation Vasculopathy of the Coronary Arteries: State-of-the Art Review
articles.abstract: Radiation-associated coronary artery disease (RACAD) is a distinct form of coronary artery disease with several specific biological and clinical aspects as well as key knowledge gaps. RACAD is prevalent in patients with cardiac exposure to radiotherapy. As radiotherapy is integral to the effective treatment of many thoracic malignancies, improved long-term survivorship is coupled with increased risk for RACAD. Ionizing radiation induces free radical generation and activation of proinflammatory cascades, leading to endothelial dysfunction and accelerated atherosclerosis. Risks for RACAD are determined both by radiotherapy, including the radiation dose and the proximity of coronary arteries to the radiotherapy field, and by patient-specific factors, such as younger age, higher baseline cardiovascular risk, and concurrent cardiotoxic systemic therapies. Importantly, radiotherapy delivery is highly individualized on the basis of tumor location and treatment strategy, resulting in heterogeneous coronary exposure to radiation and patient-to-patient variability. Clinical presentation may occur early, within 1 to 2 years, especially in patients with higher cardiac radiation doses (eg, lung or esophageal cancer), or after a latency period of 5 to 20 years with lower cardiac dose radiation exposure (eg, left-sided breast cancer). Patients generally present with symptoms similar to conventional coronary artery disease. However, RACAD symptoms may be underrecognized in cancer survivors due to overlapping treatment-related fatigue, pulmonary disease, or competing oncologic symptoms. Diagnosis and management generally follow standard coronary artery disease guidelines while incorporating cancer-specific considerations, such as planned oncologic surgeries, bleeding risk, postradiotherapy complications such as atretic internal mammary arteries, and cardiotoxic effects of systemic cancer therapies. Primary prevention of RACAD is critical, emphasizing advances in precision radiotherapy, including delivery techniques with improved coronary dosimetry, and cardiac shielding. Key knowledge gaps include understanding long-term outcomes with contemporary 3-dimensional conformal radiotherapy techniques, validated cancer-specific risk prediction models on the basis of coronary dosimetry, optimal surveillance protocols, targeted molecular pharmacotherapies, and risk analysis of percutaneous versus surgical management of RACAD. Prospective studies are needed to develop cancer- and dosimetry-specific risk calculators, validating cardioprotective interventions, and improving multidisciplinary cardio-oncology collaboration to optimize early detection of RACAD and timely intervention in the growing population of cancer survivors.
