Arabidopsis cyclin‐dependent kinases and MAP65 phosphorylation link microtubule dynamics with salt stress adaptation
articles.abstract: Working model illustrating the CDK‐MAP65‐microtubule module mediating salt stress adaptation in Arabidopsis. Summary Plants possess sophisticated regulatory mechanisms to balance growth and stress responses. Cyclin‐dependent kinases (CDKs) are established regulators of cell division and endoreduplication, yet their roles in abiotic stress responses remain poorly understood. Here, using reverse genetics, biochemical, and cell biological approaches, we show that Arabidopsis (Arabidopsis thaliana) CDKB1s contribute to salt stress adaptation through a mechanism involving the phosphorylation of MAP65‐1 and MAP65‐2, two microtubule‐associated proteins essential for cytoskeleton dynamics under salt stress. Loss of CDKB1 function enhances salt tolerance, accompanied by attenuated plasma membrane depolarization and reactive oxygen species accumulation. In vitro phosphorylation assays demonstrate that CDKB1;1 directly phosphorylates MAP65‐1 at Ser‐503. Genetic analyses indicate that phospho‐dead MAP65 variants confer enhanced salt tolerance, whereas phosphomimetic variants compromise tolerance even in the cdkb1;1 1;2 background, supporting a critical role for MAP65 phosphorylation status at these sites in salt stress adaptation. We further found that CDKA;1 can similarly interact with and phosphorylate MAP65‐1, suggesting a potential parallel role for CDKA;1 in this process. Collectively, our findings identify a regulatory module involving CDKs, MAP65, and microtubules that links cell cycle kinases and cytoskeleton dynamics with plant salt stress adaptation.

articles.title: Beyond sanctions: where the costs of nursery pollination are borne
Cell‐type‐specific PIN‐FORMED 3‐mediated polar auxin transport regulates cambial activity and tension wood formation in Populus tomentosa
articles.abstract: Phloem‐specific silencing of PIN3 impairs polar auxin transport and auxin response in Populus tomentosa. Summary Auxin is a central regulator of tree secondary growth and forms maxima in the vascular cambium, yet how these maxima are established remains elusive. Here, we functionally characterized two redundant PIN‐FORMED 3 (PIN3) paralogs from Populus tomentosa to define their roles in secondary growth and gravity‐induced tension wood (TW) formation. We employed fluorescent reporter lines, clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats‐generated knockout mutants, phloem‐specific RNA interference transgenic plants and isotopic auxin transport assays to dissect PIN3 functions during secondary growth of poplar stems. Loss of function of PIN3 paralogs severely compromises cambial proliferation, secondary xylem differentiation and TW development. PIN3 proteins display cell‐type‐specific polar localization with basal polarity in phloem cells and outer lateral polarity in endodermal cells. Phloem‐expressed PIN3 facilitates basipetal auxin transport and is required for cambial auxin response. Upon gravistimulation, endodermal PIN3 repolarizes along the gravity vector, correlating with TW formation. Our findings identify a cell‐type‐specific, PIN3‐mediated auxin transport mechanism that contributes to auxin‐driven secondary growth of tree stems.

articles.title: Drought‐induced plant dominance shift amplifies functional niche differentiation in steppe communities
articles.abstract: Community trait variation (a), community‐weighted trait overlap (b), intraspecific trait variation (ITV, c), and its relative contribution to community trait variation (rITV, d) for all the four examined traits under different treatments (mean ± SE, n = 12). Summary Trait‐based studies on community assembly under environmental change often overlook intraspecific trait variation (ITV), despite its considerable role in modulating community dynamics, which may largely mislead the inference of community assembly. Under simulated extreme droughts in a temperate steppe, we integrated ITV and interspecific trait variation for four key traits, plant height (Height), specific leaf area (SLA), leaf dry matter content (LDMC), and leaf thickness (LT), to examine how drought alters functional niche structure and underlying processes. Drought shifted communities toward conservative resource‐use strategies, reduced community variation in LT, and interspecific trait overlap in terms of SLA, LDMC, LT, and the multivariate trait space, whereas community‐level ITV remained stable across all traits. These changes were driven primarily by diversity loss and increases in the dominance of fewer species, with negligible effects of intraspecific trait plasticity or species turnover. Communities with fewer but more dominant species exhibited smaller trait overlap. Our findings advance our understanding of the paradigm of trait convergence under environmental filtering. Drought‐induced diversity loss amplifies functional niche differentiation, underscoring the critical role of species reorganization through dominance shifts, with little evidence for intraspecific trait plasticity in mediating community assembly under climate extremes.

articles.title: Engineering uORFs in wheat improves abiotic stress tolerance without growth penalties
articles.abstract: Precise editing of upstream open reading frames enabled in situ fine-tuning of gene expression in allohexaploid wheat, thereby enhancing abiotic stress tolerance without growth penalties. Summary Developing climate-resilient crops is critical for ensuring global food security, yet agricultural productivity is frequently constrained by the trade-off between stress tolerance and growth. This challenge is particularly acute in allohexaploid wheat, a staple crop susceptible to abiotic stresses, underscoring the demand for precise gene regulation. Here, we established a simple, efficient, and transgene-free method for regulating gene expression in allohexaploid wheat by disrupting or creating de novo upstream open reading frames (uORFs) via genome editing. Using ribosome profiling, we identified 1199 actively translated uORFs across the wheat genome and developed a dual-luciferase screening pipeline to pinpoint potent translational repressors of positive regulators of abiotic stress. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated disruption of the uORFs in TaCIPK14 and TaGGP1 elevated downstream protein accumulation, thereby enhancing drought, cold, and salt tolerance of plants. Furthermore, base editing was employed to generate de novo uORFs in TaMADS26, effectively downregulating gene expression and improving drought resilience. Notably, both the transgene-free uorf TaGGP1-ACG and uORFTaMADS26 mutants conferred pronounced yield advantages under drought conditions without incurring growth penalties under well-watered conditions. This study provides a predictable and precise way for modulating gene expression, enabling the coordinated improvement of stress resilience and agronomic performance in wheat.

articles.title: MicroRNA 160 controls the auxin response factor–class III peroxidase module and couples salicylic acid and redox signaling networks in the potato hypersensitive response to potato virus Y
articles.abstract: miR160 links salicylic acid, auxin, and redox signaling with the growth–defense trade‐off in the potato hypersensitive response to potato virus Y. Summary Hypersensitive response (HR) is an effector‐triggered immune response leading to pathogen restriction and local cell death. Small RNAs (sRNAs), mediating RNA silencing, have a well‐established role in antiviral immunity; however, their role in HR has not been addressed to date. We applied a spatially resolved sRNA‐omics approach to uncover changes at the sRNA level and the dynamics of sRNA–gene regulatory networks in potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) HR to potato virus Y (PVY). We show that miR160 is repressed in cells adjacent to HR lesions in the resistant cultivar, but not in PVY‐sensitive, salicylic acid (SA)‐depleted plants. Beyond its canonical regulation of StARF10 and StARF17, miR160 controls a broader regulatory network spanning auxin signaling, cell‐wall remodeling, redox homeostasis, and tuberization. Elevated miR160 levels promote susceptibility‐associated traits, reduce thermotolerance, and suppress genes strongly activated in HR. Mechanistically, we identify a novel miR160–StARF10/StARF17–StPRX28 module that links miR160 repression to the induction of a Class III apoplastic peroxidase in HR, with SA acting upstream. Together, these findings establish miR160 as an important regulatory node that connects SA–auxin–redox signaling pathways and tunes development, defense, and heat resilience, and highlight miR160 as a promising target for fine‐tuning tolerance to multiple stresses with minimal yield loss.

articles.title: No need to exceed: tomato ripening is controlled by a small amount of ethylene
Accurate Atomic Correlation Energies and Virial Trends for Correlation-Consistent Effective Core Potentials III: Quantitative Separation of Fixed-Node Biases and Localization Errors in Cs-Rn
articles.abstract: Atomic benchmarks for sixth-period elements (Cs-Rn) are established to sub-millihartree precision under correlation-consistent effective core potentials (ccECPs) using coupled-cluster [up to CCSDT(Q)] and full configuration interaction methods. These references systematically characterize electron correlation, potential-to-kinetic energy partitioning, and combined fixed-node and locality biases ($η$) in fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo (FNDMC). The valence kinetic-to-total energy ratio ($ξ$) departs from the non-relativistic all-electron Coulombic virial limit ($ξ=100\%$), remaining confined between 25.8$\%$ and 37.6$\%$. The Un-pseudizing of semi-core shells decreases $ξ$ as the attractive potential energy deepens faster than the accompanying kinetic energy escalates. Periodic trends in $ξ$ reveal a $5d$ plateau near 34$\%$, with a lanthanide-contraction-driven maximum in Hf, followed by a sharp decline across the $6p$ block. In FNDMC, $η$ escalates rapidly at the onset of group-1/2 and toward the $6p$ closed-shell limit, peaking at 5.42$\%$ in Rn. Although fixed-node errors dominate $η$ in most sixth-period elements, a locality error inversion occurs in Bi, with Pb exhibiting comparable error magnitudes. Furthermore, core-valence partitioning alters trial wavefunction nodal topology: in Tl, three-dimensional nodal cross-sections reveal isolated toroidal domains that confine walkers. This work completes the periodic-table-wide ccECP database from H to Rn, revealing how pseudopotential choices govern energy partitioning, nodal topology, and the balance between fixed-node and localization errors.

articles.title: Boosting fluorescence and polarization with nanophotonics for single-molecule chiral sensing
articles.abstract: Detecting chirality is essential in chemistry and biomedicine. Circular dichroism identifies chiral molecules through their differential absorption of circularly polarized light. However, its sensitivity is limited by vanishing absorption at low concentrations. Fluorescence-based methods have already enabled other optical techniques to reach the single-molecule limit and could, in principle, also extend chiral detection to reach this sensitivity regime. They are marred, however, by the combination of weak fluorescence signals and low polarization contrast. To overcome these limitations, we leverage high-index dielectric nanophotonics to simultaneously enhance both fluorescence and polarization for chiral sensing. We propose a reciprocity-based analytical framework for a chiral dipolar emitter coupled to a nanoantenna and reveal the different contributions and trade-offs governing the enhancement of circularly polarized fluorescence. Guided by this insight, we tailor achiral dielectric nanostructures to reach a 1000-fold enhancement of fluorescence intensity together with a 10-fold increase in polarization. Crucially, we show that accounting for extrinsic polarization effects in the angular emission patterns of nanophotonic structures is indispensable for reliable enantiomer discrimination. Our approach opens a realistic path for single-molecule chiral sensing.

articles.title: Epitaxial Displacement-etched GaAsSb Quantum Dots Emitting at Telecom Wavelengths
articles.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are essential components for integrated photonic and quantum information systems, yet current epitaxial growth techniques face significant limitations in complexity of growth, material selection, and density tunability. Here we report a displacement etch technique that enables controlled formation of GaAsSb QDs with emission at telecommunications wavelengths. Our approach uses arsenic molecular flux (As$_2$) to react with antimonide surfaces through thermodynamically favorable displacement reactions, creating three-dimensional quantum confined nanostructures without requiring strain-driven growth or complex droplet-based processes. Density functional theory shows the two competing As-for-Sb exchange pathways to be nearly equivalent in both reaction energy and activation barrier, which places morphological control in the subsequent adatom kinetics rather than in the surface reaction itself. A single process parameter, the As$_2$ exposure, sets the QD areal density across three orders of magnitude, from 10$^2$ to 10$^5$ $μm^{-2}$, covering both isolated emitters and dense gain media. Structural analysis reveals well-defined GaAsSb QDs with a mixed GaAs/GaSb composition and no extended defects. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence measurements confirm emission at 1550 nm (0.8 eV) within the telecommunications C-band, with characteristic QD-like temperature dependence. Because the QDs form on a lattice-matched GaSb surface in a single growth step, the technique offers a practical route to C-band emitters built into the GaSb/AlGaSb device family already used for mid-infrared sources and detectors.

articles.title: Low-Field J-Coupling Spectroscopy Measured with a Diamond Nitrogen Vacancy Spectrometer
articles.abstract: Nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond (NVs) are point defects well suited to quantum sensing of magnetic fields. NV spin states can be initialized and read out optically with high spatial resolution, enabling detection of pL-scale volumes of nuclear spins. Using Coherently Averaged Synchronized Readout (CASR), standard NMR spectroscopy techniques such as free decay, spin echo, and PGSE have been performed with Hz-scale spectral resolution using NV-diamond sensors. However, using NV detection for conventional high-resolution NMR at multi-tesla fields is challenging due to the need to manipulate NV electronic spins at resonance frequencies 100 GHz or higher. Low-field J-coupling spectroscopy provides an alternative path to chemical resolution in a regime more easily accessible to NVs. Here, we demonstrate homonuclear and heteronuclear J-coupling spectroscopy using an NV-NMR spectrometer based on permanent magnets operating at $\sim$890 kHz proton Larmor frequency (bias magnetic field $\sim$21 mT). This field strength enables chemical characterization based on J-coupling using sequences such as Synchronized Echo (SyncE) and Spin-Echo Double Resonance (SEDOR), which do not require the strong chemical shift dispersion and pristine field homogeneity of high-field NMR. The frequency range is easily detected by NVs using standard XY dynamical decoupling sequences and is well-suited for applying Overhauser DNP, which can boost proton signal by two orders of magnitude. We acquire initial NV-NMR measurements of T$_1$, T$_2$, and Overhauser DNP in glycerol before advancing to SEDOR spectroscopy of methanol-$^{13}$C and a methanol-$^{13}$C/acetonitrile-2-$^{13}$C mixture at sample volumes $\sim$50 pL, in which we demonstrate measurement of $^1J_\text{CH}$ couplings and resolution between species. We also acquire a homonuclear J-coupling spectrum of a natural-abundance propylene carbonate sample.

articles.title: Microphase Separation and Ionic Aggregation in Oppositely Charged End-Functionalized Polymer Blends
articles.abstract: We study the phase behavior of binary blends of polymers with oppositely charged termini using an ion-correlation-augmented self-consistent field theory (IC-SCFT). Under the low dielectric conditions typical for organic polymer melts, strong ion correlations drive association of multiple chain ends, leading to emergent multichain architectures that go beyond a simple ion-paired diblock copolymer picture previously used to interpret recent experiments. At moderate to strong polymer segregation, the resulting phase diagram differs considerably from this effective-diblock prediction: ion clustering broadens the lamellar and cylindrical windows while suppressing the network phases, the reverse of the trend for end-charged diblock copolymers. At weak segregation, the two polymers remain miscible even as ion clustering persists, and decreasing chain length drives the clusters themselves through a sphere-to-cylinder-to-lamella shape transition, connecting continuously to the aggregation behavior of classical terminally charged ionomers in the limit when one of the polymer species shrinks to just the charged end. These results reveal that ion clustering -- beyond simple pairwise bonding -- shapes the self-assembly of end-charged polymer blends.

articles.title: Rovibrational dynamics in strongly-coupled gas-phase methane
articles.abstract: Polaritons, the hybrid light-matter states formed when molecular transitions are strongly coupled to an optical cavity mode, appear to alter chemical dynamics, reactivity, and photophysics, though the mechanisms and reproducibility of these effects remain hotly debated. Nearly all reports in polariton chemistry rest on spectroscopic measurements of optical cavity transmission. Interpretation of these experiments therefore relies on understanding the linear and nonlinear spectroscopy of strongly-coupled systems. Working in the gas phase can dramatically simplify spectroscopic observables, as the intermolecular and environmental interactions that complicate the response of condensed-phase systems can be minimized. Our prior work introduced a platform for gas-phase molecular polaritons and demonstrated that linear cavity transmission spectra in the strong coupling regime are well described with classical Fabry-Pérot cavity physics. Here, we extend this platform to the nonlinear spectroscopy of cavity-coupled rovibrational transitions of methane. We monitor transient changes in the cavity transmission spectrum following optical pumping of intracavity molecules via an axis orthogonal to the longitudinal cavity axis. We find that the classical Fabry-Pérot cavity treatment quantitatively reproduces our transient spectra and allows for extraction of the collisional relaxation and transport timescales of intracavity molecules. We observe no difference in the dynamics of strongly-coupled methane versus free-space, non-cavity control experiments. This effort connects our gas-phase work to the much larger body of transient condensed-phase polariton spectroscopy and represents a step towards predictive understanding of molecular dynamics under strong coupling.

articles.title: Water-Driven Porous Silicon as a Platform for Blue Materials
articles.abstract: Living organisms control water to transport matter, transfer energy and drive chemical reactions. In this perspective, we argue that porous silicon can give engineering materials comparable control over water. Its pore architecture, surface chemistry and semiconducting skeleton can be shaped across length scales with the precision of semiconductor processing and, like the water it can host, it relies on one of the most abundant chemical elements on Earth. Liquids in porous silicon, most often water, can flow as a continuum through pores a few nanometers wide, strain the skeleton through capillary and electrosorption stresses, shift structural color, switch transparency, and modulate or generate electrical signals. We describe three directions to combine and extend these effects and overcome their limitations. Pore hierarchy resolves the classical trade-off between interface area and transport speed by combining large and small pores and thereby allows functions to be scaled from thin planar films to three-dimensional components. Surface modification becomes a design variable that tunes the interaction between water and the pore wall. It can be set locally and, with switchable coatings, on demand. Finally, pores only a few molecules wide alter the properties of water itself. In the absence of a bulk-like volume, water can become dielectrically anisotropic and highly conductive. Altogether, these steps turn porous silicon from a responsive material into an adaptive, water-driven material.

articles.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Allylic Substitution with Alkynylogous Silyl Enol Ethers En Route to Chiral Allenes
articles.abstract: Despite their potential as building blocks of allenes, alkynylogous enol silanes have rarely been employed in organic synthesis. Herein, we establish their utility as nucleophiles in catalytic asymmetric allylic substitution, which results in skipped enallenes bearing two vicinal stereogenic elements (axial and central chirality). This iridium-catalyzed reaction utilizes α-alkynyl silyl enol ethers as alkynylogous nucleophile for reaction with easily accessible racemic branched allylic alcohols and endows tetrasubstituted axially chiral allenones, bearing a δ-stereocenter exclusively as a single regioisomer in moderate to good diastereoselectivity (up to 11:1 dr) and in most cases with high enantioselectivity (up to >99.5:0.5 er). The densely functionalized γ-allylic allenones can be elaborated into useful building blocks, including a highly substituted chiral 2-allyl furan derivative. Through this work, α-alkynyl enol silanes are introduced as alkynylogous nucleophiles in transition metal catalysis.

articles.title: Deep-Learning-Driven Discovery and Engineering of Imine Reductase for the Efficient Synthesis of Chiral Opine Derivatives
articles.abstract: The narrow amine donor scope of imine reductases (IREDs) limits their application in the synthesis of opine compounds. Herein, we report a machine learning (ML)-guided protein engineering strategy to address this limitation. An IRED from an unclassified Ensifer, IRED5, was identified through deep-learning-based screening for its strict enantioselectivity toward methyl glycinate. Subsequent engineering using a few-shot learning for protein fitness prediction approach yielded the M178T/A208L/P241V/A36E/S67Q/Q187N (M6) variant with six mutations across the active site and protein surface. Kinetic analysis showed 156-fold toward methyl pyruvate and 72-fold improvements toward methyl glycinate in catalytic efficiency, respectively, over the wild-type (WT) enzyme. M6 accepted diverse keto esters and amino acid esters, enabling stereoselective formation of opine derivatives bearing two stereocenters. Structural and computational analyses revealed the molecular basis for activity enhancement. In preparative synthesis, M6 achieved complete conversion at a 3 M substrate loading, corresponding to a space time yield of 366 g·L–1·d–1. At a 4 M substrate loading, conversion remained high at 95.4% with a space time yield of 525 g·L–1·d–1, affording 10.5 g of enantiopure methyl N-(2-methoxy-2-oxoethyl)-d-alaninate (1a) in 75.0% isolated yield with > 99.9% ee. This work establishes an efficient biocatalytic route to opine compounds and demonstrates the utility of ML-guided enzyme engineering in expanding IRED synthetic capability.

articles.title: Diastereoselective Heterogeneous Hydrogenation of Fused Arenes Directed by Amines and Alcohols
articles.abstract: The heterogeneous hydrogenation of aromatic compounds using supported metal catalysts is an efficient strategy to increase the three-dimensionality and molecular complexity of organic molecules. However, most heterogeneous hydrogenation methods lack stereoselectivity or rely upon the steric properties of the substrate for stereocontrol, which limit their predictability and generality for pharmaceutical synthesis applications. In this work, we develop two synthetic methods for the amine- and hydroxyl-directed hydrogenation of benzofused arenes using Rh/C and Pt3Cu/SiO2 as heterogeneous catalysts, respectively. Mechanistic studies on the amine-directed reaction reveal that simultaneous adsorption of the amine and benzene functional groups to the Rh metal surface is extremely strong, outcompeting the adsorption of the benzene or amine individually and enabling good turnover and high diastereoselectivity toward the amine-directed product. A broad scope of benzofused scaffolds are effective substrates, generating up to four stereocenters in a single step. The utility of the method is demonstrated in the synthesis of a pyridine bisoxazoline compound derived from perhydro-cis-aminoindanol.

articles.title: High-Density Iridium Single Atoms on Vanadium-Doped TiO2 for Electrochemical Water Oxidation Catalysis
articles.abstract: Water oxidation in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) uses IrO2 nanoparticles supported on corrosion-resistant TiO2. However, the low conductivity of TiO2 imposes electronic transport limitations that necessitate high Ir loadings for effective catalysis. Here, we present a catalyst design strategy that couples a heavily V-doped TiO2 support with high-density Ir single atoms, enabling water oxidation at minimal Ir loading. In this design, Ti-site-substituted V provides n-type doping, and selective V leaching creates cation vacancies that anchor Ir as isolated atoms. TEM with convolutional neural network (CNN)-based analysis shows Ir single-atom density increases with V content, accompanied by lower charge-transfer resistance and higher Ir-specific activity. The density functional theory indicates that cation-site Ir introduces a midgap state below V 3d levels and shifts neighboring V 3d orbitals toward the Fermi level. Ir1/V-TiO2 achieves 1480 A gIr–1 at 1.55 V vs RHE (1.3 wt % Ir) and demonstrates device-level PEMWE operation at an Ir loading as low as 0.027 mgIr cm–2.

articles.title: Reductive Dispersion of In2O3 into H-CHA and Reversible Formation of Isolated In(I)/In(III) Species under H2/O2 Redox Cycling
articles.abstract: The reductive dispersion of metal oxides into isolated cationic species in zeolites is an important strategy for generating well-defined catalytic sites, yet its kinetics and molecular mechanism remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate the H2-induced redispersion of In2O3 physically mixed with H-CHA using in situ/operando UV–vis spectroscopy, In K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), SEM-EDS mapping, modulation-excitation spectroscopy, H2-TPR, XRF, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Time-resolved UV–vis spectroscopy quantitatively tracks the consumption of bulk-like In2O3 under H2 and reveals that the redispersion rate depends on temperature, H2 concentration, In2O3 precursor properties, and zeolite framework. Higher temperatures and H2 concentrations accelerate the process, with the highest reliable initial rate observed at 600 °C under 10% H2. In K-edge XANES indicates selective formation of reduced In species assigned to framework-stabilized In+ rather than metallic In0, demonstrating a partial-reduction pathway in CHA. H2-TPR provides quantitative redox evidence consistent with reductive solid-state ion exchange and reversible reduction of isolated oxygen-containing In species. SEM–EDS mapping shows the disappearance of surface In-rich domains after H2 treatment, consistent with indium redistribution, while XANES provides bulk-sensitive evidence for formation of reduced In species. Operando redox-cycling experiments reveal reversible interconversion between In(I) and oxygen-containing In(III) species under H2/O2 switching. DFT calculations using representative 1Al and 2Al CHA models suggest that local Al environments can influence the relative stability of framework-bound reduced In(I) and oxygen/hydroxyl-containing In(III)-type species. Together, these results support a two-step mechanism in which bulk In2O3 is first reduced to mobile In+ species and then anchored at acid sites within the zeolite framework. This work provides mechanistic insight into reductive redispersion and offers design principles for regenerable indium-based zeolite catalysts.

articles.title: Synergy of Ni Nanoparticles and MoO x Species for Selective Hydrodeoxygenation of Lignin into Cycloalkanes
articles.abstract: The selective hydrodeoxygenation of lignin as a substitute for fossil resources into aviation fuel-range cycloalkanes faces significant challenges due to its complex structure and diverse reaction pathways. Herein, we introduced MoOx species onto Ni nanoparticles-loaded Beta zeolite (Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta), which catalyzed the complete hydrodeoxygenation of lignin dimers and lignin-derived phenols into the corresponding cycloalkanes under mild conditions (200 °C, 2 MPa H2). Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta also enabled the hydrodeoxygenation of real lignin, achieving a cycloalkanes selectivity of over 83%. Mechanistic studies indicated that the synergistic effect between Ni nanoparticles and MoOx species was key to enhancing the hydrodeoxygenation performance. Ni nanoparticles enabled the adsorption and dissociation of H2, and horizontally adsorbed benzene ring in the oxygen-containing substrate, while adjacent MoOx species with abundant oxygen vacancies facilitated the vertical adsorption of oxygen-containing groups in the ring-saturated intermediates and the activation of C–O bonds. Simultaneously, the strong hydrogen spillover on Ni-0.2MoOx/Beta ensured the benzene ring hydrogenation and the cleavage of C–O bonds. This work provides an approach for designing non-noble metal catalysts for lignin hydrodeoxygenation, holding significant value for advancing the application of lignin-based aviation fuels.

articles.title: Grain Boundary Character Governs Lithium Deposition Uniformity on Polycrystalline Copper
articles.abstract: In anode-free Li metal batteries, a bare current collector must be converted into a reversible Li metal anode during the first charge, making Li nucleation decisive for reversibility. However, how current collector microstructure governs Li nucleation and growth remains poorly understood, since prior studies focused on single-crystal surfaces to identify favorable crystallographic orientations, leaving grain boundaries unexplored. Here, we identify grain boundary density and character in copper current collectors as key regulators of Li deposition uniformity. Systematic annealing decouples grain size from surface chemistry, revealing that deposition uniformity improves with copper grain coarsening but saturates as disordered boundaries are eliminated during grain growth, leaving predominantly low-energy configurations. Atomistic simulations show disordered boundaries impose high barriers to Li adatom migration, whereas ordered boundaries and adjacent low-index terraces provide low-barrier pathways for redistribution. Copper foils engineered beyond this threshold sustain uniform Li plating across diverse electrolytes and improve cyclability in anode-free cells.

articles.title: Overcoming Indium-Tin-Oxide Optical Losses in InAs Colloidal Quantum-Dot Light-Emitting Diodes at 1550 nm
articles.abstract: Light-emitting diodes (LEDs) based on colloidal InAs quantum dots (QDs) have emerged as promising light sources for the short-wave infrared (SWIR) range. However, their development is limited by relatively low photoluminescence quantum yield as well as intrinsic device design challenges. Here, we report LEDs with electroluminescence (EL) in the SWIR based on InAs/ZnSe core/shell colloidal QDs, synthesized via a seedless one-pot approach that enables the rapid growth of relatively large InAs cores. Zirconium-doped indium oxide (InZrO) was used as the bottom transparent electrode owing to its significantly higher infrared transparency compared to the commonly employed tin-doped indium oxide (ITO). These two key innovations pushed the EL beyond 1500 nm, with external quantum efficiencies of 3.0, 1.2, and 0.6% at 1093, 1198, and 1547 nm, respectively.

articles.title: Pressure-Driven Topological Reconfiguration toward Fast-Charging Hard Carbon with Plateau-Capacity Retention
articles.abstract: Conventional carbonization of semi-coke induces excessive ordering of aromatic skeletons, producing dense graphitic structures that hinder Na+ intercalation and suppress low-potential plateau capacity. Here, we develop a rapid thermomechanical coupling sintering strategy using moderate pressure to drive π–π interactions and topological reconfiguration of aromatic units. This process suppresses excessive graphitization while constructing interconnected, twisted pseudo-graphitic domains with abundant closed nanopores. At 1000 mA g–1, PTR-HC reaches 80% SOC in ≈14.4 min and retains 90.1% of its plateau capacity, enabled by abundant Na+ storage sites and rapid diffusion pathways. Kinetic analyses reveal accelerated Na+ transport and a thin, NaF-rich solid-electrolyte interphase with fewer organic components. In situ XRD and Raman attribute slope capacity to surface/defect adsorption and intercalation and the plateau capacity to quasi-metallic Na clusters in closed pores. This work establishes pressure-driven topological engineering as a promising strategy for upgrading semi-coke into fast-charging hard carbon with high plateau-capacity retention.

articles.title: Vacuum-Evaporated Molecules with Giant Spontaneous Orientation Polarization for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Interfacial losses at the perovskite/C60 and C60/metal contacts limit inverted perovskite solar cell performance. Here, we introduce a vacuum-evaporated molecule with giant spontaneous orientation polarization, 6F-2PI, for simultaneously tailoring both interfaces. Incorporating 6F-2PI increases the work function of perovskite, reducing the conduction band offset at the perovskite/C60 interface, which facilitates electron extraction. Concurrently, its phthalimide moieties passivate defect states, suppressing nonradiative recombination, as evidenced by a 0.03 eV recovery in quasi-Fermi level splitting. At the C60/metal interface, 6F-2PI also delivers efficient charge extraction, improved interfacial contact, and thermal resilience. Moreover, its hydrophobic fluorinated units prevent moisture ingress. Consequently, this dual-interface modulation boosts PCE from 18.5% to 22.5% with exceptional device stability, retaining over 90% of its initial efficiency after 2000 h under ambient conditions. Furthermore, this framework exhibits universal compatibility across both vacuum-deposited and solution-processed devices and simplifies processing for mass production.

articles.title: High thermoelectric performance in n-type–cubic (SnSe)0.55(PbTe)0.45 polycrystals via suppressed ionized impurity scattering
Suppression of structural transitions in iron: Magnetic stabilization of the bcc-phase via defect control
The Risk of an H5N1 Influenza Pandemic
articles.abstract: The last 110 years have seen four influenza A pandemics, where viruses have emerged from mammals or birds with the ability to transmit and cause disease in human populations. Since 2021, a high-pathogenicity strain of avian influenza, H5N1, has caused a panzootic (pandemic of animals), with global spread in wild birds, resulting in frequent spillovers into farmed poultry and into mammals, including mammal species not previously known to be affected by influenza A. This has created increased opportunity for reassortment, mutation, human infection, and potential adaptation to transmit. The risk to humans and the impact are difficult to quantify but of mounting concern to public health bodies. Here, we examine the risk of an H5N1 pandemic emerging and spreading in humans and the potential impact of an H5N1 pandemic.

articles.title: Amyloid-β Immunotherapy in Alzheimer's Disease: Challenges and Opportunities
articles.journal: Annual Review of Pathology: Mechanisms of Disease
articles.abstract: Passive anti–amyloid-β immunotherapy has shifted from repeated phase 3 failure to reproducible, although modest, clinical slowing in biomarker-defined early Alzheimer's disease. We review lessons from first-generation antibodies, including inadequate target engagement, late-stage enrollment, and limited outcome sensitivity. We then compare second-generation agents (i.e., aducanumab, lecanemab, and donanemab) highlighting amyloid-β species selectivity, plaque clearance kinetics, and durability, and we discuss emerging delivery innovations. Safety is dominated by amyloid-related imaging abnormalities, likely reflecting cerebrovascular amyloid vulnerability, and requires timely baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) screening; APOE -informed counseling; and standardized, front-loaded MRI surveillance with symptom-triggered evaluation. We summarize prevention trials in autosomal dominant and sporadic preclinical populations and consider prospects for combination or sequential regimens with tau-targeting therapies. Finally, we focus on biomarker-guided implementation: blood-based prescreening, confirmation pathways, monitoring of biological response, and treat-to-clear or stopping concepts, alongside unresolved issues of health-system readiness, equity, and budget impact. Registry-enabled learning is emphasized to generate real-world safety and effectiveness evidence.

articles.title: Manipulating the Rat Embryo: Genetic and Stem Cell–Based Technologies for Physiological Research
articles.abstract: Laboratory rats ( Rattus norvegicus ) have been invaluable to biomedical research and are well-suited for physiological analyses. Nevertheless, technical challenges in embryo and genetic manipulation have historically hindered the generation of genetically modified rats, thereby limiting their use for in vivo functional genetic studies. Recent advances, including genome editing and pluripotent/germline stem cell technologies, have substantially expanded rat genetic engineering. This review summarizes the historical background and recent advances in rat embryo manipulation and highlights the rapid development of genetic tools in rats, now catching up with those available in mice. These advances provide an opportunity to reassess the value of rats as experimental models. Furthermore, the combined use of mice and rats, exemplified by interspecific chimeras and comparative studies, offers new insights into conserved and species-specific physiological mechanisms across mammals.

articles.title: Consensus, Disagreements, and Open Questions in the Psychology of Misinformation
articles.abstract: Research on misinformation has expanded rapidly over the past decade. This review examines areas of consensus and contention within the literature on misinformation, with particular attention to conceptual definitions, measurement approaches, and theoretical explanations. We outline views on what it means to be susceptible to misinformation and advocate for assessing susceptibility by focusing on the ability to discern true from false claims. Although exposure to fake news is less common online than many think, we argue that misinformation—more broadly construed—continues to be a major problem. We review evidence on cognitive and socio-affective mechanisms underlying susceptibility to misinformation, including repetition effects, lack of analytic reasoning, political identity, and information environments. We also evaluate interventions such as fact-checking, prebunking, psychological inoculation, and accuracy prompts. Overall, the literature reveals several robust findings but also significant methodological limitations and theoretical disagreements that suggest fruitful future directions for misinformation research.

articles.title: State Cannabis Policy and Public Health Research in the United States: Policy Disconnects and Research Gaps
articles.abstract: Ongoing liberalization and legalization of cannabis policy in the United States have shifted the focus of policy discussions to how legal markets should be regulated to protect public health. We reviewed the scientific literature on cannabis legalization, mapped current state cannabis policies using the National Conference of State Legislatures cannabis policy domains, and conducted a scoping review of peer-reviewed studies from 2015 to 2026 that measured specific cannabis policies and health or use outcomes. Across the 48 included studies, evidence was concentrated in licensing and business practices, nonmedical adult use regulations, medical program regulations, and local control. Our scoping review suggests that retail availability, outlet density, proximity, and local restrictions shape cannabis exposure and use. Evidence was limited for product regulations, taxes and revenue allocation, hemp/cannabidiol policies, justice system provisions, and public health/research policies. Future research should incorporate detailed policy coding, implementation measures, market data, surveillance data, and stronger researcher–policymaker linkages.

articles.title: Akkermansia muciniphila attenuates macrophage efferocytosis to enhance anti-PD-1 efficacy in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer
articles.abstract: Jiang et al. show that Akkermansia muciniphila reshapes the tumor immune environment to overcome PD-1 resistance in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS CRC). Mechanistic studies and a phase 1 trial support gut microbiome modulation as a promising strategy to improve immunotherapy in this common treatment-resistant disease.

articles.title: Divergent interplay between STIM1 and STIM2 sets the efficacy of central synapses
articles.abstract: Stromal interaction molecules (STIMs) are endoplasmic reticulum resident calcium (Ca2+ sensors that modulate Ca2+ homeostasis. Mammals express two isoforms, STIM1 and STIM2, but whether they serve redundant or distinct roles in neurotransmission remains poorly defined. Using Ca2+ imaging and electrophysiology in hippocampal neurons lacking STIM1, STIM2, or both, we examined presynaptic and postsynaptic functions of STIMs at excitatory and inhibitory synapses. Both isoforms redundantly activated store-operated Ca2+ entry and amplified presynaptic Ca2+ influx, sustaining neurotransmitter release by expanding the readily releasable pool of synaptic vesicles and accelerating vesicle replenishment. These presynaptic roles were synapse specific: STIM1 predominantly supported excitatory synapses, whereas STIM2 was critical for the inhibitory counterparts. Postsynaptically, STIM1 and STIM2 exerted opposing effects on glutamate and GABA receptor levels, such that simultaneous loss of both isoforms rescued postsynaptic function. Together, the findings show that STIM1 and STIM2 differentially tune synaptic efficacy according to synapse type and subcellular compartment.

articles.title: Early-life high-fat diet accelerates the development of vagal satiation signaling and predisposes females to overconsumption
articles.abstract: Overconsumption of foods rich in fats, sugars, and calories is a major contributing factor to increased risk for cardiometabolic disease. Ingestive experience with these foods can begin early in children, yet there is limited understanding of the impact of early life nutrition on the development of vagal afferent neurons necessary for coordinating appetitive and satiating behaviors. To address this gap, mice reared on a chow diet (control) were compared to those reared on a high-fat diet (HFDEARLY). We demonstrate that the vagally mediated satiation response to cholecystokinin (CCK) does not mature until adolescence in chow-reared mice. However, HFDEARLY exposure triggers a precocious maturation of this response, accompanied by transcriptomic changes in the nodose ganglion. Durable changes in orosensory processing and appetitive behaviors are also evident in adult female HFDEARLY mice, which consume more lipid and calorie-dense liquid diet than controls, suggesting a lasting, sex-specific vulnerability to overconsumption of palatable, energy-dense foods.

articles.title: Lymphangiogenesis driven by VEGF-C reshapes tumor immune landscape and enables tumor eradication by viral immunotherapy in mouse melanoma models
articles.abstract: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor C (VEGF-C), a key lymphangiogenic growth factor, has been implicated in improving responses to cancer immunotherapy. We investigated the impact of VEGF-C on the efficacy of oncolytic virotherapy with avian paramyxoviruses APMV-1 (NDV) and APMV-4. Treatment of B16F10 tumors lacking VEGF-C delays tumor growth, and complete responses (CRs) are rare. In contrast, virotherapy of VEGF-C-expressing tumors leads to CRs in most mice. Rechallenged mice remain tumor- and metastasis-free for over two years, indicating durable immunity. VEGF-C-induced lymphangiogenesis correlates with high CD8+ and CD4+ T cell densities near lymphatic vessels. Spectral flow cytometry shows changes in the composition and activation of CD8+ T cells, CD4+ T cells and NK cells associated with CRs, including enrichment of CD8+CD25+PD-1+ effector T cells. T cell composition changes in sentinel and contralateral lymph nodes, indicating a systemic response. These findings demonstrate that VEGF-C-driven remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment enables durable CRs to APMV virotherapy.

articles.title: NAD+ precursor treatment prevents cardiomyopathy but disrupts erythroid maturation in mitochondrial progeria
Neoplastic and non-neoplastic astrocyte states converge on mesenchymal and injury-response programs during glioblastoma recurrence
articles.abstract: Glioblastomas initially respond to radiotherapy but invariably recur, often within high-dose radiation treatment fields. Although stromal radiation responses are incompletely understood, evidence suggests that the tumor microenvironment becomes tumor-supportive after therapy. Using a genetically engineered glioblastoma mouse model, we profiled healthy brain, primary tumors, and post-radiotherapy recurrences with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics and immunofluorescence. Across 13 non-neoplastic cell types and 10 tumor cell states, we mapped transcriptional adaptations accompanying progression from healthy brain to primary and recurrent glioblastoma. We find distinct astrocyte states linked to disease stage, including reactive, non-neoplastic astrocytes and tumor cells adopting reactive astrocyte-like phenotypes. Reactive astrocyte-like tumor cells with mesenchymal and injury-response signatures are enriched after radiotherapy and persist in recurrent tumors. Receptor-ligand interactions between reactive astrocytes and tumor cells include known and putative drivers of aggressiveness. These findings highlight convergent reactive astrocyte programs in astrocytes and tumor cells as potential mediators of glioblastoma radioresistance.

articles.title: The COX2-PGE2-PKA axis suppresses antiviral immunity by inhibiting mtDNA-dependent STING activation
articles.abstract: The stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway is essential for mounting robust innate immunity, yet its chronic activation can drive detrimental inflammation. Although multiple cell-autonomous mechanisms that restrain STING signaling have been reported, whether inflammatory mediators within the tissue microenvironment regulate STING activation remains elusive. Using herpes simplex virus type 1 infection as a model of STING activation, we revealed that the COX2-PGE2-PKA axis functions as a critical negative regulator of STING-mediated antiviral innate immunity. Mechanistically, PGE2 acts through the EP4-PKA cascade to induce PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1)-mediated mitophagy by phosphorylating STOML2 at Ser29. This pathway facilitates the clearance of damaged mitochondria that serve as a source of immunostimulatory cytosolic mitochondrial DNA, thereby attenuating downstream STING activation and type I interferons while promoting viral replication. Together, these findings establish mitochondrial quality control as the mechanistic link between PGE2 signaling and mtDNA-dependent STING activation and identify the COX2-PGE2-PKA pathway as a druggable therapeutic target to enhance STING-mediated innate immunity.

articles.title: NKG2D overexpression potentiates CAR-T cells through costimulation by tumor NKG2D ligands
articles.abstract: Li et al. show that activated CAR-T cells upregulate NKG2D ligands (NKG2DLs), rendering them susceptible to NK cells. Overexpressing NKG2D shields endogenous ligands and harnesses tumor NKG2DLs for costimulation, thereby enhancing CAR-T cell persistence, tumor infiltration, and antitumor efficacy across multiple models.

articles.title: Targeting MMGT1 enhances immunotherapy efficacy in triple-negative breast cancer
articles.abstract: Liu et al. demonstrate that high membrane magnesium transporter 1 (MMGT1) expression promotes immune evasion via a senescence-associated secretory phenotype that induces CD8+ T cells exhaustion. Targeting MMGT1 represents a promising strategy to improve anti-PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy.
